# CreateDrawer (`create/create-drawer`)

> The right-side form drawer every item created or edited inside a resource opens, such as a domain, a record, an environment, a variable or a rule: a panel header with the title, a muted one-line description and the cl…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-drawer/create-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-drawer")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CodeEditor, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, Hint, IconButton, Input, InputGroup, Item, KeyValueList, Link, NumberInput, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioGroup, SchemaForm, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, StatusIndicator, Switch, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

create domain; add domain; create domain form; add domain drawer; edit domain; new domain; create drawer; custom domain; criar domínio; adicionar domínio; novo domínio; create in drawer; add record; add environment; criar em gaveta; form drawer; side drawer form; add item drawer; edit drawer; dns record form; nested resource form; gaveta de formulário; adicionar registro; formulário lateral; add origin drawer; form in drawer; formulário em gaveta; nested drawer; stacked drawers; drawer on drawer; create related item; create option in select; child form; gaveta aninhada; gavetas empilhadas; criar item relacionado; add rule; create origin in drawer; build and deployment; build deployment settings; deployment settings; deployment defaults; deploy configuration; workload deployment defaults; build settings; configurações de build; configurações de deploy; implantação; create deployment settings; deployment settings drawer; criar configuração de deploy; certificate; upload certificate; tls certificate; pem; certificate expiry; certificado; importar certificado; certificado tls; create environment; environment form; ip allowlist; branch tracking; function instance; function arguments; schema form in drawer; criar ambiente; instância de função

The right-side drawer that adds or edits something that only exists inside another resource: a domain, a DNS record, an environment, a variable, a rule. The user is working on the resource behind it and must keep it in view, so the form slides over the page instead of replacing it. They fill a few sections, press the one commit button and land back where they were, with the new item in the list. The drawer opens over a console page: ItemRows and NestedDrawer draw that page as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

## When to use

- The item belongs to a resource that is already open (a domain on a workload, a record in a zone, a rule or an origin on a resource), per the surface rule in `skills/webkit-create-surface`.
- Editing that same item from its row menu; the drawer opens on its values and saves them.
- A first-level tuple normally created in bulk, such as variables, the one exception the surface rule allows.
- A select needs another item of the same resource that may not exist yet, such as the origin a new rule sends requests to: the NestedDrawer shape creates it in a second drawer and selects it back.
- A form needs a resource that does not exist yet, first-level ones included, such as the digital certificate of a workload being created: offer `Create certificate` in the field, and the drawer holds that resource's own create form (`large` over a page, `medium` over a drawer) and selects it back. The reader never leaves the form to create it.

## When not to use

- A resource the sidebar routes to: create it on a page with `create/create-page`, or `create/create-wizard` when it needs several pages.
- A blocking yes or no question, or a destructive guard: use `edit/delete-dialog`.
- Deploying what exists: use `create/deploy-drawer`, which commits a deployment rather than a record.
- Binding a whole resource that may be reused or created in a create flow: use `create/resource-picker`.
- A missing resource whose creation takes several steps, such as a project imported from a repository: open its create page in a new tab and give the field a `Refresh` option.
- Editing the settings of the resource itself: use `edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

- A. Trigger — `Button` (required)
- B. Drawer frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent` (required)
- C. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle` (required)
- D. Sections — `PanelBody`, `SettingsSection` (required)
- E. Environment select — `Field`, `Select` (required)
- F. Domain source — `Field`, `RadioGroup` (required)
- G. Domain name — `Field`, `InputGroup` (required)
- H. Certificate — `Field`, `Select`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- I. Context alert — `Alert` (optional)
- J. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- K. Certificate import — `SettingsSection`, `Field`, `Button`, `PanelFooter` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-drawer.md](blocks/create/create-drawer.md).

## Do

- Open on a blank form every time, or on the edited item's values, and clear every error on open.
- Lock the `fieldset` and pass `:disabled` to every control from the same flag while saving; release it on success and on failure.
- Validate on submit only: an empty required field gets the amber required prompt after Save is pressed.
- Close the drawer on success and show the new item in the list behind it, with a toast that names it (every variant does).
- On a failed save keep the drawer open with the values, release the fieldset and show a danger `Alert` with Retry above the footer (SaveError).
- Stack a second, medium drawer for a missing item of the same resource, such as an origin for a rule, and select the new one back into the parent.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't create in a dialog, or open a page for an item that lives inside a resource.
- Don't add Cancel next to the commit button.
- Don't flag fields while the user is still typing, or show required and invalid on one field at once.
- Don't hide a required field inside a collapsed section.
- Don't reset the form on close; the content would jump while the drawer slides out.
- Don't deploy or publish as a side effect of Save.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** one string, `Add <Product Module>` inside a resource, e.g. "Add Domain"; editing keeps the verb the row menu used.
- **Description:** one or two muted sentences with a period under the title, e.g. "A domain is what puts an environment on this resource. Say where it answers, and name the address."
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "Where the domain answers."
- **Options:** labels name the choice, descriptions one sentence, e.g. "Use your own DNS and point it to this resource."
- **Helper text:** states the consequence of the current value, e.g. "Production publishes with the Deployment Settings set to Single."
- **Required:** "This field is required."
- **Create option:** `Create <Object>` at the foot of the select, e.g. "Create Environment".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", select rather than pick.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open, moves it to the first field on open and returns it to the trigger on close.
- The `form` has an `aria-label` that matches the title; `DrawerTitle` names the dialog.
- Every select trigger is described by its `Field.Description` (or its `Field.Error`) through the `Field`, so the consequence is read with the value.
- Required fields carry the Required marker from the start; an error is a `Field.Error` with `role="alert"` and the control is `aria-invalid`.
- The choice cards are a radio group named by the Domain source label; each card's title and description are the radio's name and description.
- The loading button keeps its label and announces the busy state; the disabled `fieldset` keeps keyboard users out of the form while saving.
- Escape, the close button and the overlay all dismiss; none of them submit.

## States

- Default: Add Domain opened from the resource's Settings tab, blank, on the free domain option.
- AddEnvironment: the same form opened from the environment menu, titled and saved as Add Environment.
- EditDomain: opened from a domain row menu on www.example.com, with the Certificate select showing the covering wildcard.
- AddRecord: the DNS zone record form; Name and Value are flagged as required only after an empty Add Record.
- ItemRows: Add Origin on the Origins page of the storefront resource, a large drawer whose sections are `Item` rows in flush cards, saved together by one Add Origin.
- NestedDrawer: Add Rule on the storefront resource's Rules Engine, with an Origin select whose Create Origin option opens a second, medium drawer and selects the new origin back.
- DeploymentSettings: the drawer that creates a Deployment Setting, with General and Routing and policy sections.
- Certificate: Create Certificate opened with shop.example.com pasted as a server certificate: the details panel reads Issued to shop.example.com, Issued by Example Test CA and the expiry with the days left; the private key is empty, so Save flags it.
- CreateEnvironment: Create Environment with General, Settings, Protection and Branch tracking sections; the IP allowlist and Branch tracking switches each reveal their fields, a duplicate name or an invalid address is flagged only after Create Environment. Opened from Add Domain's Environment select it stacks at medium size above that drawer and selects the new environment back.
- SaveError: Add Domain after a failed save: the drawer stays open with acme-store and Production kept, the fieldset released, and a danger Alert with Retry above the footer.
- FunctionInstance: Add Function Instance (or Edit from a row) with a Function `Select`, a Name, and the arguments as a `SchemaForm` of the chosen function's schema with a Fields or JSON `ToggleGroup`; the JSON `CodeEditor` marks a parse error, and required arguments are flagged only after submit.

## Asked as

create hub; creation center; new project; start a project; import from github; import repository; start from template; template gallery; create from git; central de criação; novo projeto; importar repositório; começar de um template; create project; where to start; começar um projeto

The Creation Center, where a new project starts. The user arrives from Home or a Create action with something to deploy and needs to pick its source in one look: a repository from their Git account, a template, or a file or folder from their machine. The page puts the two main sources side by side, Import from GitHub and Start from template, under one heading, and offers file and folder upload in the heading.

## When to use

- Use create-hub as the first screen of every new project, where the user picks Git, a template or an upload.
- The entry point of every new project, before the user has decided where the code comes from.
- The user may import an existing repository, start from a framework or starter template, or upload local files.
- The choice leads to a focused flow outside the console shell, such as `create/deploy-template`.

## When not to use

- Creating a first-level resource that has no source code: use `create/create-page`.
- Configuring and deploying once the source is known: use `create/deploy-template`.
- A first-level resource created in ordered steps: use `create/create-wizard`.
- Adding something inside an existing resource: use `create/create-drawer`.
- The drop target and upload progress after a folder is dropped: those are `state/project-intake`.
- Teaching a module to a new account: use `state/first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Git connect — `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Alert`, `Link` (required until connected)
- D. Repository search — `Select`, `Input` (required once connected)
- E. Repository list — `Card`, `Item`, `Button`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `EmptyState` (required once connected)
- F. Template gallery — `Input`, `ScrollArea`, `Card`, `EmptyState` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-hub.md](blocks/create/create-hub.md).

## Do

- Keep both sources visible at once from the large breakpoint, the Git column first.
- Show the connect state only until an account exists, then go straight to the list.
- Let the search accept a pasted repository URL, so the user does not have to find it in the list.
- Keep template sections in the same order on every visit; Recommended first.
- Offer file and folder buttons in the heading so uploading works without a mouse.
- Show a failed connection or a failed load with a danger `Alert` and a way to retry, and a search with no match with an `EmptyState` and Clear search.

## Don't

- Don't put the hub inside the console shell or open it in a drawer; it is a focused page.
- Don't replace the list with a spinner while a scope loads; use skeleton rows in its shape.
- Don't add a Continue or Next button; each Import and each template card starts its flow.
- Don't let the template gallery push the page into a long scroll on large screens; it scrolls inside its own area.
- Don't show templates as a dense table; the glyph and sentence are what the user scans.
- Don't hand-write the file and folder links or underline them at rest; use `Button variant="link"`.

## Copy

- **Heading:** a verb phrase for the task, e.g. "Start a new project"; description one sentence with a period, e.g. "Start from a repository or use a framework template."
- **Column titles:** short fragments, e.g. "Import from GitHub".
- **Connect state:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect your repository"; description one sentence, e.g. "Select a Git provider to connect your repository and start the deployment process."
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Continue with GitHub", "Import", "Load more", "Clear search".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what it takes, e.g. "Search repositories or paste a repository URL".
- **Template cards:** title is the template name; description one sentence, e.g. "Compile Rust to WebAssembly and run it."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, select rather than choose or pick, no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`; column titles are `h2`, the template section labels `h3`, and template titles sit below them (the integration Card title, and `h4` on a Recommended card).
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link, the account button, the scope `Select` and the search each have an `aria-label`.
- Each template tile is reached through its title link, which covers the tile; Enter follows it. Each Import button is named after its repository.
- The loading region sets `aria-busy="true"` with one `role="status"` line; skeleton rows are hidden from assistive technology.
- Upload works from the keyboard: the file and folder buttons in the description open the system picker.
- The `ScrollArea` is named so screen reader users know which region scrolls.

## States

- Default: no Git account connected; the connect state beside the template gallery.
- Connected: jane-doe is the selected scope and its ten most recently pushed repositories are listed, with Load more for the rest.
- RepositoriesLoading: a scope was just picked; six skeleton rows stand in for the repositories.
- ConnectError: the GitHub connection failed; a danger Alert under Continue with GitHub.
- LoadError: the repositories failed to load; a danger Alert with Retry in place of the list.

# CreatePage (`create/create-page`)

> The page a first-level resource is created on in one screen: its own creation header with no sidebar, a centred form column opening with a small page heading, then stacked sections, each a heading with a Hint over a f…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-page/create-page.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-page")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, RadioGroup, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Switch, Tag, Textarea, Toast
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

create page; create resource page; create zone; full page create form; top-level create page; new resource form; creation page; página de criação; criar recurso; formulário de criação; single page create; create purge; create service page; criação em uma página; sectioned form; single column form; form with sections; formulário em seções; formulário de uma coluna; import zone file; create dns zone; importar arquivo de zona; create organization; new organization form; organization mark; criar organização; one page create; create form page

The page a first-level resource is created on when everything it needs fits on one screen. The user arrives from the module's `Create <Object>` button, answers the required fields at the top, leaves the defaulted ones folded under Advanced, and commits from a bar that never scrolls away. The page has its own URL, its own creation header and no sidebar, so it survives a reload and the back button, and leaving it returns to the list.

## When to use

- Use create-page only to create a first-level resource on one page; its settings page is edit-resource (`edit/edit-resource`).
- The resource is one the sidebar routes to (a domain, a service, a purge) and the user came only to create it (`skills/webkit-create-surface`).
- Its fields fit in a few sections without depending on each other's answers step by step.
- An action that takes a form and runs once, whose submit names what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).

## When not to use

- The fields split into steps that unlock in order, or one answer adds a step: use `create/create-wizard`.
- The resource binds another one and then deploys: use `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy).
- Deploying a repository, a template or an uploaded folder: start at `create/create-hub` and deploy with `create/deploy-template` (ImportFromGit covers a Git import).
- The thing is created inside another resource (a record in a zone, a rule in an application): use `create/create-drawer`.
- The settings page of an existing resource, with the save bar that mounts only after a change: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Never put a create form in a dialog.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item` (required)
- D. Field rows — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError` (required)
- E. Switch rows — `Switch` (optional)
- F. Commit bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-page.md](blocks/create/create-page.md).

## Do

- Put every required field in the first band; never inside Advanced, so a failed submit always points at something on screen.
- Validate on submit only, then clear each message as soon as its field is edited.
- Give every control an `aria-label` that repeats its row title.
- Keep Cancel and the submit in the same bar, submit last, and name the submit after what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).
- Lock the whole `fieldset` and every control with one `submitting` flag while the request is in flight, and put `:loading` on the submit.
- On success, show a toast that names the resource and opens it; on failure, an error toast with Retry that keeps the values (`skills/webkit-errors`). Every submit in this block models the request: Default, CreateZone, CreatePurge, CreateService and CreateOrganization.

## Don't

- Don't show the sidebar on this page, or open it as a modal over the list.
- Don't stretch the commit bar across the page or build the centred card by hand; it is `SaveBar variant="centered"`.
- Don't print the band's guidance as a paragraph under its title; use the `hint`.
- Don't mark fields required or invalid before the first submit, or show both states on one field.
- Don't make Save deploy, publish or charge as a side effect; creating is not deploying.
- Don't add a validation summary at the top; each message sits at its field.
- Don't squeeze a textarea or radio group into the right-hand cell; stack the row.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label, verb first with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Domain". Identical to the button that opened the page.
- **Description:** one sentence on what the resource is, e.g. "A domain holds the DNS records that answer authoritatively for a hostname."
- **Section titles:** the domain, not the widget, e.g. "General", "Target", "Delivery settings", "Advanced".
- **Row descriptions:** a full sentence with a period, saying what the value does, e.g. "Identifies the domain in this list. It is not the hostname."
- **Submit:** one verb, e.g. "Save", "Purge", "Deploy". Cancel is always exactly "Cancel".
- **Required message:** "This field is required."
- **Invalid message:** what to enter, with an example, e.g. "Enter a valid domain name. Example: example.com."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no parentheses in labels, no "please".

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holding one `form`, labelled by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby`, with `novalidate` so the page's own messages replace the browser's.
- A `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` groups the sections.
- Each message is tied to its control with `aria-describedby` and appears only on submit; required and invalid are announced through the control's own state.
- The collapsed Advanced region is `inert` while closed, so keyboard focus never lands in hidden fields.
- The back `IconButton` and the account trigger have `aria-label`s; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: header, heading, General, Advanced toggle, then the bar's Cancel and Save (CreateZone adds Import before them).

## States

- Default: the Create Domain page at rest; General holds Name and Domain name, Advanced is collapsed, the bar shows Cancel and Save. Importing a zone file belongs to CreateZone, not to this page.
- CreateZone: Create Zone after a zone file is imported; a Records section lists each imported record (type `Tag`, value, TTL) with a Remove `IconButton` per row and Discard import in the card footer. Import in the bar and a paste into Domain name both read a BIND zone file, skip the SOA and nameserver records, fill an empty Name and Domain name from `$ORIGIN`, and confirm in a toast; a file with no records raises an error toast. The list previews the first 50 records with an "and N more" line, and a re-import skips records already listed.
- CreateOrganization: General with Name and a Mark color chosen from six `RadioGroup` cards (`variant="card"`) (each color built from semantic tokens: primary, warning, danger, success, info and the text grays, never palette primitives), each an `Avatar` with `pattern="marble"` seeded by the name in that color's `colors`, above an In the header preview drawn the same way, an Owner `Item` with Owner and Active `Tag`s, First workspace and a collapsed Advanced of `Select`s; a name already in use is invalid on submit, and the request ends in a success toast or an error toast with Retry.
- CreatePurge: a Target band of radio choice cards for Layer and Purge type, an Arguments textarea that follows the type, a warning alert and a bar with Cancel and Purge.
- CreateService: a long create with a small `PageHeader` (Create Service, breadcrumb Services / Create Service) and five groups of rows, each under an `h2`, under the same centred `SaveBar` with Cancel and Save.
- RequiredFields: Create Service after Save on the empty form; Name and Address show "This field is required." until edited.

## Related

- `create/create-wizard` — the same job split into steps.
- `create/create-drawer` — create inside a resource without leaving it.
- `settings/settings-form` — the edit page that reuses these sections.
- `state/form-validation` — required and invalid states on submit.
- `view/table-view` — the list whose `Create <Object>` button opens this page.
- `SettingsRow` — the field row every section is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.

`Default` (primary) · `CreateZone` · `CreateOrganization` · `CreatePurge` · `CreateService` · `RequiredFields`. Code: [blocks/create/create-page.md](blocks/create/create-page.md), `get_block("create/create-page", { variant })`.

# CreateWizard (`create/create-wizard`)

> The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time, built on the `Wizard` component: the creation header, a page heading, then the Wizard with its step rail on the start side (completed steps reachable,…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/create-wizard/create-wizard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/create-wizard")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, Hint, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, RadioGroup, RadioGroup, SectionHeader, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Switch, Tag, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Wizard
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

multipage create; multi-step create page; stepper create; create wizard; step by step form; criação em etapas; formulário em etapas; review step; review and create; confirm before create; wizard review; summary before submit; revisar; etapa de revisão; revisão antes de criar; review before create; summary step; revisar antes de criar; provision wizard; create service wizard; two-step wizard; create and deploy; bind domain and deployment; create resource in steps; assistente de criação; criar serviço; asistente de creación; crear en pasos

The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time. It is the `Wizard` component in a creation page: the user first says where the resource runs, then answers each step's fields in order, and only reaches the create action on the last step. The Wizard's rail shows how far they are and lets them return to any step already passed; if the host they chose lacks a module the resource needs, a step is inserted that offers to turn it on, so nothing is created that would silently never be read. The same frame creates a resource that must be bound and deployed in one act (CreateAndDeploy).

## When to use

- Use create-wizard when a first-level resource is created in ordered steps (a later answer changes what is asked); it is the Wizard component in a creation page.
- A first-level resource whose fields fall into groups that make sense one at a time (general, then type, then entries) and where a later group depends on an earlier answer.
- The resource must first bind to a host (a policy, an application) and that choice can change what is asked next.
- A resource that is useless until it is bound to another and deployed, such as a service that serves a project on a domain: use the CreateAndDeploy variant, whose last action creates and deploys.
- A code resource whose editor needs a whole step to itself.

## When not to use

- Everything fits on one screen without order: use `create/create-page`.
- The resource is created inside another one: use `create/create-drawer`.
- A new project from a code source (Git, a template, an upload): start at `create/create-hub` and deploy with `create/deploy-template`.
- Binding an existing or new resource inside a form step: use `create/resource-picker`.
- Deploying an existing package from inside a resource: use `create/deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Wizard — `Wizard`, `Wizard.Step` (required)
- D. Where it runs — `Input`, `Item`, `Tag`, `FieldError`, `Button` (required)
- E. Module step — `Card`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Switch` (conditional)
- F. Field steps — `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError` (required)
- G. Choice cards — `RadioGroup` (optional)
- H. Long entry — `Textarea`, `FieldError` (optional)
- I. Review — `SectionHeader`, `Alert`, `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Button` (required)
- J. Create and deploy — `Card`, `Field`, `Input`, `Item`, `RadioGroup` (CreateAndDeploy)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/create-wizard.md](blocks/create/create-wizard.md).

## Do

- Ask where the resource runs first, and insert the module step only when the chosen host needs it.
- Validate one step at a time in the `next` handler, and show the message under the field that failed.
- Keep Cancel apart from Previous and Next, on the opposite side; the Wizard footer does this.
- Keep the create action on the last step only; every step before it says Next.
- Keep the chosen host visible in the chooser even when it falls outside the first six.
- Label the final action with every act it performs: "Create and deploy" when it also deploys.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't build the rail, the step heading or the footer by hand; the `Wizard` owns them.
- Don't let the user skip ahead to steps not reached yet.
- Don't block the create when a module is off; warn, offer the switch and let the user go on.
- Don't repeat the step title as a second heading inside the card.
- Don't validate fields of later steps, or judge a field while it is being typed.
- Don't put a required field inside Advanced, or show both the existing list and the new fields at once.

## Copy

- **Title, breadcrumb and last submit:** the create label with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Access List"; "Create and deploy" when the last step also deploys.
- **Step titles:** short nouns, e.g. "Where it runs", "General", "List settings", "Project", "Domain and deployment".
- **Step descriptions:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "Select the policy whose rules match it. It needs IP filtering on."
- **Chooser:** the search placeholder and `aria-label` name what is searched, e.g. "Search policies"; Next with no answer says "Select a policy, or continue without one."
- **Module tag:** the missing module and its state, e.g. "IP filtering off".
- **Module alert:** the consequence in one sentence, e.g. "acme-staging has IP filtering off, so no rule reads this list until the module is on."
- **Escape routes:** verb first, e.g. "Create a policy", "Continue without a policy".
- **Required message:** "This field is required.", or what to do, e.g. "Select the project this service serves, or create a new one."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Choose"; no em dash; no "simply".

## Accessibility

- The `Wizard` takes an `aria-label` naming the flow; locked rail steps cannot be focused or activated, and focus moves to the new step's heading on every step change.
- The page has one `h1` (the `PageHeader`); each step heading is an `h2` drawn by the Wizard.
- Host rows are native `button`s with `aria-pressed`; the chooser's search has an `aria-label` and Enter selects the first match.
- Choice cards are a `RadioGroup` named with `aria-label`; each `RadioGroup.Item` is labelled by its card.
- Required messages are tied to their control with `aria-describedby`; focus stays on the step after a failed Next.
- Step transitions honour reduced motion.

## States

- WhereItRuns: the first step; the chooser of policies with search, module tags and the two escape routes.
- ModuleOff: acme-staging was chosen with IP filtering off, so the IP filtering step shows the warning, the switch card and the note.
- ListSettings: the settings step; Type as radio choice cards and the List textarea, with Previous and Next (Review follows). Next with an empty list stays and shows the message.
- Review: the last step, read-only, with the create action in the footer. Where it runs is one `Alert` whose severity says whether anything will read the resource; What gets created pairs each value with the property it is sent as and shows long lists as their first five `Tag`s and a count; What can reference it names the consumers. Each band that maps to a step has an outlined Edit (`aria-label` names the band) that jumps back to that step. Create re-validates every step and, on a failure, opens the first step with an error.
- CreateAndDeploy: Create Service on its Project step with the paged project list; Next is gated on the project, and step two ends on Create and deploy with its loading state.

## Review step

- Add a Review step when the create has three or more steps or binds the resource to something; skip it for a one-step create.
- Show values as they will be sent, with the property name under each, and never show secrets in clear.
- Put Edit on each band, and on a value whose step differs from its band's (Name, on General); after the edit, Next walks forward through the later steps, already filled, back to Review.
- Say plainly when nothing will read the resource yet (unbound, or a module off) with a warning `Alert`, not a disabled create.

## Related

- `Wizard` — the component this block is built on; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `create/create-page` — the same job when the fields fit one screen.
- `create/create-hub` and `create/deploy-template` — a new project from Git, a template or an upload.
- `create/resource-picker` — the Existing or New band CreateAndDeploy binds its project with.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — the build log Create and deploy hands the column to (InCreateFlow).
- `create/deploy-success` — the screen a create-and-deploy ends on.
- `edit/function-editor` — the editor a code resource can use as one step.
- `state/form-validation` — required and invalid states on Next.

## Steps

- where-it-runs
- module
- general
- settings
- review

## Variants

`WhereItRuns` (primary) · `ModuleOff` · `ListSettings` · `Review` · `CreateAndDeploy`. Code: [blocks/create/create-wizard.md](blocks/create/create-wizard.md), `get_block("create/create-wizard", { variant })`.

# DeployDrawer (`create/deploy-drawer`)

> The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by the outlined Deploy button on a service or a project.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/deploy-drawer/deploy-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/deploy-drawer")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Input, Item, Link, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Popover, RadioGroup, Separator, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Spinner, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

deploy drawer; deploy panel; deploy service; choose versions to deploy; dependencies before deploy; release drawer; gaveta de deploy; implantar serviço; escolher versão

The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by Deploy on a service or a project. The user is about to put a version into traffic and needs to confirm exactly what goes out (each resource and dependency at a version), where it goes (a project and one of its environments) and what else it reaches (every project that shares the environment's Deployment Settings). One Deploy at the foot commits all of it.

## When to use

- A service or a project has a ready version and the user deploys it from its page or list.
- The deploy reaches more than the resource itself: dependencies at their own versions, or other projects through shared Deployment Settings.
- A service deploys to a project that may not exist yet; the Project section creates it in place.

## When not to use

- A release of several resources reviewed together: use `create/release-impact`. This drawer is the canonical surface for deploying one service or one project.

- Creating or editing an item inside a resource: use `create/create-drawer`.
- The first deploy at the end of a create flow: use `create/deploy-template` or `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy), which stream the create-flow card of `detail/deployment-logs` in the page.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `detail/deployment-logs` or `detail/version-detail`.
- Binding one resource to another without deploying: use `create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Trigger and frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerContent` (required)
- B. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle` (required)
- C. Sections — `PanelBody`, `SettingsSection` (required)
- D. Resources card — `Card`, `Separator`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Avatar`, `Button` (required)
- E. Dependencies — `Accordion`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- F. Project — `ToggleGroup`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu` (required on a service)
- G. Environment — `RadioGroup`, `Tag` (required)
- H. Projects impacted and commit — `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on a service)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/deploy-drawer.md](blocks/create/deploy-drawer.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that will go out, even when the user changes nothing.
- Preselect the last used project and environment, and say so with a tag.
- List every project a shared Deployment Setting reaches before the user deploys, not after.
- When no version is pinned, open as Build and deployment with a Building row, keep the other sections faded and `inert`, and disable Deploy until the build lands.
- On a project, warn with an `Alert` above the environments when its Deployment Settings also deploy elsewhere.
- Keep an environment that Strict Deployment Settings lock visible but disabled, with a Strict tag and one sentence naming the settings and the service they keep bound.
- Tag an environment Also deploys (warning) when the chosen environment's shared settings reach it, and say once, in a warning `Alert`, how many environments go live at once.
- Say in an info `Alert` when the deploy replaces another service on the chosen project, naming both.
- When a choice changes what the deploy reaches, reload that section in place: `Skeleton` rows, `aria-busy` on the region and one `role="status"` line; never clear the whole drawer.
- Tag a dependency other services reference as Shared, name them in a `Tooltip`, and say once that a shared dependency deploys at one version.
- Resolve the drawer in place: while the resources and environments load, keep the section titles and render `Skeleton` blocks shaped like the Resources card and the environment cards, with `aria-busy` and one status line, and Deploy disabled.
- When the targets fail to load, replace the sections with one danger `Alert` saying what failed and an outlined Retry; Deploy stays disabled.
- When the project has no environment, show the Environment section as a bordered small `EmptyState` with Add environment, and say in the footer why Deploy is disabled. A Resources card with nothing bound says so in one line instead of disappearing.
- When a dependency has no ready version, disable Deploy and say why in the footer, next to the button it disables.
- After Deploy, follow `state/async-submit`: the drawer closes and one toast per run turns from Deploying… into the outcome, with Edit (reopens the drawer with the same choices) and Redeploy.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't deploy one service from a dialog, or ask for confirmation after Deploy; the drawer is the review. This is the one confirmation rule across the deploy surfaces: the surface that shows what goes live is the review, and nothing confirms it again. A release of several resources is reviewed on a page (`create/release-impact`, whose single `ConfirmDialog` states the reach); a dropped folder is reviewed in the Drop confirm of `create/deploy-progress-dialog`.
- Don't hide dependencies or impacted projects behind a second step.
- Don't let Change version list hundreds of versions at once; search plus Load more.
- Don't add a second commit such as Save as draft; one Deploy.
- Don't print the shared-settings warning on each impacted row; it belongs once, above them.
- Don't hide a locked environment, or let it be picked and fail at deploy time.
- Don't offer View deployments in the outcome toast; it carries Edit and Redeploy.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** "Deploy" on all three; "Build and deployment" as the title only while a build runs first.
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "The project whose domains serve the service."
- **Version control:** "Change version", named "Change version of <resource>" for assistive technology; search placeholder and `aria-label` "Search versions"; footer "Load 10 more".
- **Project modes:** "Use existing" and "Create new".
- **Environment descriptions:** one sentence on how it serves, e.g. "Live traffic. One version serves the domain, and deploying replaces it."
- **Footer summary:** "1 change goes live in Production." or "3 changes go live in Production."
- **Load failure:** "The deploy targets for project-01 couldn't be loaded. Check your connection and try again." with "Retry".
- **No environment:** "No environment on this project", one sentence on why there is no target, and "Add environment"; footer "Add an environment to deploy."
- **Tags:** one or two words, e.g. "Ready", "Active", "Last used", "Selected", "New".
- **In progress:** the progressive verb with `…`, e.g. "Building…".
- **Run toast:** "Deploying web-app…" with "<version> to <environments>. It keeps running if you leave."; the outcome "web-app is live in Production." or "web-app wasn't deployed." with what failed and that nothing changed; actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **Locks and reach:** "<settings> is Strict, so <service> stays bound to <environment>."; "Also deploys"; "<settings> is shared, so it deploys at one version."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish or activate; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the Deploy trigger on close.
- The `form` and the `ToggleGroup` carry `aria-label`s; the environment group is named by its `aria-label`.
- The version menu is a `role="menu"` moved with the arrow keys, each version a `menuitem` named by its version, author and age; the current one carries `aria-current`; search inputs have an `aria-label` that matches the placeholder.
- Each impacted environment group has an `aria-label` with its count, e.g. "Projects impacted in Production (3)".
- Faded sections during a build are `inert`, so keyboard users cannot reach controls that do nothing yet.
- A section that reloads carries `aria-busy="true"` with its `Skeleton` rows `aria-hidden`, and a `role="status"` line reads Loading the projects this deployment reaches, or Loading dependencies.
- A locked environment's radio is `disabled`; its reason is the card's description, so it is read with the choice.
- The Shared tag sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard, and its name already says who else references it.
- A disabled Deploy is described by the footer line that explains why (`aria-describedby`).
- Run progress and outcome reach screen readers through the toast region, so the user hears them from any page.
- Glyphs in rows are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; tags give the state in words.

## States

- Service: a service deploying environment first; Resources, Project with the last used project, Environment and Projects impacted, and the footer counting the one version change that goes live in Production.
- Building: no pinned version; titled Build and deployment with a Building row in place of Resources, the other sections faded and inert, Deploy disabled.
- ServiceProjectFirst: the project-first flow; Resources, the Project card with the last used project and a Change popover, then every environment.
- Project: deploying a project; its service and storage in Resources, Production and Preview, and a warning about other projects that share its storefront settings.
- Environment: a locked Strict environment, an Also deploys tag, the replace and multi-environment `Alert`s, Projects impacted grouped per environment and reloaded on switch; the run ends in a success toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Loading: the resources and environments resolving; `Skeleton` blocks under the Resources and Environment titles, an `aria-busy` region with a status line, Deploy disabled.
- LoadError: the deploy targets failed to load; a danger `Alert` with Retry, which reloads them as Skeletons, and Deploy disabled.
- NoEnvironment: nothing bound and no environment; a one-line empty Resources card, an `EmptyState` with Add environment, and Deploy disabled with the reason in the footer.
- Dependencies: the open Dependencies disclosure with a Shared dependency, a not-versioned integration and a dependency with no ready version that blocks Deploy; changing the service version reloads the list. The first run fails and its toast offers Edit and Redeploy; Redeploy succeeds.

## Related

- `create/create-drawer` — the drawer that creates items rather than deploying.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — the run a deploy streams once it starts.
- `state/async-submit` — the toast and outcome rule every deploy started here follows.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — the logs of a deploy after it ran.
- `detail/version-detail` — what a version contains before it is deployed.
- `create/resource-picker` — the Existing or New pattern the Project section follows.
- `SettingsSection` — the band each section uses; see `skills/webkit-create-surface` for the drawer commit model.

## Variants

`Service` (primary) · `Building` · `ServiceProjectFirst` · `Project` · `Environment` · `Dependencies` · `Loading` · `LoadError` · `NoEnvironment`. Code: [blocks/create/deploy-drawer.md](blocks/create/deploy-drawer.md), `get_block("create/deploy-drawer", { variant })`.

# DeployProgressDialog (`create/deploy-progress-dialog`)

> The modal progress of one deploy that sends several Deployment Settings live, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/deploy-progress-dialog/deploy-progress-dialog.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/deploy-progress-dialog")`
- Components: Button, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, EmptyState, Item, OutcomeIcon, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Progress, Spinner, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy progress; deploy progress dialog; drop to deploy; deploy a folder; multi deploy progress; progresso do deploy; arrastar e implantar; progreso del despliegue

The modal progress of one deploy that sends several Deployment Settings live, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The user dropped a folder (or started a deploy whose environment deploys through several Deployment Settings) and wants to see each one go live, know which failed and why, and retry only those. The page behind the dialog is a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`); the dialog teleports over it.

**The toast stays the standard.** Every deploy reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy (`state/async-submit`). This dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy path and for a deploy that fans out to several Deployment Settings; even there the outcome still reaches the user through the toast, so they can close the dialog and leave.

## When to use

- A folder dropped on a service deploys straight to an environment.
- One deploy sends several Deployment Settings live that can succeed or fail independently.

## When not to use

- A deploy of one service or project: use `create/deploy-drawer`, which closes and reports through the toast.
- A deploy with build steps and logs: use `detail/deployment-logs`.
- Reviewing what a multi-resource release reaches before it runs: use `create/release-impact`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drop confirm — `Dialog`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `Tag`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on the drop path)
- B. Progress frame — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `OutcomeIcon` (required)
- C. Progress — `PanelBody`, `Progress` (required)
- D. Filter — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- E. Rows — `Item`, `OutcomeIcon`, `Spinner`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- Outcome toast — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md).

## Do

- Let each Deployment Setting settle on its own and keep the ones that succeeded live.
- Say why a row failed on the row itself.
- Offer Retry failed for the failed rows only.
- Report the outcome through the toast as well, so the user can close the dialog.

## Don't

- Don't use this dialog for a single deploy; the toast is enough.
- Don't trap the user in the dialog while the run goes on; let them hide it (the toast keeps reporting) and reopen it with Show progress.
- Don't roll back the settings that succeeded because another failed.

## Copy

- **Drop:** "New production deployment", "Dropped files", "Deploy to Production".
- **Title:** "Deploying 2 of 5…", "Deployed 5 Deployment Settings", "Deployed 4 of 5 Deployment Settings".
- **Tally:** "4 succeeded, 1 failed. Each Deployment Setting deploys on its own, and the ones that succeeded stay live."
- **Tags:** Queued, Deploying, Done, Failed. **Actions:** Retry failed, Hide (while running), Close.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, the progressive verb with `…`.

## Accessibility

- The dialog traps focus and is named by its title and described by the tally.
- The `Progress` bar is named; a `role="status"` line announces the outcome once settled.
- `OutcomeIcon` names its outcome; tags give the state in words, glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- The dropped files list is a focusable scroll region with an `aria-label`; paths are `dir="ltr"`.
- Motion: the marks honour reduced motion and the `Spinner` stops under it.

## States

- Running: two settled, one deploying, two queued; advances to its outcome.
- Drop: the confirm that starts a drop-to-deploy run.
- PartialError: settled with one failure, Retry failed, error toast.
- Success: every setting deployed, success toast.

## Related

- `state/async-submit` — the toast rule this block follows.
- `create/deploy-drawer` — the standard way to deploy.
- `create/release-impact` — what a release reaches, before it runs.
- `OutcomeIcon` — the settled mark.

## Variants

`Running` (primary) · `Drop` · `PartialError` · `Success`. Code: [blocks/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md), `get_block("create/deploy-progress-dialog", { variant })`.

# DeploySuccess (`create/deploy-success`)

> The outcome screen a create flow ends on, in the terminal column of the wizard page: a heading with its lead and, for a Git source, the scope as a Tag; the deployment card with a preview tile, the service name with a…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/deploy-success/deploy-success.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/deploy-success")`
- Components: Button, Card, CodeBlock, Item, Link, SectionHeader, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy success; deployment successful; deployed; success page; deployment complete; next steps after deploy; wizard finish; deploy concluído; sucesso do deploy; aplicação publicada

The screen a create flow ends on. The user has just watched a deploy finish and needs three answers before leaving: is it live and where, what exactly was created or bound along the way, and what to do next. The page answers them in that order in the terminal column of the wizard, then offers one way out to manage the resource.

## When to use

- A create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a source or provision wizard) has finished and the resource is serving, or was created for the first time.
- The flow created or bound more than one resource and the user should see each one.
- A resource was made from the CLI and nothing serves it yet: the CliCreated state shows how to deploy it.

## When not to use

- The run is still going or has failed: keep the create-flow card of `detail/deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow) on screen.
- A resource created from a form that does not deploy: end on the resource's page with a success toast that names it, as `skills/webkit-create-surface` describes; there is no outcome screen.
- An item added inside a resource from a drawer: use `create/create-drawer` and close it on save.
- The onboarding steps for a CLI resource on its Overview tab: use `detail/get-started`.

## Building blocks

- A. Outcome heading — `Tag` (required)
- B. Deployment card — `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Link`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Resources list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag` (required)
- D. Next steps — `Card` (required)
- E. Manage — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/create/deploy-success.md).

## Do

- Lead with the outcome and the live address; the user came to see it work.
- Tag every resource Created or Bound so the list doubles as a receipt of what the flow touched.
- Open the domain and the repository in a new tab with `Link target="_blank"`, and a `Tooltip` saying so.
- Drop the scope tag and the repository row when the flow had no Git source.
- In CliCreated, replace the deployment card with next steps that deploy the resource, and add the Get started paths for the CLI and GitHub Actions.

## Don't

- Don't celebrate: no confetti, no exclamation, no emoji. State the fact.
- Don't put more than one Recommended tag among the next steps.
- Don't add a Deploy again or Create another action; the user starts a new flow from the Creation Center.
- Don't leave the screen without a way into the resource; Manage is required.
- Don't repeat the resource list inside the deployment card.

## Copy

- **Heading:** the object and the past-tense result in sentence case, e.g. "Resource deployed", or "Resource created" when nothing serves it.
- **Lead:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "You deployed a new resource." followed by "Source:" and the source tag. Never a dangling fragment after the period.
- **Status tag:** one word, e.g. "Live"; resource tags "Created" or "Bound".
- **Links:** verb first, e.g. "Visit site", "Add custom domain"; tooltips name the target, e.g. "Open acme/web-app in a new tab".
- **Next steps:** title verb first in two or three words, e.g. "Customize domain", "View analytics"; description one sentence with a period.
- **Exit:** "Manage service", the verb and its object.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no ampersand, no "please".

## Accessibility

- The heading is the page's only `h1`; the service name and the section titles are `h2`.
- The preview tile is decorative (`aria-hidden`); Visit site names the address.
- Links that open a new tab say so in their `Tooltip`, not only with the external-link glyph.
- Glyphs in rows and cards are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the Created or Bound tag gives the state in words.
- A next-step card is one focusable link or button with a visible focus ring; its title and description are its name.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading, deployment card, resources, next steps, Manage.

## States

- Default: a deployed service from a Git source, with the scope, the deployment card, four resources and three next steps.
- CliCreated: a resource made from the CLI that nothing serves yet; no deployment card, one resource row, next steps to deploy it here or on a new service, and the Get started paths.

## Related

- `detail/deployment-logs` — the run this screen follows (InCreateFlow).
- `create/deploy-template` — a flow that ends here.
- `create/create-wizard` — its CreateAndDeploy variant ends here with its own title.
- `detail/get-started` — the source of the CLI and GitHub Actions steps the CliCreated state embeds; CliCreated copies its section verbatim, so change the command copy there first and copy it here.
- `detail/resource-detail` — where Manage leads.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `CliCreated`. Code: [blocks/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/create/deploy-success.md), `get_block("create/deploy-success", { variant })`.

# DeployTemplate (`create/deploy-template`)

> The deploy template page, a focused flow outside the console shell: the creation header with Back to Creation Center and the Start from a template crumb, the template preview card naming the repository it clones from,…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/deploy-template/deploy-template.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/deploy-template")`
- Components: Accordion, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Checkbox, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, Select, Skeleton, Switch, Tag, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deploy template; clone template; template deploy page; connect git provider; deploy from template; one click deploy; start from a template; implantar template; clonar template; conectar git; deploy uploaded project; deploy imported repository; implantar projeto enviado; import from git form; import from git; importar do git; where it runs; select a service; choose service to deploy to; install integration template; integration template; add integration to service; origin proxy template; instalar integração

A focused page, outside the console shell, where the user turns a template into a running project. They chose a template in the Creation Center and now need to see what it clones, connect a Git provider if they have none, name the repository it creates, fill the settings the template requires and deploy. The same column then shows the build and the outcome, so the user never leaves the page.

## When to use

- Use deploy-template for the configure-and-deploy step once the source (repository, template or uploaded folder) is chosen.
- The user picked a template, a Git import or an upload from `create/create-hub`, and the next step is to deploy it.
- The flow creates a repository from a source in the user's Git account and deploys from it on every push.
- The template needs a few settings (tokens, a domain) before its first build can run.
- The project must first say which service it runs on (WhereItRuns), or the template is an integration that adds records and a rule to a service instead of cloning code (InstallIntegration).

## When not to use

- Choosing what to start from: use `create/create-hub`.
- A first-level resource created from a form with no source code: use `create/create-page`.
- Provisioning a resource and binding it to another: use `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy).

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Template and Git step — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (required)
- C. Browse templates — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/deploy-template.md](blocks/create/deploy-template.md).

## Do

- Keep the template preview card at the top of the column through every phase, so the user always sees what is being deployed.
- Ask for Git first; show the form only once a provider is connected.
- Let Deploy check the form: show each missing required value under its field and open the collapsed group that holds it. Disable Deploy only while the settings load, or on an upload until a Root (/) is picked.
- Keep build and variable settings in their collapsible groups, prefilled with defaults, so a template that needs nothing more deploys in one press.
- Mark a secret variable with the locked Secret checkbox and mask its value, with a show control beside it.
- Hand the same column to the create-flow card of `detail/deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow) on Deploy, then to `create/deploy-success`.
- Trim the form to the repository fields for Import from Git, and to the uploaded files for Upload a Project.

## Don't

- Don't open this flow inside the console shell or a drawer; it is a page with its own header.
- Don't ask for settings the template does not use, or move a required setting out of view.
- Don't create the repository before Deploy is pressed.
- Don't replace the page with a new route for the build; the column changes, the page stays.
- Don't put a Cancel next to Deploy; the back control and Browse templates already leave.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** the entry point, then the template name, e.g. "Start from a template" then "Nuxt E-commerce".
- **Back control:** `aria-label` names the destination, e.g. "Back to Creation Center".
- **Git step:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect a Git provider"; description one sentence saying what happens, e.g. "Nuxt E-commerce is cloned into a repository in your account, then deployed from it on every push."
- **Provider buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Continue with GitHub"; the link names the place, e.g. "Manage connected providers".
- **Form heading:** e.g. "Deploy your project"; settings labels 1 to 3 words with the constraint in the description, e.g. "You can find this token in the API credentials of your store."
- **Groups:** "Build and output settings", "Environment variables"; rows "Key", "Value", "Secret"; the reveal control "Show value" or "Hide value".
- **Errors:** "<label> is required.", e.g. "Root directory is required."
- **Upload:** breadcrumb "Upload a project"; "Project files"; "Root (/)" with "Select a file".
- **Import:** breadcrumb "Import from Git"; preview "Import and deploy the acme-web repository from GitHub."
- **Commit:** "Deploy", the same verb on the button and in the run that follows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash in labels or `aria-label`s, no parentheses in labels.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark under the header; the step title is an `h2` and the settings group an `h3`.
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link and the account button each have an `aria-label`.
- The repository name has a visible `Field.Label` tied to its input by its `Field`; the privacy switch is labelled Public repository and announces its on or off state.
- Settings use `Field` labels and descriptions, so each input announces its name and constraint.
- Required fields carry the Required marker; a failed Deploy puts each error in a `Field.Error` (`role="alert"`) tied to its input.
- Each `Accordion` trigger is a button that announces its expanded state; the Value input is labelled by its Value label, the Key row by its Key label, and the show control is a toggle with `aria-pressed`.
- The uploaded files list is a `ul` named by the folder, inside a focusable scroll region (`role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`) so it scrolls from the keyboard; while settings load the region is `aria-busy` with one status line.
- The page enter animation stops under reduced motion.

## States

- ConnectGit: no Git provider yet; the template preview over the Connect a Git provider card and Browse templates.
- Form: GitHub connected; scope and repository name side by side, public by default, over the store domain setting and the Build and output settings and Environment variables groups; Deploy shows the missing access token under its field.
- BuildSettings: after a failed Deploy; both groups open, a Build preset on the detected Nuxt preset, and the required access token in error.
- SettingsLoading: the template settings loading as Skeleton bands, Deploy disabled.
- ImportFromGit: a repository imported from GitHub; scope and repository name over one collapsed Build and output settings group.
- Upload: a dropped folder; project name and build preset, the Project files card and a required Root (/) for a static project with no index.
- WhereItRuns: the service chooser before the Git step, with search, Create Service and Continue without a service.
- InstallIntegration: the Origin Proxy integration on service-01; its settings, What gets added and Add to service-01, which shows the required origin message.

## Related

- `create/create-hub` — where the user picks the template.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — the build card (InCreateFlow) the column shows after Deploy.
- `create/deploy-success` — the outcome the column ends on.
- `top-bar/creation-bar` — the header this page uses.
- `state/project-intake` — the upload path that reaches this page with files instead of a template.

## Steps

- where-it-runs
- connect-git
- form

## Variants

# ReleaseImpact (`create/release-impact`)

> The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/release-impact/release-impact.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/release-impact")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Badge, Button, Card, Checkbox, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Field, Input, OverflowCount, PageHeader, SaveBar, Select, Skeleton, Spinner, Switch, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

release impact; review and deploy; release composer; what a deploy changes; dependency versions; deployment impact; impacto do release; revisar e implantar; impacto del despliegue

The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once: a service, the policy in front of it, its storage, its error page and every dependency they reference. The user is about to put all of it into traffic and needs to see, before deploying, which version of each resource goes out, which dependencies go with it, and every Deployment Setting, environment and project the release reaches. One Deploy release at the foot commits it, after one confirmation.

## When to use

- A release spans several resources that deploy together, each at its own version.
- The release reaches projects through shared Deployment Settings, and the user must see how far it goes before it goes.
- Dependencies are detected from the resources and may be shared between them.

## When not to use

- Deploying one service or project from its page: use `create/deploy-drawer`, which is the default way to deploy.
- Watching several Deployment Settings activate after a deploy started: use `create/deploy-progress-dialog`.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `detail/deployment-logs`.
- Switching one resource back to an earlier version: use `detail/version-detail` (Revert).

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Outcome — `Alert`, `Button` (required after a run)
- C. Resource cards — `Card`, `Switch`, `Tag`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Resource and version — `Field`, `Input`, `Select`, `Tag` (required)
- E. Dependencies — `Badge`, `Accordion`, `Alert`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Select` (required when a resource references others)
- F. Impact — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `Button` (required)
- G. Footer and commit — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- Before the review: choosing the Deployment Settings

What each part takes: [blocks/create/release-impact.md](blocks/create/release-impact.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that goes out, including the ones the user did not touch.
- Say what tracking the latest Ready version resolves to now.
- Block Deploy release only for something the user can fix here, and say what it is in the footer.
- Keep Deploy possible when the impact cannot be computed; say the impact is unknown.
- Report the outcome in the page `Alert` with Edit and Redeploy; the toast only announces it and dismisses itself.

## Don't

- Don't hide shared dependencies; changing one changes it everywhere in the release.
- Don't confirm twice: the page is the review, the `ConfirmDialog` is the only step before the run. Deploying one service or one project is `create/deploy-drawer`, which confirms nothing after Deploy; this page is only for a release of several resources.
- Don't keep the user on the page while it runs; the run reports wherever they are.
- Don't draw the Flow view with `FlowDiagram` until its list semantics pass axe.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Review and deploy". **Commit:** "Deploy release"; in progress "Deploying…".
- **Confirmation:** "Deploy this release?" and one sentence with the resources, versions and reach.
- **Selecting settings:** title "Select Deployment Settings"; search "Search 6 Deployment Settings"; "2 selected", "Select all", "Clear"; workloads "4 workloads affected" or "No workloads deploy with it yet"; no match "No Deployment Settings match" with "Clear search"; footer "Select at least one Deployment Setting to continue."
- **Versions:** "Track latest Ready", "resolves at deploy", "Pin a ready version", tag "Current".
- **Blockers:** "<name> has no Ready version, so the release cannot be deployed."
- **Outcome:** "Release deployed." / "The release wasn't deployed." with the cause and that nothing changed in traffic.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- Each resource card is a `section` named by its type and resource; the Resources heading takes focus on Edit.
- Every `Select` is labelled through its `Field` (visible for the resource, `sr-only` for dependencies).
- The include `Switch` has an `aria-label`; its `Tooltip` repeats it for pointer users.
- The Shared `Tag` sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard.
- The Impact region is `aria-busy` while loading and announces it in a `role="status"` line.
- In ChooseSettings each group is a `role="group"` named by its heading, each choice card is a `label` around its `Checkbox`, the selected count is a polite live region, and a loading workloads count is read as text rather than a bare `Skeleton`.
- The `ConfirmDialog` traps focus and returns it to Deploy release.

## States

- ChooseSettings: the step before the review; grouped checkbox choice cards with search, Select all and Clear, a loading workloads count, an inactive setting with its activate link, and Continue disabled until one is selected.
- Ready: every resource with a version, the impact computed, Tree view.
- Loading: the impact being computed.
- Unavailable: the impact could not be read; Retry lands on a truncated list.
- MissingVersion: a resource without a Ready version blocks the deploy.
- Error: the last run was refused; an error toast announces it, and Edit and Redeploy sit on the page `Alert`.

## Related

- `create/deploy-drawer` — deploying one service or project.
- `create/deploy-progress-dialog` — several Deployment Settings activating after the deploy.
- `state/async-submit` — the toast rule every deploy follows.
- `detail/version-detail` — one version, its history and revert.

## Variants

`Ready` (primary) · `ChooseSettings` · `Loading` · `Unavailable` · `MissingVersion` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/create/release-impact.md](blocks/create/release-impact.md), `get_block("create/release-impact", { variant })`.
