- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CodeBlock, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, ConsoleLayout, CopyButton, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PasswordInput, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-unsaved-changes`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ux-heuristics`

## Asked as

settings page; resource settings; settings of one resource; resource settings page; settings tab; application settings; workload settings; firewall settings; edit settings; página de configurações; configurações do recurso; aba de configurações; save bar; unsaved changes bar; sticky save bar; discard and save; commit bar; barra de salvar; alterações não salvas; salvar alterações; edit resource; editar recurso; data stream; data stream settings; log streaming; stream destination; sampling; log template; configurações do data stream; envio de logs; streaming de logs; stale record; changed elsewhere; overwrite changes; conflict on save; danger zone; delete resource; type the name to confirm; zona de perigo; excluir recurso; alterado em outro lugar; leave page guard; unsaved changes dialog; cache settings; cache policy; browser cache; edge cache; tiered cache; configurações de cache; protocol settings; https ports; http/3; tls version; mutual authentication; mtls; autenticação mútua; waf settings; waf rule set; threat sensitivity; configurações do waf

The settings page of one existing resource. The user comes here to change how the resource is named, what it runs with and whether it is active, review the change, and commit it or throw it away. Every field sits in a labeled section of the form column, and one save band appears only once something has changed, so the page reads as the resource's current state until the user edits it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the resource breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`; the save band sticks to the bottom of the layout's scrolling region.

## When to use

- Use edit-resource for the Settings tab or settings page of one resource, with anchored sections and a save bar that appears after the first edit.
- A resource has a Settings tab (or, with no tabs, its own `/<resource>/:id/settings` page) with fields grouped into a few sections.
- Changes are reviewed together and committed in one save, with a way to discard them all.
- Some settings are fixed or paid and must be shown locked, with the reason beside them.

## When not to use

- Creating the resource for the first time: use `create/create-page`, which shares this field list.
- Account or organization settings outside one resource (profile, preferences, notifications): use `settings/settings-form`.
- A resource whose content is code or a document: use `edit/function-editor`.
- Deleting the resource: the Danger zone action opens `edit/delete-dialog`.
- A short list of attached records inside a section: use `detail/attached-resources` as that section's body.

## Building blocks

- A. Resource tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (optional)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Settings sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError`, `Switch` (required)
- D. Locked settings — `Tooltip`, `Switch` (optional)
- E. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- F. Conditional fields — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError` (optional)
- G. Template editor — `SettingsRow`, `FieldError` (optional)
- H. Section warnings and server errors — `SettingsSection`, `Button` (optional)
- I. Leave guard — `Tabs`, `SaveBar` (optional)
- J. Changed elsewhere — `Button`, `SaveBar` (optional)
- K. Danger zone — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `SettingsRow`, `Button`, `Input` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/edit/edit-resource.md).

## Do

- Show the save bar only while the form differs from the saved record.
- Disable the whole fieldset while saving, not each field separately.
- Give every section a short hint that says what it controls, and an anchor so a link can land on it.
- Keep locked settings visible, disabled, with the reason and the way to unlock them.
- Put destructive actions in a Danger zone section at the end, never in the save bar.
- Check every field when Save is pressed and show errors only then; see `skills/webkit-errors`.
- Put the choice that decides other fields first, and show only the fields that choice needs.
- Show a preset document read-only, with Copy, beside the way to make it editable.
- Mark the tab that holds unsaved changes with `dirty`, and ask before leaving it while dirty.
- Offer Save changes in the leave dialog when the form can be saved from there; the user keeps their work without going back.
- Say when the record changed elsewhere as soon as it is known, and ask before Save overwrites it.
- Keep the edits on screen after a reload with an Undo, so a stale form never loses work silently.
- Ask for the resource name before a delete, with a copy button beside the name.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't place a permanent Save button at the top or bottom of the page; the save bar appears on demand.
- Don't save on each toggle; changes wait for Save.
- Don't hide fields the user cannot change; lock them and say why.
- Don't use `size="medium"` or larger for the Settings heading; the tab bar or breadcrumb already names the resource.
- Don't add a Cancel button that leaves the page; Discard restores the record in place.
- Don't report a rejected destination or credential in a toast; it belongs above the section it concerns.
- Don't echo a saved secret back into its field.
- Don't rely on the dot alone: the dirty tab also says "Unsaved changes" to screen readers.
- Don't overwrite a record that changed elsewhere without the overwrite confirmation.
- Don't put Delete in the save bar, the page heading or a menu of the form; it lives in the Danger zone.
- Don't enable the delete confirm button before the typed name matches.

## Copy

- **Heading:** "Settings", with one sentence ending in a period, e.g. "Core configuration for this project."
- **Section titles:** short nouns, e.g. "General", "Modules", "Subscription modules", "Status".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that says what the setting does, e.g. "When disabled, the project stops serving traffic."
- **Save bar:** state what changed and when it applies, e.g. "Project settings changed." with the hint "Saving publishes them on the next deployment."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Locked reason:** one sentence with the way out, e.g. "Contact sales to activate this module."
- **Server error on a section:** what happened, then what was kept, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer the test record, so the stream was not saved. Your other changes are still here."; the field reason is one line, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer within 10 seconds."
- **Leave dialog:** "Unsaved changes", "This page has changes you haven't saved. If you leave now, they're discarded." (with Save: "Save them before you leave, or discard them and continue."); buttons "Keep editing", "Discard changes", "Save changes". These are the built-in `unsavedChanges` messages in en, pt-BR and es.
- **Changed elsewhere:** "Changed elsewhere." + "This project was saved by someone else after you opened it. …"; button "Reload"; dialog "Overwrite changes made elsewhere?" with "Go back" and "Overwrite and save"; after a reload "Edits discarded." with "Undo".
- **Danger zone:** section "Danger zone" with "Actions that cannot be undone."; row "Delete this project"; dialog "Delete project", "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.", "To confirm, type <name>"; buttons "Cancel" and "Delete project".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form has an `aria-label` and its `fieldset` a visually hidden `legend` with the same words, e.g. "Main settings".
- Every `Input` and `Switch` has an `aria-label` matching its row title.
- A disabled `Switch` keeps its `Tooltip`, so keyboard and pointer users can still read why it is locked.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and an icon marked `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar enters after the form in reading order and its motion respects reduced motion.
- An invalid field points at its `FieldError` through `aria-describedby`; on Save the first invalid field takes the focus.
- A section `Alert` is announced by `Alert` itself; its recovery `Button` is a real button inside it.
- The `CodeEditor` and the read-only `CodeBlock` are named after their row (`Data set`, `Copy the data set as JSON`).
- The dirty tab mark is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden "Unsaved changes" joins the tab's accessible name, and under forced colors the dot paints in `CanvasText`.
- The leave dialog is a `ConfirmDialog`: focus moves into it, Escape and the close button count as Keep editing, and focus returns to the control that asked to leave.
- The changed-elsewhere notice sits in a polite live region and takes focus after Reload so the change of values is announced; both its actions are real buttons.
- The delete confirmation `Input` is labelled by the "To confirm, type …" sentence (`aria-labelledby`); the `CopyButton` has its own name ("Copy the project name") and announces Copied.

## States

- ProjectSettings: a project's Settings tab with General, Modules and Subscription modules; the save bar is hidden until an edit.
- DeployableSettings: a deployable resource's Settings tab with General, Domains, collapsed Advanced settings and the Danger zone, whose Delete resource opens the type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog` of `edit/delete-dialog`.
- PolicySettings: a security policy's Settings tab with General, Modules with one locked on, Debug rules and Status.
- WafSettings: a WAF rule set's Main Settings tab with General, Status (Active and the Blocking or Learning Mode `Select`) and Threats, one row per threat family with a Sensitivity `Select` beside its `Switch`; the Sensitivity is disabled while its threat is off, and Save confirms in a toast.
- ResourceSettings: a first-level resource with no tabs at its own settings route; Save checks every field before it commits.
- UnsavedChanges: after one edit; the save bar is up with Discard and Save.
- Saving: while the request is in flight; Save is loading and Discard is disabled.
- DataStream: a data stream at its own settings route with General, Source, Sampling, Template and Destination; the destination fields follow the connector, Save sends one test record, and an endpoint that does not answer raises the section `Alert` of the form-validation rule.
- StaleRecord: the form holds edits and the record changed elsewhere; the warning notice with Reload is up, Save asks before overwriting, Reload turns the notice into Edits discarded with Undo.
- DangerZone: the settings end with the Danger zone; Delete project opens the typed-name confirmation, enabled only on a match, loading while the delete runs.
- CacheSettings: one cache setting of an application; General, Browser cache, Edge cache and the collapsed Advanced cache key. Rows that only apply under a switch or an override sit one level in (`SettingsRow` `level`). An edge TTL under 60 seconds and an empty allowlist or denylist are field errors with their reason, focused on Save. Save deploys and reports through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Protocols: the protocol settings of a workload; ports per protocol, TLS version and cipher suite, then Mutual authentication. Mutual authentication stays off, with a helper line saying why, until HTTPS is on; once on it shows the mode as `Field` choice cards, the trusted CA picker (search, expiry beside each certificate, Upload certificate in its footer opening a `Drawer`) and the revocation lists. Save checks a port per protocol and a CA, then deploys through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- UnsavedChanges (leave guard): the Settings tab carries the dirty dot, and switching tabs while dirty opens the Unsaved changes dialog.

## Settings that deploy

Some settings only take effect once the resource is deployed (cache settings of an application, protocols of a workload). For those:

- Say so in the save bar hint, e.g. "Saving deploys storefront to Production."
- On Save, validate first (field errors per the form-validation rule), then run the deploy on its own: a loading toast while it runs, then the async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the form, focus on its first field) and **Redeploy**. Never offer View deployments.
- Keep the form usable while it runs; the baseline moves to the saved values only when the deploy succeeds.
- Keep switches that depend on each other consistent in both directions, e.g. HTTP/3 turns HTTPS on and HTTPS off turns HTTP/3 and mutual authentication off.

## Related

- `shell/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in; a crumb that is a control (DeployableSettings' environment) is set by the page with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb` (the module and the resource as `items`, a `Select` with `variant="ghost"` and `size="small"` in its slot).
- `create/create-page` — the create page that shares this field list.
- `detail/attached-resources` — the Domains section body in DeployableSettings.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind the Danger zone action.
- `settings/settings-form` — account settings that end with the same save band.
- `SaveBar` — the unsaved-changes band; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the section-scoped server error DataStream and the changed-elsewhere notice follow.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` (Metrics) — where the records a stream sends are counted.
- `useUnsavedChanges` — the dirty baseline and leave guard behind the save bar, the tab mark and the leave dialog.

## Variants

`ProjectSettings` (primary) · `DeployableSettings` · `PolicySettings` · `WafSettings` · `ResourceSettings` · `UnsavedChanges` · `Saving` · `DataStream` · `StaleRecord` · `DangerZone` · `CacheSettings` · `Protocols`. Code: [blocks/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/edit/edit-resource.md), `get_block("edit/edit-resource", { variant })`.

# FunctionEditor (`edit/function-editor`)

> The code editor page, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the service): the Code and Settings tabs, an editor toolbar whose ToggleGroup switches between the Code document and the Arguments doc…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/function-editor/function-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/function-editor")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CodeEditor, CopyButton, EmptyState, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, KeyValueList, Link, `LogViewerContent`, LogViewer, PageTabs, RadioGroup, `ResizableHandle`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableRoot`, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, StatusIndicator, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, Trace
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`

## Asked as

code editor; code editor page; function code editor; editor page; code and arguments editor; split editor; monaco editor; editor de código; página do editor; editar código; function editor; edge function; function detail; function arguments; json schema arguments; function settings; editor de função; argumentos da função; detalhe da função; test run; function test; run trace; span waterfall; invocation trace; testar função; execução de teste; rastreamento da execução; function code page; edit function code; function arguments page

The editing page of a service whose behavior lives in source code. The user writes and saves the code, defines the argument form each instance of the service asks for (its fields, types and defaults), and adjusts the service's settings. The editor fills the page so the code has room, and one save bar commits code, arguments and settings together. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the Services breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The editor pins its own panes, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Use the function-editor block for the code and arguments page of a function; the editor itself is the CodeEditor component.
- A resource is mainly a document the user edits as text: function code, a schema, a configuration file.
- The document comes with a structured companion (an argument form) that is easier to edit as fields than as JSON, and the user wants both views side by side.
- The same resource also has a few settings, shown on a second tab of the same page.
- The user tests the code before saving it and needs to read where the run spent its time and what it printed (variant TestRun).

## When not to use

- A resource made only of settings: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Ordered conditions and actions the user composes without code: use `edit/rule-builder`.
- Free key and value pairs such as environment variables: use `edit/variables`.
- Running queries and reading results: use `view/query-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Editor toolbar — `ToggleGroup`, `Button` (required)
- C. Code document — `CodeEditor`, `FieldError` (required)
- D. Test run — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle` (optional)
- E. Arguments split — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle`, `CodeEditor`, `Button` (required)
- F. No fields — `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (optional)
- G. Field list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- H. Field settings — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `FieldError` (required)
- I. Settings tab — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `FieldError` (required)
- J. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/function-editor.md](blocks/edit/function-editor.md).

## Do

- Let the editor fill the pane; the page scrolls inside the editor, not around it.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill`.
- Show the schema JSON and the fields form side by side, so the user can check one against the other.
- Keep collapsed fields as one-line summaries with their tags, and open settings only for the field being edited.
- Lock fields that cannot change after creation, with a lock glyph and a description that says so.
- Use one save bar for both tabs, and take the user to the tab that holds the error.
- Show a test run under the code it ran, on the same page: the trace and the logs on one clock, the summary first.
- Select the span the user most likely wants (the slowest or the failed one) when the run finishes.

## Don't

- Don't put the code editor inside a card, a drawer or a modal.
- Don't add a page heading above the tabs; the layout's breadcrumb names the service.
- Don't size the page with `calc(100dvh - …)`; it overflows under a notification.
- Don't save from inside the Arguments pane or a field; Save lives in the bar.
- Don't flag a new field's name before the user has touched it.
- Don't let the schema pane squeeze the fields pane below a usable width; collapse it instead.
- Don't open a test run in a dialog or a new page; it covers the code the user is about to fix.
- Don't save as a side effect of Run test; a test runs the code in the editor, saved or not.
- Don't report a test run with a toast; the result lives in the pane, where the user is looking.

## Copy

- **Tabs and documents:** single nouns, e.g. "Code", "Settings", "Arguments".
- **Field count:** a number and the noun, e.g. "1 field", "2 fields".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add field", "Remove form", "Discard", "Save".
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, e.g. "This form has no fields"; description says what to do, e.g. "Add the first argument the service reads."
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "This field is required.", "Another field already uses this name."
- **Save bar:** "You have unsaved changes."
- **Test run:** status as one word ("Completed", "Running", "Failed"); the outcome as the status code and what happened, e.g. "200, served from the transform and written to cache."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Both editors have an `aria-label` that names the document, e.g. "Source code", "Argument form schema, as JSON".
- The split is labeled "Argument form", its panes "Schema" and "Fields", and the handle "Resize the schema".
- Each field has native Move up and Move down buttons named with the field ("Move quality up"); moves are announced in a polite live region.
- The expand button sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and names the field it opens.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar's motion respects reduced motion.
- In TestRun the vertical split is labeled "Code and test run", its panes "Source code" and "Test run", and the handle "Resize the test run". The pane is a `section` named by its Test run heading, with Trace and Logs as `h3`s.
- The trace is a `treegrid` with one tab stop (see `Trace`); the running state is announced by a `status` line.

## States

- Code: the Code tab with the Code document filling the editor pane.
- Arguments: the Arguments document of image-optimizer, the schema on the left and two fields on the right, one expanded.
- NoArguments: the Arguments document of a service with no form, the empty schema and the no fields empty state.
- TestRun: the Code document with a finished test run of image-optimizer under it, the origin fetch selected in the trace; Run test shows the running state.
- Settings: the Settings tab with General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status; editing raises the save bar.
- Saving: a change to the Code document is being saved; Save shows its loading state, Discard and the fields are disabled and the editors are read-only.

## Related

- `shell/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in.
- `edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern the Settings tab follows.
- `view/query-editor` — an editor page that runs queries and shows results.

# RuleBuilder (`edit/rule-builder`)

> A rule builder drawer, the richest form pattern: a large right-side drawer with General, Phase, Criteria, Behaviors and Status sections over a single Save in the footer.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/rule-builder/rule-builder.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/rule-builder")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Combobox, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, Field, `FieldDescription`, Input, Item, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioGroup, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Switch
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

rules engine; rule form; add rule; criteria and behaviors; if then rules; conditional rules; rule builder; motor de regras; criar regra; regras condicionais

A drawer where the user writes one rule of a rules engine: when it runs (the phase), the conditions that decide whether it applies, and the ordered behaviors it performs when they match. The user composes groups of variable, operator and argument rows (every row in a group must match, any group is enough), picks behaviors that fit the phase, puts everything in order and saves, without leaving the resource's Rules tab.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered list of rules, each made of conditions and actions (request and response rules, firewall rules, routing).
- Conditions combine with And inside a group and Or across groups, and the order of behaviors matters.
- The rule is edited from a list inside the resource, so the drawer opens as `Add Rule` or `Edit Rule` and keeps the list in view behind it.

## When not to use

- Free-form pairs of a name and a value: use `edit/variables`.
- A short create form of three fields or fewer: use `create/create-drawer`.
- A resource's own settings: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Logic the user would rather write as code: use `edit/function-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drawer and trigger — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody` (required)
- B. General — `SettingsSection`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- C. Phase — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `RadioGroup`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- D. Criteria — `SettingsSection`, `AttributeEditor` (grouped), `Combobox`, `Select`, `Input` (required)
- E. Behaviors — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `AttributeEditor`, `Select`, `Input`, `FieldDescription` (required)
- F. Status — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Switch` (required)
- G. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button`, `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/rule-builder.md](blocks/edit/rule-builder.md).

## Do

- Show the Name error only after a failed Save, never on first render, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Read the logic aloud in the layout: and inside a group, or between groups, then the behaviors in order.
- Make every argument field follow what was picked before it, so the user never types a value the operator or behavior cannot take.
- Offer both drag and buttons to reorder behaviors and criteria; the buttons are the keyboard path.
- Filter variables and behaviors by phase, and lock the phase on an existing rule.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for fields and `skills/webkit-errors` for error timing.

## Don't

- Don't put a Cancel button beside Save; the drawer's close button and the overlay close it.
- Don't nest groups inside groups; one level of Or over And is the whole model.
- Don't draw criteria rows by hand; `AttributeEditor` grouped mode owns their labels, errors, limits and announcements.
- Don't let the user switch an existing rule's phase; tell them to create a rule in the other phase.
- Don't open the drawer in a medium size; condition rows need three columns side by side.
- Don't clear the form while the drawer is closing.

## Copy

- **Drawer title and trigger:** `Add Rule` for a new rule, `Edit Rule` for an existing one.
- **Section hints:** one sentence saying what the section decides, e.g. "The conditions that decide whether the rule runs."
- **Logic labels:** single words, e.g. "and", "or", "Then".
- **Add buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Add condition", "Add OR group", "Add behavior".
- **Errors:** "Name is required.", "Enter the variable to compare."
- **Reorder controls:** the editor names them with the row number ("Move item 2 up", "Remove behavior 2", "Reorder group 1").
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every `Input` and `Select` trigger has a label: a `Field.Label` tied by `for`, or an `aria-label` such as "Behavior"; the criteria cells are `Field`s of the `AttributeEditor`, labelled Variable, Operator and Argument, and groups are `group`s named "Group n".
- The variable `Combobox` is a `combobox` with a `listbox` of `option`s; picking one keeps focus in the field.
- Behaviors and criteria reorder through `AttributeEditor`: a native grip button, Move up and Move down, and Alt+Arrow keys, each move announced.
- Decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the trigger on close; motion respects reduced motion.

## States

- Default: Add Rule with an empty Name, the Request phase, one empty condition and one empty behavior, Active on.
- Composed: Edit Rule for the seeded Docs rewrite rule, the phase locked with its note, one URI condition and two behaviors.
- In a list: `view/rule-list#EditRule` drives this drawer without its trigger (`v-model:open` from a rule's name and from Add Rule) and writes the saved rule back to its row.

## Related

- `create/create-drawer` — the simpler drawer create this one extends.
- `edit/variables` — a drawer for free key and value pairs; `AttributeEditor` is the component the criteria are built on.
- `view/rule-list` — the list of rules by phase this drawer opens from.
- `state/form-validation` — when errors appear after Save.
- `edit/edit-resource` — the resource settings that sit beside the Rules tab.
- `Drawer` — the side panel; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Composed`. Code: [blocks/edit/rule-builder.md](blocks/edit/rule-builder.md), `get_block("edit/rule-builder", { variant })`.

## Asked as

schema editor; create table; add column; insert row; alter column; change column type; truncate table; table schema; database schema; column types; criar tabela; adicionar coluna; inserir linha; alterar coluna; esvaziar tabela; esquema do banco

The table schema of a SQL database: the definition of one table and the drawers and dialogs that change it. A developer creates a table with its columns, adds a column, inserts a row by hand, changes a column's type or empties a table, and stays on the same surface while each change runs. It sits behind the Create Table, Add column, Insert and table menu buttons of `view/query-editor`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- A SQL database's tables are created and changed from the console rather than only with SQL.
- A table's columns, types and constraints are shown and edited one change at a time.
- A row is added by hand to check a table, without writing an INSERT.

## When not to use

- Running SQL or reading query results: use `view/query-editor`.
- Rows of a resource that is not a database (variables, records): use `edit/variables` or `detail/dns-zone-detail`.
- A form that creates a resource in its own page: use `create/create-page`.
- A generic item created inside a resource: use `create/create-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Definition surface — `Card`, `DataTable`, `Table`, `Tag`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- B. Create Table drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody`, `SettingsSection`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- C. Column rows — `AttributeEditor`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `FieldError` (required)
- D. CSV import and foreign keys — `FileDropzone`, `FileTokenGroup` (optional)
- E. Add column drawer — `Switch` (required)
- F. Insert row drawer — `PanelFooter` (required)
- G. Change type dialog — `ConfirmDialog`, `CodeEditor` (required)
- H. Truncate table dialog — `ConfirmDialog`, `CodeEditor`, `Input` (required)
- Outcome toasts — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/schema-editor.md](blocks/edit/schema-editor.md).

## Do

- Validate on submit, then keep each error next to what caused it: the field, the column row or the list.
- Keep the drawer open and its values intact when the server refuses; say so in the section `Alert`.
- Show the SQL a destructive or rebuilding change will run before it runs.
- Ask for the table name before truncating it.
- Build the column and foreign key rows on `AttributeEditor`, so drag, keyboard moves, focus and announcements match every other row editor.
- End every change with a toast whose action continues the work on the same table.

## Don't

- Don't validate column names on every keystroke; wait for the first submit.
- Don't put a deploy action (Edit, Redeploy, View deployments) on a schema change.
- Don't let a primary key be nullable; lock Not null while Primary key is on.
- Don't drop rows on a type change silently; warn that values that don't fit make it fail.
- Don't close the Create Table drawer on a server error.

## Copy

- **Titles:** `Create Table`, `Add column`, `Insert row`, `Change the type of <column>`, `Truncate <table>`.
- **Buttons:** the title's verb and object: `Create Table`, `Add column`, `Insert row`, `Change type`, `Truncate table`; Cancel beside each.
- **Errors:** `This field is required.`, `Start with a letter or an underscore; use letters, numbers and underscores.`, `Another column is also named email.`, `Add at least one named column.`, `customers already has a column named email.`, `email cannot be NULL. Enter a value.`
- **Server rejection:** `The table wasn't created. A table named customers already exists in acme-store. Your columns are kept; pick another name and create it again.`
- **Toasts:** as in building block H.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case except the product's object names (`Create Table`), no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each drawer's content is a `form` named by its title; the `fieldset` carries a visually hidden `legend` and is disabled while the request runs.
- `Field` wires every label, description and error to its control; column row controls without a visible label are named `Name of column 2`, `Type of column 2`, `Default value of column 2`.
- Column reordering comes from `AttributeEditor`: a real grip `button`, Move up and Move down, and Alt+Arrow keys, so dragging is never the only way (WCAG 2.5.7); each move is announced and focus stays on the moved row.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; the per-column menu trigger names its column.
- The read-only `CodeEditor`s are named (`Statements that will run`) and can be selected and copied.
- Drawers and dialogs trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the button that opened them.

## States

- CreateTable: the Create Table drawer open on a new table, with the default id and created_at columns.
- AddColumn: the Add column drawer with phone as varchar.
- InsertRow: the Insert row drawer after a submit with email empty, showing the NOT NULL error.
- ChangeType: the Change type dialog for email with the statements that will run.
- TruncateTable: the Truncate customers dialog waiting for the typed name.
- ImportCsv: Create Table with subscribers.csv read (six columns, six rows, a quoted comma) and one foreign key, customer_id to customers.id on delete cascade.
- Error: Create Table refused by the server because customers already exists; Alert in General and the Name field invalid.

## Related

- `view/query-editor` — the database page whose buttons open these drawers and dialogs.
- `create/create-drawer` — the drawer recipe these drawers follow.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the typed confirmation Truncate table follows.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the rule for the server's name conflict.
- `state/async-submit` — the long-action rule; schema changes use item actions, not Edit and Redeploy.
- `CodeEditor`, `Select`, `Field` — see `skills/webkit-form` and `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`CreateTable` (primary) · `AddColumn` · `InsertRow` · `ChangeType` · `TruncateTable` · `ImportCsv` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/edit/schema-editor.md](blocks/edit/schema-editor.md), `get_block("edit/schema-editor", { variant })`.

# Variables (`edit/variables`)

> A key/value editor, drawn as a variables list page and the Create Variable drawer its heading action opens.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/edit/variables/variables.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("edit/variables")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Avatar, Button, Card, Checkbox, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupRoot`, MultiSelect, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SettingsSection, Switch, Table, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

variables; environment variables; env vars; secrets; create variable; edit variable; variables list; variáveis; variáveis de ambiente; segredos; criar variável; key value editor; attribute editor; .env upload; editor de chave e valor; delete variable; clone variable; paste .env; paste env file; import .env; colar .env; importar variáveis; dotenv; network list; ip list; asn list; country list; bulk paste; lista de rede; lista de ips; lista de red; variables page; variables block; environment variables page; list of variables; página de variáveis

A list of key and value pairs and the drawer that edits them, here environment variables. The user scans the variables already defined, then opens Create Variable to type or paste several pairs at once, mark the sensitive ones as secret, and select where they apply (the whole account, or specific environments, projects, services or policies) before saving them in one step. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use the variables block for a list of key/value variables with a create/edit drawer; the key/value field itself is the AttributeEditor component.
- Users define many free-form pairs of a name and a value (environment variables, headers, metadata, tags) and often bring them from a file.
- Some values are sensitive and must be masked and write-only once saved.
- Each pair applies to a scope the user picks from existing resources.

## When not to use

- Conditions and actions evaluated in order: use `edit/rule-builder`.
- A fixed set of named settings on one resource: use `edit/edit-resource` or `settings/settings-form`.
- A short read-only list of related records inside a settings tab: use `detail/attached-resources`.
- A long document or code the user edits as text: use `edit/function-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- C. Variables table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `Table.CellId`, `Table.CellLink`, `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Row actions — `Table`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- E. Create and edit drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody` (required)
- F. Variables section — `SettingsSection`, `Button`, `ToggleGroup` (required)
- G. Key and value rows — `AttributeEditor`, `Field`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Checkbox`, `FieldError` (required)
- H. Paste .env panel — `Button`, `Textarea`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- I. JSON view — `Textarea`, `FieldDescription` (optional)
- J. Scope — `SettingsSection`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `MultiSelect`, `Input`, `Switch`, `FieldError` (required)
- K. Drawer footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- L. List states — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- M. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input`, `Button` (required)
- N. Network list drawer — `Drawer`, `SettingsSection`, `ToggleGroup`, `Button`, `Textarea`, `FieldDescription`, `AttributeEditor`, `MultiSelect` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/edit/variables.md](blocks/edit/variables.md).

## Do

- Validate only after Save is pressed; then flag each empty, malformed or duplicated key under its own pair and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep secret values masked in the list and in the drawer, and say in the hint that secrets are write-only once saved.
- Let users bring pairs in bulk: Upload, Paste .env, paste into a key, or edit as JSON.
- Before pasted pairs land, say how many were found, which lines are skipped and which keys will be replaced.
- Build the rows on `AttributeEditor` so add, remove, focus and announcements behave the same on every key and value editor.
- Keep the label of each field inside its `InputGroupAddon`, tied to the field by `for`.
- Reset the drawer on open so a closed and reopened drawer never shows stale rows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for required states and `skills/webkit-lists` for the list page.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't show required errors on first render or while the user is still typing the first pair.
- Don't offer Remove on the last remaining pair.
- Don't drop invalid pasted lines silently, and don't add duplicate keys from a paste: replace the existing value and say so.
- Don't reveal a saved secret value in the table, a tooltip or the copy control.
- Don't add a Cancel button beside Save; the drawer's close button and the overlay close it.
- Don't keep Global on together with a specific scope.

## Copy

- **Title and create action:** "Variables" and "Create Variable"; the drawer title repeats "Create Variable", or reads "Edit Variable" from a row.
- **Empty states:** "No variables yet" / "Create a variable to store a value your services read at runtime."; "No matching variables" / "No variable matches these filters."
- **Delete dialog:** title and danger button "Delete variable"; the prompt reads "Type API_BASE_URL to confirm."
- **Field placeholders:** show the format, e.g. "MY_VARIABLE" for the key, "my-variable-value" for the value.
- **Toasts:** "API_KEY created.", "3 variables created.", "API_KEY updated.", "API_KEY cloned as API_KEY_COPY.", "API_KEY deleted."; save failure "Variables not saved. You are offline; check your connection and save again."
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "Key is required.", "Use only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.", "Select at least one resource for this scope."
- **Secret control:** "Mark as secret" and "Unmark as secret"; the hint states the rule, e.g. "Secret values are hidden and write-only after saving."
- **Network list:** title "Create Network List"; types "IP/CIDR", "ASN", "Countries"; panel label "Paste one address per line"; report "7 entries found. Text after # is kept as the comment.", "Lines 4 and 8 are not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range; they are added with an error to fix.", "Line 7 is already in the list and will be skipped."; row error "198.51.100.300 is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range."; toast "Office and partners created."
- **Paste panel:** label "Paste .env contents"; report "3 variables found. Lines starting with # are ignored.", "Line 5 is not KEY=value with an uppercase key and will be skipped.", "CACHE_TTL is already in the list; its value will be replaced."; buttons "Paste .env", "Add 3 variables", "Cancel".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Upload", "Add variable", "Save".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every key and value field has a visible `label` in its addon; an invalid field sets `aria-invalid` and points to its `FieldError` through `aria-describedby`.
- Icon-only controls (Remove variable, Show value, Hide value, row actions, toolbar) carry an `aria-label` that matches their `Tooltip`.
- The Secret `Checkbox` and each scope `Switch` have an `aria-label` naming what they toggle, e.g. "Enable Project scope".
- The `ToggleGroup` is labeled "Variables view"; the hidden file input is removed from the tab order and the Upload button triggers it.
- Adding a pair moves focus to its new Key field; removing one moves focus to the pair now in its place (or Add variable); both are announced in a polite live region by `AttributeEditor`.
- The paste panel's `Textarea` is described by its report, so skipped lines and replaced keys are read with the field; Paste .env exposes `aria-expanded`, and applying announces how many variables were added.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to Create Variable on close.

## States

- List: the variables list page with the controls row and table; the drawer is closed.
- First use: no variables yet; the card holds the first-use `EmptyState` with Create Variable.
- No match: the filter matches nothing; the table shows the no-match `EmptyState` with Clear filters.
- Edit: a row's Edit opens the drawer on that variable; Save replaces it in the list and raises "<KEY> updated.".
- Save failed: the save request fails; the drawer stays open with its rows and a danger `Alert` above the sections.
- Delete: a row's Delete opens the typed confirmation; confirming removes the row and raises "<KEY> deleted.".
- Create: the drawer open with one empty pair, the Form view and Global on; errors appear only after Save.
- PasteEnv: Create Variable opens the drawer with one pair and the Paste .env panel holding a pasted file with a comment, an `export`, a skipped lowercase line and a repeated key that is already in the list; Add 3 variables merges them.
- NetworkList: Create Network List opens the drawer named Office and partners, type IP/CIDR, with the Paste list panel holding nine lines: a comment line, two lines that are not valid addresses and one already pasted above; Add 7 entries appends them as rows, the two invalid ones showing their errors.

## Related

- `create/create-drawer` — the general drawer create pattern this drawer follows.
- `view/table-view` — the controls row and table recipe the list page reuses.
- `edit/rule-builder` — a drawer for ordered conditions and behaviors instead of free pairs.
- `state/form-validation` — when and how errors appear after Save.
- `InputGroupRoot` — joins label, field and actions into one row; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `AttributeEditor` and `TagEditor` — the components behind the rows; `TagEditor` for resource tags.

## Variants

`List` (primary) · `Create` · `PasteEnv` · `NetworkList`. Code: [blocks/edit/variables.md](blocks/edit/variables.md), `get_block("edit/variables", { variant })`.

# SettingsForm (`settings/settings-form`)

> A settings form and its save strategy, one variant per strategy.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/settings/settings-form/settings-form.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("settings/settings-form")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, Field, `FieldError`, Input, Item, Link, PageHeader, SaveBar, SectionHeader, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Switch, Tag, Textarea, Toast, `use-unsaved-changes`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ux-heuristics`

## Asked as

account settings form; organization or account settings; save all; single save for the page; sticky footer save; save as one unit; cancel and save footer; salvar tudo; rodapé fixo com salvar; formulário de conta; save per group; save per section; preferences page; grouped settings save; section save button; independent groups; salvar por grupo; preferências; salvar por seção; save per card; card with its own save; project settings; configuration cards; independent saves; long settings page; salvar por card; configurações do projeto; salvar cada seção; account settings; account profile; profile page; user profile; my profile; my account; organization settings; company information; login settings; danger zone; configurações da conta; perfil; página de perfil; minha conta; configuración de la cuenta

The place the user goes to change how an account or a project behaves. They scan a few topics, change one or two values, and commit them knowing exactly what the save covers. The block is one layout with three save strategies: one save for a form that is one logical unit, one save per group, or one save per card on a long configuration page. The Profile variant is the full account profile page, the layout every account settings page (billing details, credentials, users, teams) follows. The save model follows how the page is partitioned, not the container. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the breadcrumbs, the ⌘K palette and the `<main>`.

## When to use

- Use settings-form for account or organization settings (profile, preferences, notifications), choosing SaveAll, SavePerGroup or SavePerCard.
- Account-level settings read as rows of a label, a description and a control (Profile, Preferences, Notifications): SaveAll.
- Topics on one page that the user commits independently, such as General and Notifications: SavePerGroup.
- A long configuration page where each topic needs an explanation and its own commit, such as Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection: SavePerCard.
- The signed-in account's full profile page, with its sections, MFA link, source control and Delete account: Profile.

## When not to use

- The settings tab or settings page of one resource, with anchored sections and an unsaved-changes bar: use `edit/edit-resource`.
- Changing the plan: use `account/change-plan-drawer`.
- Creating a resource: use `create/create-page` or `create/create-drawer`.
- Walking every submit outcome (invalid fields, server rejection): use `state/form-validation`.
- Deleting the account or a resource from a settings page: open `edit/delete-dialog` (its SettingsRow variant) from an outlined row.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. FeatureItem sections — `SectionHeader`, `Card`, `Item` (required)
- C. Setting rows — `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldError`, `Select`, `Switch` (required)
- D. Save — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- E. Profile sections — `SettingsRow`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Button` (Profile only)

What each part takes: [blocks/settings/settings-form.md](blocks/settings/settings-form.md).

## Do

- Pick the save strategy from how the page is partitioned: one logical unit gets one save.
- Disable only the fieldset being saved; the other groups or cards stay editable.
- Drive Save's `:loading` and the fieldset's `disabled` from one `submitting` flag.
- Validate on submit only, show the error at the field it belongs to, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep every control in a row at the same size, and every row title in sentence case.
- Explain a card's effect in an info `Alert` at the top of the card, before its fields.
- In Profile, keep preferences that apply immediately (Appearance) and external connections (Source control) out of Save, and say so in their section hints; put destructive actions in the last section, behind a type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog`.

## Don't

- Don't render a `Sidebar`, `AppHeader`, `Command` palette or `<main>` in the page; `ConsoleLayout` owns them.
- Don't mix a page-level `SaveBar` with per-card Save buttons on the same page.
- Don't put Save in the page heading or float it beside a single field.
- Don't flag empty required fields before the user presses Save.
- Don't add an error summary block or an `Alert` for field validation; the field's own state is the feedback.
- Don't put a consequence or a constraint in the row title; it goes in the description or the `Alert`.
- Don't toast a field-level server rejection; it goes to an `Alert` in the owning section with the row's control invalid.

## Copy

- **Page title:** the page's name, e.g. "Profile"; description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Define and manage personal account preferences."
- **Breadcrumb** (the route meta `ConsoleLayout` reads): the parent, then the page title exactly, e.g. "Account settings" › "Profile".
- **Choices:** sentence case and no parentheses, e.g. "Team default", "Standard protection".
- **Section heading:** a short topic noun, e.g. "General", "Notifications".
- **Row title:** names the setting in one to three words, e.g. "Timezone"; description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Times across the app are shown in this zone."
- **Save:** exactly "Save" for the footer and every group or card; Discard is exactly "Discard", never "Cancel": it restores the saved values and the reader stays on the page.
- **Errors:** what is wrong plus what to do, e.g. "Enter a valid email address."
- **Docs link:** names the topic, e.g. "Learn more about the Preview Toolbar".
- **Profile:** section hints are one sentence on what the group affects ("The company that owns the account, as it appears on every invoice."); optional fields say it in the description ("Optional. Apartment, suite or floor."); the destructive row uses one verb for the title and the button ("Delete personal account" with "Delete account", never "Remove"); the save bar reads "You have unsaved changes."; the load failure reads "The profile could not be loaded. Nothing was changed; try again." with "Retry"; the delete toast reads "Account scheduled for deletion."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The `form` is named by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby` and uses `novalidate`; the title is the page's only `h1`.
- Each group is a real `fieldset`; SaveAll gives it a visually hidden `legend` ("Profile settings").
- Every control has an `aria-label` that repeats its row title; errors are linked with `aria-describedby` only while they show.
- Disabling the `fieldset` while saving takes every control out of interaction at once; Save announces its loading state.
- Focus order follows reading order: the rows from top to bottom, then Discard and Save.

## States

- SaveAll: Profile with General, Preferences and Notifications in one fieldset and one sticky Discard and Save footer.
- Saving: the whole fieldset and Discard are disabled and Save shows its loading state.
- SaveError: the server rejects the save; an error toast with Retry says the changes are kept, and the form stays dirty with every entry.
- SavePerGroup: Preferences split into General and Notifications cards, each with its own secondary Save.
- SavingOneGroup: General is saving with its rows disabled while Notifications stays editable.
- SavePerCard: Project settings with Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection cards, each with an info `Alert`, its fields and its own Save.
- SavingOneCard: Preview Toolbar is saving with its selects disabled while Deployment Protection stays editable.
- Profile: the profile filled from the account (Billing emails empty and required), save bar hidden until a saved field changes. Saving with Account name set to `Offline` walks the failure toast; an empty Account name or a malformed billing address walks the field errors. Delete account opens the type-to-confirm dialog.
- ProfileLoading: the first load; `Skeleton` cards in place of the sections.
- ProfileError: the account did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

## Related

- `edit/edit-resource` — settings of one resource, with anchored sections.
- `account/mfa-settings` — where Profile's Manage MFA row leads.
- `state/form-validation` — every outcome of a submit.
- `state/async-submit` — a save that runs long and reports back later.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the delete row a settings page can end with.
- `SettingsRow` — the row this form is made of; see `skills/webkit-form` for the ItemGroup settings and Card with independent saves types.

## Variants

`SaveAll` (primary) · `Saving` · `SaveError` · `SavePerGroup` · `SavingOneGroup` · `SavePerCard` · `SavingOneCard` · `Profile` · `ProfileLoading` · `ProfileError`. Code: [blocks/settings/settings-form.md](blocks/settings/settings-form.md), `get_block("settings/settings-form", { variant })`.

# Console (`shell/console`)

> The console shell as one component: `ConsoleLayout`, composed once in the app around RouterView, so a console page is only its body.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/shell/console/console.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("shell/console")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Badge, Button, Card, Command, ConsoleLayout, ConsoleLayout, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, HighlightButton, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, StatusIndicator, Table, Tabs, Tag, ThemeSwitcher, Toast, Tooltip, `use-color-mode`
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

platform shell; console shell; app shell; sidebar layout; navigation rail; dashboard layout; admin layout; app layout with sidebar; estrutura do console; layout com menu lateral; menu lateral; console; console layout; layout do console; notifications panel; notifications drawer; notification center; central de notificações; painel de notificações; switch account; account switcher; organization switcher; change organization; trocar conta; trocar organização; selecionar conta; console layout component; ConsoleLayout; app layout with router view; layout do console com RouterView; account list failed to load; switch account error; erro ao carregar contas

The application shell every signed-in page renders inside. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: the navigation rail (wordmark, grouped navigation with drill-in levels, the account at its foot), one global header (breadcrumbs, search, the app's actions, the avatar) and the ⌘K palette. All of that is one component, `ConsoleLayout`: this block is the app's `App.vue` — compose it once around `RouterView` and every console page is only the body rendered through its default slot. The body here is a stand-in for `view/table-view`.

## When to use

- The root of a console app: every browse page (first-level lists, Home and dashboards, resource details with their tabs, settings) renders inside it.

## When not to use

- Create, edit and deploy flows: use the focused shell headed by `top-bar/creation-bar`, with no rail.
- Signed-out screens: `auth/sign-in` with `top-bar/auth-bar`.
- Documentation and marketing: `shell/docs`, `shell/site`.
- A page needing the resizable split panel: compose `AppLayout` directly for that page.

## Building blocks

- A. Shell — `ConsoleLayout` (required)
- B. Actions — `Button` (required)
- C. Agent — `HighlightButton` (required)
- D. Hints — `Tooltip` (required)
- E. Icon actions — `IconButton` (required)
- F. Palette groups — `Command` (required)
- G. Account menu — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- H. Theme — `ThemeSwitcher` (required)
- I. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- J. Page title — `PageHeader` (stand-in body)
- K. Table frame — `Card` (stand-in body)

What each part takes: [blocks/shell/console.md](blocks/shell/console.md).

## Do

- Compose `ConsoleLayout` once in `App.vue` and render every browse page through its default slot; replace this block's stand-in body with `<RouterView />`.
- Keep the navigation in one data file shared by the app; the rail and the palette both read it.
- Give every row an `href` (never `to` or `path`); derive a static `breadcrumbs` trail from the route.
- Let a detail page set its own trail, control crumb included, with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`.
- Frame a list or form body with `layout-boundary` + `layout-column`; open a detail body flush on `PageTabs`.

## Don't

- Don't render `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `AppHeader`, `SearchTrigger`, a `Command` palette or a `<main>` in a page; the layout owns them.
- Don't put a page's control crumb in `App.vue`, or size a body with `calc(100dvh - …)`.
- Don't render the rail on create, edit or deploy pages.
- Don't add page actions to the global header; they belong to the page's header, controls row or tab row.
- Don't hide the avatar when the rail is collapsed or in the drawer.
- Don't render the account switcher in both `sidebar-header` and `header-leading` at once; pick by the slots' `compact`.
- Don't leave an empty account table when the list fails to load; show the danger `Alert` with Retry in its place.
- Don't open the notifications region as a popover over the page; it is the layout's tools region beside the content.

## Copy

- **Palette groups:** `Recents`, `Actions`; the layout's placeholder `Search pages and commands` and its empty line come from the locale catalog.
- **Navigation and menu items:** nouns as the module pages are titled (`Personal tokens`, `Activity history`, `Build and deployment`, `Account settings`); Azion product names keep theirs (`Edge DNS`, `Real-Time Metrics`). No ampersand.
- **Status:** a short state, not a sentence: `All systems operational`.
- **Load failure:** what failed, as a sentence: `The account list could not be loaded.`; the action is `Retry`, the word every block uses (auth included).
- **Header actions:** `Create`, `Agent`.
- **Module create:** `Create` plus the entity: `Create Application`.

## Accessibility

- One `main` (the layout's), one `banner` (the header), the rail as a labelled navigation (`Main navigation`); the page body starts with its `h1` (`PageHeader`).
- ⌘K / Ctrl K opens the palette, announced through `aria-keyshortcuts` on the search; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- The rail's drawer traps focus while open, closes on `Escape` and when a row is chosen, and returns focus to the menu button.
- Icon-only controls have both an `aria-label` and a tooltip.
- The bell is a toggle (`aria-pressed`) and names the unread count; unread items carry a visually hidden `Unread:` prefix, not colour alone.

## States

- ListPage: a first-level list page in the `ConsoleLayout` default slot: no breadcrumb on a first level, the page opens on its `PageHeader` (title, description, Documentation and the create action) over the page body. The controls row and the table belong to `view/table-view`, which builds them from the Table toolbar parts; the shell does not draw them.
- DetailPage: a resource detail page rendered through `ConsoleLayout`. The page body sets its own trail with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`: Applications and the application as `items`, then the environment in its slot, a `Select` with `variant="ghost"` and `size="small"` labelled `Switch environment` (a search `Input`, each environment tagged with its deployment policy, a muted line when nothing matches, Add Environment at its foot). The default slot is flush and opens on a full-bleed `PageTabs` (Overview, Deployments, Settings, the outlined Deploy in `#actions`), sticky at the top of the layout's scrolling region so it stays in view while the tab content scrolls under it; no `main` of its own, the layout owns it.
- Notifications: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with the bell after Create and Agent in the `actions` slot; it toggles the layout's tools region (`v-model:tools-open`, `tools-label="Notifications"`), a region beside the content and a drawer when narrow. The `tools` slot holds the list as `Item.List` of `Item` rows (`Item.Media type="icon"` toned through `data-type`, title, description, time, `Item.Actions`), five at a time with `Show older` for the rest: unread items marked with a `New` tag (and a visually hidden `Unread:` prefix), Edit and Redeploy on each deploy, Mark all as read, Clear all (it empties the list and toasts `Notifications cleared.` with Undo, which brings them back), and the EmptyState `You are all caught up` once cleared. The failed deploy also shows as a flash Alert (Edit, Redeploy) in the `notifications` slot above the page. The bell's `aria-label` carries the unread count, `aria-pressed` follows the region, and the `Badge` on it is hidden from assistive technology.
- AccountSwitch: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with the current account in the `sidebar-header` slot, full width in the rail under the wordmark (square `Avatar` with its initials, the name, a sort glyph), `Switch account (Ctrl+O)` on its tooltip (to the right) and `aria-keyshortcuts`; the rail slot renders nothing while `compact` is true, and the same switcher moves to the `header-leading` slot, before the breadcrumbs, with the avatar and the chevron only (the name stays in its `aria-label`). It and the shortcut open a large `Dialog`, rendered beside the layout, with a search `Input` (name, ID or client ID) over a `Table` of the account tree: organizations, groups and workspaces indented by depth, expand and collapse buttons with `aria-expanded`, each name a button that switches, `Current` on the active one, type as `Table.CellStatus`, ID and client ID as `Table.CellId`. Each name is a `Button` with `variant="link"`. The table pages ten rows at a time (`paginated`), and while the list loads on open it shows the `Table` loading rows. Switching closes the dialog and toasts `Switched to <name>.` with the IDs; the footer shows the current account and Account settings. A search with no match shows Clear search. The search `Input` takes its `id` from `useId()` so the dialog can focus it on open.
- AccountSwitchError: the AccountSwitch dialog when the account list fails to load. A danger `Alert` (`The account list could not be loaded.`, action `Retry`) takes the place of the account `Table` under the search; the search, the title and the footer stay. Retry loads the list again and shows the table.

## Related

- `top-bar/creation-bar` — the focused shell for create, edit and deploy.
- `view/table-view`, `detail/resource-detail`, `dashboard/home-dashboard` — the page bodies rendered in the slot.

## Variants

`ListPage` (primary) · `DetailPage` · `Notifications` · `AccountSwitch` · `AccountSwitchError`. Code: [blocks/shell/console.md](blocks/shell/console.md), `get_block("shell/console", { variant })`.

# Docs (`shell/docs`)

> The documentation shell is `DocLayout`, composed once around the app's router view, so every docs page is only its article.

- Surface: docs
- Source: `blocks/shell/docs/docs.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("shell/docs")`
- Components: `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `copilotMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, `opencodeMark`, Brand, Button, CodeBlock, CopyPromptButton, DataTable, Diagram, DocAccordion, DocAccordionGroup, DocAgentCard, DocCallToAction, DocCallout, DocCard, DocCardGroup, DocCodeGroup, DocFrame, DocHeading, DocHero, DocItem, DocLayout, DocMarkdown, DocPageHeader, DocPreviousNext, DocPrompt, DocProse, DocStep, DocSteps, DocTab, DocTabs, Footer, IconButton, `ItemList`, Logo, RegistrationFrame, Select, StatusIndicator, Tag, ThemeSwitcher, `use-color-mode`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`

## Asked as

docs shell; documentation layout; docs page layout; documentation site; docs sidebar; on this page outline; knowledge base layout; layout da documentação; página de documentação; estrutura da documentação; documentation shell; docs layout; documentation article; docs article page; tutorial page; getting started guide; how-to guide; product reference page; reference documentation; docs page with steps and code; documentation home; docs home page; docs landing page; developer portal home; artigo da documentação; página de tutorial; guia de primeiros passos; página de referência do produto; página inicial da documentação; home da documentação; docs home with copy prompt and AI agent logos; your AI agent fluent in Azion card; botão copiar prompt com logos de IA; docs layout component; DocLayout; agent setup page; coding agent setup; mcp setup guide; AI agent comparison table; configurar agente de IA; página de configuração do agente; agent setup index; connect an AI agent to the docs

The documentation shell. A reader comes to learn one task and leave, so the shell keeps the page readable and the next page close. It is `DocLayout`, composed once in the app around `RouterView`: the layout owns the docs header, the navigation rail, the "On this page" rail, the search palette and the footer, and the document itself scrolls with the header and both rails sticky. Every docs page is only its article.

## When to use

- Every documentation, guide or reference page, and the docs home.

## When not to use

- Marketing pages: `shell/site`. Product pages: `shell/console`.

## Building blocks

- A. Layout — `DocLayout` (required)
- B. Header actions — `IconButton` (required)
- C. Console — `Button` (required)
- D. Theme — `ThemeSwitcher` (required)
- E. Call to action — `DocCallToAction` (optional)
- F. Masthead — `DocPageHeader` (required)
- G. Running text — `DocProse` (required)
- H. Section headings — `DocHeading` (required)
- I. Footer — `Footer` (required)
- J. Brand — `Brand` (required)
- K. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- L. Language — `Select` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/shell/docs.md](blocks/shell/docs.md).

## Do

- Compose `DocLayout` once in the app's root around `RouterView`; each route renders only its `<article>`.
- For a real page, start from a variant (Article, Reference, Landing, AgentSetup, AgentGuide): the variants build the article from the `Doc*` parts only.
- Give every `DocHeading` an `id` and pass the same ids, in document order, as `outline`.
- Put everything under `DocPageHeader` in one `DocProse`.
- Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href` (an in-app path is followed with the router); keep the rail scoped to the current product; the header section links switch products.
- Build a docs home from the Landing variant: `DocHero` with `CopyPromptButton`, then `DocAgentCard` above the Console / CLI / API cards; pass no `outline`.
- Build an index of peers (agents, SDKs, integrations) from AgentSetup: pick (a `DocTabs` filter over a `DocCardGroup`), compare (a `Table`), understand (glossary `DocCard`s). Give each peer its own page from AgentGuide.
- Render copy authored as Markdown with MDX tags (a content file, a CMS field, a sentence in data) with `DocMarkdown` inside `DocProse`, and build the `outline` from `parseDocMarkdown(source).headings`; AgentGuide uses it for its step bodies and accordion answers.
- Show a comparison of peers or a list of tools as a `DataTable` (`bordered`, imported from `data-table`) inside an element with `data-doc-block data-doc-chrome`, so the prose rules stay off it; a yes/no cell is a check or minus glyph with a visually hidden `Yes` / `No`, a category cell a `Tag` with `severity="neutral"`.
- Write the deck as the outcome (`By the end of this tutorial, …`), one action per `DocStep`, with its command as a `CodeBlock` inside the same step.

## Don't

- Don't put a `ScrollArea`, an `h-screen` frame or any inner scroll region around the article: the document scrolls, so find in page, scroll restoration and full-page captures work.
- Don't render a `<main>` in a page; the layout already renders the only one.
- Don't repeat the header, the search, the navigation rail, the outline or the footer in a page.
- Don't hand-write the outline, the pager or the masthead; the layout's outline rail, `DocPreviousNext` and `DocPageHeader` own their markup and labels.
- Don't give a `DocHeading` an id the `outline` does not list, or list an id no heading carries.
- Don't put a `DocHeading` outside `DocProse` (it renders at body size), and don't drop a `Button` row straight into `DocProse`: wrap it in an element with `data-doc-chrome`.
- Don't measure the viewport in script to place the footer brand; the `lg:` utilities and `signature="compact"` decide it in CSS.
- Don't reuse the console rail here; docs navigation is pages, not modules.

## Copy

- **Article headings:** verb-led tasks in sentence case: `Create the function`, `Verify the response`.
- **Navigation rows:** page titles exactly as the `h1` reads.
- **Step titles:** imperative, ending with a period when the step is a sentence: `Open Azion Console.`
- **Landing groups:** `Start by interface`, `Start by objective`, `Ready-made templates`, `Follow along`; card link labels are a verb and the object (`Install the CLI`).

## Accessibility

- A comparison table's yes/no glyphs are `aria-hidden` with a visually hidden `Yes` / `No` beside them; the agent name cell is a link with the mark `aria-hidden`.
- One main landmark: the layout's. The article is an `<article>` inside it, never a second `<main>`.
- One `h1` per article (the masthead or the hero); `DocHeading` levels follow it in order (2, then 3 under a 2), and outline entries target those ids.
- Landmarks: the header is a banner, the rail and the outline are labelled navigation regions, the footer is contentinfo; `Tab` runs header → rail → article → outline → footer.
- Choosing an outline entry moves focus to its heading and clears the sticky header.

## States

- Default: the chrome around a short guide; rail from `lg` (drawer below), outline with the GitHub and Community groups and the `DocCallToAction` from `xl`, the full footer under the article.
- Article: a tutorial page from the `Doc*` parts, pager in both directions, outline with an indented level 3 entry.
- Reference: a product reference page with a callout, the request-path diagram, a JSON rule and a term list; pager forward only.
- AgentSetup: an index page; the picker tabs filter the agent cards, the comparison table scrolls inside its frame on a narrow page, the outline indents its three level 3 entries.
- AgentGuide: one agent's page; steps with code, the tools table, prompts, accordions collapsed by default, pager in both directions.
- Landing: the documentation home; navigation rail, no outline rail, `DocHero` with `CopyPromptButton`, `DocAgentCard`, entry-point grids, pager forward to the first page.

## Related

- `DocLayout` — the component this block shows.
- `shell/console` (`ConsoleLayout`) and `shell/site` (`SiteLayout`) — the console and marketing counterparts.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Article` · `Reference` · `Landing` · `AgentSetup` · `AgentGuide`. Code: [blocks/shell/docs.md](blocks/shell/docs.md), `get_block("shell/docs", { variant })`.

site shell; marketing site layout; landing page layout; website layout; marketing page frame; layout do site; estrutura do site; página de marketing; website shell; marketing site shell; site layout component; SiteLayout; layout do site com SiteHeader
