# AsyncSubmit (`state/async-submit`)

> The async counterpart of the server rejection in the SectionRejected state of the FormValidation template: a deploy that runs for about half a minute, so the user walks away before it ends.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/async-submit/async-submit.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/async-submit")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, EmptyState, LogViewer, PageHeader, StatusIndicator, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-form`

## Asked as

async submit; long running action; background job status; deploy in progress; async deploy result; operation status; envio assíncrono; ação demorada; status da operação; result reaches me later

The async-action pattern, and the standard for every build and deploy screen. A long-running action the user is free to walk away from: a deploy that runs for about half a minute and asks nothing while it does. The user's job is to start it, go on working anywhere in the console, and learn how it ended without coming back to check. The page that started the run shows its status in the heading, the logs while it runs and an inline outcome when it ends; in a full app the run lives outside the page, so its progress and its outcome also travel with the user as a toast, on success and on failure.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

The run toast rides the app's one toast region, never the page's: the app installs `ToastPlugin` (`app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'bottom-right' })`) or mounts one `Toaster` near its root, beside `ConsoleLayout`, and this page body only imports `toast` from `@aziontech/webkit/toast`. A `Toaster` inside a page body is a second region for the whole app: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active, and it gives that up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, stops every toast once the user leaves the page, the opposite of a run toast that follows the user. The docs preview mounts one region around the block the way an app root does, so its frames show the toasts; a copy of the page shows them wherever the app has mounted the region.

The toasts are raised through `toast` with one id per run so each state replaces the last. Every outcome toast passes `actions: [{ label: 'Edit', onClick }, { label: 'Redeploy', onClick }]` and `closable: true`, so the app's `Toaster` renders both as `Toast.Action`s beside `Toast.Close`; the progress toast carries no action. The Running frame raises the progress toast, Error the permanent failure toast and Success the success toast; leaving the page dismisses the story's toast so the next story starts clean.

## When to use

- Use async-submit when the action runs long enough that the user leaves (build, deploy, import) and the result must reach them later.
- Any action that takes long enough to leave: build, deploy, redeploy, import, provision, a bulk change.
- When the outcome must reach the user on whatever page they are on when it lands.
- As the reference for the idle, running, failed and succeeded states of a run started from a page.

## When not to use

- A save that answers in about a second: use `state/form-validation`.
- A run the user watches to the end inside a create flow, or a deployment's own page: use `detail/deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow, DeploymentDetail).
- Confirming a finished deploy with next steps: use `create/deploy-success`.
- A deploy configured in a side panel: use `create/deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Actions — `Button` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Run status — `Tag` (required)
- D. Nothing running — `EmptyState` (idle only)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/async-submit.md](blocks/state/async-submit.md).

## Do

- Keep the run, its timer and its outcome outside the page component (a small module-scope store), so leaving the page never cancels it or loses the result.
- Show progress as a `loading` toast (no duration, not closable) that follows the user through the app while the run lasts.
- Report the end wherever the user is, on success and on failure. A failure toast is permanent (`duration: 0`) and `closable`; a success toast is `closable` with the default 6 second duration.
- Raise the toasts through `toast` only; the app mounts the region once (`ToastPlugin` or one `Toaster` at its root), so the page body never renders a `Toaster`.
- Give both toasts the same two actions through `toast()`'s `actions` option: **Edit** for the item that was deployed, and **Redeploy**. Don't rebuild the toast body in the `Toaster` slot to get two actions.
- On the page that started the run, show the outcome inline as well, with the same two actions as the toast: a danger `Alert` with the reason, **Edit** and **Redeploy** over the stopped logs, or a success `Alert` naming the new address with **Edit**, **Redeploy** and **Open service**.
- Disable Deploy and the controls that would change the run while it is in progress, with Deploy in `loading`.
- Use one toast id per run, so the progress toast turns into the outcome toast in place, and a Redeploy turns it back into progress.
- Apply this to every build and deploy screen (deploy drawers, deployment flows, redeploys from a list, imports): the run lives outside the page, the page shows the status `Tag` and the outcome `Alert`, and the toast reports wherever the user is.

## Don't

- Don't tie the run to the component that started it; unmounting a page is not an event the run hears.
- Don't let a failure toast expire; the user was not there when it arrived.
- Don't point the toast at a list of runs ("View deployments"); it carries **Edit** and **Redeploy**.
- Don't block the page with a modal or overlay while the run is in progress; the user must be able to leave.
- Don't claim an outcome before the server confirms it; the heading reads `Deploying` until it does.

## Copy

- **Page heading:** names the action and the resource, sentence case: `Deploy web-app`. Lead: what the run does and that the user may leave: `Builds acme/web-app and publishes it to production. A deploy takes about half a minute and keeps running if you leave this page; the result reports back wherever you are.`
- **Status tag:** one or two words: `Idle`, `Deploying`, `Failed`, `Deployed`.
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, description says what to do: `No deployment running` / `Start one above. It takes about 25 seconds.`
- **Progress toast:** present progressive with the single-character ellipsis, names the item: `Deploying web-app…`; description names the source and that the user may leave: `acme/web-app. It keeps running if you leave.`
- **Failure toast:** what failed and why, then the ways out: `web-app wasn't deployed.` / `The routing rules were refused.` Actions: `Edit`, `Redeploy`.
- **Success toast:** past tense, names the item and where it is live: `web-app is live.` / `It is available at web-app.example.com.` Actions: `Edit`, `Redeploy`.
- **Failure Alert:** the reason the server gave, as full sentences, with `Edit` and `Redeploy`.
- **Success Alert:** names the address and the attempts: `web-app is live at web-app.example.com. It took 1 attempt.`, with `Edit`, `Redeploy` and `Open service`.
- **Actions:** `Deploy`, `Redeploy` (never "Retry deploy" or "Try again"), `Edit`, `Open service`.

## Accessibility

- The run status is text in the heading's `Tag`, not color alone.
- Toasts are announced by the app's `Toaster`, politely except the failure toast (`danger`), which interrupts; the progress toast must not steal focus.
- The failure toast's actions and close button are reachable by keyboard, and it stays until closed.
- The logs card (Running and Error) streams into a `LogViewer`; do not announce every log line.
- Page entrance and the outcome `Alert` animate with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## States

- Idle: nothing running; the heading reads Idle and the `EmptyState` offers Deploy.
- Running: mid-run; the heading reads Deploying, the logs card streams under the Building status and the progress toast reads `Deploying web-app…`.
- Error: the routing rules were refused; the heading reads Failed, the danger `Alert` carries the reason with Edit and Redeploy, the permanent failure toast carries the same two actions, and the logs stay open on the failed step.
- Success: the run is live; the heading reads Deployed, the success `Alert` names the new address with Edit, Redeploy and Open service, the success toast carries Edit and Redeploy, and the logs card is gone.

## Related

- `state/form-validation` — the synchronous counterpart: field, section and toast placement for a save that answers right away.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — the deployment logs card (`LogViewer.Steps`) the Running and Error states reuse, and the full logs of a run the page Edit or a failure leads into.
- `create/deploy-success` — the confirmation page after a deploy completes.
- `shell/console` — the layout this body renders in, which the user moves through while the run reports back.

## Variants

`Idle` (primary) · `Running` · `Error` · `Success`. Code: [blocks/state/async-submit.md](blocks/state/async-submit.md), `get_block("state/async-submit", { variant })`.

# FirstUse (`state/first-use`)

> The block a first-level list renders before the account owns any resource of that kind: a flush Card holding an EmptyState (the resource glyph, headline, lead and a Documentation link) over an Item.List of the ways to…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/first-use/first-use.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/first-use")`
- Components: `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, Button, Card, CopyButton, EmptyState, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, Logo, Skeleton
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

empty state; empty list; first use; no resources yet; create first resource; product empty state; zero state; estado vazio; lista vazia; primeiro uso; first resource empty state

What a first-level list shows before the account owns any resource of that kind. The user's job is to create the first one, so the block replaces the empty table with a short explanation and every way to get started on the same screen: the methods to create one (import, CLI, from scratch), then the promotions that shortcut it (a Catalog template, a coding agent). Every list that is still empty renders this block with its own nouns, methods and promos.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use first-use on a list page before the account owns any resource of that kind.
- The first visit to a list page (Resources, Services, Domains…) when the account has none of that resource.
- When there is more than one way to create the first item and each deserves its own action.

## When not to use

- A list that has items but a filter or search matched none: use the no-match state of `view/table-view`.
- An empty panel inside a dashboard or detail page: use `EmptyState` alone, without the method list.
- Choosing what to create across every resource kind: use `create/create-hub`.
- The Home page before the first project: use `dashboard/home-dashboard` (its Empty state).
- A list that failed to load: that is an error, not first use; see `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Building blocks

- A. Frame — `Card` (required)
- B. Agent marks — `Logo` (optional)
- C. Explanation — `EmptyState` (required)
- D. Documentation — `Link` (required)
- E. Methods — `Item` (required)
- F. Method action — `Button` (required)
- G. Command row — `InputGroupRoot` (CLI method)
- H. Command — `Input` (CLI method)
- I. Copy — `CopyButton` (CLI method)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/first-use.md](blocks/state/first-use.md).

## Do

- Rewrite the headline, lead, methods and promos for each resource kind; the structure stays, the nouns change.
- Show the Catalog template promo only for resource kinds that have a template catalog.
- Keep one primary action across the whole block, on the method most users take.
- Keep the documentation link as the only action in the `EmptyState`.
- Hold the block's own footprint while the account reloads (the empty-state band, one row per method and the promo cards, in `Skeleton`s), so it does not jump in.

## Don't

- Don't draw an agent mark by hand (an `img` or a CSS mask): `Logo` already inks it for the theme.
- Don't show list controls (search, filters, pagination, column settings) over a list that has never had an item.
- Don't render this block for a filtered list with no matches; that state says how to clear the filter.
- Don't show it while the list is still loading; the user would see "create your first" for an account that has items.
- Don't add a second primary button to a promo card; the whole card is the action.

## Copy

- **Headline:** names the first action and the noun: `Create your first resource`.
- **Lead:** one sentence on the ways in: `Start from scratch, from a template or by importing your code.`
- **Method title:** two or three words for how: `From GitHub`, `Via CLI`, `From scratch`.
- **Method description:** one sentence on what happens: `Import a repository and deploy it on every push.`
- **Method action:** one verb: `Import`, `Create`.
- **Promo title:** sentence case, product names capitalized: `Start from a Catalog template`, `Set up your coding agent`.
- **Promo description:** one sentence on the result: `Deploy a framework starter and the resource that serves it, in one step.`
- **Documentation link:** `Documentation`.

## Accessibility

- The method icons and promo marks are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`, `alt=""`); the titles carry the meaning.
- Each promo is a real link (`<a href>`) covering the card, because both navigate; the Catalog one opens a new tab, shows the external-link glyph and says so to screen readers.
- The command `Input` has an `aria-label`; the copy button has its own label and announces the copied state.
- The documentation link opens in a new tab; say so in the destination or let `Link` mark it.
- The headline is the page's first heading under the list title, not a second `h1`.

## States

- Default: the explanation, three create methods and the two promos.
- Loading: while the account reloads, `Skeleton`s draw the block's footprint (empty-state band, three method rows, two promo cards) in a busy status region.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the list this block stands in for once the first item exists, and the home of the no-match state.
- `create/create-hub` — every create entry point across resource kinds.
- `create/deploy-template` — where the Catalog template promo leads.
- `state/project-intake` — the drop target and upload overlay an empty page can also render.
- `state/page-skeleton` — the skeleton painted before the page knows whether the list is empty.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading`. Code: [blocks/state/first-use.md](blocks/state/first-use.md), `get_block("state/first-use", { variant })`.

<!-- blocks/state/form-validation.md -->

# FormValidation (`state/form-validation`)

> A standalone form that walks through every state a submit can land in, one story per state, on a single Create Variable page with no card around it: a heading, then `Field`s wrapping `Input`, `Select` and `Textarea` s…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/form-validation/form-validation.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/form-validation")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, DropdownMenu, Field, `FieldError`, IconButton, Input, Item, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, RadioGroup, SaveBar, SectionHeader, Select, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Switch, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

form validation; validation errors; submit states; required fields; server error on submit; conflict error; saved state; validação de formulário; erros de validação; campos obrigatórios; submit outcomes; every submit outcome; server validation; server-side error; rejected save; field scoped error; section error; stale reference; linked resource deleted; api error on save; reload options; form error; erro de formulário; validação no servidor; erro da api; salvamento rejeitado; error de formulario; validación en el servidor

Every state a submit can land in, on one create form. The user's job is to create a resource and, when something stops the save, to know exactly which control to touch and that nothing they typed was lost. The primary is a short Create Variable page (heading, four fields straight on the canvas, Cancel and Create); the variants walk it through validation, the in-flight lock, an unscoped failure, a conflict, success and loading. The Section variants carry the same rules to a long sectioned create page, where the server rejects the save because of one section: another user deleted the origin the form links to, so the page takes the user to that section, says what happened and that nothing else was lost, offers the one action that recovers (Reload origins) and marks the field with its own reason. The Section variants are a focused create page with their own creation header and no rail.

This block is a page body for a create page: render it under the focused creation header (`top-bar/creation-bar`), not in `ConsoleLayout`.

## When to use

- Use form-validation as the reference for every submit outcome of a create or edit form: required, invalid, in flight, conflict, section rejected, unscoped failure, saved.
- As the reference for the submit states of any create or edit form: what happens on Create with gaps, while the request is in flight, and on each kind of answer.
- A short create form with a handful of fields and no sections (a variable, a key, a token).
- A long, sectioned create or edit form whose save can be rejected because of one section (a linked resource deleted or changed by someone else): SectionRejected, SectionReloading, SectionReloaded.

## When not to use

- A sectioned create page with many settings and a sticky save bar: build it from `create/create-page` and apply these states to it.
- A create that runs for tens of seconds and can be left (build, deploy, import): use `state/async-submit`.
- Settings of an existing object saved section by section: use `settings/settings-form`.
- Signed-out screens: use `auth/sign-in`, where nothing toasts.
- A create launched from a list without leaving it: use `create/create-drawer`.

## Where the error renders

| Error                                                                   | Where it renders                                                                                                                                                                     | Variant          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| A value the user left empty or typed wrong (client-side)                | On the field: `required` or `invalid`, its message in the description, focus on the first field in error                                                                             | ValidationErrors |
| A value the server refused that one field owns (a key already in use)   | On the field (`invalid` with its reason) and in a danger `Alert` above the fields of its section; never a toast                                                                      | Conflict         |
| A rejection one section of a long form owns (a linked resource deleted) | A danger `Alert` under that section's heading with the recovery action, the field `invalid` with its own reason, the section scrolled into view and the field focused; never a toast | SectionRejected  |
| A failure no field or section owns (network, timeout, 500)              | `toast.error` with Retry, every entry kept                                                                                                                                           | ServerError      |
| A save that went through                                                | `toast.success` naming the new object, the form cleared                                                                                                                              | Saved            |

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (loading only)
- C. Field — `Field` (required)
- D. Text value — `Input` (required)
- E. Choice — `Select` (required)
- F. Long text — `Textarea` (optional)
- G. Actions — `Button` (required)
- H. Section notice — `Alert` (conflict and rejection only)
- Section rejection (Section variants only)
- Result notices — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/state/form-validation.md](blocks/state/form-validation.md).

## Do

- Validate on submit, not on every keystroke; after the first submit, a field's message updates as the user fixes it.
- Move focus to the first field in error after a submit, after the lock is released.
- Lock the whole scope while the request is in flight: Create shows `loading`, every field and Cancel are disabled, `aria-busy` is on the form. Release it on success and failure alike.
- Keep every entry after a failed or rejected save, and say so in the copy.
- Clear the form after a success, so the next entry starts clean, and name the new object in the toast.
- On the one-section form, a key already in use raises the danger `Alert` above the fields as well as the `invalid` Key, and focus moves to Key.
- On a long form, put a section-scoped rejection in one danger `Alert` under that section's heading with the recovery on it, scroll the section into view (instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`) and focus the field with `preventScroll` after the lock is released. After the recovery, close the `Alert`, clear the stale value and flag the field `required`.

## Don't

- Don't show a validation summary at the top; each field carries its own message.
- Don't toast a rejection a field owns (a key already in use, a deleted origin). The toast dismisses itself and points nowhere.
- Don't use the amber `required` prompt for a value the server rejected; the value is present, so it is `invalid`.
- Don't disable Create to signal missing values; let submit run and show the messages.
- Don't clear the form or send the user back to the start after a rejection, and don't open more than one `Alert` for one rejection.
- Don't auto-dismiss an `Alert` that names a required action; it stays until the user recovers (see SectionReloaded).

## Copy

- **Page heading:** `Create` plus the entity, matching the page it lists: `Create Variable`. Lead: one sentence on what it is for: `Add a key-value pair your services read at runtime.`
- **Field labels:** one to three words, no colon, no parentheses: `Key`, `Value`, `Environment`, `Description`.
- **Field descriptions:** a constraint or purpose, one sentence with a period: `Uppercase letters, digits and underscores, for example API_TOKEN.`, `Optional. Up to 200 characters.`
- **Required message:** the one sentence every block uses: `This field is required.`; for a select, the action: `Select an environment.`
- **Invalid message:** what is wrong and the rule: `Use uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.`
- **Conflict message:** the fact, on the field: `A variable named API_TOKEN already exists.` The section `Alert` adds what happened and what to do: `A variable named API_TOKEN already exists in this account, so it wasn't created. Your entries are kept: change the key and press Create again.`
- **Error toast:** what did not happen, then what was kept: title `The variable wasn't created.`, description `The request didn't reach the server. Your entries are kept.`, action `Retry`.
- **Success toast:** past tense, names the object and where it applies: `API_TOKEN was created.` / `It is available in Production.`
- **Section Alert:** the fact, the cause, what was not lost, what to do: `Origin "web-origin-prod" no longer exists. Another user deleted it while you were filling in this form, so the service wasn't created. Nothing else was lost: reload the origin list and select another one.` Field reasons: `This origin no longer exists.`, then `Select an origin to continue.`
- **Actions:** `Cancel`, `Create`, `Retry`; on the long form `Cancel`, `Save`, `Reload origins`.

## Accessibility

- The `<form>` is labelled by the heading (`aria-labelledby`), uses `novalidate`, and sets `aria-busy` while loading or submitting.
- Every control has a `Field.Label` bound by `for`; the description and message are wired to the control by `Field`.
- The loading region is `role="status"` with an accessible name (`Loading the form`).
- Focus moves to the first field in error, only after the lock is released, since a disabled control cannot take focus.
- Toasts are announced by the app's `Toaster` region; the error toast keeps its Retry reachable by keyboard.
- A section `Alert` sits in reading order before the fields it governs; its action is a real button reachable by keyboard.
- In SectionRejected focus moves to the refused field with `preventScroll`, so the scroll to the section heading is the only movement; the reloading `Skeleton` has an accessible name.

## States

- Default: the empty Create Variable form, idle.
- ValidationErrors: Create pressed with gaps; empty Value and Environment take `required`, the malformed Key takes `invalid`, each with its own message, and focus moves to Key.
- Submitting: the request is in flight; Create shows `loading`, the fields and Cancel are disabled.
- ServerError: the request failed and no field owns it; an error toast with Retry, the lock released, every entry kept.
- Conflict: the key is already in use; the danger `Alert` opens above the fields, Key takes `invalid` with its reason and focus, and nothing toasts.
- Saved: the save went through; a success toast names the variable and where it is available, and the form is cleared.
- Loading: the form data is still arriving; `Skeleton` rows hold the layout and Create is disabled.
- SectionRejected: on the long Create Service form, another user deleted the origin and Save was pressed; the page scrolls to Origin, the danger `Alert` opens under its heading with Reload origins, and focus lands on the Origin select, which reads This origin no longer exists.
- SectionReloading: Reload origins in flight; its button loads, the select gives way to a `Skeleton`, Save is disabled.
- SectionReloaded: the list is back without the deleted origin; the `Alert` closes, the select is cleared and flagged required with Select an origin to continue.

## Related

- `state/async-submit` — the long-running counterpart: use it when the action runs long enough that the user leaves (build, deploy, import) and the result must reach them later.
- `skills/webkit-errors` — where every error renders, row by row.
- `create/create-page` — the sectioned create page these states apply to.
- `auth/sign-in` — the signed-out version, where every outcome lands in one card `Alert` and nothing toasts.
- `settings/settings-form` — the same field states on an existing object.
- `Field` — the label, description and state triad every field here uses.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `ValidationErrors` · `Submitting` · `ServerError` · `Conflict` · `Saved` · `Loading` · `SectionRejected` · `SectionReloading` · `SectionReloaded`. Code: [blocks/state/form-validation.md](blocks/state/form-validation.md), `get_block("state/form-validation", { variant })`.

# NotFound (`state/not-found`)

> The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/not-found/not-found.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/not-found")`
- Components: Button, CopyButton, EmptyState, LineFigure, `Error403`
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

404 page; not found page; page not found; 403 forbidden page; access denied page; 500 error page; server error page; error page; resource not found; página não encontrada; página de erro; acesso negado; erro 404; erro 500

The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for: the address leads nowhere (404), the user may not see it (403), or the server failed to build it (500). The user's job is to understand, in one sentence, that the problem is the address or the access and not their work, and to get somewhere useful in one click. The block keeps the error code out of the headline (it is in the figure and in a hidden `h1`) and says what happened in plain words.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A route that matches nothing: the catch-all route of the app renders the primary.
- A route the user's role does not include: render Forbidden instead of hiding the page silently or sending them to the home page.
- A page whose server request failed as a whole (the data the page needs did not arrive and nothing on it can render): render ServerError.
- A valid route whose record does not exist (a deleted service, a stale link with an old ID): render ResourceNotFound inside the console shell.

## When not to use

- One region of a page failed to render while the rest works: wrap the region in `ErrorBoundary`; it shows a danger `Alert` with Try again in the region's place.
- A list with no items yet: use `state/first-use`. A list whose filter matched nothing: use the no-match state of `view/table-view`.
- A form the server rejected: use `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected).
- A build or deploy that failed: use `state/async-submit`; its toast and page `Alert` carry Edit and Redeploy.
- The account itself could not load after sign-in: that is an auth screen; see `auth/sign-in`.

## Building blocks

- A. Figure — `LineFigure` (`@aziontech/webkit/line-figure`)
- B. Message — `EmptyState` (required)
- C. Actions — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/not-found.md](blocks/state/not-found.md).

## Do

- Render the block on the address the user asked for; do not redirect to `/404`, so reloading tries the real address again and the browser history stays honest.
- Answer with the matching HTTP status when the server renders the page (404, 403, 500), so crawlers and monitoring see it.
- Keep the shell (navigation, header) around ResourceNotFound and around a 403 inside the console, so the user can move on without the back button.
- Give a 500 an error reference the user can quote to support, and log the same reference on the server.
- On 403, say who can grant access (an account admin) and offer the switch when the user belongs to more than one account.

## Don't

- Don't blame the user (`You typed a wrong URL`) or show a stack trace, a raw status line or an exception message.
- Don't hide a 403 behind a 404 inside the product: a user who followed a link from a teammate needs to know to ask for access. Use 404 for a 403 only where revealing that the page exists would leak information.
- Don't add a search box, a sitemap or a list of popular pages; two actions are enough.
- Don't auto-redirect after a countdown; the user decides where to go.
- Don't put the error code in the visible title; the figure already shows it.

## Copy

- **Title:** what happened, sentence case, no code: `Page not found`, `You don't have access to this page`, `Something went wrong on our side`, `Service 4821 not found`.
- **Description:** why, and what to do: `There is nothing deployed at this address. Check the URL or head back to the start.` On a 500, reassure: `Nothing you saved was lost.`
- **Primary action:** where it goes: `Go to home`, `Back to services`; or what it does: `Retry`.
- **Secondary action:** `Docs`, `Switch account`, `System status`.
- **Reference:** `Error reference: req_7f3c91ab`, in `text-label-code-sm`, wrapped in `<bdi>` so it keeps its order in right-to-left pages, with a `CopyButton` (`Copy the error reference`) so the user can paste it to support.

## Accessibility

- Each variant has exactly one `h1` (visually hidden) naming the error code, so the page has a heading and the code is announced even though the figure is decorative.
- Every variant is a body inside the layout's `main`, with no `main` of its own.
- The figure is `aria-hidden` (inside the `EmptyState` icon wrapper); never put the only statement of the error in the art.
- The `EmptyState` is `role="status"`, so a client-side route change to this page is announced.
- Retry shows the `Button` loading state while the page reloads; the button keeps its label.
- Buttons that open a new tab carry an icon; do not rely on colour.

## States

- Default: 404, the animated azion-404 line figure, Page not found, Go to home and Docs.
- Forbidden: 403, the 403 numeral art, You don't have access to this page, Go to home and Switch account.
- ServerError: 500, the warning icon tile, Something went wrong on our side, Retry, System status and the error reference with its copy button.
- ResourceNotFound: a bordered EmptyState in the console's content column naming the missing service and its ID, with Back to services.

## Related

- `shell/console` — the shell that frames ResourceNotFound and a 403 inside the product.
- `state/first-use` — an empty list, which is not an error.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — a server rejection scoped to a form section.
- `state/async-submit` — the outcome of a build or deploy, with Edit and Redeploy.
- `auth/sign-in` — the sign-in screens, including the account that could not load.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Forbidden` · `ServerError` · `ResourceNotFound`. Code: [blocks/state/not-found.md](blocks/state/not-found.md), `get_block("state/not-found", { variant })`.

# PageSkeleton (`state/page-skeleton`)

> The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving: the Home overview (Overview), the first-access Home (Onboarding), the whole shell while an expired session signs out (Session, with one body per family…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/page-skeleton/page-skeleton.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/page-skeleton")`
- Components: Card, Item, Skeleton
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

page skeleton; loading skeleton; skeleton screen; page loading state; wireframe loading; carregando; esqueleto de carregamento; tela de carregamento; whole page loading; shell skeleton

The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving. The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home).

Overview and Onboarding are page bodies for the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`); the Session wires stand in for the whole app, layout included.

## When to use

- Use page-skeleton for the first paint of a whole page or shell; inside a block use that block's Loading variant.
- The first paint of a page whose data is still loading, when the layout is known.
- Home, before its metrics and recent activity arrive (Overview), or before the first project (Onboarding).
- Over the whole app while an expired session signs out (the Session wires), so the user sees the page dissolve into its frame instead of a blank screen.

## When not to use

- A single control or panel loading inside a ready page: use `Skeleton` or `Spinner` inside that panel only.
- A form whose options are loading: use the Loading state of `state/form-validation`.
- A dashboard's own loading: use the Loading variant of that dashboard block (for example `dashboard/analytics-dashboard`).
- A long upload or build: use `state/project-intake` or `state/async-submit`, which report progress.
- After the sign-out completes: `auth/sign-in` (SessionExpired).

## Building blocks

- A. Bands — `Skeleton` (required)
- B. Frames — `Card` (required)
- C. Lists — `Item` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/page-skeleton.md](blocks/state/page-skeleton.md).

## Do

- Draw the exact grid of the page that is coming: same columns, gaps and breakpoints.
- Use the real layout utilities (`layout-column`, `layout-boundary`, `--layout-section-gap`), not fixed sizes.
- Hide the bands from assistive technology and announce the wait once: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-busy="true"`, with a short screen-reader text on every wire.
- Size the session wire to the measured header and rail in the app, so the frame does not move when it appears.
- Fade the session wire in with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## Don't

- Don't show a wire for less than a perceptible moment; if the data arrives within about 300 ms, paint the page directly.
- Don't use a generic spinner for a page whose layout is known.
- Don't animate each band independently; a shimmer comes from `Skeleton`.
- Don't mix real content and bands in one card; the card swaps in whole.
- Don't let the wire collapse to a few lines on wide screens; it holds the page's full footprint.

## Copy

- **Bands:** no visible text. The wire has nothing to read.
- **Screen-reader status (session):** states what is happening, as a sentence: `Session expired. Signing you out.`
- **Screen-reader status (page):** names what is loading: `Loading the overview.` on the Overview wire, `Loading Home.` on the Onboarding wire.

## Accessibility

- The bands are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"` on the wire's body).
- The region that stands in for the page is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-busy="true"`; clear `aria-busy` when the content lands.
- The wire takes no focus and traps none; the real page receives focus as it would on a normal load.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` on the entrance and on the shimmer.

## States

- Overview: the Home overview wire: heading, the four-metric strip, the side card, and the five-column row of list panels.
- Onboarding: the first-access Home wire: headline and prompt bands over three door cards, each with its illustration stage, three text lines and an action.
- Session: the whole shell as a wire over a list page: header bar, navigation rail with grouped items, the list controls row and a table card with header, eight rows and pagination.
- SessionDetail: the same over a detail page: tab bands under the header, a heading and two cards of field rows in the data column.
- SessionForm: the same over a create page: a heading and two cards of field rows in the create column, with the save bar held at the foot.
- SessionHome: the same over Home: the Overview wire centred in the data column.
- VersionDetail: the version page loading; form-column heading bands and two sectioned flush cards whose rows end in a switch band, one `role="status"` region with `aria-busy`, no tabs.

## Related

- `dashboard/home-dashboard` — the Home page the Overview and Onboarding wires stand in for.
- `view/table-view` — the list page the Session wire draws.
- `detail/resource-detail` — the detail page the SessionDetail wire draws.
- `create/create-page` — the create page the SessionForm wire draws.
- `detail/version-detail` — the version page the VersionDetail wire stands in for.
- `auth/sign-in` — where the session wire lands once the sign-out completes.
- `shell/console` — the header and rail the session wires reproduce.

## Variants

`Overview` (primary) · `Onboarding` · `Session` · `SessionDetail` · `SessionForm` · `SessionHome` · `VersionDetail`. Code: [blocks/state/page-skeleton.md](blocks/state/page-skeleton.md), `get_block("state/page-skeleton", { variant })`.

# ProjectIntake (`state/project-intake`)

> The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the drop target (`FileDropzone` with `directories`, its title saying what dropping does and a Choose a folder `Button` as the keyboard way in), the…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/state/project-intake/project-intake.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("state/project-intake")`
- Components: Alert, Button, FileDropzone, UploadProgress
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-motion-polish`

## Asked as

drop zone; drag and drop upload; upload project; folder upload; initializing project; file drop; arrastar e soltar; enviar projeto; upload de arquivos

The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: a drop target fills the page body and says what will happen, with a Choose a folder button for anyone not dragging; once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay lists the received files with their status until the upload is done and the deploy takes over.

DropZone is a page-body overlay inside the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`); Initializing covers the whole screen.

## When to use

- Pages where dropping a project is a shortcut to deploying it: Home, its empty state, a creation hub, and a project detail page.
- Showing upload progress per file, when the files are few enough to list.

## When not to use

- Choosing a single file as a form value: use a file upload field inside the form (`skills/webkit-form`).
- Browsing or managing stored files: use `view/file-browser`.
- The build and deploy that follow the upload: use `state/async-submit` and `detail/deployment-logs`.
- Importing from a repository: use the From GitHub method in `state/first-use` or `create/deploy-template` (ImportFromGit).

## Building blocks

- A. Drop target — `FileDropzone` (required)
- B. Keyboard way in — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/state/project-intake.md](blocks/state/project-intake.md).

## Do

- Keep the drop target where a drop does something, with Choose a folder beside the message.
- Say what dropping does, not how to drop: the user is already dragging.
- Render Initializing over the page the drop came from (Home, its empty state, the creation hub), so the user keeps their place.
- Advance the rows in order and keep finished rows visible while the list is short; past 50 files list only what is still moving.
- Keep Choose a folder in the drop target; drag and drop is a shortcut, never the only way.

## Don't

- Don't use a percentage bar alone for a handful of files; the per-file rows say more.
- Don't hide a failed file in the list; say it in the `Alert` and keep Retry on its row.
- Don't show the drop target on pages where a drop does nothing.
- Don't keep the overlay up after the upload ends; hand over to the deploy's own progress.

## Copy

- **Drop heading:** what the drop does, one line: `Drop your project to deploy it`. On a project page: `We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.`
- **Drop lead:** what is accepted, full sentences: `A project folder, or the files inside one. We detect what it is built with.`
- **Overlay heading:** one word for the phase: `Initializing`.
- **Overlay progress:** what is happening and how far, with a period: `Setting up your deployment. 2 of 5 files.`
- **Summary:** count and total size: `5 files, 8.36 KB`.
- **Failure:** what failed and what to do: `1 file could not be uploaded. Retry it, or remove it from the folder and drop the project again.`

## Accessibility

- The drop target names itself through its title and description; Choose a folder is the keyboard and screen reader path, and the number of received files is announced once.
- `UploadProgress` announces the transfer summary in its own status region, without stealing focus; the overlay itself is not a live region, so rows changing are not re-announced.
- Each row says its status in words; glyphs are decorative.
- Every fade and the row advance honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- DropZone: the drop target fills the page body with the drop message and Choose a folder.
- Initializing: the overlay mid-upload, two files uploaded, the third uploading, two queued, each row with its status in words, path and size.
- UploadError: one file failed; its row shows the reason and Retry, and a danger `Alert` above the list sums it up with Retry.

## Related

- `state/first-use` — an empty list page that can also render the drop target.
- `create/create-hub` — a creation hub that renders the drop target and Initializing.
- `dashboard/home-dashboard` — Home and its empty state, which render both surfaces.
- `state/async-submit` — how the deploy that follows reports back.

## Variants

`DropZone` (primary) · `Initializing` · `UploadError`. Code: [blocks/state/project-intake.md](blocks/state/project-intake.md), `get_block("state/project-intake", { variant })`.

## Asked as

auth header; signed-out header; login page header; onboarding header; public console header; header without navigation; logged-out top bar; cabeçalho de login; cabeçalho deslogado; barra do topo sem navegação; top bar; auth bar; signed-out top bar; barra de autenticação

The top bar of every signed-out and first-run screen: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the onboarding steps. The user has no session yet, so the bar has one job: say where they are (Azion) and offer the one way out that needs no account, the documentation. Everything a signed-in bar carries (navigation, search, Create, the account avatar) is left out because there is nothing to act on.

## When to use

- Use auth-bar on signed-out and onboarding screens (brand + Documentation, no navigation).
- Above the auth card on sign in, sign up, reset password and MFA screens (`auth/sign-in`).
- Above the onboarding steps that run before the organization exists (`account/onboarding-form`).

## When not to use

- Any page with a session: `ConsoleLayout` already renders the console bar (`shell/console`); a create, edit or deploy flow uses `top-bar/creation-bar`.
- Documentation pages: `DocLayout` renders their bar (`shell/docs`). Marketing pages: `SiteLayout` and `SiteHeader` render theirs (`shell/site`).

## Building blocks

- A. Bar — `AppHeader` (required)
- B. Brand — `Brand` (required)
- C. Documentation — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/top-bar/auth-bar.md](blocks/top-bar/auth-bar.md).

## Do

- Keep the bar identical across every signed-out step so the user knows they are still in the same flow.
- Let the page under it own the heading and the primary action (the auth card).

## Don't

- Don't add an avatar, a menu or a search: a control that implies a session reads as broken when there is none.
- Don't put the Sign in or Sign up switch in the bar; it lives in the card as a link.

## Copy

- **Documentation button:** one noun, sentence case, no icon-only variant: `Documentation`.
- **Brand link label:** names the destination: `Azion home`.

## Accessibility

- The `AppHeader` is a landmark with its own label (`Console`); keep one per page.
- The brand is a link with an accessible name, not a decorative image.
- Tab order is brand, then Documentation; nothing else in the bar takes focus.

## States

- Default: the only state; the bar never changes between signed-out steps.

## Related

- `auth/sign-in` — the sign-in and sign-up card this bar sits above.
- `account/onboarding-form` — the first-run steps render the same bar.
- `shell/console` — the bar once the user is signed in, rendered by `ConsoleLayout`.
- `top-bar/creation-bar` — the bar of a signed-in focused flow.

## Variants

`Default` (primary). Code: [blocks/top-bar/auth-bar.md](blocks/top-bar/auth-bar.md), `get_block("top-bar/auth-bar", { variant })`.

# CreationBar (`top-bar/creation-bar`)

> The console bar for the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail.

## Asked as

creation header; focused shell header; create flow header; flow header with back button; header without sidebar; edit flow header; deploy flow header; cabeçalho de criação; cabeçalho de fluxo; barra com botão voltar; create page header; create zone header; wizard header; header with back and breadcrumb; creation flow top bar; focused page header; cabeçalho da página de criação; cabeçalho do assistente; top bar; creation bar; top navigation without rail; focused top bar; barra de criação

The top bar of the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. ## When to use

- The deploy flows (`create/deploy-template`) and the Creation Center (`create/create-hub`).

## When not to use

- Keep the avatar even when back and crumb are gone.

## Don't

- Don't add Create, search or the Agent button: they invite the user to start a second task.
- Don't make the last crumb a link.

- `Breadcrumb` renders a labelled `nav`; the last crumb is the current page (`aria-current`).
- Focus order: back, brand, crumbs, avatar.

## States

- Default: back button, brand, breadcrumb to the list, and the avatar.
- CreateHub: the back control returns Home and the crumb is the single current page.

# CardView (`view/card-view`)

> The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/card-view/card-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/card-view")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CardList, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Input, Link, PageHeader, Pagination, PropertyFilter, Tag, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

card view; cards view; card list; cards list; resource cards; grid of cards; card grid page; gallery of resources; applications as cards; selectable cards; cards with filters; cards with pagination; visualização em cards; lista em cards; cartões de recursos; grade de cards

The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources people tell apart by a handful of fields or a picture rather than by comparing one column across many rows (applications, sites, images).
- Each item has a short, stable set of fields (four to six) that reads well as label and value pairs.
- Users act on several items at once (delete, move, tag) and need the selection to survive paging and filtering.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and visible fields must survive the next visit.

## When not to use

- Records compared and sorted column by column, or more than six fields per item: use `view/table-view`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use `detail/resource-detail` or `detail/dns-zone-detail`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- Templates to start from: use `view/template-browser`.
- Choosing a starting point to create from (products): use `create/create-hub` or `create/deploy-template`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `view/file-browser`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `state/first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Bulk action — `Button` (required)
- D. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)
- E. Card preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- F. CardList — `CardList`, `Link`, `Tag` (required)
- G. Pagination — `Pagination` (required)
- H. No matching applications — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- I. Empty listing and load failure — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Alert`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/card-view.md](blocks/view/card-view.md).

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call with `selection: { mode: 'multiple' }` and bind `cardListProps`, `paginationProps`, `propertyFilterProps` and `preferencesProps` with `v-bind`.
- Keep the controls row, the cards and the pagination in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Name every card with a link to the resource in the `header` slot, and keep its fields to the few that tell one item from another.
- Render the fields from `preferences.columns`, so the order and visibility set in the dialog reach every card.
- Count the selection in the bulk action's label and disable it at zero.
- Put every Delete behind the confirmation dialog, with the count in its title and the names in its body.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens and the page live in the query string, and give the list a `storageKey` of its own.
- Choose page sizes that fill whole rows of four.
- Branch on `status`: `empty` replaces the cards with the create state, `no-match` fills the `#empty` slot with Clear filters.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`.
- Don't make the whole card a link or a click target when it is also selectable; the name link opens it and the checkbox selects it.
- Don't put row-style action menus on every card for actions the bulk action already covers.
- Don't vary a card's height or field order from one card to the next; every card shows the same fields in the same order, with a dash for a missing value.
- Don't truncate the name in the header to fit a badge; the status lives in the fields.
- Don't hide Delete when nothing is selected; disable it so its place in the row stays put.
- Don't show the first-use empty state when filters hide every card, or Clear filters when the account has none.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Applications". Description: one sentence with a period.
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Application"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state repeats the same label.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter applications".
- **Bulk action:** the verb, then the count in parentheses, e.g. "Delete", "Delete (3)".
- **Field labels:** one or two words, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Status", "Domain", "Region", "Requests in 24h", "Owner". Preferences title: "Card preferences".
- **Delete dialog:** title `Delete <n> applications`, consequence `The selected applications will be deleted, along with their domains and settings:` followed by the names, prompt `Type delete to confirm.`, actions `Cancel` and `Delete applications` (singular for one).
- **No match:** "No matching applications", then "No application matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No applications yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create an application to start serving traffic."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- `CardList` is a list named by its `aria-label`; each card is labelled by its header, and its checkbox is named by the same text.
- Select all items is a visible, labelled checkbox, not an icon; its state is mixed when part of the page is selected.
- Field labels and values are a `dl`, so each value is read with its label; status is a `Tag` with text, never color alone.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Delete, Preferences, Select all items, each card's checkbox and link, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, names itself by its title, labels its input by the prompt and returns focus to Delete (n) when it closes.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.

## States

- Default: applications exist; the cards show them with the property filter, multi-select with Delete (n) behind its confirmation dialog, preferences and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching applications with Clear filters.
- Loading: the first load; the heading stays, the filter, Delete and preferences are disabled, and `CardList` shows its placeholder cards (`loading`, `aria-busy`).
- Error: the applications could not load; the heading and the disabled controls stay and a danger `Alert` with Retry takes the cards' place.
- Empty: the account has no applications; `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a flush card holding a medium empty state with Create Application replaces the cards.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the same collection, rendered as a sortable table.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind Delete (n).
- `create/create-page` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `detail/resource-detail` — where a card's name leads.
- `state/first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `useCollection`, `CardList` and `Pagination` — see `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Error` · `Empty`. Code: [blocks/view/card-view.md](blocks/view/card-view.md), `get_block("view/card-view", { variant })`.

# FileBrowser (`view/file-browser`)

> The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `DataTable` whose toolbar is the whole page header.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/file-browser/file-browser.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/file-browser")`
- Components: Alert, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, Combobox, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, EmptyState, Field, FileDropzone, FileTokenGroup, IconButton, Input, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, SplitButton, Table, `TableSearch`, Toast, Tooltip, UploadProgress
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

file browser; file manager; storage browser; bucket browser; object storage; folders and files; upload files; navegador de arquivos; gerenciador de arquivos; arquivos do bucket; upload progress; move files; move objects; drag and drop upload; enviar arquivos; mover arquivos

The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A storage resource (an Object Storage bucket, a build output) opens on its files and folders.
- Users move through a folder tree and need to know where they are and how to go back up.
- Files are compared by name, size and last change, and acted on one at a time: open, download, delete.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources of one type: use `view/table-view`.
- Rows of one resource that are records, not files (database rows, variables): use `detail/dns-zone-detail`.
- Events or logs explored over time: use `view/split-view`.
- Tables and queries of a database: use `view/query-editor`.
- Picking an existing resource inside a create form: use `create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Surface — `Card`, `DataTable` (required)
- B. Storage title and search — `TableSearch` (required)
- C. Toolbar actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- D. Columns — `CollectionPreferences` (optional)
- E. Path and create — `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton` (required)
- F. Cell recipes — `Table.CellTime` (optional)
- G. Row actions — `Table.CellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem` (required)
- H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)
- I. Empty folder — `EmptyState`, `SplitButton` (required)
- J. Upload — `SplitButton` (optional)
- K. Transfer card and outcome toast — `Button` (optional)
- L. Selection and Move — `DataTable`, `DropdownMenuItem` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/file-browser.md](blocks/view/file-browser.md).

## Do

- Keep the storage name, search, path and Add to files inside the table toolbar, on the same surface as the rows.
- Sort folders before files, keep `..` first under any sort, and sort Size and Last modified on numbers, never on display strings.
- Show the path as a `Breadcrumb` and keep the `..` row while inside a folder.
- Use one Add to files `SplitButton` for every way of adding content.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and confirm it with `edit/delete-dialog`.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Keep refused files in the upload dialog with their reason, and leave them out of the upload count.
- Run every transfer in the one floating `UploadProgress` card and let the person keep working.
- End every transfer with a toast whose action fits the files: Open folder or Retry failed.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't add a `PageHeader` above the card; the toolbar is the header.
- Don't split Upload file and Add folder into two primary buttons.
- Don't give the `..` row a row menu, a size or an author.
- Don't let the table scroll the page sideways; on a phone the grid scrolls sideways inside its card, never the page.
- Don't replace the toolbar with a full-page empty state when a folder is empty; only the table area changes.
- Don't block the page with a modal progress dialog while files upload or move.
- Don't offer View deployments, Edit or Redeploy after a storage transfer; nothing is deployed.
- Don't drop a refused file silently, and don't send a file the dialog marked as refused.

## Copy

- **Storage name:** the resource name as created, e.g. "acme-assets"; never prefixed with the type.
- **Search:** placeholder names the scope, e.g. "Search in folder".
- **Add action:** "Add to files", with options "Upload file" and "Add folder".
- **Row menu:** one verb per option, e.g. "Open", "Download", "Delete"; the trigger is named "Actions for <file>".
- **Delete dialog:** title and confirm `Delete file` or `Delete folder`, consequence `The selected folder will be deleted, along with all its files.`, prompt `Type <name> to confirm.`
- **Column headers:** short fragments, e.g. "Name", "Size", "Last modified".
- **Empty folder:** title states the fact, e.g. "This folder is empty"; description is one sentence, e.g. "Upload files or create a folder to get started."
- **Upload dialog:** title `Upload files`, primary `Upload file` or `Upload 3 files`, refusal `Larger than 300 MB, the limit per file`.
- **Drop overlay:** `Drop files to upload them to <folder>`, description `Up to 300 MB per file.`
- **Move dialog:** title `Move <name>` or `Move 2 files`, field `Destination folder`, placeholder `/ (storage root)`, errors `Use letters, numbers, dots, hyphens and slashes only.`, `A destination cannot go up with "..". Type the full path.`, `The files are already in this folder. Pick another one.`
- **Toasts:** `5 files uploaded to acme-assets.` with Open folder; `1 of 5 files weren't uploaded.` with Retry failed; `2 files moved to logs/.` with Open folder.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The card sits in the layout's one `main` landmark; the storage name is the page's `h1`.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; file and folder glyphs carry `aria-hidden="true"`, so the name cell reads as the name alone.
- The `Breadcrumb` crumbs are links the keyboard reaches in order; the last crumb is the current folder.
- Folder and `..` names are buttons, so a keyboard user opens a folder or goes up with Tab and Enter; the row click is the pointer shortcut and the Open option in the row menu repeats it.
- Focus order follows reading order: search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns, path, Add to files, the rows.
- `Table.CellTime` names the author and reads the absolute time to screen readers.
- The drop overlay is `aria-hidden`: dragging is a pointer path, and Add to files with Browse files is the keyboard path to the same upload.
- `UploadProgress` is a region named File transfers with a polite status that announces each file finishing and the outcome; percentages are not announced. The toast repeats the outcome for people who collapsed the card.
- In the upload dialog each refused file's reason is the `aria-describedby` of its Remove button, and removing a file moves focus to the next one.
- The Move dialog's `Field` wires the label, description and error to the `Combobox`; the error is read when focus returns to it.

## States

- Default: the storage root with folders first, then files, and the full toolbar.
- InsideAFolder: inside a build folder the crumb gains the folder, a `..` row leads back up and files show glyph, size, editor and age.
- Uploading: a transfer is running in the floating card; one file fails once and can be retried; the upload dialog and the page drop overlay add more.
- Empty: an empty folder (`assets/` of a build); the `..` row stays and the empty state offers Add to files.
- Error: the folder could not load; the storage name, the path and Refresh stay, Add to files is disabled and a danger `Alert` with Retry takes the table's place.
- MoveObject: two files selected inside a build folder with the Move dialog open; moving runs in the card and ends in a toast.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the first-level list a storage resource is opened from.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind Delete on a file or folder.
- `detail/resource-detail` — the storage resource's own details and settings.
- `detail/dns-zone-detail` — records of a resource, not files.
- `FileTokenGroup`, `FileDropzone` and `UploadProgress` — the upload pieces; see their component docs.
- `state/async-submit` — the rule for long actions; storage transfers follow it with item actions instead of Edit and Redeploy.
- `DataTable` — the data-driven table this page wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `InsideAFolder` · `Uploading` · `Empty` · `Error` · `MoveObject`. Code: [blocks/view/file-browser.md](blocks/view/file-browser.md), `get_block("view/file-browser", { variant })`.

# Marketplace (`view/marketplace`)

> The marketplace page: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action over the integration catalog, the integrations installed into an existing application (templates live in `view/template-browser`): a F…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/marketplace/marketplace.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/marketplace")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, DataTable, DocProse, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, Field, Input, Item, KeyValueList, Link, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Switch, Table, Tabs, Tag, Toast, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

marketplace; integration catalog; integrations marketplace; install an integration; browse integrations; extensions catalog; plugin catalog; app store page; integration detail; installed integrations; configure integration; marketplace de integrações; catálogo de integrações; instalar integração; loja de extensões

The page where people find something made by Azion or a partner and add it to what they run. It lists integrations, installed into an existing application; templates, which start a new project, live in `view/template-browser`. People browse by need ("block bots", "split traffic"), compare by publisher and context, read what an integration does and what it may touch, then install it on one application and keep working while it installs. One `useCollection` call holds the search and the filters; one drawer holds the detail and the install; the install reports by toast wherever the person is.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use marketplace for installable integrations into an existing resource; templates live in template-browser.
- A catalog of installable add-ons (integrations, extensions, plugins) with a publisher, a category and an installed state per account.
- Installing means choosing a target (an application) and waiting for an asynchronous run.

## When not to use

- The catalog of templates a project starts from: use `view/template-browser`.
- Deploying a chosen template: use `create/deploy-template`.
- The resources the account already created: use `view/card-view` or `view/table-view`.
- Changing the settings of an installed integration on one application: use `edit/edit-resource` from Configure.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Featured — `Card` (required)
- C. Search and filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- D. Integration tiles — `Card`, `Button` (required)
- E. No matching integrations — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- F. Integration drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- G. Install outcome — `Alert` (required)
- H. Integration facts — `KeyValueList` (required)
- I. Overview — `DocProse` (required)
- J. Install form — `Field`, `Select` (required)
- K. Solution page — `Card`, `Select`, `Field`, `KeyValueList`, `DocProse` (optional)
- L. Configure screen — `Field`, `Select`, `Alert`, `Button` (optional)
- Install toast — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/view/marketplace.md](blocks/view/marketplace.md).

## Do

- Run the catalog on one `useCollection` call with `filtering`, `propertyFiltering` and `url: true`; derive the Status property from where each integration is installed.
- Use `Card variant="integration"` for every integration tile, with the installed state as the `installed` prop and one action in the `action` slot.
- Hide the Featured row while any filter is set.
- Keep templates out of this page: a template starts a project, so it lives in `view/template-browser`.
- Open the detail in a drawer so the catalog, the filter and the scroll stay put.
- Show the permissions before the install form, and the target as a required field.
- Treat install as an async run: `loading` on Install, a progress toast, then the outcome as a toast and an inline `Alert`, with actions that fit an integration (Configure, Open application; Edit, Reinstall).
- Keep the failure toast until the person closes it.

## Don't

- Don't install from the tile in one click; the person must pick the application and see the permissions.
- Don't point the outcome at a list of runs ("View installs", "View deployments"); the toast carries Configure or Edit and Reinstall.
- Don't use "Retry" or "Try again" for a failed install; the action is Reinstall.
- Don't show Install for an application that already runs the integration; filter it out of the `Select`.
- Don't badge every tile with more than one tag beside Installed; the publisher and the category are enough to compare.
- Don't add a Templates tab or template tiles; link to `view/template-browser` instead.
- Don't use `featured` for every integration tile; it marks the short Featured row only.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Marketplace". Description: "Find integrations that run on your applications."
- **Sections:** "Featured", "All integrations".
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` "Search integrations".
- **Tile action:** "Install" or "Configure"; its `aria-label` adds the name.
- **Drawer:** the name, "by <publisher>", "Overview", "Permissions", "Install" or "Install on another application", the field "Application" with "Select an application".
- **Validation:** "Select the application to install <name> on."
- **Progress toast:** "Installing <name> on <application>…" / "It keeps running if you close this panel."
- **Success:** toast "<name> is installed on <application>." / "It runs from the next request to the application.", actions "Configure" and "Open application"; the inline `Alert` says the same in one line.
- **Failure:** toast "<name> wasn't installed on <application>." with the reason as a full sentence, actions "Edit" and "Reinstall"; the inline `Alert` carries the reason and "Reinstall".
- **No match:** "No matching integrations", "No integration matches this search. Remove a filter to widen the results.", "Clear filters".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, each section heading an `h2`, each tile name an `h3`.
- Each tile's target is a real button named by the integration; the action button sits above it and is named with the integration, so "Install" is never ambiguous in a list.
- The Installed state is text in a `Tag`, never colour alone.
- The drawer traps focus, is named by `DrawerTitle`, closes on Escape and returns focus to what opened it; its form has an accessible name.
- The Application field is required and labelled; its error is tied to the `Select` through the `Field`, and focus stays on Install so the person can correct and resubmit.
- Toasts never take focus and are announced politely, the failure toast assertively; the failure toast stays until closed and its actions are reachable by keyboard.

## States

- Default: Featured, All integrations, the filter and the tiles; a tile opens the drawer and Install runs and lands as a success toast and Alert.
- Detail: the drawer is open on Request Signer with its details, overview, permissions and the install form.
- Installing: Install is running on storefront; the button is `loading`, the field disabled and the progress toast says it keeps running.
- Installed: Request Signer is installed on storefront; the success Alert, the Installed tag, Configure in the footer and the success toast with Configure and Open application.
- InstallError: the install on checkout failed; the danger Alert with the reason and Reinstall, and the permanent toast with Edit and Reinstall.
- NoMatch: the integration search "kubernetes" matches nothing; the Featured row hides and the empty state offers Clear filters.
- Loading: the search is disabled and six `Skeleton` integration tiles hold the grid in a band that is `aria-busy`.
- SolutionPage: Waiting Room as a page, storefront on 1.3.0 (Update available) and checkout on 1.4.0.
- Configure: Waiting Room settings on storefront, with the SaveBar after a change.

## Related

- `view/template-browser` — the one template catalog, grouped by category, with a filter and a README preview.
- `create/deploy-template` — where a template's Deploy leads.
- `state/async-submit` — the toast and inline outcome every install follows.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the field, section and toast placement of a form error.
- `Card` (`variant="integration"`) and `useCollection` — see `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Detail` · `Installing` · `Installed` · `InstallError` · `NoMatch` · `Loading` · `SolutionPage` · `Configure`. Code: [blocks/view/marketplace.md](blocks/view/marketplace.md), `get_block("view/marketplace", { variant })`.
