# QueryEditor (`view/query-editor`)

> The query editor page (the app passes the Databases breadcrumb to the layout): the Tables and Editor tabs, each pairing a resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` (288px at rest) with a working pane.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/query-editor/query-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/query-editor")`
- Components: Alert, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, CodeBlock, CodeEditor, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, `FieldError`, FileDropzone, FileTokenGroup, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Sidebar, Skeleton, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

query editor; sql editor; run query; query results; sql query page; query history; sql code editor; código sql; editor de consultas; editor sql; executar consulta; sql database; database tables; database detail; table schema; data grid; sql templates; banco de dados; banco de dados sql; tabelas do banco; create database; criar banco de dados; table rows; linhas da tabela; import csv; import data; csv import; importar csv; importar dados

The workspace of one SQL database. The user comes here to see which tables exist, read and edit a table's rows or its definition, and write and run queries against the data. Two tabs share one layout: a resizable side panel that lists things (tables, or past queries) beside a working pane that shows the one in use.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The editor is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the side panel, the rows, the editor and the results each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview). CreateDatabase is a focused create page with its own header and no rail, rendered outside it.

## When to use

- A database resource opens on its tables and an editor that runs SQL against them.
- Users switch between browsing data (rows, columns, constraints) and writing queries without leaving the resource.
- Results need both a table view and the raw JSON, with paging over large result sets.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of databases: use `view/table-view`.
- Rows of a resource that are not a SQL table (variables, records): use `detail/dns-zone-detail`.
- Editing a function or configuration as code: use `edit/function-editor`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `view/file-browser`.
- Events explored over time: use `view/split-view`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Tables panel — `Sidebar`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- C. Empty database — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- D. Table data — `ToggleGroup`, `Input`, `Button`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `DataTable` (required)
- E. Table definition — `Button`, `Card`, `DataTable`, `Tag` (optional)
- F. Query history — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- G. Editor — `Button`, `CodeEditor` (required)
- H. Results — `Input`, `ToggleGroup`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `DataTable`, `CodeBlock`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `EmptyState` (required)
- I. Templates drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody`, `Input`, `Item` (optional)
- J. Bulk row delete — `Button` (optional)
- K. Create database page — `Input`, `Button` (optional)
- L. Import data from CSV — `Drawer`, `Alert`, `DataTable`, `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/query-editor.md](blocks/view/query-editor.md).

## Do

- Keep both tabs on the same layout: side panel to list, working pane to act.
- Let the side panel resize and collapse, and keep its width when the user switches tabs.
- Make the editor read-only and disable its toolbar while a query runs, and show Run query loading.
- Show the outcome of a run in the Results band: the rows, a success `Alert` with what ran, or a danger `Alert` with why it failed.
- Offer JSON beside Table for results, so the raw shape is one click away.
- Confirm Delete table with `edit/delete-dialog`.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill` (every variant but CreateDatabase), so the panes scroll on their own instead of the page.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't open a separate page for a table or a query; they open in the pane.
- Don't run a query on every keystroke; Run query is the only trigger.
- Don't hide the tabs when the database is empty.
- Don't put a second primary action in a pane; Insert on Data and Run query on Editor are the only ones.
- Don't let the results scroll the page sideways; they scroll inside their band.
- Don't size the root with `calc(100dvh - …)`; `data-layout-fill` fits it to the layout's `main`.

## Copy

- **Tabs:** one noun each, e.g. "Tables", "Editor".
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>`, e.g. "Create Table", the same in the panel and the empty state.
- **Editor toolbar:** verb-first, e.g. "Run query", "Prettify", "Templates".
- **Editor placeholder:** one instruction, e.g. "Write your SQL query here".
- **Search:** names the scope, e.g. "Search tables", "Search queries", "Search templates".
- **Empty states:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No tables yet" with "Create your first table to store your data."; "Ready to execute" with "Execute a query to see the results here."
- **Import:** `Import data from CSV` opens `Import data into <table>`; the submit is `Insert <n> rows`; per-line errors read `Line <n>: <column> “<value>” is not <expected> (<type>).` or `<column> is empty and cannot be.`
- **Row menus:** verb and object, e.g. "Delete table", "Run query", "Delete query".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the tabs are a real tab list, so arrow keys move between Tables and Editor.
- Each side `Sidebar` is named (Tables, Query history) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The `CodeEditor` has the `aria-label` "SQL editor"; its markers are listed in its problems list as text, not by colour.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; the rows table is named `Rows of <table>` and its selection checkboxes come from `DataTable`, named per row.
- On Create Database, the Name error is the input's `aria-describedby` and focus returns to the input after a failed submit.
- `ToggleGroup`s are named ("Table view", "Result view") and each paged table names its own pagination.
- The templates drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape.
- In the import drawer each mapping `Select` is named `Table column for <CSV column>`, the mapping and the per-line errors are named lists, and the ready count is a polite live region, so changing a mapping announces the new count.

## States

- Tables: the Tables tab with the tables listed in the side panel and the selected table's Data view in the pane.
- Schema: the Definition view of customers, with the Columns heading, Add column and a card of column name, type and constraints.
- NoTables: a database with no tables; the side panel says so and the pane shows the Create Table empty state.
- Query: the Editor tab after a query ran, with the history in the side panel, the statement in the editor and its rows in Results.
- Templates: the Editor tab before anything ran, with Results ready to execute and the SQL quick templates drawer open over it.
- Loading: the tables list and the selected table's rows are loading; `Skeleton` lines hold the side panel and the rows table shows its loading state.
- TableData: the events table, 137 rows paged 25 at a time, with two rows selected and Delete 2 rows in the toolbar.
- ImportCsv: the empty subscribers table with the import drawer open on a seven-row file: `plan_name` still on Skip (Insert asks to map `plan`), `referrer` skipped, three lines with errors (a non-boolean, an empty required email, a date that does not parse).
- CreateDatabase: the create database page with its Name and Active fields; try `acme-store` for the name conflict and a name starting with `offline` for the failed request.
- Error: the selected table's rows did not load; the Data view shows a danger `Alert` that names the table and offers Retry.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the database list this workspace is opened from.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind Delete table.
- `edit/function-editor` — editing code that is not a query.
- `edit/schema-editor` — the Create Table, Add column, Add row, Alter column and Truncate table drawers and dialogs behind this page's buttons.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the rule the Create Database name conflict follows.
- `detail/dns-zone-detail` — records of a resource without SQL.
- `DataTable` — the definition and results tables; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

`Tables` (primary) · `Schema` · `NoTables` · `Query` · `Templates` · `Loading` · `Error` · `TableData` · `ImportCsv` · `CreateDatabase`. Code: [blocks/view/query-editor.md](blocks/view/query-editor.md), `get_block("view/query-editor", { variant })`.

# RuleList (`view/rule-list`)

> An ordered list of rules grouped by phase, the Rules tab of an application or a firewall.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/rule-list/rule-list.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/rule-list")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Combobox, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, Field, `FieldDescription`, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Switch, Tag, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

rules list; rules engine list; reorder rules; rule order; drag and drop reorder; firewall rules; request and response phases; review changes; enable disable rule; lista de regras; ordem das regras; reordenar regras; regras do firewall; fases de requisição e resposta; lista de reglas; reordenar reglas

An ordered list of rules grouped by phase: the Rules tab of an application (Request and Response phases) or a firewall (Request only). Order is behavior here, so the list is built to change the order safely: drag, keys, a typed position or Move up and Move down move a rule, every move is announced, and nothing runs in the new order until the user reviews the changes and saves.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered program of rules and the user needs to see it, reorder it and turn rules on or off: application rules engine, firewall rules, routing rules.
- Rules split into phases that never interleave (request and response), each with its own order.
- Changes to the order must be reviewed before they apply to live traffic.

## When not to use

- Records whose order does not matter: use `view/table-view`.
- Writing or editing one rule's criteria and behaviors: use `edit/rule-builder`, which this list opens from Add Rule and from a rule's name.
- Fewer than two rules that can move: show the list without the Order controls.

## Building blocks

- A. Header — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Search — `Input`, `Alert` (required)
- C. Phases — `Card`, `Accordion` (required)
- D. Rules table — `DataTable`, `Tag`, `Field`, `Switch` (required)
- E. Order controls — `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- F. Save bar and review — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert` (required)
- G. States — `EmptyState`, `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/rule-list.md](blocks/view/rule-list.md).

## Do

- Keep phases separate: a rule moves only within its phase, and drag ignores drops on another phase.
- Offer every way to move: drag for a pointer, arrow keys, Home and End on the grip, a typed position for long jumps, and Move up and Move down for touch and switch access.
- Say why a control is disabled, in its accessible name and its tooltip.
- Collect changes and apply them only after Review changes and Save; the review lists every rule whose position changes, not only the one the user dragged.
- Let a rule be turned off in place; an inactive rule keeps its position and is skipped at runtime.
- Follow `skills/webkit-tables` for the table, `skills/webkit-form` for the save bar and `skills/webkit-errors` for the failed save.

## Don't

- Don't save on every drop; one wrong drag would reorder live traffic.
- Don't allow reordering while a search hides rows; positions would be ambiguous.
- Don't let anything move above a locked default rule, or turn it off.
- Don't put the review in a toast or a popover; it is a decision with a list to read.
- Don't offer drag as the only way to reorder.

## Copy

- **Phase triggers:** "Request phase", "Response phase", with "5 rules" or "2 of 5" beside.
- **Order control names:** "Reorder Docs rewrite, position 5 of 5" (the table's grip, described by its drag-or-arrow hint), "Position of Docs rewrite in the Request phase. Type a number from 2 to 5 to move it.", "Move Docs rewrite up", and when disabled "Move Default rule down. The default rule runs first and stays first."
- **Disabled reasons:** "The default rule runs first and stays first.", "Clear the search to change the order rules run in.", "There is no other rule in this phase to move it past."
- **Announcements:** "Docs rewrite moved to position 3 of 5 in the Request phase.", "Changes discarded. The rules are back in their saved order."
- **Save bar:** "3 changes to the rules, not saved yet." with Discard and Review changes.
- **Review lines:** "<Rule> moves from position 5 to 3.", "<Rule> is turned on."
- **Failure:** "The new order wasn't saved. The rules still run in the saved order; save again to apply it."
- **Success toast:** "Rule order saved." with "The application runs its rules in the new order."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each phase is a disclosure: the trigger is a button inside an `h2` with `aria-expanded`, and the panel is a region named by it.
- Every Order control has a name that includes the rule and the phase; disabled controls include the reason.
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the grip, the position field, Move up, Move down, the rule link and its switch, in that order; the grip moves the rule with Up, Down, Home and End and Escape cancels a drag. Focus follows the moved rule.
- Moves and discards are announced once in a polite `role="status"` region that exists from the first render.
- The `Switch` is named "Run <rule>"; its visible Active or Inactive text is hidden from the accessibility tree so the state is read once, from `aria-checked`.
- The review dialog traps focus, returns it to Review changes on close, and is not dismissible while saving; the failure `Alert` is read when it appears.
- Drop targets show a 2 px accent line and the dragged row fades; transitions respect reduced motion.

## States

- Application: Request and Response phases, a locked Default rule first in Request, one inactive rule per phase.
- Firewall: one Request phase, every rule movable.
- ReviewChanges: two moves and one status change, the save bar and the review dialog open.
- SaveError: the review dialog open with the failure `Alert` and Save again.
- Searching: "cache" typed, reordering off with its `Alert`, phases reading "n of total".
- Empty: a firewall with no rules, the Request phase showing its `EmptyState`.
- Loading: skeleton rows in each phase, the search and Add Rule disabled.
- LoadError: the rules did not load; a danger `Alert` with Retry replaces the phases.
- EditRule: the list composed with `edit/rule-builder`. A rule's name is a button ("Edit Docs rewrite") that opens the builder `Drawer` as Edit Rule, seeded with the rule and its phase locked; Add Rule in the header or in an empty phase opens it as Add Rule in that phase. Saving an edit updates the row and says so in a toast; a new rule lands last in its phase with a toast that offers Edit. Neither is an order change, so the `SaveBar` still counts only moves and switches. Product pages (an application's or a firewall's Rules tab) compose the two the same way.

## Related

- `edit/rule-builder` — the drawer that adds or edits one rule.
- `view/table-view` — lists whose order does not matter.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the failed-save `Alert` pattern the review dialog follows.
- `view/waf-tuning` — the WAF tuning list a firewall's WAF rule links to.

## Variants

`Application` (primary) · `Firewall` · `ReviewChanges` · `SaveError` · `Searching` · `Empty` · `Loading` · `LoadError` · `EditRule`. Code: [blocks/view/rule-list.md](blocks/view/rule-list.md), `get_block("view/rule-list", { variant })`.

# SplitView (`view/split-view`)

> The events explorer (the app marks its Events navigation entry active): the controls row (`FilterMenu`, event search, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied `FilterMenu.ChipGroup`, and the explorer.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/split-view/split-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/split-view")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Button, Chart, Checkbox, Chip, CodeBlock, CopyButton, DataTable, DateRangePicker, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, FilterMenu, IconButton, Input, Item, `PanelHeader`, Popover, PropertyFilter, Resizable, Sidebar, Skeleton, Tabs, Tag, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

real-time events; events visualizer; event explorer; log explorer; logs viewer; request logs; events search; eventos em tempo real; visualizador de eventos; explorador de logs; split view; master detail; list and detail panes; visão dividida; query language; events query; saved searches; saved queries; query history; date range; time range picker; investigation tabs; event document; consulta de eventos; buscas salvas; intervalo de datas

The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The explorer is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the fields panel, the log and the event document each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Events or logs explored over time, where the volume chart and the rows must agree on one period and one set of filters.
- Users pivot on field values (level, source, status, host) to find a pattern, then read one event's full document.
- The record has more fields than a table row can hold, so the full document opens beside the list instead of in a details page.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources the user creates and manages: use `view/table-view`.
- The log of one deployment or build run: use `detail/deployment-logs`.
- Metrics and charts without a row-level log: use `dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `view/file-browser`.
- Querying a database with SQL: use `view/query-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Filter — `FilterMenu` (required)
- B. Search and toolbar — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Applied filters — `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` (optional)
- D. Fields panel — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `Field`, `Checkbox`, `Popover`, `Item`, `Accordion`, `Tag` (optional)
- E. Log — `Chart`, `Skeleton`, `DataTable`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Event document — `Resizable`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `CodeBlock` (required)
- G. Narrow document — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `Tag`, `CodeBlock` (required)
- H. Query bar — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- I. Saved and recent queries — `Popover`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `Item`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- J. Investigation tabs — `IconButton`, `Input`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- K. Document tools — `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/split-view.md](blocks/view/split-view.md).

## Do

- Drive the summary, the chart and the table from one filtered set, so every number agrees.
- Let a click or drag on the chart set the period, and show the period as a filter the user can clear.
- Keep the row selected while its document is open, and switch between pane and drawer by the explorer's width, not the viewport's.
- Let `FilterMenu` count the applied fields on its trigger and `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` show each one in field order.
- Pick the empty message that matches why the log is empty.
- In query mode, keep the applied query text as the user typed it, and save and list that text.
- Keep each investigation tab self-contained: its own filters, search and period.
- Let the document act on the log (Filter by, Exclude), so a pivot is one click from the value.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill`, so the panes scroll on their own instead of the page.

## Don't

- Don't navigate away to read one event; the document opens beside the log.
- Don't add a second filter surface (a row of `Select`s, a filter bar in the fields panel) beside the Filter menu.
- Don't hide the controls row or the summary when the log is empty.
- Don't encode level by colour alone; the chart has a card with level names and counts, and the table shows level as text.
- Don't let a wide log scroll the page sideways.
- Don't size the root with `calc(100dvh - …)`; `data-layout-fill` fits it to the layout's `main`.
- Don't offer the query bar and the Filter menu at once; pick the one that fits the users.
- Don't guess the meaning of a query that mixes AND and OR; say so and let the user fix it.
- Don't let investigation tabs grow without a limit, and never close the last one.

## Copy

- **Search:** placeholder names what is searched, e.g. "Search events, hosts, paths or addresses"; `aria-label` "Search events".
- **Summary labels:** short nouns, e.g. "Events", "Errors", "Avg request time".
- **Chart hint:** one instruction, e.g. "Drag across the chart, or hold Shift with the arrow keys and press Enter, to filter the log to a span."
- **Empty log:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No events in this window" with "Widen the period or clear a filter to see more of the log."
- **Fields panel:** controls name the panel, e.g. "Hide the fields panel", "Show the fields panel".
- **Document:** drawer title "Event"; close button "Close the event document".
- **Query bar:** `aria-label` "Query events"; placeholder with one real example; the range "Events time range".
- **Saved queries:** "Name the current query", Save, "Delete <name>"; empty "No saved queries yet. Name the current query to keep it."
- **Tabs:** "New investigation", "Actions for <name>", Rename, Duplicate, "Close investigation"; limit "Up to 5 investigations stay open. Close one to start another."
- **Document tools:** "Search in this event", "Filter by <field> <value>", "Exclude <field> <value>", "Copy the fields shown as JSON"; no match "No field matches “<text>”."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The explorer sits in the layout's one `main` landmark; each `Sidebar` is named (Fields, Event document) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The chart is `Chart`'s one tab stop with an `aria-label` that carries the summary (busiest bucket) and the instruction; arrow keys move between buckets, Shift extends a span, Enter commits it, and the tooltip follows keyboard focus as it follows the pointer.
- The Errors value carries an `aria-label` with its share of all events.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; decorative glyphs are `aria-hidden="true"`. The row detail button names its event and carries `aria-expanded`.
- Value options in the fields-panel popovers are buttons with `aria-pressed`, so applied values are announced; the Filter menu's own rows come from `FilterMenu`.
- The document drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape; motion is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Query: the bar is a `combobox` whose invalid state sets `aria-invalid` and points `aria-describedby` at the reason; the mixed AND / OR message and the saved-query confirmations are `role="status"`.
- Sessions: the tabs follow the `Tabs` keyboard map (arrows, Home, End); F2 renames and Delete closes the focused tab, and the same actions sit in a named menu for pointer and screen-reader users; focus returns to the tab after rename or close.
- EventDocument: Filter by and Exclude are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) named with the field and value; the match count of the document search is announced in a `role="status"`.

## States

- Default: live traffic with the summary, the chart and the log filled, and no filters applied; while Refresh runs the summary values and the chart show `Skeleton`s and the table its loading rows.
- Loading: the first load; `Skeleton`s hold the summary values and the chart band and the table shows its loading rows.
- Filtered: errors from the Security and Access Control sources; the Filter button counts three fields and each shows as a `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` chip.
- Empty: a workspace with no traffic yet; the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows No events yet.
- Error: the event request failed; the fields panel stays and the log pane shows a danger `Alert` that says the events did not load, with Retry, which reruns the request like Refresh.
- Query: `level = Error AND host = api.example.com` over the last 24 hours, with two saved and two recent queries.
- Sessions: three investigation tabs, API errors active.
- EventDocument: an error event's document open, with Host is not legacy.example.com applied.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the same controls row over a resource list.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — logs of one deployment run.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the metrics view for the same traffic.
- `shell/console` — the layout this explorer renders in.
- `DataTable` — the log table; see `skills/webkit-tables`, `skills/webkit-data-viz` and `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Filtered` · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Error` · `Query` · `Sessions` · `EventDocument`. Code: [blocks/view/split-view.md](blocks/view/split-view.md), `get_block("view/split-view", { variant })`.

# TableView (`view/table-view`)

> The canonical first-level list page: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description, the outlined medium Documentation action and a primary large Create Resource, the page's only large contr…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/table-view/table-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/table-view")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, EmptyState, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, PropertyFilter, StatusIndicator, Table, Tag, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `utils/csv`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

list; list page; resource list; module list; index page; resources index; list with filters; workloads list; listagem; lista de recursos; página de listagem; resource table; data table; table; sortable table; paginated table; table with copy id; listing table; tabela de listagem; tabela; tabela de recursos; tabela paginada; list controls; filter bar; search and filter; table toolbar; filter chips; column visibility; filtros; barra de filtros; busca e filtro; table view; index table; visualização em tabela; property filter; filter tokens; collection preferences; table preferences; saved preferences; filters in the url; shareable filters; use collection; filtro por propriedade; preferências da tabela; filtros na url; deployments list; deployment history; lista de deploys; histórico de deploys

The first-level index of one resource type, in rows. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource among many, narrow the list by its attributes, compare records column by column, and act on one: open it, deploy it, clone it, delete it, or create a new one. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row and the table it narrows.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources of one type that has no dedicated block (applications, workloads, domains).
- Users compare many records by the same few attributes (status, domain, owner, last change) and need to sort, filter and page through them.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and columns must survive the next visit.
- The list must survive its last row being deleted: the page keeps its heading and controls and the table gives way to an empty state.

## When not to use

- Resources people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column: use `view/card-view`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use the table inside `detail/resource-detail` or `detail/dns-zone-detail`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- People on the account: use `account/users`. Teams and their permissions: use `account/team-permissions`. API tokens: use `account/personal-tokens`. The audit log: use `account/activity-history`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `view/file-browser`.
- Events or logs explored over time with a chart and a document pane: use `view/split-view`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `state/first-use`, which teaches the module before any list exists.
- Choosing one existing resource inside a form: use `create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Listing actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- D. Table preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- E. Resource table — `Card`, `DataTable` (required)
- F. Cell presets — `Table.CellLink`, `Table.CellId`, `Table.CellStatus`, `Table.CellTime` (optional)
- G. Row actions — `Table.CellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem` (required)
- H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)
- I. No matching resources — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- J. Failed and empty listing — `Alert`, `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/table-view.md](blocks/view/table-view.md).

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call and bind its props with `v-bind`; let it own the filter, sort, page and preferences.
- Keep the controls row and the table in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens, the sort and the page live in the query string and a filtered list can be shared or reloaded.
- Give the list a `storageKey` of its own and lock the column that names the row.
- Keep `CollectionPreferences` the last control of the row and every control on it medium.
- Branch on `status`: `loading` shows the table's skeleton rows, `error` swaps the table for a danger `Alert` with Retry, `empty` swaps it for the empty listing, `no-match` fills the table's `#empty` slot with Clear filters.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and always behind the confirmation dialog.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover, a chip row or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`; one control narrows the list.
- Don't filter, sort or page rows in a `computed` outside the collection, or pass `:data`, `paginated` and `v-model:globalFilter` by hand beside `tableProps`.
- Don't build a columns popover of `Switch`es; column visibility and order belong to `CollectionPreferences`.
- Don't wrap a bordered table in a padded card, or let the page scroll sideways for a wide table.
- Don't add a second create button to the controls row.
- Don't show the first-use empty state when filters hide every row, or Clear filters when the account has none.
- Don't replace the heading and controls with a full-page empty state when the rows run out; only the table area changes.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Resources". Description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "View and manage your resources."
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Resource"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state repeats the same label.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter resources".
- **Properties:** the column header's words, e.g. "Name", "Author", "Status", "Domain".
- **Icon buttons:** a verb or noun in sentence case, e.g. "Refresh", "Download CSV", "Row actions". Preferences title: "Table preferences".
- **Column headers:** one or two words without punctuation, e.g. "Name", "ID", "Domains", "Status", "Last modified".
- **No match:** "No matching resources", then "No resource matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No resources yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create a resource to start serving traffic on your domains."
- **Copy buttons:** name what they copy, e.g. "Copy resource ID", "Copy domain name".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder; each token's remove button names the token, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Refresh, Download CSV, Preferences, table, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, is named by its title and labels its input by the prompt.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.
- Sorting is announced by the table header; the row menu is reachable by keyboard and closes back to its trigger.
- Links that open a new tab add "(opens in a new tab)" in visually hidden text; the `+N` popover names its count and the copy buttons name what they copy.

## States

- Default: resources exist; the table shows them with the property filter, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching resources with Clear filters.
- Empty: every resource was deleted on an account that is not new; `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a flush card with Create Resource and Documentation replaces the table.
- Loading: the first load; the heading stays, the filter, Download CSV and preferences are disabled, Refresh spins and the table shows its skeleton rows.
- Error: the resources could not load; the heading and the disabled controls stay, and a danger `Alert` with Retry takes the table's place (`status` is `error` when a server-mode `fetch` rejects).
- Deployments: the deployments list with Version (Current tag), Status with a spinner while Building and the run's duration, the project link, the environment tag and the author with the time; a row click opens the deployment, the row menu holds View details, Redeploy and Promote to production, and Refresh, no match and empty behave as in Default and Empty.

## Related

- `view/card-view` — the same collection, rendered as selectable cards.
- `create/create-page` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `create/create-drawer` — create without leaving the list when the form is three fields or fewer.
- `detail/resource-detail` — where a row name leads; its Deployments tab renders the Deployments table without the page heading.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `state/first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `DataTable` and `useCollection` — the table this page wraps and the state behind it; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

template browser; template gallery; template catalog; start from a template; browse templates; templates by framework; template preview; template readme; deploy a template; starter templates; galeria de templates; catálogo de templates; navegar templates; começar a partir de um template; pré-visualizar template; template marketplace; search templates; templates catalog; project templates; pick a template

The catalog of templates a person starts a project from. ## When to use

# WafTuning (`view/waf-tuning`)

> The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set: the requests it matched, grouped by rule, so the user can allow the legitimate ones.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/view/waf-tuning/waf-tuning.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("view/waf-tuning")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, Table, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

waf tuning; web application firewall; allow rules; false positives; attacks table; matched requests; waf allowed rules; threshold; ajuste do waf; falsos positivos; permitir regras; ajuste de waf; falsos positivos waf

The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set. It shows the requests the rule set matched, grouped by the rule that matched them, with enough context (hits, top addresses, countries and paths) for the user to tell an attack from a false positive, and turns the legitimate ones into allowed rules with a recorded reason.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A security rule set blocks or flags traffic, and users need to review what it caught and allow what is legitimate.
- Each finding is a rule that matched many requests, summarized by its sources and targets.
- Allowing changes what the rule set lets through, so it needs a reason that stays with the change.

## When not to use

- A plain list of records to browse and act on one at a time: use `view/table-view`.
- Charts of attack volume over time: use `dashboard/security-dashboard`.
- Editing the allowed rules once created: an `edit-resource` form on the Allowed Rules tab.

## Building blocks

- A. Header — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Threshold settings — `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Matches table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `Table.CellTags`, `EmptyState`, `Alert` (required)
- D. Allow dialog — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `Button` (required)
- E. Outcome — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/view/waf-tuning.md](blocks/view/waf-tuning.md).

## Do

- Sort by hits so the noisiest rules come first, and keep the sort when settings change.
- Show sources and targets as samples with a count of the rest, not as full lists.
- Say how many allowed rules the action creates before the user confirms it.
- Require a reason, and validate it only after the user tries to allow.
- Keep the selection when settings change, so the user can narrow the list and still act on what they checked.

## Don't

- Don't allow from a single click on a row; allowing changes what the rule set blocks.
- Don't hide the threshold settings in a menu; they decide what the list shows.
- Don't put a free-text reason in a toast or a confirm without a field.
- Don't use real or customer addresses in examples; use documentation ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24).

## Copy

- **Header action:** "Allow selected" (disabled), then "Allow 2 selected".
- **No match:** "No matching rules", "No rule, IP address, country or path matches “cache”.", "Clear search".
- **Settings labels:** "Time range", "Minimum hits".
- **Empty after threshold:** "No rule reaches the minimum", "No rule matched 100 times or more in the last 24 hours. Lower the minimum hits or widen the time range."
- **First use:** "No matches yet", "This rule set has not matched any request. Matches appear here as traffic arrives."
- **Dialog:** title "Allow 2 rules", submit "Allow rules", reason error "Enter why these requests are legitimate."
- **Outcome:** "6 allowed rules created." and "The allowed rules weren't created. Nothing changed in the rule set; try again."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Time range and Minimum hits have visible labels; the search and Refresh have accessible names.
- The selection checkboxes and sort buttons come from `DataTable` and are named per row and column.
- The dialog is a labelled `form`: its title names it, the reason is a required `Field` whose error is tied by `aria-describedby`, and Enter in a text field does not submit by accident because the reason is a `Textarea`.
- The failure `Alert` is read when it appears; focus stays in the dialog and returns to the allow action on close.
- Code-font values (rule ids, addresses, paths) are plain text; nothing depends on color.

## States

- Default: five rules matched in the last 24 hours, minimum 100 hits.
- Allow: two rules checked and the dialog open.
- AllowError: the dialog with the failure `Alert` and Try again.
- Empty: no match yet, no settings.
- Loading: settings disabled, skeleton rows.
- LoadError: the matched requests did not load; a danger `Alert` with Retry takes the table's place and Export to CSV is disabled.

## Related

- `view/rule-list` — the firewall's rules, where a WAF rule set is applied.
- `view/table-view` — the list recipe this table follows.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the failure pattern in the dialog.
- `dashboard/security-dashboard` — attack volume over time.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Allow` · `AllowError` · `Empty` · `LoadError` · `Loading`. Code: [blocks/view/waf-tuning.md](blocks/view/waf-tuning.md), `get_block("view/waf-tuning", { variant })`.

<!-- components/button.md -->

# Button

> The labelled control that triggers an action. `variant` ranks the action in its view (one `primary`, the rest `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `danger` for a destructive one, or `link` for an action that reads as a link), `size` fits it to its context, and `loading` and `disabled` cover the states in between. With `href` it renders an anchor that looks the same, so a call to action that navigates needs no second component.

- Import: `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Button `variant="link"` when the text runs an action (no navigation) but should read like a link.
- Trigger an action that needs a visible text label: in a form, dialog footer, toolbar or page header.
- Mark the main action of a view with `variant="primary"` and the lesser ones with `secondary`, `outline` or `ghost`.
- Submit or reset a form with `type="submit"` / `type="reset"`.
- A call to action that navigates: set `href` (and `target`) and it renders as an anchor with the same look.
- An action that reads as a link — inline in a table cell or a summary (`Connect Git Repository`, `3 rules`, `Resources pending deletion`) — and opens a drawer, a picker or a flow instead of a URL: `variant="link"`. It is still a `<button>`, so keyboard and screen readers get an action.

## Do

- Keep one `variant="primary"` per view or region; use `danger` only for destructive actions.
- variant="link"` has no box: no height, padding or surface, `text-body-sm` in the link colour, underlined on hover. `size` does not apply to it; place it where body text sits (a cell, a summary line, under a section).
- Set `loading` while the action resolves: it swaps the icon for a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and suppresses `click`, so the handler needs no extra guard.
- Use `iconPosition="leading"` for a glyph that names the action and `"trailing"` for one that points where it goes; add `animated` only on marketing CTAs with a trailing icon.
- Put brand or product marks in the `leading` slot; `icon` takes an Azion icon class.
- label` is required and is the accessible name; never pass an empty string to get an icon-only control.

## Don’t

- The control is icon-only → use `icon-button`.
- One default action with related alternatives in an attached menu → use `split-button`.
- A standalone navigation link with a trailing icon and a ghost hover → use `link`.
- Link-looking text that goes to a URL in a table cell → `Table.CellLink`; a `variant="link"` Button is for an action with no destination.
- A hand-written `<button class="text-(--text-link) …">` → use `variant="link"`.
- The single AI or highlight entry point that must stand out from every other action → use `highlight-button`.

## Related

- `icon-button` — icon-only counterpart with the same sizes and a required `ariaLabel`; its `ghost` variant matches this one.
- `split-button` — joins a Button to a chevron menu of related actions.
- `highlight-button` — the same prop surface without `variant`, drawn with the brand gradient and a rotating glow rim.
- `link` — a text link that navigates to a page, resource or URL.
- `toggle-group` — a group of mutually exclusive options, not a single action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label text, the fallback of the default slot (pass one or the other). Use `IconButton` for icon-only controls. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outline' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger' \| 'link'` | `'primary'` | false | Visual variant. `link` draws an inline text action in the link colour, with no box. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows loading state and disables activation. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the icon drawn beside the label. |
| `iconPosition` | `'leading' \| 'trailing'` | `'leading'` | false | Which side of the label the icon sits on. `leading` is a glyph that names the action; `trailing` is a glyph that points at where it goes. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Nudges a trailing icon along its axis on hover. Off by default; marketing CTAs opt in. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, renders as a link (`<a>`). |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when `href` is set. |
| `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'` | `'button'` | false | Native button type. `submit` lets the control submit its form; `disabled` and `loading` still block it. Ignored when `href` is set. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | — |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The visible label, as shadcn and Radix take children; falls back to `label`. Plain text keeps the button's typography. |
| `leading` | — | A mark drawn before the label, ahead of a leading `icon`. It stays first when `iconPosition="trailing"`, so a brand mark and a trailing chevron can share one control. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; `data-loading` the `loading` prop; `data-inert` is set while disabled or loading
- `data-size` mirrors `size`; every variant, size and inert utility switches on these `data-*` attributes in one flat class (no class presets in script)
- `data-variant` mirrors `variant`; with `variant="link"` the button has no box (no height, padding, surface or state layer), the label is `text-body-sm` in `var(--text-link)` turning `var(--text-link-hover)` and underlined on hover, and `size` is ignored; disabled and loading drop it to `var(--text-disabled)`; under forced colors it reads as `LinkText` with no border.
- With `type="submit"`, `disabled` (native) and `loading` (the click is cancelled) both stop the form from submitting, including implicit submission on `Enter`
- Touch: the drawn size is unchanged (28/32/40 px, all above the 24 px minimum); on a coarse pointer an invisible `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to at least 44 × 44 px around the button.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Forced colors: the filled variants (primary, secondary, danger) have no border of their own, so under `forced-colors: active` every button draws a 1px `ButtonBorder` edge (`GrayText` when disabled); outside forced colors nothing changes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Motion: the hover nudge of an `icon-position="right"` arrow moves toward the end (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: the label (and an `aria-label` when given) are consumer copy.

## Responsive

- The button never wraps its label (`whitespace-nowrap`); keep labels short, or let the layout stack buttons on narrow screens.
- Touch: drawn heights are 28 / 32 / 40 px; a `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to 44 px on a coarse pointer.
- No hover-only affordance: every state reads without hover.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <Button
    variant="primary"
    size="large"
    label="Button"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/button.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/button.md).

<!-- components/button-group.md -->

# Button Group

> A toolbar of icon actions that belong to one surface (a code panel, a table header, a preview), after Cloudscape's button group. Each item is an icon button that names itself in a tooltip: a plain action, an on / off toggle, or a menu of options. Items past `visibleCount` collapse into one More actions menu. The toolbar is one tab stop with roving focus, so a row of six icons costs the keyboard user one Tab, not six.

- Import: `import ButtonGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/button-group'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ButtonGroup for a toolbar of icon actions on one surface (code panel, table header); one default action with alternatives is a SplitButton.
- A row of icon actions on one surface: Copy, Format, Wrap lines, Download above a code editor.
- Compact actions in a panel header where labels would not fit, each explained by its tooltip.
- A mix of actions and on / off view toggles (wrap lines, show whitespace) that sit together.
- More actions than the space allows: keep the frequent ones visible and move the rest into the overflow menu with `visibleCount`.

## Do

- Give the toolbar an `aria-label` that names the surface ("Editor actions"), and every item a `label` that says what it does ("Copy code", not "Copy"). Write the kebab attribute (`aria-label`, `:aria-label` when the name changes, `aria-labelledby` when a visible heading already names the surface), never the camelCase `ariaLabel` attribute.
- The `ariaLabel` prop is optional in the types on purpose: vue-tsc does not camelize `aria-*` attributes onto props, so a required `ariaLabel` made the obvious `aria-label="…"` fail to type-check in a fresh create-vue app. The lint rule `webkit/require-accessible-name` keeps the name required instead: it flags a `ButtonGroup` with neither `aria-label` nor `aria-labelledby`.
- Keep the most used actions first; `visibleCount` moves the tail into More actions, never the head.
- Use a toggle only for a state the user can see change (wrapped lines); flip `pressed` in your `@toggle` handler — the component never stores it.
- Set `loading` on an action while its request runs instead of disabling the whole group.
- Use `variant="ghost"` on a surface that already has a border (a panel header) and `outline` on the canvas.
- Do not mix text buttons into the group; a text action belongs beside it as its own `Button`.

## Don’t

- A choice of exactly one option among several (view mode, period) → use `toggle-group`.
- One primary action with related alternatives → use `split-button`.
- A single icon action → use `icon-button` (with a `tooltip`).
- Page or form actions with text labels (Save, Cancel, Create) → use `button`s laid out by the page.
- A long list of commands or navigation → use `dropdown-menu`.

## Related

- `icon-button` — every item renders one; ButtonGroup adds the toolbar role, roving focus and overflow.
- `toggle-group` — a radiogroup of mutually exclusive options; ButtonGroup toggles are independent (`aria-pressed`).
- `split-button` — one main action plus a menu, with a visible text label.
- `dropdown-menu` — the menu behind menu items and the More actions overflow.
- `tooltip` — the visible name of each icon.
- `code-editor` — the usual host of an editor toolbar (`toolbar` slot).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `ButtonGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | Actions, toggles and menus, in reading order. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the toolbar, written as the `aria-label` attribute. Empty only when `aria-labelledby` names the toolbar; then no `aria-label` renders. |
| `variant` | `'ghost' \| 'outline'` | `'ghost'` | false | Visual variant of every button. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token of every button. |
| `visibleCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Items shown as buttons; the rest go into the More actions menu. Unset shows every item. |
| `overflowLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the overflow button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`More actions`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, id: string)` | An action or a menu option was chosen (from the bar or the overflow). |
| `toggle` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, detail: { id: string; pressed: boolean })` | A toggle was activated; `pressed` is the new state to store. |

## Sub-components

_none_ — items are data (`items`), because every item has the same anatomy (icon, label, state) and the overflow menu must re-render the same items as menu options.

## States

- Visual states per item: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `pressed` (toggle, `data-pressed`, `--bg-selected`), `loading` (action), `disabled`.
- Root data attributes: `data-variant`, `data-size`; each item `data-slot="button-group-item"` with `data-id="<id>"`.
- Overflow: a pressed toggle shows a check and a hidden "On" in the More actions menu; a menu item becomes a labelled group of its options.

## Accessibility

- `role="toolbar"` with `aria-orientation="horizontal"` and a mandatory accessible name: `aria-label` (static or bound) or `aria-labelledby`. `webkit/require-accessible-name` flags a ButtonGroup with neither, and an empty name renders no `aria-label` attribute.
- Keyboard map: one tab stop (the last focused item, else the first enabled); `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move and wrap (swapped under `dir="rtl"` through `logicalArrowKey`); `Home` / `End` jump to the ends; `Enter` / `Space` activate; on a menu item `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown` open the menu, `Escape` closes it and returns focus to its button.
- Each icon button's accessible name is its `label`; the tooltip shows the same text on hover and focus.
- Toggles expose `aria-pressed`; the pressed fill is backed by an outline in forced colors.
- Disabled items leave the roving order; loading actions keep focus and announce through the button's busy state.
- Contrast: icon buttons follow `IconButton` (≥ 3:1 for the glyph, ≥ 4.5:1 for focus ring and labels).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the row follows the inline direction; the overflow button is always last (inline end).
- Icons: not mirrored (the consumer passes a directional icon when meaning depends on direction).
- Keyboard: arrows follow the visual order under `dir="rtl"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source | Override prop   |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | --------------- |
| `buttonGroup.moreActions` | `More actions` | `overflowLabel` |
| `buttonGroup.pressed`     | `On`           | —               |

- Item labels are consumer copy.

## Responsive

- The row wraps (`flex-wrap`) instead of overflowing a narrow container; use `visibleCount` to keep one line on small screens.
- Touch: targets follow `IconButton` sizes; prefer `size="large"` on touch-first surfaces.
- No hover-only affordance: every label is the accessible name and is reachable by focus.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ButtonGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/button-group'
  import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

  const wrap = ref(false)
  const last = ref('')

  const items = [
    { id: 'copy', label: 'Copy code', icon: 'ai ai-copy' },
    { id: 'format', label: 'Format document', icon: 'ai ai-align-left' },
    { id: 'wrap', type: 'toggle', label: 'Wrap lines', icon: 'ai ai-move-horizontal' },
    {
      id: 'download',
      type: 'menu',
      label: 'Download',
      icon: 'ai ai-download',
      options: [
        { id: 'download-js', label: 'Download as .js' },
        { id: 'download-zip', label: 'Download as .zip' }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const resolved = computed(() =>
    items.map((item) => (item.type === 'toggle' ? { ...item, pressed: wrap.value } : item))
  )

  const onToggle = (event, { id, pressed }) => {
    if (id === 'wrap') wrap.value = pressed
    last.value = `${id}: ${pressed ? 'on' : 'off'}`
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <ButtonGroup
      :items="resolved"
      aria-label="Editor actions"
      @click="(_event, id) => (last = id)"
      @toggle="onToggle"
    />
    <p
      class="m-0 text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      aria-live="polite"
    >
      Last action: {{ last || 'none' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/button-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/button-group.md).

<!-- components/copy-button.md -->

# Copy Button

> Icon-only control that copies a string to the clipboard and briefly confirms success. Composes `IconButton` for visuals and interaction tokens, and `Tooltip` for its name: an icon-only button is silent to a pointer user until hovered, so the glyph is always labelled on hover/focus. The tooltip text is the same string as the accessible name — `ariaLabel` while idle, `copiedLabel` for the two seconds after a write — so the confirmation is seen as well as announced. It is suppressed with `disabled`.

- Import: `import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CopyButton next to any value (API key, ID, snippet) to copy it; to copy a ready-made agent prompt without showing it use CopyPromptButton.
- Next to a value the user will paste elsewhere: an ID, a domain, a token, a CLI command.
- Inside key/value rows, terminal mocks and code samples that need a one-click copy.

## Do

- Pass the exact text in `value`; an empty `value` makes the click a no-op.
- Localize `ariaLabel` and `copiedLabel`: each is both the accessible name and the tooltip text.
- Listen to `copy` for analytics or a toast; it fires only after the clipboard write succeeds.
- The click stops propagation, so it is safe inside clickable rows and cards.
- Set `size="small"` in dense rows; the default is `large`, the house size of an action.

## Don’t

- The action is anything other than copying → use `icon-button`.
- A labelled "Copy" action in a form or dialog footer → use `button`.
- A full code sample with its own copy control → use `code-block`.

## Related

- `icon-button` — the control it composes; `variant` and `size` are forwarded to it.
- `tooltip` — composed to show `ariaLabel` and then `copiedLabel` on hover and focus.
- `code-block` — already embeds a copy-button for its content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | Text copied to the clipboard on activation. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name while idle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy`). |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name while the copied state is shown. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copied`). |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outline' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'ghost'` | false | Visual variant forwarded to `IconButton`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token forwarded to `IconButton`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: string)` | Emitted after a successful clipboard write; `value` is the copied text. |

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `copied`, `disabled`
- `data-state` mirrors `idle` or `copied`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- The composed `Tooltip` carries its own `data-state` (`open` | `closed`) and is disabled with the button
- Fallback: when `navigator.clipboard.writeText` rejects (permission denied, insecure context, unfocused document), the button loads a small `Popover` anchored to itself (lazily, through `defineAsyncComponent`, so entries that copy do not grow): the title `Copy manually`, the value in a read-only small `Input` labelled `Value to copy`, focused and selected, and `Press Ctrl+C to copy.` (`⌘C` on macOS). `copy` is not emitted and the state stays `default`. `Esc` or a click outside closes it and returns focus to the button. Strings come from `copyButton.fallbackTitle`, `fallbackField` and `fallbackHint`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: inherited from `IconButton` (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`)
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates copy.
- ARIA: `aria-label` toggles between `ariaLabel` and `copiedLabel` when copied, and a visually hidden `role="status"` region (`<testId>__status`) announces the copied label for 2 s, since a name change on the focused button is not announced by most screen readers.
- Attributes: consumer `class`, `id`, `aria-describedby` and listeners land on the root `span` (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- Fallback popover: `role="dialog"` named by its title and described by the key hint; focus moves into the selected read-only field and returns to the button on close.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states (the icon swap comes from IconButton).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: a single icon button; nothing to mirror. The copy and check glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key logic.
- User data: the copied value is not rendered.

## Internationalization

| Key             | English source | Override prop |
| --------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `common.copy`   | `Copy`         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `common.copied` | `Copied`       | `copiedLabel` |

## Responsive

- Size follows `size` (IconButton 28 / 32 / 40 px) with IconButton's 44 px coarse-pointer target.
- The tooltip opens on focus as well as hover.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
</script>

<template>
  <CopyButton
    value="https://example.com/deploy/abc123"
    aria-label="Copy URL"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/copy-button.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/copy-button.md).

<!-- components/copy-prompt-button.md -->

# Copy Prompt Button

> The "Copy prompt" button of a docs or product home: one dark chip that copies a ready-made prompt for a coding agent and, after its label, shows the marks of the agents it works with (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor by default). The chip carries the design system's AI treatment, the same three layers as `HighlightButton`: a blurred gradient glow rotating behind it, the brand-accent gradient over the glow, and a dark scrim over both that holds the white label at contrast; on hover the gradient and the scrim fade to a quarter and the glow blooms through. It is dark in both themes (it renders under `data-theme="dark"`), so it reads as the AI entry point next to a primary button, and a tooltip says what it does. The marks are single-colour and decorative, drawn in the chip's own ink; their names reach screen readers as the button's description ("Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor"). With `closable` a dismiss button sits beside the chip, and dismissing removes both from the layout.

- Import: `import CopyPromptButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-prompt-button'`
- Category: action · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CopyPromptButton to copy a ready-made agent prompt without showing its text; a visible value gets a CopyButton.
- The hero of a documentation home or a product landing, beside the primary action (`Get started`), when the page hands its reader a prompt for their agent.
- Inside `DocAgentCard`, the "Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" card of a docs home (it renders this button by default).

## Do

- Put it second, after the primary `Button` (`Get started`), and explain what the prompt does in one line below the row (`DocHero`'s `note` slot).
- Keep the default agents unless the product supports a different set; pass `:agents="[]"` to draw the label alone.
- Pass the exact prompt in `value`; the button copies it as it stands.
- Do not recolour the marks: they are single-colour by design and follow the chip's ink.
- To draw a mark from the agent's asset file instead of the icon font, give the agent a `logo` (`@aziontech/webkit/assets/claude-symbol-color.svg`); `Logo` flattens it to the chip's ink.
- Set `closable` where the chip is guidance the reader can put away (a first-use overview), not where it is part of a page's composition (a hero). Bind `v-model:open` to remember or restore the choice (`close` still fires with the click).

## Don’t

- To show the prompt text itself on the page → use `DocPrompt` (it renders the text with its own copy control).
- To copy a value, a token or a code snippet → use `CopyButton`.
- As a generic dark button → use `Button variant="secondary"`.

## Related

- DocPrompt` — the prompt rendered in full, with a copy control.
- DocAgentCard` — the docs-home card that places this button in its left column.
- DocHero` — the docs-home masthead whose `actions` slot holds `Get started` and this button.
- CopyButton` — the icon-only copy control; this button shares its clipboard fallback.
- HighlightButton` — the AI-flow button whose glow, gradient and scrim this chip shares.
- Logo` — draws an agent mark from its asset file in the chip's ink.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | The prompt copied to the clipboard on activation. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible text and accessible name while idle; empty uses the catalog's `Copy prompt`. |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible text announced after a copy; empty uses the catalog's `Copied`. |
| `agents` | `CopyPromptButtonAgent[]` | `Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor` | false | The agents whose marks follow the label, in order; each is `{ name, icon?, logo? }`, drawn from `logo` through `Logo` when set and from the `icon` glyph otherwise; an empty list draws no marks. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the button; `copy` is not emitted. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a dismiss button beside the chip; activating it removes both from the layout and emits `close`. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: string)` | Fires with the click and `value` after the clipboard write succeeds. When the write is refused, the copy fallback popover opens instead. |
| `close` | `MouseEvent` | Fires with the click on the dismiss button (`closable`), after the chip removes itself; whether it stays away is the page's decision. |

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `true`  | `update:open` | Whether the chip is shown, via `defineModel('open')`. The dismiss button sets it to `false`; set it back to `true` to show the chip again. Unbound, the chip keeps its own state. |

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `hover` (the gradient and the scrim fade to 25% and the rotating glow blooms through), `focus-visible` (ring), `copied` (the label swaps to a check and `Copied` for two seconds, without changing the width), `disabled` (the AI layers hide and the chip takes the disabled fill), `dismissed` (`open` is false: the chip and its dismiss button unmount).
- `data-state` is `idle` or `copied`; `data-disabled` mirrors `disabled`.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed` (the tooltip owns its own open state).

## Accessibility

- Pattern: a WAI-ARIA APG **button** (`<button type="button">`); its accessible name is the label (`Copy prompt`, then `Copied` while the copied state shows). A `Tooltip` on hover and focus says what it does (`Copies a setup prompt for your AI coding tool`).
- With `closable`, the dismiss control is a separate `IconButton` beside the chip (never inside it), named `Dismiss`; dismissing unmounts both, so neither stays in the tab order.
- The agent marks are `aria-hidden`; their names form the description through `aria-describedby` ("Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor").
- A polite `role="status"` region next to the button announces `Copied` after a successful copy.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the chip, then the dismiss button when `closable`; `Enter` and `Space` copy on the chip and dismiss on the dismiss button; `Esc` closes an open tooltip (owned by `Tooltip`).
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Contrast: the white label and marks sit on the 80% black scrim at rest (≥ 4.5:1 in both page themes); on hover the scrim thins over the accent gradient and the label stays above 3:1 for its large button type.
- Touch target: 40 px tall; `pointer-coarse:min-h-11` raises it to 44 px.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the rotating glow and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-`/`pe-`, `gap-`); the label leads at the inline start, the marks follow it and the dismiss button follows the chip. The glow, gradient and scrim layers are symmetric.
- Icons: brand marks and the dismiss `×` are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source                                  | Override prop         |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `copyPromptButton.label`     | `Copy prompt`                                   | `label`               |
| `copyPromptButton.copied`    | `Copied`                                        | `copiedLabel`         |
| `copyPromptButton.worksWith` | `Works with {agents}`                           | `agents`              |
| `copyPromptButton.tooltip`   | `Copies a setup prompt for your AI coding tool` | — (provider messages) |
| `copyPromptButton.dismiss`   | `Dismiss`                                       | — (provider messages) |

- Agent names are brand names and are not translated.

## Responsive

- The chip keeps its intrinsic width; the label truncates with an ellipsis before the marks shrink when the row is narrower than the chip.
- Touch: 40 px tall, 44 px on `pointer: coarse`.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the chip wraps to its own line inside a wrapping action row.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import CopyPromptButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-prompt-button'

  const prompt =
    'Set up the Azion CLI, connect the Azion docs over MCP and link this project to my Azion account.'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Button
      label="Get started"
      variant="primary"
      size="large"
      href="#"
    />
    <CopyPromptButton :value="prompt" />
  </div>
</template>
```
