<!-- components/conversation-history.md -->

# Conversation History

> The list of past conversations with an assistant, in a side panel or drawer: titles grouped by when they were last active (Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, Older), the open one marked current, and an optional Delete per row. Choosing a row sets `v-model` to its id; the owner loads that conversation into `Conversation`.

- Import: `import ConversationHistory from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation-history'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An assistant keeps past conversations and the person returns to one.
- The left rail or a drawer of a chat page.

## Do

- Title each conversation from its first prompt, short; the full title shows on hover through `title`.
- Fix the reference time so the groups match on the server and the client: set `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` once (every time-relative component below reads it), or pass `now` here to override it for this list.
- Confirm deletes of anything older than today with a `ConfirmDialog` in the `remove` handler.

## Don’t

- Messages of the open conversation → `Conversation`.
- Navigation between product areas → `Sidebar` or `NavigationMenu`.
- A searchable table of records → `TableRoot`.

## Related

- `conversation` — shows the conversation the history selects.
- `drawer` — holds the history on narrow screens.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `{ id: string; title: string; updatedAt: string \| number \| Date }[]` | `[]` | false | Conversations, any order; they are sorted newest first inside their group. |
| `now` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference time for the groups. Empty uses the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, then the current time; set either when the list is rendered on the server. |
| `removable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a Delete button on each row that emits `remove`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder rows while the history loads. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation history`). |
| `modelValue` | `string \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, id: string)` |  |

## v-model

| Model     | Type             | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                          |
| --------- | ---------------- | ------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string \| null` | `null`  | `update:modelValue` | Id of the open conversation; its row is `aria-current="page"`. |

## States

- Groups render only when they have items; inside a group, newest first.
- Active row: `data-active` and `aria-current="page"`, the selected surface.
- Empty: one muted line, `No conversations yet.`
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` and five skeleton rows; no group headings.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `nav` named by `ariaLabel`; each group is a `ul` labelled by its visible heading (`aria-labelledby`).
- Each conversation is a `button` with its title as the name; the open one carries `aria-current="page"`.
- Delete is an `IconButton` named `Delete <title>`, shown on every row (not hover-only), so it is reachable by keyboard and touch.
- Keyboard: `Tab` moves through rows and their Delete; `Enter`/`Space` open a conversation.
- Loading sets `aria-busy` on the list.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical spacing; Delete sits at the inline end of the row.
- Icons: the trash glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none beyond `Tab`.
- User data: titles render in `<bdi>` with `dir="auto"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                              | English source          | Override prop |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------- |
| `conversationHistory.label`      | `Conversation history`  | `ariaLabel`   |
| `conversationHistory.today`      | `Today`                 | —             |
| `conversationHistory.yesterday`  | `Yesterday`             | —             |
| `conversationHistory.previous7`  | `Previous 7 days`       | —             |
| `conversationHistory.previous30` | `Previous 30 days`      | —             |
| `conversationHistory.older`      | `Older`                 | —             |
| `conversationHistory.emptyTitle` | `No conversations yet.` | —             |
| `conversationHistory.delete`     | `Delete {title}`        | —             |

- Groups use calendar days in the browser's time zone, not 24-hour windows.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; it fills the width it is given.
- Narrow: titles truncate on one line with the full title in `title`.
- Touch: rows are 32 px tall with the Delete button's 40 px touch target.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConversationHistory from '@aziontech/webkit/conversation-history'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const now = '2026-11-11T15:00:00'
  const items = ref([
    { id: 'c1', title: 'Purge the cache after a deploy', updatedAt: '2026-11-11T14:20:00' },
    { id: 'c2', title: 'Why is my function returning 502?', updatedAt: '2026-11-11T09:05:00' },
    { id: 'c3', title: 'Set up a WAF rule for login attempts', updatedAt: '2026-11-10T18:40:00' },
    { id: 'c4', title: 'Image optimization query parameters', updatedAt: '2026-11-07T11:00:00' },
    {
      id: 'c5',
      title: 'Migrate DNS records from another provider',
      updatedAt: '2026-10-28T16:30:00'
    },
    { id: 'c6', title: 'Edge storage pricing', updatedAt: '2026-08-02T10:00:00' }
  ])
  const active = ref('c2')

  const remove = (event, id) => {
    items.value = items.value.filter((item) => item.id !== id)
    if (active.value === id) active.value = null
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xs)">
    <ConversationHistory
      v-model="active"
      :items="items"
      :now="now"
      removable
      @remove="remove"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Feedback Reason Dialog

> Asks why an assistant response was not helpful, right after the thumbs-down in `ChatMessage.Feedback`: a small dialog with one required reason (radio buttons) and optional details, then Send feedback. It turns a bare thumbs-down into a signal the team can act on, without a page or a form of the owner's own. The owner opens it, sends the payload it emits and closes it.

- Import: `import FeedbackReasonDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/feedback-reason-dialog'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- After a thumbs-down on an AI response, to collect the reason.
- Any rating of generated content that needs a short, categorised reason.

## Do

- Open it only after a thumbs-down; a thumbs-up needs no reason.
- Keep the reasons short and mutually exclusive; the last is `Other`, and details stay optional.
- Close it from the `submit` handler once the request succeeds; keep it open with `loading` while it is sent.

## Don’t

- General product feedback with several fields → a page or `Drawer` form.
- A confirmation with no input → `ConfirmDialog`.

## Related

- `chat-message` — `ChatMessage.Feedback` holds the thumbs that open it.
- `confirm-dialog` — the same dialog anatomy for a yes/no decision.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reasons` | `{ value: string; label: string }[]` | `[]` | false | Reasons offered, in order. Empty uses the catalog's five: inaccurate, not helpful, did not follow the request, unsafe or harmful, other. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The feedback is being sent: Send feedback shows a spinner and the form is locked. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Dialog title. Empty uses the locale catalog (`What went wrong?`). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, payload: { reason: string; details: string })` |  |

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Opens the dialog; the reason and details reset each time it opens. Unbound, the dialog keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Idle (open): no reason chosen, Send feedback enabled.
- Invalid: submitted without a reason; the fieldset is invalid and its error is announced.
- Loading: Send feedback spinner, radios, details and Cancel disabled.
- `data-state` on the dialog mirrors `open` / `closed` (from `Dialog`).

## Accessibility

- A modal `Dialog` named by its title and described by its one-line description; focus moves into it and returns to the thumbs-down on close.
- The reasons are a `fieldset` with a `legend` (`Reason`), a `RadioGroup` with one `RadioGroup.Item` per reason and its label; the details `Textarea` is labelled `Details (optional)`.
- Submitting without a reason marks the fieldset invalid, shows the error text and focuses the first radio; nothing is sent.
- Keyboard: `Tab` through radios (arrows within the group), details, Cancel, Send feedback; `Enter` in a radio submits; `Escape` closes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical spacing only; the footer actions sit at the inline end.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: radio arrows follow the page direction (native).
- User data: details render with `dir="auto"` through `Textarea`.

## Internationalization

| Key                                                                                  | English source                                                                                    | Override prop |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.title`                                                         | `What went wrong?`                                                                                | `title`       |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.description`                                                   | `Your answer helps improve future responses.`                                                     | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.reason`                                                        | `Reason`                                                                                          | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.details`                                                       | `Details (optional)`                                                                              | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.detailsPlaceholder`                                            | `What did you expect instead?`                                                                    | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.required`                                                      | `Choose a reason.`                                                                                | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.cancel`                                                        | `Cancel`                                                                                          | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.send`                                                          | `Send feedback`                                                                                   | —             |
| `feedbackReasonDialog.inaccurate`, `notHelpful`, `ignoredRequest`, `unsafe`, `other` | `Inaccurate or made up`, `Not helpful`, `Did not follow my request`, `Unsafe or harmful`, `Other` | `reasons`     |

## Responsive

- Container queries: the dialog body is the `@container/panel` from `PanelBody`.
- Narrow: the dialog is the `small` size and becomes full width under `sm`; the footer buttons stretch (from `PanelFooter`).
- Touch: radios and buttons keep their 40 px targets.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'
  import FeedbackReasonDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/feedback-reason-dialog'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const answer =
    'Turn on **Image Optimization** in the application settings, then add `?ims=300x` to the image URL.'
  const feedback = ref(null)
  const reasonOpen = ref(false)
  const sending = ref(false)

  const onFeedback = (value) => {
    feedback.value = value
    if (value === 'down') reasonOpen.value = true
  }

  const sendReason = () => {
    sending.value = true
    setTimeout(() => {
      sending.value = false
      reasonOpen.value = false
    }, 600)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ChatMessage timestamp="10:44">
      <StreamingResponse :content="answer" />
      <template #actions>
        <ChatMessage.Actions>
          <ChatMessage.Feedback
            :model-value="feedback"
            @update:model-value="onFeedback"
          />
        </ChatMessage.Actions>
      </template>
    </ChatMessage>
    <FeedbackReasonDialog
      v-model:open="reasonOpen"
      :loading="sending"
      @submit="sendReason"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/prompt-input.md -->

# Prompt Input

> The composer of a generative AI chat (Cloudscape prompt input, AI Elements PromptInput): a text area that grows with the prompt up to `maxRows`, a Submit control that becomes Stop while a response is being generated, a toolbar row for secondary controls (attach, mode), an attachments row above the text, an optional character limit with a counter, and constraint text under it (a disclaimer or the shortcuts it accepts). Enter submits; Shift+Enter adds a line; an IME composition never submits. It is controlled: the owner holds the text, receives `submit` with the trimmed prompt, and clears it. While `status` is `pending` or `streaming` the reader can keep typing the next prompt, but cannot submit it until the response ends or they press Stop.

- Import: `import PromptInput from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The input of any conversation with the generative AI assistant.
- A single "Ask about this page" box that opens a conversation.

## Do

- Placeholder is a suggested question with no end punctuation (`Ask a question`); never the only instruction.
- Put the disclaimer and the shortcuts in `hint`, not in the placeholder.
- Set `status` from the request so Submit turns into Stop; wire `stop` to abort it.
- Clear `v-model` in the `submit` handler and keep focus in the input.
- Use `maxLength` only when the backend has a limit; the counter is the warning.

## Don’t

- A text field in a form → `textarea` inside `field`.
- Search over a list → `input` with a search icon or `property-filter`.
- A command palette → `command`.

## Related

- `textarea` — the form control; this one has no visible label and submits on Enter.
- `conversation` — the log above it; only the log scrolls.
- `suggestion-group` — prompts the reader can send without typing.
- `file-dropzone`, `chip` — what attachment flows compose into the `attachments` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Hint shown while empty, a suggested question with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Ask a question`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the text area; the input has no visible label. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Prompt`). |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `0` | false | Character limit; shows an `n/max` counter and blocks submit over it. `0` means no limit. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `1` | false | Rows shown while empty. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `6` | false | Rows the text area grows to before it scrolls. |
| `status` | `'ready' \| 'pending' \| 'streaming'` | `'ready'` | false | Request lifecycle: `pending` and `streaming` swap Submit for Stop and block another submit; typing stays allowed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the text area, the submit control and every control in the slots' row. |
| `menus` | `PromptInputMenu[]` | `[]` | false | Shortcut menus opened by a trigger character at the start of a word: `/` for commands, `@` for things to reference. Choosing an option inserts `<trigger><label>` and adds it to `references`. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `references` | `PromptInputReference[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:references`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, payload: { value: string; references: PromptInputReference[] })` |  |
| `stop` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attachments` | — | Attached files or context chips, above the text. |
| `actions` | — | Secondary controls at the inline start of the toolbar; inside a `fieldset` disabled with the input. |
| `hint` | — | Constraint text under the input; referenced by `aria-describedby`. |

## Sub-components

_None — monolithic with slots. Exports: `"./prompt-input": "./src/components/ai/prompt-input/prompt-input.vue"`.
Exported type: `PromptInputStatus = 'ready' | 'pending' | 'streaming'`. Composed DS components:
`icon-button` (Submit, Stop). Exposes `focus()`._

## v-model

| Model                | Type                     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model`            | `string`                 | `''`    | `update:modelValue` | The prompt being written, via `defineModel`. The owner clears it in its `submit` handler.                                                             |
| `v-model:references` | `PromptInputReference[]` | `[]`    | `update:references` | What the prompt references, added by the menus and shown as removable chips above the text; removing a chip also removes its `<trigger><label>` text. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-disabled`; `data-invalid` while over `maxLength`.
- `ready`: Submit (primary `IconButton`, `ai ai-arrow-up`), disabled while the prompt is empty, over the limit or `disabled`.
- `pending` / `streaming`: Stop (secondary `IconButton`, `ai ai-stop`) replaces Submit; Enter does nothing.
- Over the limit: border turns `--danger-border`, the counter turns danger, `aria-invalid="true"`, and a polite live region says how many characters are over.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the container shows `focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Enter` submits; `Shift+Enter` new line; `Tab` moves to the slot controls, then Submit / Stop. IME composition (`isComposing`) never submits.
- Shortcut menus (`menus`): typing a trigger at the start of a word opens a listbox above the input with up to eight options matching what follows it. Focus stays in the text area, which points at the list with `aria-controls` and at the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant` (a `textarea` cannot take `role="combobox"`); `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move, `Enter` or `Tab` choose, `Escape` closes, and Enter does not submit while the list is open. A polite status reads `3 suggestions` or `No matches`. The text area lists the triggers in `aria-keyshortcuts`. References are a list named `References` of removable `Chip`s.
- ARIA: the `<textarea>` is named by `aria-label` (no visible label, as Cloudscape allows for an input with an action button), described by the counter and the hint, `aria-invalid` over the limit; Submit and Stop are named icon buttons.
- The placeholder never carries required information (it disappears on typing).
- Touch target: `IconButton` medium (44 px on coarse pointers).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; actions at the inline start, Submit at the inline end.
- Icons: the arrow-up and stop glyphs are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: arrows move in the shortcut menu only while it is open; vertical, so not mirrored.
- User data: the text area follows the document direction; mixed prompts render with the browser's bidi.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source                      | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `promptInput.label`          | `Prompt`                            | `ariaLabel`   |
| `promptInput.placeholder`    | `Ask a question`                    | `placeholder` |
| `promptInput.submit`         | `Submit`                            | —             |
| `promptInput.stop`           | `Stop generating`                   | —             |
| `promptInput.count`          | `{count}/{max}`                     | —             |
| `promptInput.overLimit`      | `{count} characters over the limit` | —             |
| `promptInput.menuResults`    | `{count} suggestion(s)` (plural)    | —             |
| `promptInput.noMatch`        | `No matches`                        | —             |
| `promptInput.menuReferences` | `References`                        | —             |

- Formatting: counts go through `Intl.NumberFormat` (the `t()` number formatting).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; full width of its host.
- Narrow: the toolbar wraps its slot controls; Submit stays at the inline end.
- Touch: `enterkeyhint="send"` on mobile keyboards; targets 44 px on coarse pointers.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PromptInput from '@aziontech/webkit/prompt-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const prompt = ref('')
  const last = ref('')

  function send(event, { value }) {
    last.value = value
    prompt.value = ''
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <PromptInput
      v-model="prompt"
      @submit="send"
    >
      <template #hint>The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information.</template>
    </PromptInput>
    <p
      v-if="last"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      Submitted: {{ last }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/prompt-input.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/prompt-input.md).

<!-- components/reasoning.md -->

# Reasoning

> Shows the model's thinking before its response (Cloudscape Thinking pattern, AI Elements Reasoning): a disclosure whose label reads `Thinking` (pulsing) while the model reasons and `Thought for 14 seconds` once it is done, with the trace inside. Collapsed by default in a chat, where the response is the main content. The duration comes from the server (`duration`) or is measured from `streaming` turning on to turning off, rounded to whole seconds. An optional `Skip thinking` lets the reader ask for the response now.

- Import: `import Reasoning from '@aziontech/webkit/reasoning'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The model performs extended reasoning before answering, and the trace helps the reader trust or check the response.

## Do

- Keep it collapsed in chat; open it by default only where reasoning is the point (an editor, a review).
- Never show secrets, token counts or system prompts in the trace.
- Do not replace the label with trace text; the label stays `Thinking` until done.
- Offer `skippable` only when the model can answer meaningfully without finishing.

## Don’t

- Ordinary loading with no reasoning → `response-loading`.
- Agent actions with side effects (calls, commands) → `tool-call` and `tool-approval`.
- Progressive steps of a long task → a `stepper` or a list of `tool-call`s.

## Related

- `response-loading` — loading without a trace.
- `tool-call` — what the agent did, rather than what it thought.
- `streaming-response` — renders a Markdown trace inside the slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The model is still reasoning: the label reads `Thinking` and pulses; when it turns false the label shows how long it took. |
| `duration` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Seconds the reasoning took, when the server reports it. Without it the component measures from `streaming` turning on to turning off. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; collapsed is the default in a chat, where the response is the main content. |
| `skippable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Offers `Skip thinking` while streaming, for a model that can answer before it finishes reasoning. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skip` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The trace: short narration, steps, inline code. Kept as it was once thinking ends. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./reasoning"`. Composed DS components: `button` (Skip thinking)._

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                           |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | The trace was expanded or collapsed. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-state="open|closed"` (disclosure), `data-streaming`.
- Label: `Thinking` while streaming; `Thought for {n} seconds` with a duration; `Thought for a few seconds` when neither was measured nor given.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the trigger.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles; `Tab` to Skip thinking.
- ARIA: a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` the trace; glyphs `aria-hidden`; a polite visually hidden status announces the completed label (`Thought for 14 seconds`) when thinking ends. The trace is not live.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on the muted label and trace.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: `border-s` / `ps-` put the trace rule on the inline start.
- Icons: sparkles and chevron-down are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source                           | Override prop |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `reasoning.thinking`       | `Thinking`                               | —             |
| `reasoning.thought`        | `Thought for {count} second(s)` (plural) | —             |
| `reasoning.thoughtBriefly` | `Thought for a few seconds`              | —             |
| `reasoning.skip`           | `Skip thinking`                          | —             |

- Formatting: plural rules through `Intl.PluralRules`; the count through `Intl.NumberFormat`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: the trigger and Skip wrap.
- Touch: the trigger is text-sized; Skip is a small `Button` (44 px on coarse pointers).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Reasoning from '@aziontech/webkit/reasoning'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <Reasoning :duration="14">
      <p>The reader asks why the cache hit ratio of storefront dropped this week.</p>
      <p>
        Checking the cache settings of <code>storefront</code>: query strings are part of the cache
        key, and a campaign started on Monday adds <code>utm_source</code> to every link.
      </p>
      <p>Each campaign link is a new cache key, so most requests miss the cache.</p>
    </Reasoning>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/reasoning.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/reasoning.md).

<!-- components/response-branches.md -->

# Response Branches

> Pages through alternative versions of one assistant response: after Regenerate, or when the model returned several candidates, the message shows one version at a time with a `‹ 2 of 3 ›` pager under it. The owner keeps every version and renders the active one in the default slot; the component owns only the position and the pager. It is the AI Elements `Branch` pattern, rebuilt on WebKit's `IconButton` and tokens.

- Import: `import ResponseBranches from '@aziontech/webkit/response-branches'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ResponseBranches to page through alternative versions of one AI response; rows of a table or list use Pagination.
- A response was regenerated and the earlier versions stay available to compare.
- A model returned several candidates and the person picks the one to keep reading.

## Do

- Move to the new version when Regenerate finishes (set `v-model` to the last index) so the person sees what they asked for.
- Keep the versions in the order they were made; the newest is last.
- Do not render the pager inside the slot; it belongs to the component so its position and labels stay the same across versions.

## Don’t

- Pages of one long list → use `Pagination`.
- Steps of a flow → use `Stepper`.
- Different documents side by side → use `Tabs`.

## Related

- `chat-message` — the message whose body the branches wrap; its actions hold Regenerate.
- `streaming-response` — a new version streams in the slot while the pager already counts it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number` | `—` | true | How many versions exist. With one or none the pager is not drawn. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the pager group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Response versions`). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Locks the pager, for example while a new version streams. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { index: number } | The active version. Rendered once; the owner switches its content by `index`. |

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                              |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model` | `number` | `0`     | `update:modelValue` | Zero-based index of the version shown, clamped to `0 … count - 1`. |

## States

- `data-count` on the root; `data-index` mirrors the clamped index.
- First version: Previous is disabled; last version: Next is disabled.
- `disabled`: both buttons are disabled and the counter is muted.
- `count` ≤ 1: only the slot renders.

## Accessibility

- The pager is `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel` (`Response versions`); Previous and Next are `IconButton`s named `Previous version` / `Next version`.
- The counter (`2 of 3`) is a polite live region, so moving announces the new position once; the slot is not live.
- Keyboard: `Tab` reaches Previous and Next; `Enter`/`Space` move; a disabled end button leaves the tab order.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical spacing only; the pager sits at the inline start.
- Icons: the chevrons mirror under `dir="rtl"` through `IconButton`'s directional icons, so Previous always points to the inline start.
- Keyboard: none beyond the buttons.
- User data: the slot follows the page direction.

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source         | Override prop |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- |
| `responseBranches.label`    | `Response versions`    | `ariaLabel`   |
| `responseBranches.previous` | `Previous version`     | —             |
| `responseBranches.next`     | `Next version`         | —             |
| `responseBranches.position` | `{current} of {total}` | —             |

- Numbers in the counter use the locale's digits through the catalog template.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: the pager stays one row (two 28 px buttons and a short counter).
- Touch: buttons are `IconButton` small, with the 40 px touch target from `IconButton`.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ChatMessage from '@aziontech/webkit/chat-message'
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
  import ResponseBranches from '@aziontech/webkit/response-branches'
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const versions = ref([
    'Purge the cache from **Edge Cache › Purge**: choose *URL*, paste the paths and confirm.',
    'Use a **wildcard purge** (`/assets/*`) when many files changed at once; it clears every match in one request.',
    'If the files change on every deploy, add a **version to the file name** instead of purging: the new name is a new cache entry.'
  ])
  const active = ref(2)
  const regenerating = ref(false)

  const regenerate = () => {
    if (regenerating.value) return
    regenerating.value = true
    setTimeout(() => {
      versions.value = [
        ...versions.value,
        'Purge by **cache key** from the API (`POST /purge/cachekey`) to automate it in your pipeline.'
      ]
      active.value = versions.value.length - 1
      regenerating.value = false
    }, 800)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ChatMessage timestamp="10:44">
      <ResponseBranches
        v-model="active"
        :count="versions.length"
        :disabled="regenerating"
      >
        <template #default="{ index }">
          <StreamingResponse :content="versions[index]" />
        </template>
      </ResponseBranches>
      <template #actions>
        <ChatMessage.Actions>
          <CopyButton
            size="small"
            :value="versions[active]"
          />
          <IconButton
            icon="ai ai-refresh"
            aria-label="Regenerate response"
            variant="ghost"
            size="small"
            :loading="regenerating"
            @click="regenerate"
          />
        </ChatMessage.Actions>
      </template>
    </ChatMessage>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/response-loading.md -->

# Response Loading

> Use ResponseLoading only while a generative AI answer is being produced; never for loading product data, which uses Skeleton (known shape), Spinner (inline) or Progress (measurable). The loading state of a generative AI response (Cloudscape generative AI loading states and loading bar, AI Elements Loader): visible loading text — `Generating a response`, `Loading list of workloads` — paired with three pulsing dots (`inline`, for text) or an indeterminate bar (`bar`, where a table, list or code block is about to appear). It waits `delay` milliseconds before showing anything, so a response that arrives within a second never flickers a loading state.

- Import: `import ResponseLoading from '@aziontech/webkit/response-loading'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Processing: the model has the prompt but has produced nothing yet (`ChatMessage` renders it for `state="pending"`).
- Generation of mixed content: a bar where a table or code block will appear while text streams.

## Do

- Text says `[Generating|Loading] <what>` without end punctuation: `Generating a response`, `Loading list of workloads`.
- Keep the default 1 s delay; set `delay` to 0 only when the owner already delayed.
- Use the bar only for non-text content; stream text instead of loading it.

## Don’t

- Model reasoning with a trace → `reasoning`.
- Loading a page or table of product data → `skeleton`, `spinner`, `progress`.
- Determinate progress → `progress`.

## Related

- `chat-message` — renders this while `pending`.
- `progress` — the indeterminate bar it draws.
- `reasoning` — thinking with a trace.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible loading text, `Generating <what>` or `Loading <what>`, with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Generating a response`). |
| `variant` | `'inline' \| 'bar'` | `'inline'` | false | inline` pulses three dots beside the text (text responses); `bar` draws an indeterminate bar under it, where a table, list or code block is about to appear. |
| `delay` | `number` | `1000` | false | Milliseconds to wait before showing anything, so a fast response never flickers a loading state. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./response-loading"`; type `ResponseLoadingVariant`. Composed DS components: `progress`._

## States

- `data-variant`; `data-state="closed"` until the delay has passed, then `data-state="open"`. Before that the `role="status"` region exists but is empty, so the text is announced when it appears.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing focusable.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: `role="status"` (polite) holds the visible text; dots and bar are `aria-hidden`. Loading is always conveyed in text, not only in motion.
- Reduced motion: dots stop pulsing; the bar stops sweeping.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; the bar sweeps from the inline start (handled by `Progress`).
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source          | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------- |
| `responseLoading.generating` | `Generating a response` | `label`       |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: the bar fills the width up to `--container-xs`.
- Touch: nothing interactive.
- Reflow: wraps.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ResponseLoading from '@aziontech/webkit/response-loading'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <ResponseLoading />
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/response-loading.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/response-loading.md).

<!-- components/sources.md -->

# Sources

> The list of sources a generative AI response drew on (Cloudscape's sources expandable section, AI Elements Sources): a disclosure titled `3 sources` that opens an ordered list — number, linked title, one-line description. Item `n` carries the id `<anchor>-source-<n>`, the target of the `[n]` citations `StreamingResponse` renders; following a citation opens the list and brings the item into view.

- Import: `import Sources from '@aziontech/webkit/sources'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A response is grounded in documents, pages or records the reader may want to open or verify.

## Do

- Order items as the response first cites them, so `[1]` is item 1.
- Use the page title, not the URL, as the title; add the site or section as the description.
- Keep the list collapsed by default; the inline citations are the primary path.

## Don’t

- Related links that the response did not use → `help-panel` links or a plain list.
- A single source → cite it inline with a link; a list of one is noise.

## Related

- `citation` — the inline `[n]` that points here.
- `streaming-response` — renders the citations; share the `anchor`.
- `chat-message` — sources sit inside the assistant message, under the response.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SourcesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The sources behind the response, in citation order; item `n` is what `[n]` points at. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Id prefix of the list items (`<anchor>-source-<n>`); pass the same value to `StreamingResponse` so its citations link here. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the disclosure. Empty uses the locale catalog (`3 sources`). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven: a source list is a record set the response already holds, like table rows.
Exports: `"./sources"`; exported type `SourcesItem` (`title`, `href?`, `description?`) from `sources/types.ts`,
shared with `StreamingResponse`._

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Expanded or collapsed, by the trigger or by following a citation. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-state="open|closed"`; renders nothing when `items` is empty.
- Following a `#<anchor>-source-<n>` link (`hashchange`) opens the list and scrolls the item into view.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: trigger, links and the targeted item show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles; `Tab` through the links.
- ARIA: `button` with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the list is an `<ol aria-label="Sources">` so numbers are announced by position; the visual number chip is `aria-hidden`.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; the number chip sits at the inline start.
- Icons: book and chevron-down are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: titles render with the document direction.

## Internationalization

| Key             | English source               | Override prop |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------- |
| `sources.count` | `{count} source(s)` (plural) | `title`       |
| `sources.label` | `Sources`                    | —             |

- Formatting: `Intl.PluralRules` and `Intl.NumberFormat` through `t()`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: titles and descriptions truncate with an ellipsis.
- Touch: links are text-sized inside 24 px rows.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Sources from '@aziontech/webkit/sources'

  const items = [
    {
      title: 'Real-Time Purge',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
      description: 'Azion documentation · Cache'
    },
    {
      title: 'Cache settings',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
      description: 'Azion documentation · Applications'
    },
    {
      title: 'Purge by wildcard',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
      description: 'Azion documentation · Cache'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <Sources
      :items="items"
      anchor="purge-answer"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/streaming-response.md -->

# Streaming Response

> Renders a model's Markdown as it streams in (AI Elements Response / Streamdown), safely. The content is parsed by a small Markdown parser into a tree and rendered with Vue elements — never `v-html` — so raw HTML in model output shows as text, `javascript:` and `data:` links are dropped (only `http(s)`, `mailto`, relative and `#` links survive), and images render as their alt text. It covers what responses use: paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, inline code, links, lists, block quotes, GFM tables, rules and fenced code (rendered with `CodeBlock`, copyable). Incomplete Markdown is tolerated while streaming: an unclosed `**` renders bold to the end, an unclosed code fence stays a plain `<pre>` until it closes (no highlighting churn), and a half-written link shows its text only. Numbered citations `[1]` become `Citation` references resolved against `sources`, linked to the `Sources` list under the response through a shared `anchor`. A blinking caret marks the end while `streaming`; the region is `aria-busy` until the stream ends.

- Import: `import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use StreamingResponse for model Markdown that arrives while it renders; a whole documentation page written in MDX uses DocMarkdown.
- The content of every assistant `ChatMessage`.
- Any generated text on a page (an explanation, a summary) that arrives token by token.

## Do

- Pass the accumulated text on every chunk; the parser is cheap and the output is keyed by block.
- Keep `streaming` true until the stream closes, then false (removes the caret, highlights an open fence).
- Give the response and its `Sources` the same `anchor` so `[n]` links to item `n`.
- Do not post-process model output into HTML; there is no HTML path.

## Don’t

- Authored documentation prose → `doc-prose`.
- Code alone → `code-block`.
- Trusted HTML from your own CMS → render it with your CMS pipeline; this component deliberately renders no HTML.

## Related

- `chat-message` — the host of a response.
- `citation`, `sources` — inline references and the list they point at.
- `code-block` — what fenced code renders as.
- `response-loading` — the loading text before the first token, or a bar where a table is coming.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | false | The model's Markdown so far. Parsed into elements, never injected as HTML: raw tags render as text and only http(s), mailto, relative and hash links survive. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Tokens are still arriving: shows the caret, marks the region busy and keeps an unclosed code fence as plain text until it closes. |
| `sources` | `SourcesItem[]` | `[]` | false | Sources the `[n]` citations in the content resolve against (title in the tooltip and the accessible name). |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | The `anchor` of the `Sources` list under the response; citations link to its items. Empty renders unlinked numbers. |

## Sub-components

_None public. Internals shared by the AI family in `src/components/ai/lib/`: `parse-markdown.ts`
(`parseMarkdown`, `parseInline`, `safeHref`, `plainText`) and `markdown-inline.vue` (recursive inline
renderer, also used by `ToolApproval` for backticks in its title). Exports: `"./streaming-response"`. Composed DS
components: `code-block`, `citation`._

## States

- `data-streaming` and `aria-busy="true"` while `streaming`.
- Caret: inside the last paragraph or heading, else after the last block; only while `streaming`.
- Open fence while streaming: `<pre data-testid="…__pending-code">`; closed fence or stream ended: `CodeBlock`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: links and the table scroller carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches links, citations, the copy control of each code block and a wide table's scroller.
- ARIA: `aria-busy` while streaming (screen readers wait); the caret is `aria-hidden`; headings start at `h3` (`#` → `h3`) so a response never outranks the page; tables use `th scope="col"`. Announcing the finished text is the `Conversation`'s job.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for body, muted quote and link text.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities (`ps-` list indent, `border-s` quotes, `text-start` cells).
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: code blocks and inline code are `dir="ltr"`; prose follows the document.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings (the content is the model's; `Citation` and `CodeBlock` carry their own).

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: tables and code scroll horizontally inside their own frame; prose wraps (`break-words`).
- Touch: no hover-only affordance.
- Reflow: no page-level horizontal scroll at 320 px; tables are the exception, inside their scroller.

## Examples

### Default

````vue
<script setup>
  import StreamingResponse from '@aziontech/webkit/streaming-response'

  const content = [
    '## Purge one URL',
    '',
    'Use **Real-Time Purge** when one object changed at the origin. Purges by `URL` take effect in a few seconds.',
    '',
    '1. Open Real-Time Purge from the products menu.',
    '2. Choose *URL* as the purge type.',
    '3. Paste the address and select Purge.',
    '',
    '| Purge type | When to use it |',
    '| --- | --- |',
    '| URL | One object changed |',
    '| Wildcard | A folder changed |',
    '',
    'The same purge from the CLI:',
    '',
    '```bash',
    'azion purge urls --urls https://www.example.com/styles.css',
    '```'
  ].join('\n')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <StreamingResponse :content="content" />
  </div>
</template>
````

<!-- components/suggestion-group.md -->

# Suggestion Group

> A group of prompts the reader can send without typing (Cloudscape support prompt group, AI Elements Suggestion): support prompts on an empty conversation, follow-up questions after a response, or the choices of a clarifying question. Each prompt is a button; choosing one emits `select` with the click event and the item, and the owner either sends it or places it in the prompt input to edit.

- Import: `import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The empty state of an assistant, to show what it can do (vertical, up to five).
- After a broad response, to narrow it (horizontal chips, up to five, most likely first).
- A follow-up question with predefined answers.

## Do

- Five or fewer, ordered by likelihood.
- Write prompts as the reader would ask them, under 72 characters, sentence case, no end punctuation needed for questions you send verbatim.
- Disable the group while a response is generating.
- Remove follow-ups once the reader sends anything else.

## Don’t

- Navigation or filters → `tabs`, `toggle-group`, `property-filter`.
- Choices that are a form value → `radio-group`.
- More than five options → let the reader type; the prompt input stays available.

## Related

- `prompt-input` — the open-ended alternative that must stay reachable.
- `empty-state` — hosts the vertical support prompts before the first message.
- `chip`, `button` — visual cousins; prompts are their own control because they send text.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SuggestionGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | Up to five prompts, most likely first. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Suggested prompts`). |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | false | horizontal` wraps chips in a row (follow-up questions under a response); `vertical` stacks them (support prompts on an empty conversation). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every prompt, while a response is being generated. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: SuggestionGroupItem)` |  |

## Sub-components

_None. Data-driven (`items`), like Cloudscape's support prompt group. Exports: `"./suggestion-group"`;
types `SuggestionGroupItem`, `SuggestionGroupOrientation`._

## States

- `data-orientation`, `data-disabled`; renders nothing when `items` is empty.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between prompts (each is a native button; five at most keeps the tab order short); `Enter` / `Space` chooses.
- ARIA: `role="group"` with `aria-label`; icons `aria-hidden`; native `disabled`.
- Touch target: 32 px rows, 44 px on coarse pointers.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities, `text-start`.
- Icons: product icons are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none beyond Tab.
- User data: prompt labels follow the document direction.

## Internationalization

| Key                     | English source      | Override prop |
| ----------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| `suggestionGroup.label` | `Suggested prompts` | `ariaLabel`   |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: horizontal chips wrap; vertical prompts fill the width.
- Touch: 44 px on coarse pointers.
- Reflow: wraps, no horizontal scroll.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SuggestionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/suggestion-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const sent = ref('')
  const items = [
    { id: 'ttl', label: 'What TTL should my images use?' },
    { id: 'wildcard', label: 'How do I purge a whole folder?' },
    { id: 'origin', label: 'Why does the origin still get requests?' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-3xl) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <SuggestionGroup
      :items="items"
      aria-label="Follow-up questions"
      @select="(event, item) => (sent = item.label)"
    />
    <p
      v-if="sent"
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
    >
      Sent: {{ sent }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tool-approval.md -->

# Tool Approval

> A user-authorized action in a conversation (Cloudscape user-authorized actions, AI Elements Confirmation): the agent proposes something with consequences — call a tool, run a command, deploy, delete — and the reader approves or denies it before anything runs. The card states the action as a question (``Allow `npm test`?``), says what will happen, shows exactly what will run in its body (a `CodeBlock` with the command, `KeyValueList` with parameters), and offers Deny and Approve. Once decided, the buttons give way to the outcome in text (`Approved`, `Denied`, `Request expired`) so the decision stays in the thread. Irreversible actions (`variant="danger"`) turn Approve destructive and can require typing a phrase first. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.

- Import: `import ToolApproval from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-approval'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ToolApproval only inside an AI conversation when an agent asks permission to run a tool or command; for a person confirming an action they started use ConfirmDialog.
- One-time authorization of a consequential action proposed by an agent: a production deployment, a purge, a command.
- An irreversible action (delete): add `confirmationPhrase`.

## Do

- Title is a question naming the action and target; put tool and command names in backticks (code).
- Match the approve label to the title verb (`Deploy`, `Delete`) when it is not a generic tool call.
- Never pre-focus or pre-select Approve for a risky action.
- Do not leave a request pending forever: expire it (`status="expired"`) and have the assistant say nothing ran.
- After Deny, the assistant acknowledges in the conversation ("Skipping that step.").

## Don’t

- Tools already trusted for the session → record the call with `tool-call`, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started themselves in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
- A form → this card only approves or denies.

## Related

- `tool-call` — the record of the call after it is approved (or `denied`).
- `confirm-dialog` — confirmation of the reader's own destructive action.
- `code-block`, `key-value-list` — what will run, in the body.
- `chat-message` — the assistant acknowledges the decision in the next message.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The question, naming the action: ``Allow `npm test`?``, `Approve deployment to production?`. Backticks render as code. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on what will happen and to what; backticks render as code. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'approved' \| 'denied' \| 'expired'` | `'pending'` | false | pending` asks; `approved`, `denied` and `expired` replace the buttons with the outcome in text. |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'danger'` | `'default'` | false | danger` for an action that cannot be undone: the approve button turns destructive. |
| `confirmationPhrase` | `string` | `''` | false | A word the reader must type before Approve enables, for irreversible actions (the resource name). Empty asks for no typing. |
| `approveLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the approve button, the verb of the title (`Deploy`, `Delete`). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Approve`). |
| `denyLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the deny button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deny`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | A decision is being sent; both buttons are inert and Approve shows its loading state. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approve` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |
| `deny` | `(event: MouseEvent)` |  |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | What exactly will run: a `CodeBlock`, or `KeyValueList` with parameters. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./tool-approval"`; types `ToolApprovalStatus`, `ToolApprovalVariant`.
Composed DS components: `button`, `status-indicator`; the title and description reuse
`StreamingResponse`'s inline renderer so backticks render as code (no HTML). Exposes `focus()`._

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-variant`.
- `pending`: phrase field (when `confirmationPhrase`), Deny (outlined) and Approve (primary, or danger with `variant="danger"`); Approve disabled until the phrase matches.
- `approved` (success), `denied` (warning), `expired` (neutral): a `StatusIndicator` with the outcome; the typed phrase resets when the card returns to `pending`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: buttons and the phrase input show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`; the heading shows a ring when `focus()` moves focus to it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` through the body, the phrase field, Deny, Approve; `Enter` / `Space` activates. No focus trap, no initial focus (Cloudscape: the one-time decision card is not a dialog).
- ARIA: `role="group"` labelled by its `h3` title and described by the description; the phrase field has a visible `<label>`; a polite live region announces the outcome; outcomes are text, never color alone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; buttons align to the inline end.
- Icons: the shield is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: code in the title and body is `dir="ltr"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source             | Override prop  |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------- |
| `toolApproval.approve`      | `Approve`                  | `approveLabel` |
| `toolApproval.deny`         | `Deny`                     | `denyLabel`    |
| `toolApproval.approved`     | `Approved`                 | —              |
| `toolApproval.denied`       | `Denied`                   | —              |
| `toolApproval.expired`      | `Request expired`          | —              |
| `toolApproval.confirmLabel` | `Type {phrase} to confirm` | —              |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: buttons wrap; the body's code scrolls inside its block.
- Touch: medium buttons (44 px on coarse pointers).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import ToolApproval from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-approval'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const status = ref('pending')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-3xl)">
    <ToolApproval
      title="Allow `azion deploy --env production`?"
      description="Deploys the current build of storefront to production. The previous version stays available for rollback."
      approve-label="Deploy"
      :status="status"
      @approve="status = 'approved'"
      @deny="status = 'denied'"
    >
      <CodeBlock
        :tabs="[
          {
            label: 'Shell',
            value: 'cmd',
            code: 'azion deploy --env production --workload storefront',
            language: 'bash'
          }
        ]"
        :show-line-numbers="false"
      />

  </div>
</template>
```

# Tool Call

> One tool or command the agent invoked, shown in the conversation (AI Elements Tool, Cloudscape progressive steps): a row with the tool name in code font, an optional plain description, and a status (`Waiting`, `Running…`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Denied`), with the call's input and output in a collapsible panel. It is the record of what the agent did; authorization before it runs is `ToolApproval`.

- Import: `import ToolCall from '@aziontech/webkit/tool-call'`
- Category: ai · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An agent calls a tool, an MCP server, an API or a CLI command during a response, and the reader should see what ran and what came back.

## Do

- Name the tool exactly as it is (`list_workloads`) and describe it in plain words (`Listing your workloads`).
- Collapse details by default; open them on error so the reader sees why.
- Redact secrets from inputs and outputs.

## Don’t

- Asking the reader to allow a call → `tool-approval` (then a `tool-call` records it).
- The model's reasoning → `reasoning`.
- A long-running job outside a chat → `progress` / `status-indicator` on the resource.

## Related

- `tool-approval` — the authorization step before a sensitive call.
- `status-indicator` — the status the row shows.
- `code-block`, `key-value-list` — what goes in the input and output slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `—` | true | The tool or command identifier, shown in code font (`list_workloads`). |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | What the call does in the reader's words (`Listing your workloads`). Empty shows only the name. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'running' \| 'success' \| 'error' \| 'denied'` | `'running'` | false | pending` waits for authorization, `running` is in flight, then `success`, `error` or `denied` (the reader refused it). |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled; details start collapsed. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | — | The parameters the tool is called with (`CodeBlock`, `KeyValueList`). |
| `output` | — | What the tool returned, or the error it failed with. |

## Sub-components

_None. Exports: `"./tool-call"`; type `ToolCallStatus`. Composed DS components: `status-indicator`._

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                     |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Details expanded or collapsed. Unbound, the state is local and starts from `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-status` mirrors `status`; `data-state="open|closed"` only when a slot makes it expandable.
- Status mapping: `pending` neutral, `running` info with spinner, `success` success, `error` danger, `denied` warning.
- Without `input` / `output` the row is static (no button).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the trigger.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` to the trigger, `Enter` / `Space` toggles the details.
- ARIA: the trigger is a `button` with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`; the status is a `StatusIndicator` inside a `role="status"` region the ToolCall owns (StatusIndicator itself is not live), so a change from Running to Completed is announced; Input and Output are `section`s labelled by their `h4`.
- Status is conveyed in text, never by color alone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities (`ms-auto` on the chevron, `text-start`).
- Icons: wrench and chevron-down are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: the tool name is `dir="ltr"` code.

## Internationalization

| Key                | English source | Override prop |
| ------------------ | -------------- | ------------- |
| `toolCall.pending` | `Waiting`      | —             |
| `toolCall.running` | `Running`      | —             |
| `toolCall.success` | `Completed`    | —             |
| `toolCall.error`   | `Failed`       | —             |
| `toolCall.denied`  | `Denied`       | —             |
| `toolCall.input`   | `Input`        | —             |
| `toolCall.output`  | `Output`       | —             |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: title and name truncate; the status stays visible.
- Touch: 40 px row.
- Reflow: code in details scrolls inside its block.

    />

      status="running"

<!-- components/bar-list.md -->

# Bar List

> Use BarList for a ranked top-N breakdown inside a chart card; a list of mixed rows with actions is Item rows. A ranked list of named values: each row is a tinted bar whose length is the value against the largest one, with the name inside the bar and the formatted value in a right-aligned column. It reads as a list, not a chart — no axes, no grid — so it suits top-N breakdowns inside a card, where a horizontal `chart` would spend its width on an axis gutter.

- Import: `import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'`
- Category: chart · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Top-N breakdowns inside a card: top paths, top countries, top user agents, top rules triggered.
- A ranking where the name matters as much as the size, and names are long enough to need the bar's full width.
- Rows that lead somewhere — a filtered view of that path or country — via `href` or `item-click`.

## Do

- Keep it to about ten rows; fold the tail into an "Other" row in the data rather than scrolling.
- Leave `sort` on `descending` for rankings; use `none` only when the order itself carries meaning (pipeline steps, weekdays).
- Pass the same `formatValue` as the chart beside it so a number reads the same in both.
- Give interactive rows a destination the user expects — a filtered view of that item — not a detail drawer of the whole list.

## Don’t

- Several series per category, or values over time → use `chart`.
- A share of a whole where the parts sum to 100% → use `donut-chart`.
- One value against a limit (quota, usage) → use `progress`.

## Related

- `chart` — horizontal bars with an axis, for comparing several series per category.
- `donut-chart` — the share view of the same breakdown when the parts sum to a whole.
- `chart-card` — the box a BarList sits in on a dashboard.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BarListItem[]` | `[]` | false | Rows to rank; each item is `{ id?: string; name: string; value: number; href?: string }`. An item with `href` renders as a link. |
| `sort` | `'descending' \| 'ascending' \| 'none'` | `'descending'` | false | Row order; `none` keeps the order of `items`. |
| `color` | `ChartColor` | `1` | false | Hue of the bars: a categorical slot (1–6), `other`, or a status. The fill is that hue tinted over the surface. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders rows without an `href` as buttons that emit `item-click`. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `formatCompact` | false | Formats the value column. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton rows in place of the list. |
| `refetching` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Holds the previous rows at reduced opacity while new data loads (the same as `chart`). |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Error message; when set, the list renders an error state in an `alert` region instead of rows: a bordered small `EmptyState` with the error mark, `barList.errorTitle` and the message (the `error` slot replaces it). |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title: why the list is empty, or what to do next. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: BarListItem)` | A row activated — a clickable row, or a link row (the link still navigates). `item` is the consumer's own item object. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default `EmptyState` shown when `items` is empty. |
| `empty-actions` | — | Actions under the default empty state (a Clear filters or Retry). |
| `error` | — | Replaces the default error state shown while `error` is set. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` (interactive rows only), `loading` (Skeleton rows), `refetching` (previous rows at 60% opacity), `error` (error state in an `alert` region), `empty` (`EmptyState`). Precedence: loading, then error, then empty.
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`; `data-refetching` mirrors `refetching`; `data-error` is set while an error shows
- `data-interactive` on a row that is a link or a button
- Bar width: `value / max`, at least 2% when the value is above zero, 0 when it is zero

## Accessibility

- The root is an `<ol>` named by `ariaLabel`; each row is an `<li>` whose text reads "name, value" in order. The bar is decorative.
- A link row is a native `<a>`; a clickable row is a native `<button>`; a static row is neither, and is not focusable.
- Keyboard map: Tab moves between interactive rows; Enter activates (Space too on buttons).
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface)` on interactive rows (the offset takes the surface color, so it never shows as a white gap in the dark theme).
- `aria-busy` on the root while `loading` or `refetching`.
- Name and value text clear 4.5:1 on the tinted fill and on the bare surface in both themes.
- Interactive rows are 32px tall and full width; a transparent hit area (`before:` pseudo-element, 4px above and below) makes the pointer target 40px without changing the look.
- Forced colors: the bar fill keeps its colour (`forced-color-adjust: none`); forced to `Canvas` it vanished and left only the labels (`src/test/forced-colors-charts.test.ts`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'

  const items = [
    { name: '/home', value: 843 },
    { name: '/documentation', value: 384 },
    { name: '/blocks', value: 108 },
    { name: '/imprint', value: 46 },
    { name: '/cancellation', value: 3 }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <BarList
      aria-label="Top paths"
      :items="items"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/bar-list.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/bar-list.md).
