# Timestamp

> Timestamp shows one moment — when a request ran, a deployment finished, a key was created — in the form the reader needs: the local date and time, the same in UTC, or a relative phrase (`5 minutes ago`) that updates every minute. Activating it opens a small panel that lists the moment as UTC (ISO 8601), local time with its time zone, the reader's browser time when the app's time zone differs from it, the relative phrase and the raw value it was given, each with a copy button, so an operator can paste the exact value into a query or a ticket. It accepts a `Date`, an epoch in milliseconds or microseconds, or an ISO string, and reads the app-wide time zone from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`time-zone`), so an app-level time zone picker changes every timestamp at once. Use it anywhere outside a table: log details, cards, side panels, activity lines. `Table.CellTime` keeps its own author-plus-relative-time layout and shares the parsing and the relative phrasing with Timestamp.

- Import: `import Timestamp from '@aziontech/webkit/timestamp'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Timestamp to display a moment in time in the app's time zone, copyable; to pick a date use DatePicker or DateRangePicker.
- A detail panel, card or log line shows when something happened and people may need the exact or UTC value.
- An app lets people pick a display time zone and every absolute time must follow it.
- A list outside `Table` shows relative times that should stay current.

## Do

- Pass the value from your data as it comes (`'2026-11-14T12:04:31Z'`, `1794657871000`, or the microseconds a log store returns); do not pre-format it.
- Set the app's time zone once on `WebkitProvider` (`time-zone`) rather than on each Timestamp; use the `time-zone` prop only for a value that belongs to another zone (a schedule in the customer's zone).
- Use `format="relative"` for recent activity, `local` for audit records and logs, `utc` for values people compare across teams.
- In an example, a test or a server render, fix `now` on the provider and give a time zone, so the text does not depend on when or where it renders.

## Don’t

- A table column of modification times with the author → use `Table.CellTime` in a `#cell-<id>` slot.
- A date the person edits → use `date-picker` (one date) or `date-range-picker` (a range).
- A duration (`1.2 s`, `3 days`) → plain text formatted with `useLocale().formatNumber`; Timestamp is a point in time.

## Related

- `webkit-provider` — `time-zone` sets the zone every Timestamp below it reads; `now` fixes the reference time of relative phrases.
- `table` — `Table.CellTime` is the table preset for modification times; it shares Timestamp's parsing and relative phrasing.
- `copy-button` — the copy control on every row of the panel.
- `popover` — the panel Timestamp opens.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | The moment: a `Date`, an epoch in milliseconds (microseconds when the number has 15 digits or more), a numeric string, or an ISO string. Empty or unparseable renders a muted dash with no panel. |
| `format` | `'relative' \| 'local' \| 'utc'` | `'local'` | false | What the text shows: the relative phrase that updates every minute, the date and time in the time zone, or the date and time in UTC. The panel always lists every form. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | IANA time zone of the local time (`America/New_York`). Empty reads the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `time-zone`, then the browser's zone. |

## States

- `data-format` on the root mirrors `format`.
- `data-state` on the root: `open` while the panel shows, `closed` otherwise (from `Popover`).
- Invalid or empty `value`: the root shows a muted dash, renders no trigger and no panel, and carries `data-invalid`.
- Before mount, with no time zone from the prop or the provider, the text renders in UTC so the server and the first client render agree; after mount it switches to the browser's zone. With a time zone, server and client render the same text.
- The relative phrase reads the provider's `now` when set, else a shared clock that ticks each minute; under 45 seconds it reads `just now`, under an hour in minutes, beyond that in the largest whole unit.
- An unknown time zone name falls back to UTC instead of throwing.
- The browser row appears only after mount and only when the effective time zone differs from the browser's.

## Accessibility

- The text is a native `button` wrapping a `time` element whose `datetime` is the ISO 8601 UTC value; the button has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded` (from `PopoverTrigger`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the trigger; `Enter` or `Space` opens the panel; inside the panel `Tab` moves between the copy buttons and wraps back to the trigger; `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.
- The panel is a non-modal `dialog` named by a visually hidden title (`Timestamp details`); the rows are a description list (`dl`), so each value is read with its label.
- Every copy button is named after its row (`Copy UTC`, `Copy Local`); the copied state is announced by `CopyButton`.
- Visible focus: the trigger and the copy buttons draw the ring token.
- Contrast: `var(--text-default)` and `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface-raised)` are theme-guaranteed.
- `motion-reduce:*`: the panel and the hover colour transition both pair with a reduced-motion fallback.
- Touch target: the copy buttons use the `small` `IconButton` size with the row padding around them; the trigger is inline text and grows with the text it sits in.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-`/`pe-`, `gap`, `text-start`), so the panel rows mirror under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the copy glyph does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the ISO, local, browser and raw values render `dir="ltr"` so digits and separators keep their order; the trigger text is isolated with `dir="auto"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                  | English source      | Override prop |
| -------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| `timestamp.title`    | `Timestamp details` | —             |
| `timestamp.utc`      | `UTC`               | —             |
| `timestamp.local`    | `Local`             | —             |
| `timestamp.browser`  | `Your browser`      | —             |
| `timestamp.relative` | `Relative`          | —             |
| `timestamp.raw`      | `Raw value`         | —             |
| `timestamp.copy`     | `Copy {label}`      | —             |
| `timestamp.justNow`  | `just now`          | —             |

- Dates, times and relative phrases are formatted with `Intl` in the provider's locale (`useLocale().formatDate` and `formatRelativeTime`), with Latin digits.
- The UTC row is ISO 8601 and the raw row is the value as given; neither is translated.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: the trigger wraps with the surrounding text; the panel is at most `--container-xs` wide and long values wrap (`break-all`) instead of overflowing at 320 px.
- Touch: the trigger opens on tap; the panel closes on outside tap.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Timestamp from '@aziontech/webkit/timestamp'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'

  const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 14, 12, 10)
  const VALUE = '2026-11-14T12:04:31Z'
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    :now="NOW"
    time-zone="America/New_York"
  >
    <dl
      class="grid grid-cols-[auto_1fr] items-baseline gap-x-(--spacing-md) gap-y-(--spacing-sm) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)"
    >
      <dt class="text-label-sm text-(--text-muted)">Local</dt>
      <dd><Timestamp :value="VALUE" /></dd>
      <dt class="text-label-sm text-(--text-muted)">UTC</dt>
      <dd>
        <Timestamp
          :value="VALUE"
          format="utc"
        />
      </dd>
      <dt class="text-label-sm text-(--text-muted)">Relative</dt>
      <dd>
        <Timestamp
          :value="VALUE"
          format="relative"
        />
      </dd>
    </dl>
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tutorial-panel.md -->

# Tutorial Panel

> The guide that runs tutorials beside the real product. It lives in the page's tools or help region, lists the tutorials a reader can take, and while one runs it shows the tutorial's tasks and the reader's place in them. The steps themselves happen on the page: each step points at a `Hotspot` placed beside the real control, and the current step opens there in a popover. `TutorialPanel.Provider` wraps the whole page (the content and the tools region), holds the running tutorial and the current step, and is what the panel and every `Hotspot` read. It is the stateful layer over `help-panel`: the panel is a `HelpPanel` with its `Header`, and draws each tutorial with its own internal task list (6.0 moved the former `HelpPanel.TutorialPanelTutorial` and `HelpPanel.Task` here; `HelpPanel` no longer has a tutorial mode). Design call (M2.9, WP app-layout): neither the design sample nor the Console Kit has a guided tutorial, so the model is Cloudscape's tutorial panel, hotspot and annotation context, rebuilt on WebKit parts.

- Import: `import TutorialPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use TutorialPanel for guided tutorials whose steps point at real controls through Hotspot.
- A reader learns a product task by doing it on the real screen, step by step, with the instructions pointing at the control they need next.
- A product offers several tutorials in its help region and records which ones the reader finished.
- A first-run or onboarding flow guides the reader through a real create and deploy, not a mock.

## Do

- Wrap the whole page in `TutorialPanel.Provider`, so the panel and every hotspot share one state.
- Keep tutorials as data (`TutorialPanelTutorial[]`): the panel lists them and the hotspots on the page read the same steps. This is the one place a config array is right — the step content is shown away from where it is declared.
- One step, one control. Write the step title as the action (`Name the service`) and the content as one or two sentences.
- Place every `Hotspot` a tutorial names on the page that runs it. A step whose hotspot is missing still shows in the panel, and focus moves to it there.
- Set `completed` on a tutorial from what the product recorded (the `complete` event), not from a click.
- Bind `v-model:active` and `v-model:step` and persist them when a tutorial must survive a navigation.

## Don’t

- Static help beside the page, with no guided run → use `help-panel`.
- The step rail of a multi-step task in the app → use `stepper`, or `wizard` for a create flow with its footer.
- A multi-step create flow whose steps are forms in one surface → use `wizard`.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates inside a page → use `stepper`.
- A single tip pinned to one control → use `popover` or `hint`.
- An empty page that needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `hotspot` — the marker beside a real control; the current step opens from it. Every step names one by `hotspotId`.
- `help-panel` — the parts the panel draws with; use it alone for help without a guided run.
- `popover` — what a hotspot opens; the step's title, content and Previous / Next live in it.
- `drawer` — the host of the tools region on narrow screens; the panel goes inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The panel's heading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Tutorials`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One line under the heading. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the panel's landmark. Empty uses the title. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the tutorials load. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completion` | { tutorial: TutorialPanelTutorial } | Extra content on the completion screen, such as a feedback link. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-provider`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: `index.ts` attaches the provider to the panel, so
`<TutorialPanel.Provider>` resolves from the same import. The panel has no open state (the tools region
that hosts it owns that), so there is no `Trigger` / `Content`. State flows through `provide`/`inject`
(`injection-key.ts`, provided by the provider): the panel reads it through
`composables/use-tutorial-panel-context.ts`, which throws outside a provider, and `Hotspot` reads it through
the optional variant, which returns null so a hotspot outside a provider renders only its content.

- `tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue` — Holds the tutorials, the running tutorial (`v-model:active`), the current step (`v-model:step`, flat across tasks), whether the reader dismissed the current step…
  - Props: `tutorials?: TutorialPanelTutorial[]` (default `[]`).
  - Models (`defineModel`): `v-model:active` (`string \| null`, default `null` — the parent owns it when bound, the provider keeps it locally when not), `v-model:step` (`number`, default `0`, same rule; equals the step count once the tutorial is finished).
  - Events: `update:active` (`string \| null`) and `update:step` (`number`) from the models; `start` (`(event: Event, id: string)` — the tutorial id, on Start and Restart), `exit` (`(event: Event, id: string)` — on Exit or Back to tutorials), `complete` (`(event: Event, id: string)` — on Finish of the last step). Each fires from a button the reader activated (in the panel or a `Hotspot` popover, through the context), so the DOM event comes first and the tutorial id second.
  - Slot: `default` — the page, with the panel and every hotspot inside.

- `parts/tutorial-panel-tasks.vue` — internal, not exported: a tutorial's title, description, a progress line derived from the registered tasks (`2 of 3 complete`, `aria-live="polite"`), the ordered task `<ol>` and an a…
- `parts/tutorial-panel-task.vue` — internal, not exported: one task, a numbered marker, a title and its steps.

Exported types: `TutorialPanelTutorial` (`id`, `title`, `description?`, `completed?`, `tasks`), `TutorialPanelTaskData` (`title`, `steps`), `TutorialPanelStep` (`title`, `content`, `hotspotId`).

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/tutorial-panel/
├── tutorial-panel.vue                    (root; the panel views)
├── tutorial-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                              (compound: attaches Provider)
├── injection-key.ts                      (types + TutorialContext)
├── composables/
│   ├── use-tutorial-panel-context.ts           (strict and optional injectors)
│   └── use-tutorial-panel-tasks-context.ts     (task registry; throws outside the task list)
├── tutorial-panel-provider/
│   └── tutorial-panel-provider.vue
├── tutorial-panel-tasks/
│   └── tutorial-panel-tasks.vue          (internal)
└── tutorial-panel-task/
    └── tutorial-panel-task.vue           (internal)
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./tutorial-panel": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/index.ts",
"./tutorial-panel-root": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel.vue",
"./tutorial-panel-provider": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue"
```

Composed DS components (relative imports): `help-panel` (root, `Header`), `button`, `empty-state`, `tag`.

## States

- Visual states: `list`, `running`, `complete`, `empty` (no tutorials, rendered by a small `EmptyState` titled with `tutorialPanel.emptyTitle`), `loading`
- `data-view` on the root: `list` | `running` | `complete`
- `data-completed` on each list item mirrors the tutorial's `completed`
- In `running`, each task's status is derived from the current step: `success` when every step of the task is behind it, `pending` otherwise; the task that holds the current step is `active`. The current step's row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- `complete` shows a completion section (check icon, `TutorialPanelTutorial complete`, `You finished <title>.`, the `completion` slot, Restart and Back to tutorials) above the task list, every task complete.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the composed `Button`s carry the standard ring; focus targets that are not controls (the list heading, the completion heading, the current step row) take `tabindex="-1"` and `outline-none` because they receive focus only programmatically.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through Start / Restart, Exit, Restart and Back. Focus management: Start moves focus to the current step's popover (through its hotspot) or, when that hotspot is not on the page, to the step's row in the panel; Finish moves focus to the `TutorialPanelTutorial complete` heading; Exit and Back move focus to the list's heading.
- ARIA: the panel is a `HelpPanel` complementary landmark named by `ariaLabel` or the title. Each list item's Start button is described by its tutorial's heading (`aria-describedby`), so repeated buttons are distinct. The task progress line is `aria-live="polite"`. The current step row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on muted ink over `--bg-surface` in both themes.
- Touch target: the composed `Button`s (small) meet 24 px; the panel adds no other control.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; every row is a flex row that follows `dir`.
- Icons: `ai ai-circle-check` (not mirrored), `ai ai-log-out` on Exit (not mirrored; it names the action, not a direction).
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                                  | English source                                                | Override prop |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `tutorialPanel.title`                | `Tutorials`                                                   | `title`       |
| `tutorialPanel.description`          | `Learn the product by doing a real task, one step at a time.` | `description` |
| `tutorialPanel.listLabel`            | `Available tutorials`                                         | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.emptyTitle`           | `No tutorials yet.`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.start`                | `Start tutorial`                                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.restart`              | `Restart tutorial`                                            | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.exit`                 | `Exit tutorial`                                               | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.back`                 | `Back to tutorials`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completed`            | `Completed`                                                   | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completedTitle`       | `TutorialPanelTutorial complete`                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completedDescription` | `You finished {title}.`                                       | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.taskCount`            | `{count} task` / `{count} tasks`                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.stepCount`            | `{count} step` / `{count} steps`                              | —             |

- Formatting: plurals through `Intl.PluralRules` (the catalog's plural messages); tutorial content is the consumer's own text.

## Responsive

- Container queries: inherits `@container/help-panel` from `HelpPanel`; no breakpoint of its own — the list and the task rows stack at every width.
- Narrow: the panel goes inside a `Drawer` (the tools region on phones); its content reflows to the drawer width.
- Touch: targets are the composed small `Button`s (≥ 24 px; the drawer host gives them room).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; titles wrap.

<!-- components/card-list.md -->

# Card List

> Use CardList to show a collection of records as selectable cards instead of table rows; for one bordered box use Card, and for the frame of a dashboard chart use ChartCard. A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It follows Cloudscape's collection model — `items`, `itemKey`, `selectedKeys` (a key array) — which is not yet the same as Table's (`data`, `rowKey`, `rowSelection` record); `useCollection` binds it through `cardListProps`, and selection (single or multiple, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.

- Import: `import CardList from '@aziontech/webkit/card-list'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
- The card form of a list page (`view/card-view`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.

## Do

- Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
- Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
- Use `selectionMode="multiple"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.
- Pass items typed with your own interface (`Domain[]`): the slots read `item.name` with that type, so never cast `item` in a slot or widen the items to `Record<string, unknown>[]`.

## Don’t

- Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
- A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
- A single content box → use `card`.

## Related

- use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardListProps` is the binding.
- `table` — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
- `property-filter`, `collection-preferences`, `pagination` — the controls around it.
- `card` — one standalone card.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TItem[]` | `[]` | false | The items, one card each. |
| `itemKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field that identifies an item; selection keys read it. |
| `selectionMode` | `'none' \| 'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'none'` | false | No selection, one card, or several cards with a select-all above them. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards and sets aria-busy while true. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `selectedKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | CardListItemSlotProps<TItem> | Card title; names the card and its selection control. |
| `default` | CardListItemSlotProps<TItem> | Card body: the item's fields. |
| `empty` | — | Shown when there are no items. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:selected-keys`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Keys (`item[itemKey]`) of the selected cards; keys of items not on the current page are kept.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `selected`, `loading`, `empty`
- `data-state` on each card: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` when selected
- `data-selection` on the root mirrors `selectionMode`; `aria-busy` while loading

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the checkbox, the radio and the links in the header slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the select-all, each card's control and its content; `Space` toggles a control.
- ARIA: the cards are a named `list` of `listitem`s; each checkbox is labelled by its card's header (`aria-labelledby`), and in single mode each card's `RadioGroup.Item` has no label text and forwards `aria-labelledby` (the header id) to its radio; the select-all has a visible label; the root sets `aria-busy` while loading.
- Selection is never conveyed by color alone: the control is checked.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) and ≥3:1 for the selected border.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the checkbox and the single-mode radio both sit at the end of the header row.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: the slots isolate user data (`<bdi>` around domains in the examples).

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source              | Override prop |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `cardList.label`            | Items                       | `ariaLabel`   |
| `cardList.selectAll`        | Select all items            | —             |
| `cardList.emptyTitle`       | No items yet                | `empty` slot  |
| `cardList.emptyDescription` | Items you create show here. | `empty` slot  |

- Formatting: none; the slots format the item's fields.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/card-list`; one column below `@xl` (644 px), two from `@xl`, three from `@4xl` (1024 px), four from `@6xl` (1388 px), so a card is never narrower than about 310 px.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): one card a row at full width.
- Touch: the checkbox and radio grow their hit area on `pointer: coarse` (from the inputs); nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/collection-preferences.md -->

# Collection Preferences

> The preferences panel of a collection, after Cloudscape's collection preferences: a cog button opens a dialog (or a drawer) with the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; a locked column always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density. Changes are a draft until Confirm; Cancel, `Esc` and the close button discard them. It holds no saved state itself: `useCollection` saves the confirmed value in `localStorage` and `preferencesProps` binds the value, the columns and the page sizes in one `v-bind`. It is the one column chooser of a table. Placed in a DataTable's `toolbar` slot with no `columns`, it reads the table through context: the columns are the table's hideable leaf columns (a column with `hideable: false` is listed locked), the draft starts from the table's column visibility and order, and Confirm writes both back to the table (`update:columnVisibility`) besides emitting `confirm` and `update:preferences`. Bound to `useCollection`, `preferencesProps` supplies `columns` and the context is not read.

- Import: `import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CollectionPreferences for every 'how this list looks' setting: page size, visible and ordered columns, density, wrap.
- A table or card collection whose people choose how many items a page shows and which fields they see.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, which saves the result per collection.

## Do

- Lock the column that names the item (`locked: true`): a row without its name is unreadable.
- Show only the sections the collection uses (`sections`): cards have no striped rows.
- Keep the trigger at the end of the controls row, after Refresh and Download.

## Don’t

- Settings of the resource itself (not of how the list shows it) → use a form page or `dialog`.

## Related

- use-collection` — saves the preferences; `preferencesProps` is the binding.
- `data-table` — takes `density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`, the visible columns and their order; inside its toolbar this panel edits its columns with no wiring.
- `card-list` — takes the page size and the visible fields.
- `property-filter` — sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `CollectionPreferencesColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns to show, hide and order. Empty reads the enclosing DataTable's columns, or hides the columns section outside one. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Page sizes offered. Empty hides the page size section. |
| `sections` | `CollectionPreferencesSection[]` | `['page-size', 'columns', 'wrap-lines', 'striped', 'density']` | false | Sections the panel shows, in this order. |
| `container` | `'dialog' \| 'drawer'` | `'dialog'` | false | Opens in a centered dialog or a side drawer. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Panel title and trigger label. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |
| `preferences` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:preferences`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: CollectionPreferencesValue)` | Same value, for a handler that is not a model. |
| `cancel` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Cancel was activated; the draft is discarded. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open: () => void } | Replaces the cog button; call `open` to open the panel. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `undefined`, via `defineModel('open')`. Whether the panel is open; the trigger, Confirm, Cancel, the close button and `Esc` update it. Unbound, the panel keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`.
- **`v-model:preferences`** — `CollectionPreferencesValue`, default `{}`, via `defineModel('preferences')`. Set on Confirm with the sections shown (`update:preferences`). Unbound, the panel keeps the confirmed values itself, so it reopens on them.

## States

- Visual states: `closed`, `open`; the trigger reflects `disabled`
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed`
- Move up is disabled on the first column, move down on the last; a locked column's switch is disabled and on, and its label carries `data-locked` (muted, default cursor)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the buttons, switches, radios and the toggle group.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens; `Tab` is trapped in the panel; `Esc` closes; focus returns to the trigger on close; after a move, focus stays on the moved column's button.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a dialog named by its title; the page size and the columns are `fieldset`s with a `legend`; each move button is named `Move <column> up|down`; the density group is labelled by its heading.
- Columns reorder with buttons, never by drag only (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`); the drawer opens from its own side logic.
- Icons: the up and down arrows are vertical and not mirrored; the cog is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: column labels are plain text; none.

## Internationalization

| Key                                                       | English source                                  | Override prop |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `collectionPreferences.title`                             | Preferences                                     | `title`       |
| `collectionPreferences.confirm` / `cancel`                | Confirm / Cancel                                | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.pageSize`                          | Page size                                       | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.pageSizeOption`                    | {count} item / {count} items (plural)           | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.columns`                           | Columns                                         | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.columnsDescription`                | Choose which columns show, and their order.     | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.alwaysShown`                       | Always shown                                    | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.moveUp` / `moveDown`               | Move {column} up / Move {column} down           | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.wrapLines` (+ `Description`)       | Wrap lines / Show the whole text of every cell. | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.striped` (+ `Description`)         | Striped rows / Shade every other row.           | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.density`, `comfortable`, `compact` | Density, Comfortable, Compact                   | —             |

- Formatting: page sizes go through the plural rules and number format of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/preferences` on the sections and `@container/preferences-actions` on the footer (`@md`: buttons side by side).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the dialog becomes a bottom sheet (from `dialog`), the footer buttons stack at full width.
- Touch: radios and column rows are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long column labels truncate.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const columns = [
    { id: 'name', label: 'Name', locked: true },
    { id: 'status', label: 'Status' },
    { id: 'region', label: 'Region' },
    { id: 'requests', label: 'Requests' }
  ]

  const preferences = ref({
    pageSize: 25,
    columns: [
      { id: 'name', visible: true },
      { id: 'status', visible: true },
      { id: 'region', visible: false },
      { id: 'requests', visible: true }
    ],
    wrapLines: false,
    striped: false,
    density: 'comfortable'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <CollectionPreferences
    v-model:preferences="preferences"
    :columns="columns"
    :page-size-options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/data-grid.md -->

# Data Grid

> An editable, spreadsheet-like grid: rows of records and typed columns where people move a cell cursor with the keyboard, edit cells in place, select ranges and copy them, the way an SQL editor's results and a database table editor work. It shares the table's visual language (header band, row dividers, row selection, a pinned first column, the same tokens) but renders the WAI-ARIA **grid** pattern (`role="grid"`, `gridcell`, one roving tab stop), not a read-only table. **Why a component of its own.** DataGrid is not an `editable` mode of `data-table` and is not composed from `table`'s parts, for three reasons. Table's parts render the **table** pattern (`role="table"`, `cell`, every link and button its own tab stop), while a grid needs `gridcell`s inside one roving tab stop with a cell cursor; switching the roles and the focus model inside the same parts would make every read-only table pay for it. In-cell editors must be borderless and fill the cell, so they are a bare `input` and `select` styled with the tokens, not the package's `Input` and `Select`, whose frames and overlays fight a 40 px cell. And DataGrid needs no sorting, filtering or paging engine: it loads no `@tanstack/vue-table` and no virtualization library, so an editing screen stays at about 9 KB. **The rows are the edited value.** Where `data-table` takes `data` and only emits `update:data` when rows are reordered, DataGrid's rows are what the person edits, so they are its `v-model`: every committed edit writes a new array with a copy of the edited row, and `change` reports the cell, the new value and the previous one. Adding and deleting rows are hooks: the grid emits `row-add` and `row-remove` and the app changes the rows. Thousands of rows scroll natively inside `maxHeight`, each row is laid out lazily with CSS `content-visibility: auto`, and each row re-renders only when its cells, its cursor or its range change.

- Import: `import DataGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/data-grid'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DataGrid only when people edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style; for a short list of rows in a form use AttributeEditor, for read-and-act lists use DataTable (a hand-composed Table for small static ones).
- A database table editor or the editable results of a query: typed cells (text, number, boolean, a choice), keyboard-first editing, copy of a cell range.
- Bulk corrections across rows, where opening a drawer per record would be slower than editing the cells.

## Do

- Give every row a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`): the cursor, the selection and the edits follow it.
- Type each column (`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `select`) so the editor matches the value; mark computed or key columns `editable: false`.
- Freeze the first column (`frozen-first-column`) when it names the row and the grid scrolls sideways.
- Keep adding and deleting in the app: handle `row-add` and `row-remove`, then write the new rows to the `v-model`. Confirm a delete of more than a few rows in a `confirm-dialog`.
- Use `readonly` while saving or for people who may not edit; the cursor, selection and copy still work.

## Don’t

- People read, sort, filter, select and act on records but do not edit cells → use `data-table` (or a hand-composed `table`).
- A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
- One record edited field by field → use a form with `field` controls.
- Key and value pairs shown for reading → use `key-value-list`.

## Related

- `data-table` — the read-and-act table (sorting, filters, paging, toolbar parts); DataGrid is its editable counterpart.
- `table` — the parts and tokens DataGrid shares its look with.
- `attribute-editor` — a few rows of the same fields inside a form.
- `collection-preferences` — the display preferences of a list; DataGrid's column widths are dragged in place instead.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `DataGridColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns in order: `{ id, header, type?, options?, editable?, width?, minWidth?, align? }`; `type` picks the editor (default text). |
| `rowKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field used as the stable row id (cursor, selection and edits follow it). |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Adds a leading checkbox column with Select all. |
| `frozenFirstColumn` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pins the first data column to the inline start edge while the grid scrolls sideways. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | No cell can be edited; the cursor, range selection and copy still work. |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length) of the scrolling viewport; the header stays on top. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the grid when no visible heading names it. |
| `modelValue` | `TRow[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `rowSelection` | `Record<string, boolean>` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:rowSelection`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `(event: Event, edit: DataGridCellEdit)` | A cell edit was committed (Enter, Tab, blur, a toggle); `edit` is `{ row, columnId, value, previous }`. |
| `row-add` | `(event: Event)` | The `add` function of the toolbar slot ran; the app appends a row to the `v-model`. |
| `row-remove` | `(event: Event, rows: TRow[])` | The `remove` function of the toolbar slot ran with rows selected; the app removes them from the `v-model`. |
| `copy` | `(event: ClipboardEvent, text: string)` | Ctrl+C or Cmd+C copied the selected cell range as tab-separated text (rows by line), also written to the clipboard. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolbar` | { selectedRows: TRow[]; selectedCount: number; add: (event: Event) => void; remove: (event: Event) => void } | Action band above the grid (add and delete buttons); `add` and `remove` emit the row hooks. |
| `empty` | — | Shown in place of the rows when there are none. Defaults to a small `EmptyState`. |

## v-model

| Model                   | Type                      | Default | Emits                 | Notes                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model`               | `TRow[]`                  | `[]`    | `update:modelValue`   | The rows. A committed edit writes a new array with a copy of the edited row.                                            |
| `v-model:row-selection` | `Record<string, boolean>` | `{}`    | `update:rowSelection` | Selected row ids (the same shape as DataTable's `rowSelection`). Space on the checkbox column and Select all change it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row), `focus-visible` (the cursor ring on the active cell or header), `selected` (cells in the range: `data-selected`, `aria-selected="true"`; rows checked: `data-state="selected"`), `editing` (`data-editing` on the cell with the editor open), `readonly` (`data-readonly` on the root; non-editable cells carry `aria-readonly`).
- `invalid`: a number cell whose text is not a number stays in its editor on Enter or Tab, with `data-invalid` on the cell and the editor, `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing to a message (`dataGrid.invalidNumber`, `role="alert"`) under the cell; nothing is committed until the text parses or Escape restores the value. Blur with an invalid text discards it and keeps the previous value.
- `empty`: no rows, the `empty` slot (default `EmptyState`, `dataGrid.emptyTitle`) under the header, outside the grid's rows; the header and toolbar stay.
- No `disabled` state: a grid people may not edit is `readonly` (the cursor, ranges and copy keep working). No `loading` or `error` state of its own: the app shows a `Skeleton` or an `Alert` around the grid while it loads; DataGrid never fetches.
- `data-frozen="start"` on the first column's cells with `frozenFirstColumn`; `data-resizing` on a header while its width is dragged.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: the WAI-ARIA APG **data grid**. The grid element is `role="grid"` with `aria-rowcount` (rows + header) and `aria-colcount`, named by `ariaLabel`, or by an `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` passed to DataGrid (both are forwarded to the grid element, not the frame), `aria-multiselectable="true"` (a cell range can always be selected) and `aria-readonly="true"` while `readonly`. Rows are `role="row"` with `aria-rowindex` (1-based, header is 1) and `aria-selected` when row selection is on; header cells `role="columnheader"`, body cells `role="gridcell"`, each with `aria-colindex`; every gridcell carries `aria-selected` (`true` in the range, `false` outside it) and a cell that cannot be edited `aria-readonly="true"`. The empty state renders outside the grid's rows, so `aria-rowcount` stays exact.
- One tab stop: exactly one cell of the grid has `tabindex="0"` (the active cell, the first body cell at start; the header row is part of the cursor), every other cell, checkbox and resize handle `-1`. `Tab` enters the grid on the active cell and `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leave it. The editor inside a cell takes focus while editing and returns it to the cell when it closes.
- Keyboard map (cell cursor): `Arrow` keys move one cell, up into the header row and back (inline arrows follow the reading direction); `Home` / `End` the first / last cell of the row; `Ctrl+Home` / `Ctrl+End` the first / last cell of the grid; `PageUp` / `PageDown` ten rows; `Shift` with an arrow, `Home` or `End` extends the range over body cells; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leave the grid. `Enter` or `F2` opens the editor of a body cell and, on a header cell, moves focus to its resize handle; typing a character opens a text or number editor with that character (select and boolean cells do not open on typing); `Space` toggles a boolean cell, the row checkbox, or Select all on its header; `Delete` / `Backspace` clears an editable text or number cell; `Ctrl+C` / `Cmd+C` copies the range; `Ctrl+A` / `Cmd+A` selects every cell.
- Keyboard map (editing): `Enter` commits and moves down; `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` commit and move to the next / previous cell (wrapping across rows), the one case where Tab moves inside the grid; `Escape` cancels and restores the value; blur commits. A select editor is a native `select`: its arrow keys change the choice without committing, and Enter, Tab or blur commit it. An invalid number keeps the editor open (see States).
- Row checkboxes are named after the row: `dataGrid.selectRow` (`Select row {row}`) filled with the first column's text, else the row key.
- Resize handles are `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow` (the width in px), `aria-valuemin` (`minWidth`, 64 by default), `aria-valuemax` (960) and a name (`dataGrid.resize`: `Resize Name`); they are reached with Enter from their header cell, `Arrow Left` / `Arrow Right` change the width by 16 px, and `Escape` or `Enter` return focus to the header cell.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` inset on the active cell or header; the editor uses the same ring (`--danger-border` while invalid).
- Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for text (muted header text included); the selected surface keeps the text contrast.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch: cells and headers are 40 px high, 44 px under `pointer: coarse`; tapping a cell moves the cursor there, a second tap opens the editor; the resize handle has a 24 px hit area, 44 px under `pointer: coarse`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`start-0`, `ps-` / `pe-`, `text-start` / `text-end`, `border-e`); the frozen first column pins to the inline start edge, and the resize handle sits on the inline end edge of each header.
- Icons: none of its own; the row checkbox and the empty state are the package's components.
- Keyboard: `Arrow Left` / `Arrow Right` follow the reading direction (`logicalArrowKey`): under `dir="rtl"` `Arrow Left` moves to the next cell; a resize handle's `Arrow Right` widens under `ltr` and `Arrow Left` widens under `rtl`.
- User data: cell text renders in a `<bdi>`, so ids, domains and numbers keep their own direction.

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source                | Override prop |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------- |
| `dataGrid.selectAll`        | `Select all rows`             | —             |
| `dataGrid.selectRow`        | `Select row`                  | —             |
| `dataGrid.resize`           | `Resize {column}`             | —             |
| `dataGrid.invalidNumber`    | `Enter a number`              | —             |
| `dataGrid.emptyTitle`       | `No rows yet`                 | `empty` slot  |
| `dataGrid.emptyDescription` | `Add a row to start editing.` | `empty` slot  |
| `dataGrid.true`             | `Yes`                         | —             |
| `dataGrid.false`            | `No`                          | —             |

- Formatting: `number` cells render with `Intl.NumberFormat` in the locale of the nearest `WebkitProvider`; the editor and the copied text use the raw number. Strings come from the locale catalog through `useTranslate` (`dataGrid` group).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: the grid is a two-dimensional surface that keeps its columns at every width.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the viewport scrolls sideways inside the grid, with the frozen first column still in view; the toolbar wraps.
- Touch: cells and headers are 44 px high under `pointer: coarse` (40 px otherwise); the resize handle's hit area is 44 px under `pointer: coarse` (24 px otherwise); editing opens on a second tap; nothing is hover-only.
- Reflow: a data grid is the WCAG 1.4.10 exception for two-dimensional content: the grid scrolls horizontally inside its frame, never the page.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DataGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/data-grid'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const rows = ref([
    { id: '1', name: 'Acme Inc.', plan: 'business', seats: 12, active: true },
    { id: '2', name: 'Jane Doe', plan: 'free', seats: 1, active: true },
    { id: '3', name: 'John Smith', plan: 'pro', seats: 3, active: false },
    { id: '4', name: 'Priya Patel', plan: 'pro', seats: 5, active: true },
    { id: '5', name: 'Sam Lee', plan: 'free', seats: 1, active: false }
  ])

  const columns = [
    { id: 'name', header: 'Name', type: 'text', width: 200 },
    {
      id: 'plan',
      header: 'Plan',
      type: 'select',
      options: [
        { label: 'Free', value: 'free' },
        { label: 'Pro', value: 'pro' },
        { label: 'Business', value: 'business' }
      ]
    },
    { id: 'seats', header: 'Seats', type: 'number', align: 'end', width: 120 },
    { id: 'active', header: 'Active', type: 'boolean', width: 120 },
    { id: 'id', header: 'ID', editable: false, width: 96 }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <DataGrid
    v-model="rows"
    :columns="columns"
    aria-label="Customers"
    frozen-first-column
  />
</template>
```
