# Pagination

> Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the `Table` component.

- Import: `import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Pagination to page through the rows of a table or list; alternative versions of one AI response use ResponseBranches.
- A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
- You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
- The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Description`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.

## Do

- Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `active` / `disabled` state and every click.
- page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
- Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
- Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
- Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

## Don’t

- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
- It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-previous-next`.
- The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.

## Related

- `table` — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
- `doc-previous-next` — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `total` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Total item count. When set, the Pagination runs in data-driven mode and renders its own controls. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` | false | Page-size options offered in the rows-per-page selector. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | false | Page numbers shown on each side of the current page before collapsing into an overflow ellipsis. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Pagination`). |
| `page` | `number` | `1` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:page`). |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:pageSize`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | — | Left region: page-info text (typically PaginatorInfo). In data-driven mode, overrides the default "Showing X to Y of Z entries" text. |
| `default` | — | Center region: pagination navigation buttons (composition mode only — ignored in data-driven mode, where the buttons are rendered internally). |
| `controls` | — | Right region: rows-per-page selector (PaginatorPageSize). In data-driven mode, overrides the internally-rendered selector. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-page-size`

## Sub-components

- `pagination-button/pagination-button.vue` — one segment of the numbers strip, 28px tall with a 28px minimum width and no horizontal padding; it carries no radius of its own except the outer corners at the two ends of…
- `pagination-description/pagination-description.vue` — muted page-info text container (default slot), `.text-body-xs` / `var(--text-muted)`.
- `pagination-page-size/pagination-page-size.vue` — rows-per-page selector (native `<select>`), 64×28 (same height as the numbers strip), `var(--shape-control)` radius, `var(--bg-canvas)` frame over a `var(--bg-surface)…

## v-model

| Model               | Type     | Default | Emits             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:page`      | `number` | `1`     | `update:page`     | Current page, 1-based (data-driven mode), via `defineModel('page')`. Previous / Next / a page number / Arrow keys change it. Unbound, the Pagination keeps the page itself (uncontrolled), so it still moves. |
| `v-model:page-size` | `number` | `10`    | `update:pageSize` | Rows per page (data-driven mode), via `defineModel('pageSize')`. Changing it through the selector also resets the page to `1`. Unbound, the Pagination keeps the size itself.                                 |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, current page (`active` prop), `disabled`
- The page buttons render as one **segmented strip**: a single container carrying the `var(--border-default)` border and the `var(--shape-control)` radius, with the buttons butted against each other at zero gap. Only the two end buttons round their outer corners.
- `data-type` on PaginationButton: `previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are mutually exclusive: pressing a button drops the hover layer and shows the `var(--bg-active)` layer alone, so the pressed surface reads one step below hover.
- `data-active` on PaginationButton mirrors the current-page `active` prop; `aria-current="page"` set when active.
- `data-disabled` on PaginationButton mirrors the `disabled` prop; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled` set.
- Data-driven mode: `Previous` is disabled on the first page, `Next` on the last; the current page button is `active` (`aria-current="page"`); the overflow ellipsis (`more`) is non-interactive: an `aria-hidden` `span`, out of the tab order, that emits nothing.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/pagination`. The page list stays whole at every width (`siblingCount` already caps it at seven slots, e.g. `1 2 3 4 5 … 60`), so a phone footer reads the same numbered strip as a desktop one, as in the design sample; when the box is too narrow for the info text and the controls on one line, the strip and the page-size control wrap together under the info text, aligned to the end.
- Touch: the buttons and the page-size select are drawn at 28 px on every pointer. On a coarse pointer (`pointer-coarse:`) each button carries an invisible, `aria-hidden` hit area that extends it to 44 px tall (vertical only: the buttons are butted, so the width stays the drawn 28 px), and the select itself grows to 44 px tall inside its 28 px frame, which draws the border, surface and focus ring.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on every pagination button.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves across buttons and the rows-per-page selector; `Enter`/`Space` activates a button; disabled buttons and the overflow ellipsis are skipped. In data-driven mode, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` inside the button group go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection`).
- ARIA: root `<nav>` with `aria-label` (the `ariaLabel` prop); current-page button sets `aria-current="page"`; in data-driven mode each number button is named from the locale catalog (`pagination.page`, "Page 3") instead of the bare digit; disabled buttons set the `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled`; icon glyphs and the overflow ellipsis are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: each button is drawn 28×28 (above the 24×24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8) so the strip stays compact in a table footer; on a coarse pointer its hit area grows to 28×44 invisibly and the page-size select's to its full width × 44. The width cannot grow because the buttons are butted with no gap; growing the drawn size instead was rejected because it turned the phone footer into an oversized strip that no longer matched the design sample.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`).
- Keyboard: in data-driven mode `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <template #info>
      <Pagination.Description>Showing 1 to 10 of 20 entries</Pagination.Description>
    </template>

    <Pagination.Button
      type="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <Pagination.Button
      type="number"
      active
      >1</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button type="number">2</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button type="number">3</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button type="more" />
    <Pagination.Button
      type="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />

    <template #controls>
      <Pagination.PageSize
        :model-value="10"
        :options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
      />
    </template>
  </Pagination>
</template>
```

<!-- components/pagination-button.md -->

# Pagination Button

> PaginationButton is one segment of the pagination's numbers strip: a 28px-tall native `button` that renders a page number or a Previous / Next chevron, or — for `type="more"` — an inert, decorative overflow ellipsis (`span`, `aria-hidden`), chosen by `type`. It is the part `pagination` renders in data-driven mode and the one consumers compose by hand in composition mode, where it is reached as `Pagination.Button` (or imported standalone from `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`). It owns the segment's surface, current-page (`active`) and `disabled` treatment, but not the strip's frame, border or the page state, which belong to the `pagination` root and the consumer.

- Import: `import PaginationButton from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Compose a custom page strip inside `pagination`'s default slot (composition mode), one button per Previous, page number, overflow and Next.
- Render the current page of a hand-wired pagination with `active`, and the unavailable Previous / Next ends with `disabled`.

## Do

- Place it only inside `pagination`'s default slot: the strip's border and frame come from the root, and the outer radius is applied through `first:` / `last:`, so only the first and last buttons of the strip round their corners.
- Pass `aria-label` on every `previous` and `next` button: those types render an `aria-hidden` icon only and have no accessible name otherwise. `more` is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so it takes no `aria-label`.
- Put the page number in the default slot of `type="number"` only; the other types ignore the slot.
- Set `active` on exactly one number button (it sets `aria-current="page"`), and `disabled` on Previous at the first page and Next at the last.
- In composition mode you own every click: listen to `click` and update the page yourself; a `disabled` button never emits it.

## Don’t

- You know the item count → pass `total` to `pagination` and bind `v-model:page`; it renders and wires every PaginationButton itself.
- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table instead.
- The control is a previous / next link between documentation pages → use `doc-previous-next`.
- It is a standalone action outside a pagination strip → use `button` or `icon-button`; this button has no radius or frame of its own except at the strip's ends.
- It is a "Load more" control at the end of a list → use `button`.

## Related

- `pagination` — the root that frames the strip and, in data-driven mode, renders these buttons; re-exports this component as `Pagination.Button`.
- pagination-description` — the page-info text that sits beside the strip.
- pagination-page-size` — the rows-per-page selector placed in the pagination's `controls` slot.
- `icon-button` — a standalone icon-only action with its own frame and radius.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'previous' \| 'next' \| 'number' \| 'more'` | `'number'` | false | Button role within the pagination. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the current page (filled surface + aria-current). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | Fires on activation. Not emitted while `disabled` (the native `disabled` attribute also blocks it), and never for `type="more"`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page number. Rendered only when `type` is `number`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, current page (`active` prop), `disabled`.
- Root: a native `button` with `type="button"`, or a `span` with `aria-hidden="true"` when `type` is `more` (inert: not focusable, no hover / active layer, no `active` / `disabled` treatment, never emits `click`); attributes (including `aria-label` and `class`) are forwarded to it (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- `data-type` mirrors `type` (`previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`). `previous` renders `ai ai-chevron-left`, `next` renders `ai ai-chevron-right`, `more` renders `ai ai-ellipsis`; only `number` renders the default slot. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are two stacked pseudo-element layers (`before:` hover, `after:` active) and are mutually exclusive: pressing hides the hover layer and shows the active layer alone.
- `data-active` is present when `active` is set; it adds `var(--bg-selected)` and a `var(--border-default)` border, and sets `aria-current="page"`.
- `data-disabled` is present when `disabled` is set; the button also gets the native `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled="true"`, mutes the foreground to `var(--text-disabled)`, shows `cursor-not-allowed`, hides both state layers and keeps the type's own surface.
- Coarse pointer: a `number`, `previous` or `next` button renders an empty `aria-hidden` `span` (`data-slot="touch-target"`) that is shown only under `pointer-coarse:` and extends the hit area vertically to 44 px; the drawn button does not grow.
- Test ids: `<pagination testId>__button` when rendered inside a `pagination` (`data-pagination__button` by default), `data-pagination__button` outside one; a consumer `data-testid` wins.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: native button — `Tab` focuses; `Enter` / `Space` activates; a `disabled` button is skipped by `Tab`; the `more` ellipsis is a `span` and never receives focus.
- ARIA: `aria-current="page"` when `active`; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled="true"` when `disabled`; the chevron icons are `aria-hidden="true"`, so `previous` and `next` take their accessible name from a consumer `aria-label` (data-driven `pagination` sets one on both); the `more` ellipsis root is `aria-hidden="true"` and decorative, so it needs no name.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` / `var(--bg-selected)`; disabled uses `var(--text-disabled)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none`, `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:after:transition-none` on the state transitions.
- Touch target: drawn 28×28 on every pointer (above the 24×24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8); on a coarse pointer an invisible `aria-hidden` child (`data-slot="touch-target"`) extends the hit area to 28×44. The width stays 28 because the buttons are butted into the strip (see `pagination`). The inert `more` span has no hit area.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`).
- Keyboard: arrow keys are handled by `pagination`, swapped under `dir="rtl"`.
- User data: none.

## Usage

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
  import PaginationButton from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <PaginationButton
      type="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <PaginationButton
      type="number"
      active
      >1</PaginationButton
    >
    <PaginationButton type="number">2</PaginationButton>
    <PaginationButton type="more" />
    <PaginationButton
      type="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />
  </Pagination>
</template>
```

<!-- components/property-filter.md -->

# Property Filter

> One field that filters a collection by properties and free text, after Cloudscape's property filter. Typing suggests a property, then an operator, then a value, and each choice becomes a removable token (`Status = Active`); text typed without a property becomes a free-text token. Two or more tokens combine with Match all (and) or Match any (or). With `mode="query"` the same field edits one query string instead (`level = Error AND method = GET`), after the Console Kit events query bar: suggestions follow the word at the caret (a field, an operator, a value, then AND or OR), a check explains what is wrong under the field, and Enter submits the text with its flat token list. Since spec v4, tokens mode also builds one level of nested conditions (`grouped`: each group has its own Match all / Match any, and the groups combine with the query's operation — `(Status = Active or Status = Paused) and (Region = US East or Region = EU West)`), fetches the values of a property as the person types (`loadValues`, with a loading and an error row and a count per value), groups the operator suggestions (Equality, Comparison, Text match), and hands the value of a property marked `customValue` to the `value` slot (a date picker, a number range). It edits a `PropertyFilterQuery` and never filters anything itself: `useCollection` (or the server) applies the query, and `propertyFilterProps` binds the query, the properties and the match count in one `v-bind`.

- Import: `import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PropertyFilter when people type queries with operators (Status = Active, Requests > 100) or free text they want to keep.
- A list or table that people narrow by several fields at once (status, region, owner) and by text.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, client or server mode.
- Filters that must survive a reload or a shared link: the query serializes into the URL through `useCollection`.
- With `mode="query"`: an explorer (events, logs) whose users type queries by hand, keep and reuse them as text, or need a grammar of the product (pass `validate` and `suggest`).

## Do

- Give every property with a closed set of values its `options`, so values are suggested and tokens print labels.
- Set `type: 'number'` or `type: 'date'` on ordered properties to offer `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`.
- Bind `totalCount` so people hear how many items match after each change.
- Turn on `grouped` only when people need both and and or in one filter; most filters read better flat.
- Use `loadValues` when a property has too many values to ship (hostnames, users); return at most a few dozen per call, already filtered by the typed text, with `count` when the server knows it.
- Mark a property `customValue` when its value is easier to pick than to type (a date), and render the editor in the `value` slot; call `apply` with the value text.
- Name the field after the collection (`aria-label="Filter resources"`).
- In query mode, fields are written by `key` (no spaces); quote values that hold spaces or operator characters (`"edge cache"`). Apply the `query` of `submit` when it is not null; keep the `text` for saved and recent queries.
- A product grammar (`like`, `between`, parentheses) passes `validate` and `suggest`; `submit` then carries `query: null` for text the built-in grammar cannot flatten, and the product parses `text` itself.

## Don’t

- A single text search over a short list → use `input` bound to `filterProps`.
- A few fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or `chip` filters.
- Inside a DataTable toolbar, `Table.Filter type="property"` renders this field wired to the table's filters; bind PropertyFilter to `useCollection` yourself only for OR queries or free text.
- Faceted picks from a known set of values per field (status, region, owner), shown as chips → use `filter-menu`. PropertyFilter is for expression search: typed tokens, operators, free text and a query people keep as text.

## Related

- use-collection` — applies the query; `propertyFilterProps` is the binding.
- `table` — the collection it usually filters.
- `card-list` — the card form of a collection.
- `collection-preferences` — the panel that sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `properties` | `FilteringProperty[]` | `[]` | false | Properties the suggestions offer, with their operators and values. |
| `totalCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Items that match the query, announced next to the tokens. Hidden when unset. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `freeText` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Accepts typed text with no property as a free-text token. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field and the tokens. |
| `mode` | `'tokens' \| 'query'` | `'tokens'` | false | tokens` turns each choice into a token; `query` edits one query string. |
| `validate` | `(text: string) => string` | `undefined` | false | Checks the query string in query mode: '' when valid, else the message shown under the field. Replaces the built-in check. |
| `suggest` | `(text: string, caret: number) => PropertyFilterQuerySuggestion[]` | `undefined` | false | Suggestions for the word at the caret in query mode. Replaces the built-in field, operator, value and AND / OR suggestions. |
| `grouped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Tokens mode: tokens go into groups with their own Match all / Match any; Add group starts the next one. |
| `showOperations` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the Match all / Match any toggle; false keeps the tokens combined with AND (a model that holds only AND conditions, such as a table's filters). |
| `loadValues` | `(property: FilteringProperty, text: string) => Promise<PropertyFilterOption[]>` | `undefined` | false | Fetches the values of a property for the typed text, after the operator. Replaces its `options` in the suggestions. |
| `query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:query`). |
| `text` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:text`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: KeyboardEvent, payload: PropertyFilterSubmit)` | Enter with no active suggestion and a valid query; `event` is the Enter keydown. Query mode only. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | { property: FilteringProperty, operator: PropertyFilterOperator, apply: (value: string) => void } | Tokens mode. Rendered under the field, in a named `group`, once the typed text has a property marked `customValue` and an operator; `apply` adds the token and returns focus to the field. |

## v-model

| Model           | Type                  | Default                            | Emits          | Notes                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | `{ tokens: [], operation: 'and' }` | `update:query` | Via `defineModel('query')`. A token was added or removed, the operation changed, or all cleared. Tokens mode only. Unbound, the field keeps its own tokens. |
| `v-model:text`  | `string`              | `''`                               | `update:text`  | Via `defineModel('text')`. The query string changed (typing, a suggestion, Escape clearing). Query mode only. Unbound, the field keeps its own text.        |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible`, `open` (suggestions shown), `disabled`, `invalid` (query mode: after Enter or blur on a query that fails the check, then live until it passes or is cleared)
- `data-mode` on the field wrapper mirrors `mode`; query mode sets the typed text in the code type (`text-label-code-sm`)
- `aria-expanded` on the field mirrors the open suggestions; `data-active` marks the active option
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; while disabled nothing is added, removed or submitted (no `update:query`, no `submit`)
- `loading` (values): a `Loading values` row with a spinner in the suggestions while `loadValues` is pending, `aria-busy` on the listbox; `error`: a `Could not load values` row when it rejects. A newer call wins over a stale one.
- Grouped (`grouped`): each group is a bordered `group` (`data-testid="…__group"`); a pending new group shows a dashed `New group` chip until its first token.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the field's own `focus-within` ring (from `input`); tokens and buttons keep theirs.
- Keyboard map (query mode): typing opens the suggestions for the word at the caret; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option (it replaces the word and moves the caret after it) or submits the query; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`, `Home`/`End` and clicks move the caret and the suggestions follow it; `Backspace` only edits text.
- In query mode an invalid query sets `aria-invalid` on the field and `aria-describedby` to the message, which sits in a polite live region under the field; the token group is not rendered.
- Keyboard map (tokens mode): typing opens the suggestions; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option or commits the typed text; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last token (with `grouped`: cancels a pending new group first, then removes the last token of the last group).
- Operator suggestions sit in named `group`s (Equality, Comparison, Text match) inside the listbox; the arrows move across groups as one list.
- `grouped`: each group is a `group` named `Filter group <n>`; its Match all / Match any toggle is named `Combine filters in group <n>`; Add group is a button that returns focus to the field.
- `value` slot: its wrapper is a `group` named `Value of <property>`; the editor inside owns its own keyboard.
- ARIA: the field is a `combobox` (`aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`); the suggestions are a named `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected` on the active one; the tokens sit in a named `group`; each token's remove button is named `Remove <token>`; the match count is a `status` region.
- Option targets are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`, `ps-`/`pe-` from `input`); the suggestions anchor to the start edge of the field.
- Icons: the filter glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` are not direction-dependent.
- User data: suggestion labels sit in `<bdi>` so a value in another script does not reorder the line.
- Query mode: the query string keeps `dir="auto"` from `input`, so a Latin query stays left-to-right inside a right-to-left page; the message sits at the start and the match count at the end (`ms-auto`).
- Teleported content: the teleported suggestions listbox binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Internationalization

| Key                                                    | English source                                                                                | Override prop |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `propertyFilter.label`                                 | Filter                                                                                        | `ariaLabel`   |
| `propertyFilter.placeholder`                           | Filter by property or text                                                                    | `placeholder` |

| `propertyFilter.values`                                | Values                                                                                        | —             |

| `propertyFilter.and` / `or`                            | and / or                                                                                      | —             |

- Formatting: value counts use `Intl.NumberFormat` of the active locale; the match count goes through the plural rules and number format of the active locale (`Intl.PluralRules`, `Intl.NumberFormat`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/property-filter` on the root; the token row wraps.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the field takes the full width, tokens wrap onto several lines, the count moves to the end of the last line.
- Touch: options are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long tokens truncate inside the chip.

# Table

> The table's parts and its markup-only root. Compose the anatomy by hand (`Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.HeadCell` / `Table.Cell`): the component owns markup, tokens, accessibility, column sizing (an emphasized principal column), sortable headers, selectable rows and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (an actions column) and a sticky header. The root is light: it frames the scroll viewport, the toolbar band (`title` / `toolbar` slots) and the `footer`, and loads no table engine. For repeated records pass `data` + `columns` to `data-table` instead: DataTable renders through these same parts, and the context-aware toolbar parts (`Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.Export`, `Table.RefreshButton`, `Table.LiveButton`) and the cell presets (`Table.CellLink`, `Table.CellId`, `Table.CellStatus`, `Table.CellTags`, `Table.CellTime`, `Table.CellActions`) go in its slots. Inside a hand-composed `Table` the toolbar parts have no rows to act on. **Cell presets.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a cell (or a DataTable `#cell-<id>` slot): `Table.CellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `Table.CellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `Table.CellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `Table.CellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported by `./table`): the column and slot types DataTable takes (`TableColumn`, `TableCellSlotProps`, `TableHeaderSlotProps`, `TableToolbarSlotProps`, `TableStateSnapshot`, `TableExposed`, `TableAppliedFilter`, `TableFilterField`, `TableDensity`), so a page can type its columns from the compound it already imports. Their shapes are documented in `data-table`.

- Import: `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Table for records that share columns when you compose the rows by hand; for any console list of resources people scan, sort and act on, pass `data` + `columns` to DataTable, which renders through these parts.
- A small, static table, or one whose cells need a layout the column model cannot express: compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` by hand. The root loads no engine.
- The parts of a DataTable: the toolbar parts and cell presets go in its slots, imported from this compound (`Table.Search`, `Table.CellStatus`).
- Use Table for read-and-act content; for repeated records pass `data` + `columns` to `data-table`, and when people edit cells in place use `data-grid`.

## Do

- Compose `Table` by hand only for small, static tables; for repeated data use `data-table`, which renders through these parts.
- Mark the row-actions cell `type="action"` with `frozen="end"` so it pins to the trailing edge, and give the principal cell `principal` (or `grow="2"`).
- Name the table: a `Table.Caption` labels it (`aria-labelledby`), or pass `aria-label` on the root.
- Give `Table.CellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
- Import the root alone from `table-root`, or each part from its own entry (`table-row`), when only a few parts are used.

## Don’t

- Repeated records with sorting, selection, paging, filtering, virtual rows or tree rows → use `data-table` (`data` + `columns`).
- People edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
- A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
- A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
- A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `competitor-comparison`.
- Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
- A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-group` with `type="card"`.
- The same records as a grid of cards → use `card-list` (same collection, card layout).

## Related

- `data-table` — the data-driven table (`data` + `columns`, TanStack engine) that renders through these parts.
- `data-grid` — the editable, spreadsheet-like grid; a separate grid (`role="grid"`, one roving tab stop, in-cell editors) that shares these tokens, not built on these parts.
- `pagination` — the page strip; put it in a `Table.Footer` in the `footer` slot.
- `empty-state` — compose it in a full-width row when a hand-composed table has no rows.
- `item` — list rows without a column structure.
- `listing-table` — marketing section that composes a DataTable for a linked preview of a list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under a frozen header). |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); the internal row dividers are unaffected. |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | `'comfortable'` | false | Density of the body cells: `compact` shrinks their height and padding. Set `density` on `Table.Header` too for a compact header. |
| `wrapLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The scrollable region: `Table.Caption`, `Table.Header`, `Table.Body`. |
| `title` | — | Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport. |
| `toolbar` | — | Action band above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. |
| `footer` | — | Footer region rendered below the scroll viewport (`Table.Footer` + `Pagination`), so it never scrolls with the body. |

## Sub-components

- `table-header/table-header.vue` — `role="rowgroup"` header band.
- `table-body/table-body.vue` — `role="rowgroup"` body band.
- `table-footer/table-footer.vue` — footer band below the viewport, outside `role="table"` (hosts the Pagination); muted text.
- `table-caption/table-caption.vue` — caption / title line that names the table (`aria-labelledby`); `text-label-sm` muted.
- `table-row/table-row.vue` — `role="row"`, flex container.
- `table-head-cell/table-head-cell.vue` — `role="columnheader"`, height 44px.
- `table-cell/table-cell.vue` — `role="cell"`, min height 48px.
- `table-sort-button/table-sort-button.vue` — sort control used inside `table-head-cell`, rendered as the webkit `IconButton` (`variant="ghost"`, `size="small"` → 28×28) so size, padding, and alignment match the design…
- `table-toolbar/table-toolbar.vue` — flex container (end-aligned) for toolbar actions placed in the `toolbar` slot; injects the table context for its testId.
- `table-search/table-search.vue` — Use Table.Search for one free-text search over the table's rows.
- `table-filter/table-filter.vue` — Use Table.Filter only as the toolbar slot that hosts FilterMenu (`type="menu"`) or PropertyFilter (`type="property"`) wired to the table; it is not a third filter.
- `table-export-button/table-export-button.vue` — context-aware export control (an `IconButton`, download glyph, its name repeated on a `Tooltip`).
- `table-refresh-button/table-refresh-button.vue` — context-aware refresh control (an `IconButton`, refresh glyph).
- `table-live-button/table-live-button.vue` — context-aware live-tail toggle (a `Button`, outlined, label from the catalog `Live` with a leading dot that turns success-coloured and pulses while live, `motion-reduce:anim…
- `table-cell-link/table-cell-link.vue` — cross-resource link preset.
- `table-cell-id/table-cell-id.vue` — identifier preset: the value (`dir="ltr"`, tabular numbers, truncating) and a `CopyButton` pinned to the end edge named `Copy <resource> ID`.
- `table-cell-status/table-cell-status.vue` — status preset: one `Tag` (`size="medium"`, truncating).
- `table-cell-tags/table-cell-tags.vue` — tag list preset: rounded secondary tags, as many as fit the cell (measured with a `ResizeObserver` against a hidden ruler), the rest behind an `OverflowCount`.
- `table-cell-time/table-cell-time.vue` — last-modified preset: the author's `Avatar` (name on its tooltip; an email reads as a name) and a `<time datetime>` with the relative time (`just now` under 45 s), the absolute…
- `table-cell-actions/table-cell-actions.vue` — row actions preset: a `DropdownMenu` (`placement="bottom-end"`) triggered by an outlined ellipsis `IconButton` named `Actions for <name>`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `selected`
- The viewport is always a scroll container (`overflow: auto`): horizontal scroll is automatic when columns overflow; vertical scroll engages only when `maxHeight` constrains the content.
- `data-frozen` on TableHeader (`true`), TableHeadCell / TableCell (`start` | `end`), and TableRow (`true`). A frozen head/body cell renders a CSS-only fade (gradient pseudo-element) just outside its inner edge that dissolves the horizontally scrolling content into the row background (`from-transparent` → `var(--table-row-bg)`, the row-published color, so it matches the row on hover/selected) — `frozen=start` fades on the right, `frozen=end` on the left. The fade tints nothing; it only masks the content sliding under the pinned column.
- `data-state` on TableRow: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` mirrors the `selected` prop; `aria-selected` set when selected.
- `data-type` on TableHeadCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action` | `slot`) and TableCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action`).
- `data-align` on head/body cells: `start` | `center` | `end`.
- `data-grow` on head/body cells: `1` | `2` | `3` (flex weight).
- `data-sortable` and `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableHeadCell; `aria-sort` mirrors `data-sort`.
- `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableSortButton.
- `data-clickable` on TableCell mirrors the `clickable` prop.
- Density and wrapping: `data-density="compact"` on the root shrinks the body cells (`min-h-9`, `--spacing-2xs` block padding); `data-wrap` lets cell text (and any `.truncate` inside a cell) wrap. A compact header is `Table.Header density="compact"`.
- Responsive toolbar: the root is the `@container/table`; the toolbar wraps, and below `@md` of the table the `toolbar` slot moves under the title and starts at the start edge. `Table.Toolbar` wraps its controls.
- Hover-free devices: a sortable header shows its sort affordance where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the sort button and any interactive cell content.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the sort button of each sortable column (one tab stop per column, as in the APG sortable table: the header cell itself is not focusable and carries `aria-sort`) and interactive cell content; `Enter`/`Space` on the sort button toggles the sort; row click is mouse/touch (no keyboard trap). Body rows are not focusable, so `row-click` is never the only way to open a record: the principal column carries a real link or button (`Table.CellLink`, or the `cell-<id>` slot with an anchor, as the Default example does), which keyboard and screen-reader users reach instead (WCAG 2.1.1).
- ARIA: `role="table"` sits on the grid element inside the scroll viewport (testid `<testid>__table`), not on the root: the root also holds the toolbar band, the focusable scroll viewport and the footer, and any of those inside a `table` is an unallowed child (`aria-required-children`). Every `aria-*` attribute passed to `Table` (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`…) is forwarded to that element; every other attribute stays on the root. `table-caption` is a plain element (no `role`) that names the table through `aria-labelledby` unless the consumer names it with `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. The default slot is the table's content, so it holds rowgroups (and a caption) only; anything else goes in `footer` or around the `Table`. `table-header`/`table-body` `role="rowgroup"`; `table-footer` has no role (it hosts pagination or an action, not rows); `table-row` `role="row"`; `table-head-cell` `role="columnheader"` with `aria-sort` when sortable; `table-cell` `role="cell"`; selected rows set `aria-selected`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including muted header text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the sort button and row action controls.
- Filter names: `Table.Filter` hosts `FilterMenu` (its trigger counts the applied fields in its name) or `PropertyFilter` (a combobox named by `title`); see their specs.

    { id: '1005', name: 'Workload Echo', status: 'Inactive', editor: 'user5@example.com' }

    <Table.Header>
      <Table.Row>

<!-- components/topology-diagram.md -->

# Topology Diagram

> The deployment topology of a resource as a left-to-right diagram: each column is a depth (domains, project, policy, service, cache rules, integration, storage), each node a collapsible card with the resource kind, its status tag, its name and, when opened, a message and labelled fields; dashed connectors join every node of a column to the next. A node without a name is an unbound slot (dashed, Not bound) and a `bindable` node carries the bind control (bind an existing resource, change it, create one, remove it). Taken from the design sample's workload topology (`TopologyDiagramNodeData`, `TopologyNodeCard`, `TopologyBindNode`, `TopologyBindControl`, the empty node). It reuses `FlowDiagram`'s connector engine and anchors and draws its own list semantics, with no node-graph dependency.

- Import: `import TopologyDiagram from '@aziontech/webkit/topology-diagram'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The topology tab of a project, service or workload: what serves its traffic, in order, and what is still unbound.
- A review before a deploy where binding or removing a resource is staged on the diagram.

## Do

- Keep a column per depth and put the nodes that serve in parallel in the same column.
- Mark a staged change `dashed` with a warning status and a message that says the deploy applies it.
- Mark the last node of each branch `terminal` so no connector leaves it.
- Give every unbound slot a message that says what happens without it.
- Give a node `href` when its resource has a page: the name becomes a link that ends in the open glyph (`ai ai-external-link`), as every resource name in the console does.
- A node that collects many resources and adds to itself, such as Domains (add a domain), puts its `+` in the `actions` slot: an `IconButton` (`ai ai-plus`, `variant="outline"`, `size="small"`) named `Add domain` inside a `Tooltip`, picked by `node.id`. `bindable` is for a slot that holds one resource (Firewall, Custom Page): it brings its own `+` with the bind menu. Do not hand-draw a node card to get the `+`.

## Don’t

- A sequence of steps or a pipeline without data cards → use `flow-diagram`.
- A nested list of items with no flow between them → use `tree`.
- A marketing architecture picture → use `diagram`.

## Related

- `flow-diagram` — the connector engine and anchors this component reuses.
- `tree` — hierarchical data without connectors.
- `dropdown-menu` — the bind control's menu.
- detail/resource-detail` — the page whose topology tab holds it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | `TopologyDiagramLevel[]` | `[]` | false | Columns of the diagram, from the entry point to the last dependency. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards while the topology loads. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the diagram. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deployment topology`). |
| `openKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bind` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, binding: { id: string; value: string })` | An existing option was picked in the bind control; `id` is the node's id. |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, id: string)` | Remove was activated on a bound, removable node. |
| `create` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, id: string)` | Create was picked in the bind control. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | { node: TopologyDiagramNodeData } | Extra controls in a node's identity row, before the bind control. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default empty state (the package `EmptyState`, small, `topologyDiagram.emptyTitle`) shown when there are no levels. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:openKeys`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Ids of the open node cards; a header click toggles its id.

## States

- Root: `data-loading` and `aria-busy` while `loading`; empty when `levels` is empty, rendered as the package `EmptyState` (small) unless the `empty` slot replaces it.
- Node card: `data-state` `open` | `closed`; `data-dashed` for a staged or unbound node.
- Connectors: dashed, flowing; faded never (no disabled nodes).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: header buttons `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`; the scroll area when it scrolls.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through header buttons, links, copy, bind and remove controls in reading order; `Enter`/`Space` on a header toggles its card; the bind menu follows `dropdown-menu` (arrows, `Enter`, `Esc`). The scroll area is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) only when it overflows, so arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the root is a `section` named by `ariaLabel`; columns are an `ol` of `li`, each with an optional visually hidden label; each header is a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the collapsed body is `inert`; connectors are `aria-hidden`; icon-only controls are named (`Bind Policy`, `Remove Policy`, `Copy Domains Custom domain`) and carry a `Tooltip`; loading announces once through a `role="status"` line.
- The unbound dash is `aria-hidden`; the status tag says Not bound in words.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`); the columns run from the inline start.
- Connectors: the engine reads `direction` and mirrors the elbows; ports swap sides.
- Icons: the chevron rotates vertically and is not mirrored; kind icons are not mirrored.
- User data: field values carry `dir="auto"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                                                     | English source                                              | Override prop |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `topologyDiagram.label`                                 | Deployment topology                                         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `topologyDiagram.notBound`                              | Not bound                                                   | node `status` |
| `topologyDiagram.bind` / `change` / `remove` / `create` | Bind {kind} / Change {kind} / Remove {kind} / Create {kind} | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.existing`                              | Existing                                                    | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.noOptions`                             | No options yet.                                             | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.copy`                                  | Copy {field}                                                | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.emptyTitle`                            | Nothing is connected yet.                                   | `empty` slot  |
| `topologyDiagram.loading`                               | Loading the topology                                        | —             |

- Formatting: none; kinds, names, statuses and fields are data.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; each column keeps `min-w-(--size-56)` and grows to share the width.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the diagram scrolls inline in its own focusable area; the page does not.
- Touch: header buttons are full-width rows; bind, remove and copy are small icon buttons with tooltips that also work on focus.
- Reflow: the diagram is a two-dimensional figure, an accepted exception to 1.4.10 inside its own scroll area.

<!-- components/transfer-list.md -->

# Transfer List

> Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Named after the MUI Transfer List (Ant Design calls it Transfer; it was PickList before 6.0), written to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<TransferList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, `<TransferList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<TransferList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.

- Import: `import TransferListRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import TransferList from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list'`
- Category: data · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use TransferList only when the person builds a large subset and must see the chosen and remaining items side by side. To pick several values in a compact form field use MultiSelect; for two to five options use a Checkbox per option.
- Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
- Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
- Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.

## Do

- Set `item-key` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves and the selection follows the record when the lists change; without it rows and the selection are keyed by their index.
- Set `title` on both `TransferList.Source` and `TransferList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
- Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
- Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.

## Don’t

- Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
- Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
- A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.

## Related

- `multi-select` — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
- `table` — row selection over tabular data.
- `checkbox` — independent boolean or small-set multi-pick.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `itemKey` | `string` | `''` | false | Item field that identifies a record, the same name as `card-list`: each row's render key and the key of the selection, so an external change to the v-model pair keeps the selection on its records. Empty falls back to the index. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens. |
| `moveOnDoubleClick` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move. |
| `modelValue` | `TransferListValue` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `move` | `(event: Event, payload: { direction: 'to-target' \| 'to-source'; items: unknown[] })` | Fired after items move between lists; the DOM event of the control (or the double-click) first, then the direction and the moved items. |
| `item-double-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' \| 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })` | Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading } | Composition slot; receives `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, and `<TransferList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<TransferList.Controls>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-source`
- `@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-target`
- `@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list-controls`

## Sub-components

- `transfer-list-source/transfer-list-source.vue` — The source listbox (the left/top list).
- `transfer-list-target/transfer-list-target.vue` — The target listbox (the right/bottom list).
- `transfer-list-controls/transfer-list-controls.vue` — The context-aware control column between the lists.

## v-model

| Model     | Type                     | Default          | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `[unknown[], unknown[]]` | `() => [[], []]` | `update:modelValue` | Bound pair of lists as `[sourceItems, targetItems]`, two-way through `defineModel`. Each move writes the new pair back; without a bound `v-model` the component keeps the pair as local state. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (option), `focus-visible` (option / control), `selected` (option), `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` on the root mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` on a list (`transfer-list-source` / `transfer-list-target`) mirrors that list's `loading` prop
- A loading list renders a centered spinner instead of its options and sets `aria-busy="true"`; while any list is loading, both the move controls and double-click-to-move are disabled until loading clears
- Each option carries `data-selected` mirroring its selection and `aria-selected`
- Empty list (not loading, no items): the package `EmptyState` (small, `transferList.emptyTitle`, `No items`) is laid over the list box, outside the listbox element (a `status` region is not an allowed listbox child); test id `<list testid>__empty`
- Server render and hydration: the options are the direct `v-for` children of the `TransitionGroup` list (an empty list while loading) and the spinner a sibling `v-if`, so the server renders no fragment markers inside the list and the HTML hydrates as is.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each option and on every move control.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the two listboxes and the control column, one tab stop per listbox (roving `tabindex`: the last focused option, the first by default); within a listbox `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move focus, `Home`/`End` go to the first and last option, `Space`/`Enter` toggle the focused option's selection, and `Shift`+`ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` extend the selection to the next option; the move controls are activated with `Enter`/`Space`. Double-click on an option is a pointer affordance for moving it to the opposite list; the same move is reachable via select + the move controls (no keyboard-only feature is double-click-only).
- ARIA: each list is `role="listbox"` with `aria-label` from its title text; options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; the source/target listboxes set `aria-multiselectable="true"`; every move control is an icon-only button with an explicit `aria-label`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled` on both listboxes, and a disabled root becomes `role="group"` with `aria-disabled="true"`, so the titles dimmed by the root's `opacity-60` belong to a disabled control (WCAG 1.4.3 inactive-component exemption) instead of reading as low-contrast live text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (borders + icons), including the disabled state.
- A loading list sets `aria-busy="true"`; its `Spinner` is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and carries its own reduced-motion fallback. Control hover transitions pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px for every move control (medium icon-button height).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import TransferList from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const model = ref([
    [
      { id: 1, label: 'Edge Functions' },
      { id: 2, label: 'WAF' },
      { id: 3, label: 'Image Processor' }
    ],
    [{ id: 4, label: 'Cache' }]
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <TransferList
    v-model="model"
    item-key="id"
  >
    <TransferList.Source title="Available">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </TransferList.Source>

    <TransferList.Controls />

    <TransferList.Target title="Selected">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </TransferList.Target>
  </TransferList>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/transfer-list.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/transfer-list.md).
