<!-- components/doc-layout.md -->

# Doc Layout

> The documentation chrome, composed once in the app: a sticky header (the Azion Docs mark, the section links, `SearchTrigger` and the app's actions), the navigation rail (`Sidebar` + `SidebarMenu`) on the inline start, resizable by dragging its edge and collapsible to a thin edge that brings it back, the article in the layout's `<main>`, the "On this page" rail (`DocOnThisPage`) on the inline end with its own slot below it, and the footer under the article. The **document** scrolls: the header and both rails are sticky, so a full-page capture shows the whole article, the browser's find and scroll restoration work, and the dark canvas is painted to the end. The outline follows the reading position, a jump clears the sticky header, and below `lg` the rail moves into a drawer opened from the header. The `Command` palette lists every navigation page. Doc pages are only their article, rendered through the default slot.

- Import: `import DocLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-layout'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Every documentation page (guide, reference, legal, changelog): put one `DocLayout` in the app's root (around `RouterView`) and render each page's article as its default slot.
- A docs site that needs the navigation rail, the outline and the search palette without hand-composing `AppHeader`, `Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu`, `DocOnThisPage`, `Drawer` and `Command`.

## Do

- Compose the layout once, in the app's root; each route renders only its article. Never put a header, a rail or an inner scroll area in a page.
- Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href` (an in-app path is followed with the router; never `to`); leave `activeId` empty so the current page follows the route.
- Pass the page's headings as `outline` (`{ id, text, depth }`) with the same ids the `DocHeading`s carry; the layout tracks which one is in view.
- Put the theme switch in `navigation-footer`, the GitHub and Console links in `actions`, a call to action (`DocCallToAction`) in `aside`, and the site footer (`Footer variant="content"`) in `footer`.
- The page renders no `<main>` and no `ScrollArea` around the article: the document scrolls.
- Bind `v-model:navigation-open` and `v-model:navigation-width` to state the app persists (local storage, a cookie) so the rail keeps the reader's size and collapsed state across pages and reloads; leave them unbound and the rail resets on each mount.
- A drill row (`type: 'drill'`) opens its level in place; the rail's Back then reads `Back to Docs` at the first level. Set `rootLabel` when the tree is not the whole docs (`Back to API reference`); never add a hand-made Back row to `navigation`.

## Don’t

- The signed-in console → `ConsoleLayout`. Marketing pages → `SiteLayout`.
- A docs landing page with no rail (the docs home) → render it with `DocHero` and the sections, without this layout, or pass an empty `navigation` and `outline`.

## Related

- DocOnThisPage` — the outline rail; `outline` and `outlineGroups` are bound onto it.
- DocHeading` — headings whose anchor links the layout scrolls to, clearing the sticky header.
- DocPageHeader`, `DocProse`, `DocPagination` — the article parts rendered in the default slot.
- Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu` — the navigation rail; `navigation` is mapped onto `SidebarMenu` groups.
- SearchTrigger`, `Command` — the header search and the palette it opens.
- shell/docs` — the block that shows this layout with a sample docs tree.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigation` | `DocLayoutNavGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The docs tree: groups of rows, each `{ id, label, icon?, href?, tagValue?, disabled?, kind?, defaultOpen?, children? }`; an in-app `href` is followed with the router. |
| `activeId` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the current row. Empty matches the current route against each row's `href`. |
| `sections` | `DocLayoutSection[]` | `[]` | false | The header's section links (`Reference`, `Guides`), each `{ label, href? }`; shown from `lg`. |
| `home` | `string` | `'/'` | false | Where the Azion Docs mark links. |
| `outline` | `DocOnThisPageItem[]` | `[]` | false | The article's headings for the "On this page" rail, each `{ id, text, depth }`; the rail is not rendered when empty and the `aside` slot is unused. |
| `outlineGroups` | `DocOnThisPageGroup[]` | `[]` | false | Complementary link groups under the outline (GitHub, Community). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Documentation`). |
| `rootLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Names the top of the docs tree in the rail's Back button on the first drill level (`Back to Docs`); deeper levels name their parent row. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Docs`). |
| `searchOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:searchOpen`). |
| `navigationOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:navigationOpen`). |
| `navigationWidth` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:navigationWidth`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: DocLayoutNavItem)` | Fired when a navigation row or a palette page is chosen; the layout then follows its `href` (an in-app path with the router). Event first. |
| `search-select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string \| number)` | Fired when a palette item from the `search` slot is chosen. Event first. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The article, rendered inside the layout's `<main>`. |
| `actions` | — | The header's end actions after the search (GitHub, Console). |
| `navigation-footer` | — | The foot of the navigation rail and of the drawer (the theme switch). |
| `aside` | — | Content under the outline in the end rail (a `DocCallToAction`). |
| `footer` | — | The footer under the article (`Footer variant="content"`). |
| `search` | { query: string } | Extra `Command.Group`s listed before the navigation pages. |

## v-model

| Model                      | Type             | Default | Emits                    | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:search-open`      | `boolean`        | `false` | `update:searchOpen`      | Whether the search palette is open; the header search and ⌘K / Ctrl K set it.                                                                                                                  |
| `v-model:navigation-open`  | `boolean`        | `true`  | `update:navigationOpen`  | Whether the navigation rail is open from `lg`; `false` collapses it to the edge affordance that brings it back. No effect below `lg`, where the rail is a drawer.                              |
| `v-model:navigation-width` | `number \| null` | `null`  | `update:navigationWidth` | The rail's width in px after the reader drags its edge; `null` uses the natural width (`var(--container-2xs)`). Clamped by `Sidebar` between `var(--container-3xs)` and `var(--container-sm)`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; from `lg` the rail is `expanded` or `collapsed` (`Sidebar` `data-collapsed`, the edge affordance shown) and `resizing` while dragged; below `lg` the rail is a drawer (`open` / `closed`) opened from the header; the end rail shows from `xl` when `outline` or `aside` has content; the palette `open` / `closed`.
- Outline: the entry of the heading nearest the top of the viewport (under the header) carries `aria-current="location"`; choosing an entry or a heading anchor scrolls the heading under the header and updates the address hash.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid` (the article owns its states).

## Accessibility

- Landmarks: the header is `AppHeader` (`<header>` named by the catalog `Documentation sections` on its section links); the rail is the `Sidebar` `<nav>` named by `ariaLabel`; the article is inside the single `<main>`; the end rail is an `<aside>` holding the `DocOnThisPage` navigation landmarks. A page must not render a second `<main>`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` runs header → rail → article → end rail → footer; the rail's resize handle is a focusable `separator` (`Resize navigation`) moved with `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`, its collapse button (`Collapse navigation`) folds the rail and the edge affordance's button (`Expand navigation`) brings it back, all owned by `Sidebar`; `⌘K` / `Ctrl K` opens the palette (`Command`); the compact menu button opens the drawer, `Escape` closes it and returns focus. Choosing an outline entry moves focus to its heading (made focusable with `tabindex="-1"`).
- Names: the mark link (`Azion Docs home`), the compact menu button (`Open documentation navigation`) and the search (`Search docs`) come from the locale catalog.
- Visible focus: composed controls own their rings; the mark link uses `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the navigation rail sits at the inline start, the outline at the inline end, and the drawer opens from the inline start.
- Resize: dragging and the arrow keys follow the inline direction (`Sidebar` mirrors them under `dir="rtl"`); the collapse and expand glyphs mirror.
- Icons: the mark is not mirrored; `SidebarMenu` and `DocOnThisPage` mirror their own glyphs.
- Keyboard: arrow handling is `SidebarMenu`'s and `Command`'s, both direction-aware.
- User data: labels render with `dir="auto"` inside `SidebarMenu`, `DocOnThisPage` and `Command`.

## Internationalization

| Key                            | English source                  | Override prop |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `docLayout.navigation`         | `Documentation`                 | `ariaLabel`   |
| `docLayout.sections`           | `Documentation sections`        | —             |
| `docLayout.home`               | `Azion Docs home`               | —             |
| `docLayout.badge`              | `Docs`                          | —             |
| `docLayout.openNavigation`     | `Open documentation navigation` | —             |
| `docLayout.search`             | `Search docs`                   | —             |
| `docLayout.noMatch`            | `No page matches your search.`  | —             |
| `docLayout.pages`              | `Pages`                         | —             |
| `docLayout.root`               | `Docs`                          | `rootLabel`   |
| `docLayout.collapseNavigation` | `Collapse navigation`           | —             |
| `docLayout.expandNavigation`   | `Expand navigation`             | —             |
| `docLayout.resizeNavigation`   | `Resize navigation`             | —             |

- Formatting: none. Navigation and outline text is consumer data.

## Responsive

- Breakpoints (viewport, because the layout is the page): the navigation rail shows from `lg`, resizable and collapsible, and is a drawer below (no resize or collapse there); the outline rail shows from `xl`; the section links show from `lg`. The header is an `@container`, so `SearchTrigger collapsible` folds to the magnifier on a narrow header.
- Narrow: the article takes the full width; the end rail content (`aside`) is not repeated under the article.
- Touch: menu button and search are 32 px controls, 44 px on coarse pointers through their components.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the document scrolls, never an inner region.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import DocCallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-call-to-action'
  import DocHeading from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-heading'
  import DocLayout, { type DocLayoutNavGroup } from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-layout'
  import DocPageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-page-header'
  import DocProse from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prose'
  import ThemeSwitcher, { type ThemeSwitcherValue } from '@aziontech/webkit/theme-switcher'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const navigation: DocLayoutNavGroup[] = [
    {
      label: 'Fundamentals',
      items: [
        { id: 'overview', label: 'Overview', href: '/docs' },
        {
          id: 'get-started',
          label: 'Get started',
          defaultOpen: true,
          children: [
            { id: 'create-account', label: 'Create an account', href: '/docs/create-account' },
            { id: 'first-deploy', label: 'First deploy', href: '/docs/first-deploy' }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const outline = [
    { id: 'before-you-start', text: 'Before you start', depth: 2 },
    { id: 'deploy-with-cli', text: 'Deploy with Azion CLI', depth: 2 },
    { id: 'next-steps', text: 'Next steps', depth: 2 }
  ]

  const theme = ref<ThemeSwitcherValue>('system')
</script>

<template>
  <DocLayout
    :navigation="navigation"
    :sections="[
      { label: 'Guides', href: '/docs' },
      { label: 'Reference', href: '/docs/reference' }
    ]"
    :outline="outline"
    active-id="first-deploy"
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button
        label="Console"
        variant="secondary"
        size="medium"
        href="https://console.azion.com"
      />
    </template>

    <template #navigation-footer>
      <ThemeSwitcher
        v-model="theme"
        aria-label="Theme"
      />
    </template>

    <template #aside>
      <DocCallToAction
        title="Ready to build?"
        label="Deploy your first application for free."
        :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: 'https://console.azion.com/signup' }"
      />
    </template>

    <div class="layout-boundary">
      <div class="layout-column-content flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-lg)">
        <DocPageHeader
          title="First deploy"
          description="Deploy a template and see it served from the edge."
          :breadcrumbs="[
            { label: 'Get started', href: '/docs/get-started' },
            { label: 'First deploy' }
          ]"
        />
        <DocProse>
          <DocHeading
            anchor="before-you-start"
            :level="2"
            >Before you start</DocHeading
          >
          <p>You need an Azion account and a GitHub account.</p>
          <DocHeading
            anchor="deploy-with-cli"
            :level="2"
            >Deploy with Azion CLI</DocHeading
          >
          <p>Install the CLI, log in and run the deploy command from your project folder.</p>
          <DocHeading
            anchor="next-steps"
            :level="2"
            >Next steps</DocHeading
          >
          <p>Add a domain and turn on the cache for your static assets.</p>
        </DocProse>
      </div>
    </div>
  </DocLayout>
</template>
```

<!-- components/doc-markdown.md -->

# Doc Markdown

> Renders a documentation page written in Markdown with Mintlify-style MDX component tags into the documentation components. Prose becomes plain semantic HTML (headings, paragraphs, lists, block quotes, rules, tables, inline code, links, bold, italic) that the surrounding `DocProse` styles, and the component tags (`<Note>`, `<Steps>`, `<CardGroup>`, `<Tabs>`, `<CodeGroup>`, `<Update>`, `<Tooltip>` …) mount `DocCallout`, `DocSteps`, `DocCardGroup`, `DocTabs`, `DocCodeGroup`, `DocChangelogEntry`, `HoverCard` and the rest. Headings render as `DocHeading` with unique slug ids, and the named export `parseDocMarkdown` returns the same headings (for `DocOnThisPage` / `DocLayout`'s `outline`) and the frontmatter (for `DocPageHeader`). It is a small in-house reader of a fixed MDX subset, not an MDX compiler: no JSX expressions, no imports, no script, and no `v-html`, so a page's source can never run code.

- Import: `import DocMarkdown from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-markdown'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DocMarkdown for a whole documentation page written in MDX; model Markdown that arrives while it renders uses StreamingResponse.
- A docs page whose content is authored as `.mdx` / Markdown text (a content folder, a CMS field, a string in data) instead of hand-composed Doc components.
- Copy held in data that carries inline markup (a sentence with code and a link in a block's fixture) and should render the same as a page paragraph.

## Do

- Wrap it in `DocProse` and pass the page's headings to the layout from the same source: `const { headings, frontmatter } = parseDocMarkdown(source)`.
- Write one component tag per line block; a one-line callout (`<Note>Copy.</Note>`) is fine. Attribute values are strings, numbers, booleans or a string list (`tags={["API", "CLI"]}`); anything else stays literal text.
- Repeated headings are fine: the second `Test it` gets the id `test-it-2`, so anchors and the outline stay unique.
- Use `components` to swap the component a tag mounts (your own `Card`) or to add a block tag your docs use; never fork the parser.
- Write in-app links as root-relative paths (`/docs/domains`): they follow the app's router. `javascript:`, protocol-relative and other unsafe URLs render as their link text.

## Don’t

- A page composed by hand from `DocHeading`, `DocCallout`, `DocSteps` … → compose them directly inside `DocProse`; there is nothing to parse.
- Chat or AI responses streamed as Markdown → `StreamingResponse` / `ChatMessage`.
- Arbitrary MDX with JSX expressions, imports or custom script → compile it with an MDX toolchain in the app; this component reads a fixed subset only.
- Code with no prose around it → `CodeBlock` or `DocCodeGroup`.

## Related

- DocProse` — wrap this component in it; it owns the type scale, the block rhythm and the copyable inline code chips.
- DocHeading` — every Markdown heading renders as one, with the slug id the outline points at.
- DocLayout`, `DocOnThisPage` — take `parseDocMarkdown(source).headings` as `outline` / `items`.
- DocPageHeader` — takes the frontmatter's `title` and `description`.
- DocCallout`, `DocSteps`, `DocStep`, `DocCardGroup`, `DocCard`, `DocItem`, `DocAccordionGroup`, `DocAccordion`, `DocTabs`, `DocTab`, `DocCodeGroup`, `DocFrame`, `DocPrompt`, `DocChangelogEntry` — what the tags mount.
- HoverCard` — an inline `<Tooltip tip title linkLabel href>` tag renders as a HoverCard: the term is a dotted-underlined button, the card shows the title, the definition and an optional link.
- RegistrationFrame`, `ItemList` — the frame and list an `<ItemGroup>` renders its `<Item>` rows in.
- StreamingResponse` — renders chat Markdown with the AI layer's reader; this component reuses that reader's inline tokenizer and `safeHref` and adds the MDX block tags, document heading levels and anchors a docs page needs, which a chat bubble must not have.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | `''` | false | The page source: optional frontmatter, then Markdown with MDX component tags. |
| `components` | `Record<string, Component>` | `{}` | false | Replaces the component a block tag mounts, or adds a block tag, keyed by tag name (`Card`, `Note`). The tag's attributes become props. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` only; the component renders what the source holds.
- Lazy tags: a code group, tabs, an accordion, a frame, an item row or a prompt renders once its async chunk loads (in place on the server and on hydration).
- Empty: an empty `source` renders the empty root (no placeholder; the page owns its empty state).
- Unknown or malformed input: an unknown capitalized tag, an unclosed tag or an unsupported attribute expression stays literal text rather than disappearing; an unclosed tag runs to the end of the source.
- Links: a root-relative `href` is followed with the app's router (`useAppNavigation`); an `http(s)` link opens in a new tab with `rel="noreferrer"` and an announced suffix; a URL that is not `http(s)`, `mailto`, root-relative or a `#fragment` renders as plain text (the shared `safeHref` of the AI layer's Markdown reader).
- Not applicable: `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid` (static content).

## Accessibility

- Semantics: headings are real `h1`–`h4` (`DocHeading`) in source order with unique ids; lists are `ul` / `ol`; a table is a real `table` with `th scope="col"` header cells, wrapped in a horizontally scrollable region; a rule is `hr`; a quote is `blockquote`.
- Keyboard map: no keyboard handling of its own; links, heading anchors, tabs, accordions and code copy buttons are the mounted components' and follow their maps.
- Links: an external link announces `(opens in a new tab)` through a visually hidden suffix; link text is the author's.
- Visible focus: owned by `DocProse` (links) and the mounted components.
- Contrast: table header text `var(--text-muted)` and body text `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` meet 4.5:1 in both themes; no disabled state.
- Pattern: native document semantics; no WAI-ARIA APG widget of its own.
- Inside a callout, an item row or a prompt, paragraphs render as block spans so no `p` nests inside the component's own paragraph.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`text-start` on table cells, logical list padding from `DocProse`); a column aligned with `:---:` / `---:` keeps the author's `center` / `end` alignment, with `right` mapped to `end`.
- Icons: none of its own; the mounted components mirror their glyphs.
- Keyboard: none of its own.
- User data: the source text renders as is; code renders inside `DocCodeGroup`, which isolates its direction.

## Internationalization

| Key             | English source         | Override prop |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- |
| `common.newTab` | `(opens in a new tab)` | —             |

- Formatting: none. All visible text is the source's; code sample labels fall back to `DocCodeGroup`'s language names.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `DocCardGroup`, `DocChangelogEntry` and the other mounted components respond to their containers.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): a wide table scrolls inside its own region instead of the page; everything else reflows with `DocProse`.
- Touch: targets are the mounted components'; inline links follow `DocProse`.
- Reflow: no horizontal page scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; the exception is a wide table, which scrolls inside its region (WCAG 1.4.10 data-table exception).

## Examples

### Default

````vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import DocMarkdown from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-markdown'
  import DocProse from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prose'

  const source = [
    '---',
    'title: First deploy',
    'description: Deploy a template and see it served from the edge.',
    '---',
    '',
    '## Before you start',
    '',
    'You need an Acme account. Log in with `acme login`, then read the [CLI reference](https://example.com/docs/cli).',
    '',
    '- A project folder with a `package.json`',
    '- Node.js 22 or later',
    '',
    '<Note>A first deploy takes about a minute.</Note>',
    '',
    '## Deploy with the CLI',
    '',
    '<Steps>',
    '  <Step title="Install the CLI">',
    '    <CodeGroup>',
    '    ```bash npm',
    '    npm install -g acme-cli',
    '    ```',
    '    ```bash pnpm',
    '    pnpm add -g acme-cli',
    '    ```',
    '    </CodeGroup>',
    '  </Step>',
    '  <Step title="Deploy">Run `acme deploy` from the project folder.</Step>',

    '',
    '## Limits',
    '',
    '| Plan | Builds per day |',
    '| :--- | ---: |',

    '',

  ].join('\n')
</script>

<template>

<!-- components/doc-on-this-page.md -->

# Doc On This Page

> The "On this page" rail: the page's own headings, the active one lit, nested headings indented under their parent — followed by the rail's complementary groups (the repository, the community). The rail is a single path that bends inward as the outline nests, and the active marker is a dash cut from that same path, so moving between headings slides the marker **along** the line, through the bends, rather than jumping a separate bar between two positions.

- Import: `import DocOnThisPage from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-on-this-page'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Beside the body of a long documentation page, as in-page navigation over its `h2`/`h3` outline.
- To carry a page's peer links (repository, community) under the outline, each as its own named group.

## Do

- Feed it depth 2 and 3 only; the rail indents each level by 8px and a third level reads as noise.
- Own the active heading in the page (a scroll-spy) and pass it down; do not expect the rail to guess.
- Keep the complementary groups to peers of the page, never sections of it — a reader must not read "Join us on Discord" as part of what they are reading.

## Don’t

- Expecting it to track scroll. It is presentation only: `activeId` is a prop, because the page owns the scroll container and therefore owns which heading is active.
- For navigation _between_ pages — that is `DocPreviousNext` at the foot, or the sidebar.
- For an outline deeper than a couple of levels; the indent is legible for two, not for five.

## Related

- DocPageHeader` — the masthead above the body, whose `h1` is chrome, so the outline starts at `h2`.
- DocPreviousNext` — navigation between documents, where this is navigation within one.
- use-heading-navigation` — the composable a page uses to receive a rail activation and scroll its own container.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `DocOnThisPageItem[]` | `[]` | false | The headings, in document order. |
| `activeId` | `string` | `''` | false | The id of the heading currently in view. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The rail's own heading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`On this page`). |
| `groups` | `DocOnThisPageGroup[]` | `[]` | false | Complementary groups rendered below the outline, in order. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: DocOnThisPageItem)` | Fired when a rail entry is activated; the page decides what scrolling means. Event first, per `event-payloads.md`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a morphing highlight follows the pointer), and the active entry
- The active entry carries `aria-current="location"`; the marker is a dash cut from the rail path, positioned by measured length rather than by an index
- The complementary groups are deliberately drawn as peers: no rail, no indent, no active marker

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each entry takes the focus ring on `focus-visible`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the entries and then through each group's links; `Enter` activates. The rail owns no arrow-key model — it is a list of links, not a widget.
- ARIA: the outline is a `nav` named by `title`, and **each complementary group is its own named `nav`**, so the three read as three landmarks rather than one long list. Entries are `li` children of a `ul` (the axe `list` rule requires that), and the active entry carries `aria-current="location"`. The rail path and the group glyphs are decorative (`aria-hidden`). Under `dir="rtl"` the rail svg is mirrored (`rtl:-scale-x-100`), so its depth bends step toward the inline end like the entries they follow.
- The marker is never the only signal: the active entry also changes ink and carries `aria-current`, so the state does not depend on seeing the dash.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- Touch target: entries are padded rows; the rail itself is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocOnThisPage from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-on-this-page'
</script>

<template>
  <DocOnThisPage
    :items="[
      { id: 'deploy', text: 'Deploy an application', depth: 2 },
      { id: 'what-you-get', text: 'What you get', depth: 3 },
      { id: 'build-command', text: 'Build command', depth: 3 },
      { id: 'bind-a-domain', text: 'Bind a domain', depth: 2 }
    ]"
    active-id="what-you-get"
    :groups="[
      {
        label: 'Repository',
        links: [
          { label: 'View source', href: 'https://github.com/aziontech', icon: 'ai ai-github' }
        ]
      }
    ]"
    @select="(event, item) => scrollToHeading(item.id)"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/doc-on-this-page.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-on-this-page.md).

<!-- components/doc-page-header.md -->

# Doc Page Header

> The masthead of a documentation page: where the reader is (the breadcrumb), what the page is (the title), what they can do with it (a Copy Page control that hands the page to an AI tool — or, through the `actions` slot, the consumer's own menu; the trail is likewise slottable, for an application whose crumbs route rather than navigate), the deck that says what they will have by the end, and when the content last changed. It closes on a rule spanning the column, which is what gives every `h2` below it something to be subordinate to.

- Import: `import DocPageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-page-header'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DocPageHeader only on documentation pages; console pages use PageHeader.
- At the top of any documentation or changelog page, above `DocProse`.

## Do

- Give every `metaActions` entry a `tip`: two or three words name a control, and only a sentence says what it does.
- Give an entry an `href` when it has a destination, so it is a real link — then prevent the default in `action-click` if the app routes in-page.
- Let `lastUpdated` come from the page's own frontmatter. It is the author's claim that the content changed, not the file's mtime.
- Put the current page last in `breadcrumbs`; it is marked `active` for you.
- Use `title` and `details` for a page ABOUT something (a tool, a product): its mark and maker are a title, and its facts belong between the deck and the meta line.

## Don’t

- For an application screen's title — that is `PageHeader`, which carries console actions rather than a Copy Page control.
- For a section heading inside a page — the content's own `h2` does that, and the masthead's `h1` is chrome.
- The documentation home → use `DocHero` (display title, `Get started` and `CopyPromptButton`), then `DocAgentCard`.

## Related

- DocProse` — the body below it. The masthead's `h1` is chrome, so authored content starts at `h2`.
- DocOnThisPage` — the rail beside the body, which lists those `h2`s.
- Button` / `Tooltip` / `Separator` — the meta line's entries: a quiet `text` button (an anchor when the entry has an `href`), the sentence its label has no room for, and the rule between two of them.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The page title. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | The deck under the title. |
| `breadcrumbs` | `BreadcrumbItemData[]` | `[]` | false | Ancestor trail, current page last. |
| `lastUpdated` | `string` | `''` | false | When the page's content last changed. ISO date, or a ready-made string. |
| `metaActions` | `DocPageHeaderAction[]` | `[]` | false | The controls on the meta line, in reading order. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: DocPageHeaderAction)` | Fired when a meta-line control is activated; `item` is the entry that was picked. Event first, per `event-payloads.md`. A link's default navigation is the consumer's to keep or to prevent. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `breadcrumbs` | — | The trail; replaces the built-in `Breadcrumb` fed by the `breadcrumbs` prop. |
| `title` | — | The page's name; replaces the built-in `h1`, for a title that is more than a string. |
| `actions` | — | A control on the title's line. Empty by default; the meta line carries the page's actions. |
| `details` | — | Rows between the deck and the meta line — a page's own facts, tags or references. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`. The masthead holds no interactive state of its own; each meta-line entry owns its own hover, focus and tooltip.
- Each region renders only when it has content: no breadcrumb, deck, or meta line appears empty. An unfilled slot with a `v-if`-ed fallback renders no element, so a masthead with no trail pays no gap for the region; an empty `metaActions` with no date renders no meta line at all.
- `data-undated` on the meta line when there is no date: the line then starts with a `text` button, whose label sits one spacing step inside its own box, so the row is pulled left by exactly that padding to keep the ink on the column.
- The rules between entries render from `md` up only. Below that the line wraps per entry, and a rule at the end of a wrapped line has nothing after it.
- Below `sm` a passed `actions` control leaves the title's line and stacks under it at its natural width; from `sm` up the two share one row.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: inherited from `Breadcrumb`, `Button` and `Tooltip`; the masthead adds no focusable element of its own.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the breadcrumb links and then each meta-line entry in reading order; a `tip` opens on focus, not on hover alone, so a definition is never pointer-only. The separators are `aria-hidden` — three announced separators on the way to three controls is noise.
- ARIA: the root is a `header`. The title is the page's single `h1`, so authored content must start at `h2`. The "last updated" glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`) because the words "Last updated" sit beside it, and the date is wrapped in `<time datetime>` so the machine-readable value survives formatting.
- The ISO date is parsed and rendered in **UTC** on purpose: read as local time, a bare `2026-06-30` becomes the 29th for every reader west of Greenwich.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- Touch target: each meta-line entry is a standard `small` button (28px) with its own hover surface; nothing else is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocPageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-page-header'
</script>

<template>
  <DocPageHeader
    title="Deploy an application"
    description="Go from a template to a live edge application in a few clicks."
    :breadcrumbs="[{ label: 'Docs', href: '/docs' }, { label: 'Deploy an application' }]"
    last-updated="2026-06-30"
    :meta-actions="[
      {
        value: 'copy',
        label: 'Copy as Markdown',
        icon: 'ai ai-copy',
        tip: 'Copy this page as Markdown, ready to paste into an assistant.'
      },
      {
        value: 'markdown',
        label: 'View as Markdown',
        icon: 'ai ai-eye',
        tip: 'Open this page as plain Markdown in a new tab.'
      },
      {
        value: 'agent-setup',
        label: 'Agent setup',
        icon: 'ai ai-microchip-ai',
        href: '/docs/agent-setup',
        tip: 'Set up your coding agent to build on Azion.'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/doc-previous-next.md -->

# Doc Previous Next

> The previous / next pair that closes a documentation page. Each side is a link carrying an eyebrow and the destination's title; a side with no neighbour leaves its half of the row empty, so the remaining link stays anchored to its own edge rather than drifting to the centre.

- Import: `import DocPreviousNext from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-previous-next'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DocPreviousNext only at the foot of a documentation page to link the previous and next documents.
- At the foot of a page that sits in a reading order — a guide, a tutorial, a numbered series.
- Whenever "what do I read next" has a single obvious answer in each direction.

## Do

- Pass the destination's real title, not "Next page". The title is what tells the reader whether they want to go.
- Leave a side `null` at the ends of a series rather than looping around.
- Handle `navigate` when the app routes client-side; the anchor's `href` is what makes the link real for everyone else.

## Don’t

- To page through a data set — that is `Pagination`, which walks pages of rows and owns a page number. This links two neighbouring documents and knows nothing about a total.
- On a page with no reading order (a reference index, a landing page): a next link that points somewhere arbitrary is worse than none.

## Related

- Pagination` — the data counterpart; numbered pages over a collection, not two named documents.
- DocOnThisPage` — navigation _within_ the page, where this is navigation _between_ pages.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `previous` | `DocPreviousNextLink \| null` | `null` | false | The page before this one. |
| `next` | `DocPreviousNextLink \| null` | `null` | false | The page after this one. |
| `previousLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow over the previous link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Previous`). |
| `nextLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow over the next link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Next`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent, page: DocPreviousNextLink)` | Fired when either neighbour is activated; `page` is the side that was clicked. Event first, per `event-payloads.md`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (the chevron travels outward), `focus-visible`
- One side absent renders an empty placeholder so the other stays edge-anchored; there is no `data-*` state, because the component holds none

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-(--ring-color)` on each link.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each present side; `Enter` follows it. Nothing else — the component owns no keyboard model of its own.
- ARIA: the root is a `nav` labelled "Page navigation", so a screen reader announces it as a landmark distinct from the page's own nav. That name is **overridable** by passing `aria-label` — two nav landmarks may not share an accessible name (axe `landmark-unique`), so a page carrying two paginations must distinguish them. Each link's accessible name is its eyebrow plus the destination title; the chevrons are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- Touch target: each side is a padded block, comfortably over 40×40 px.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`) and their hover nudges point away from the label (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocPreviousNext from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-previous-next'
</script>

<template>
  <DocPreviousNext
    :previous="{ label: 'Deploy an application', href: '/docs/deploy' }"
    :next="{ label: 'Bind a domain', href: '/docs/domains' }"
    @navigate="(event, page) => router.push(page.href)"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/doc-previous-next.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-previous-next.md).

<!-- components/doc-prompt.md -->

# Doc Prompt

> DocPrompt renders text the reader is meant to **run, not read** — the block a documentation page uses when the next step is "say this to your agent". It is the one component in this layer whose payload is addressed to a machine, so it is the one that ships an affordance for handing it to one: a copy control wired to the exact string on screen. It is deliberately **not** a code block — a prompt is a sentence, so it carries no language, no gutter, and no syntax highlighting, and it is set in the mono face only to say "this is the literal text, copy it as it stands".

- Import: `import DocPrompt from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prompt'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DocPrompt to show a prompt the reader pastes into an agent, with its copy control.
- A documentation step, onboarding screen, or empty state whose next action is "paste this into your agent".
- A short list of example prompts a reader can try, under a heading that has already said what they are.
- Anywhere a literal string must be copied verbatim and the reader is the one who decides where it goes.

## Do

- Write the prompt once, in the default slot. It is both the visible text and the copied string, so the two cannot drift.
- Give `title` only when the surrounding page has not already said what the block is. Three one-line prompts under a "Prompts to try" heading want the bare shape.
- Use `variant="line"` for a single instruction and `variant="block"` for a priming paragraph. A one-sentence prompt broken across three lines reads as three instructions.
- Keep the prompt in the imperative and free of placeholders the reader must fill silently — if a value must be substituted, name it in the prose above.

## Don’t

- The payload is source code, a shell command, or configuration → use a code viewer, which owns languages, gutters, and highlighting; a prompt has none of them.
- The payload is a short inline token (a key, a flag, a variable name) → use `kbd` or inline code in prose.
- The block needs to run the prompt itself, or route it to a named vendor → out of scope; this component only puts the text on the clipboard.
- The "Copy prompt" action of a docs home hero or agent card, where the prompt is copied and not shown → use `CopyPromptButton` (inside `DocHero` or `DocAgentCard`).

## Related

- `copy-button` — the control DocPrompt composes. Reach for it directly when the value being copied has no block of its own.
- DocCallout` — draws attention to prose the reader should _read_; DocPrompt is for text the reader should _use_.
- DocProse` — the contract around it. The prompt marks itself `data-doc-chrome`, so prose rules stop at its edge, and `data-doc-block`, so it takes the block rung of the ladder.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'block' \| 'line'` | `'block'` | false | Wrapping paragraph capped at four lines, or one line that scrolls sideways. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | What the block is, in a word or two. Renders as a titled row above the prompt. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'ai ai-sparkles'` | false | Azion icon class for the glyph beside the title. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback prompt text when the default slot is empty. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The prompt itself: one or more sentences of literal text. Also the string the copy control carries. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible` (on the `line` shape, which is a scroll container)
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop: `block` | `line`
- `data-state` — `open` | `closed` on the prompt text of a capped `block`: `open` once the reader has opened it
- `data-capped` — present on the root when a `block` prompt is taller than its four-line cap; absent when it fits, so a prompt that fits earns no disclosure control
- `data-overflow` — on the `line` shape: `start` | `end` | `both`, whichever edge has text scrolled behind it; absent when the line fits
- `data-single-line` — on the prompt row when the prompt occupies exactly one line (`line` always; a `block` whose sentence fits its column). The row then centres the prompt against the copy control instead of top-aligning it — the control is 28px and one line of the prompt face is 19.5px, so a top-aligned pair leaves the sentence 4.25px above the control's middle. Absent the moment the prompt wraps.
- `data-doc-block` + `data-doc-chrome` are the `DocProse` contract (block rung; prose stops here)
- Empty: an empty slot with an empty `label` renders the shell with no prompt text and no copy control

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-(--ring-color)` on the `line` shape
- Keyboard map: the `line` shape takes a tab stop because it is a scroll container — a scroll container holding no focusable child is unreachable by keyboard (and an axe `scrollable-region-focusable` violation); arrow keys then scroll it. The `block` shape scrolls nothing, so it takes no tab stop. `Tab` reaches the disclosure control and the copy control; `Enter` / `Space` activate them.
- ARIA: the full prompt text is in the DOM in every state, so the cap hides nothing from a screen reader — the disclosure is a visual convenience and the state it reports is the change in its own label (`Show more` / `Show less`). Every fade gradient is `aria-hidden="true"`; the title glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`. The copy control carries its own accessible name.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons) — the prompt is `--text-default`, not the muted body ink, because the prompt IS the payload and everything around it is chrome
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on both animated states; the disclosure move is skipped rather than shortened
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on both controls (both are `size="small"` webkit controls, which meet the floor)

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Edge fades: the horizontal fades of a `line` prompt pair each physical gradient with its mirror (`bg-gradient-to-r rtl:bg-gradient-to-l`), so the fade always darkens toward the clipped edge.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the prompt text is code-like and keeps its own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocPrompt from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prompt'
</script>

<template>
  <DocPrompt title="AI Assistant">
    Deploy this repository to Azion and show me the edge URL when it is live.
  </DocPrompt>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/doc-prompt.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-prompt.md).

<!-- components/doc-prose.md -->

# Doc Prose

> The typography contract every documentation page inherits. A markdown or MDX pipeline compiles text to plain semantic HTML — `h2`, `p`, `ul`, `table`, `a`, `code` — and this container is what gives that HTML the Azion type scale, the semantic colors and the vertical rhythm, so an author writes markdown and never a class. It styles **descendants** rather than itself, so it works the same over any renderer's output, a slot of hand-written markup, or raw HTML from a CMS.

- Import: `import DocProse from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prose'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Wrapping the body of a documentation or changelog page, whatever produced its HTML.
- Giving authored prose inside a documentation block (a step's body, a tab's panel) the same type contract as the page around it.

## Do

- Mark a documentation component's root `data-doc-chrome` so prose rules stop there, and `data-doc-block` so it takes the block rung of the ladder. A callout is both.
- Do not add per-page overrides. If a rung is wrong, it is wrong for every page and belongs in this contract.
- Keep the consumer's column cap outside this component; it is typography, not layout.

## Don’t

- To cap the reading column — `DocProse` has no measure of its own. The consumer sets the width with `.layout-column-content` (`--layout-measure-content`, 876px).
- To style a webkit component's internals. Those are chrome and are excluded by design; restyle nothing from here.
- For a single run of body copy in an application screen — use the `text-body-*` tokens directly.

## Related

- DocPageHeader` — the page masthead above this container; its `h1` is chrome, so authored content starts at `h2`.
- DocCallout` / `DocCard` / `DocSteps` — blocks that sit inside prose and mark themselves `data-doc-chrome` so the contract stops at their edge.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The document body: markdown-rendered HTML or hand-written markup. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, plus `hover` and `focus-visible` on descendant links, and `hover` on an authored inline `code` chip (a ring, and a tooltip offering the copy)
- No `data-state`: the container is static and holds no state of its own
- Reflow: an inline `code` chip wraps at any character (`wrap-anywhere`, with `box-decoration-clone` so each line keeps the chip's border and padding), so a long path or URL never widens the column at 320px or at 200% zoom. Code inside `pre` keeps its lines
- Clicking an authored inline `code` chip copies its text; the tooltip reads `Copy`, then `Copied`, and falls back to `Press ⌘C to copy` on macOS (`Press Ctrl+C to copy` elsewhere, the modifier from the `kbd` catalog) with the chip selected when the clipboard is refused. A chip inside `pre`, inside a link, or generated by a component (it carries a `data-testid`, or holds child elements) is excluded
- Reads two descendant contracts: `data-doc-chrome` (every prose rule stops there) and `data-doc-block` (takes the block rung of the ladder)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: descendant links take `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through descendant links; the container itself is not focusable.
- ARIA: none — the container adds no role. The semantics are the author's HTML (`h2`, `ul`, `blockquote`), which is the point of the contract.
- Contrast: headings, `strong` and inline `code` are `--text-default` (≥14.7:1). **Body copy and list items are `--text-muted`, which is 3.78:1 on canvas and 3.95:1 on surface in light mode — under the 4.5:1 AA needs for body text** (dark is fine at 5.32:1 / 5.01:1). The contract carries that gap knowingly and in one place; closing it means a documentation body ink one step darker (`#737373` reads the same and clears AA at 4.54:1), not a per-page override.
- The chip copy adds **no tab stops**: it is a pointer shortcut over text that stays selectable the ordinary way, so a page of thirty chips does not become thirty stops. The tooltip is `role="tooltip"` and `pointer-events-none`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the descendant link transition.
- Touch target: not applicable; the container is not interactive.
- Teleported content: the teleported copy tip binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocProse from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prose'
</script>

<template>
  <DocProse>
    <h2>Deploy an application</h2>
    <p>
      Templates are ready-made projects that go live in a few clicks. You don't need any local
      tooling, and the <a href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/">template's guide</a> lists
      what each one needs.
    </p>
    <h3>What you get</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>A <strong>workload</strong> bound to its own Azion domain</li>
      <li>An edge application built from your <code>azion.config.js</code></li>
      <li>A certificate issued and renewed for you</li>
    </ul>
    <ol>
      <li>Pick a template</li>
      <li>Fill in the fields it asks for</li>
      <li>Deploy</li>
    </ol>
    <blockquote>
      <p>The first request to a location is a cache miss. Warm-up is per location, not global.</p>
    </blockquote>
    <h4>Build command</h4>
    <p>
      An h4 is a label inside a section rather than a new section, so it shares the base gap of the
      prose around it and carries its level on weight instead.
    </p>
    <hr />
    <p>A section break above resets the reader before the next part of the page.</p>
  </DocProse>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/doc-prose.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-prose.md).

<!-- components/doc-step.md -->

# Doc Step

> One numbered step of a `DocSteps` walkthrough: the circled index, the rail that continues to the next step, the step heading, and any content the author nests underneath. The number and the last-step mark come from the `DocSteps` context — the step registers itself during setup and reads its reactive index back, so an author writes a title and never a number. Rendered outside a `DocSteps` provider it throws (`useDocStepsContext must be used within DocSteps.`) instead of rendering unnumbered.

- Import: `import DocStep from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-step'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Only as a direct child of `DocSteps`, one per instruction the reader performs.

## Do

- Lead the title with the verb and keep it to one line of instruction.
- Put elaboration — prose, a code block, another component — in the body slot, not in the title.
- Never restate the number in the title; the circle carries it.

## Don’t

- Anywhere outside a `DocSteps` column — the context composable throws by design.
- For a checklist entry or a feature bullet — a step claims an order and a number.

## Related

- DocSteps` — the sibling root that numbers this; it provides the context this step registers with.
- DocProse` — the step heading marks itself `data-doc-chrome`, so prose rules stop at its edge.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The step heading. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Optional body under the step heading: prose, code, or another component. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the step is not interactive)
- The final step drops its connector rail and trailing space through a last-child CSS variant, not through state. "Am I last?" is a question about DOM order, and a registration count answers it wrong: the count grows while the parent is still rendering, so every step would read it as it stood at its own setup
- `data-step-connector` marks the rail element, so its presence is testable structurally
- `data-doc-chrome` on the heading is the `DocProse` contract (prose rules stop here)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the step is not focusable; `Tab` reaches only interactive content nested in its body.
- Keyboard map: none of its own.
- ARIA: the circled index and the rail are decorative (`aria-hidden`); the heading text and the body are the step's accessible content, read in document order — the same order the numbers claim.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text): the heading and the index use `var(--text-default)` on the page and `var(--bg-surface)` respectively, the same pairing the rest of the layer measures AA on.
- Touch target: not applicable; the component is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocStep from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-step'
  import DocSteps from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-steps'
</script>

<template>
  <DocSteps>
    <DocStep title="Install the CLI.">
      <p>Download the binary for your system and add it to your path.</p>
    </DocStep>
    <DocStep title="Log in.">
      <p>Run the login command and paste the token from your account settings.</p>
    </DocStep>
    <DocStep title="Deploy the project." />
  </DocSteps>
</template>
```

<!-- components/doc-steps.md -->

# Doc Steps

> The ordered walkthrough from the docs frame: a column of `DocStep` children joined by a rail. Each step registers itself through the context this root provides and reads its number back, so the numbering is a fact of the document order — an author writes titles, never numbers, and reordering the page renumbers it. The final registered step is marked last, which is what drops its connector and trailing space.

- Import: `import DocSteps from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-steps'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DocSteps only inside documentation prose for numbered instructions read top to bottom.
- A procedure the reader performs in order: install, link, deploy.
- Any "follow these steps" band in documentation prose, however short.

## Do

- Start each step title with the verb; keep the how in the step's body.
- Let the numbering be the document order — never encode a number into a title.
- Give a step a body only when the heading alone does not carry it; the rail stretches to cover whatever the body holds.

## Don’t

- For a wizard or form flow inside the application — that is `Stepper` (or `Wizard`), not documentation chrome.
- For an unordered list of options or features — order is the whole claim this component makes; a list that has none is a plain list or `DocItem` rows.
- For a single instruction — one step is a sentence, not a walkthrough.

## Related

- DocStep` — the sibling root this numbers; a step registers with this context on mount and throws when rendered outside one.
- Stepper` — the app's interactive step rail. Both number their steps with the same shared step registry (`useStepRegistry`), which reads the order from the page, so a step inserted between two others takes its place in the count.
- DocProse` — the contract around it. The column marks itself `data-doc-block`, so it takes the block rung of the prose ladder.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `DocStep` children, in the order they should be numbered. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the column is not interactive and holds no visual state of its own)
- Provides the numbering context (the shared step registry): each `DocStep` registers in setup, hands over its element on mount and deregisters on unmount; `index` is the 1-based position on the page; the final step's connector is suppressed by a last-child CSS variant
- `data-doc-block` is the `DocProse` contract (the column takes the block rung of the ladder)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the column is not focusable; `Tab` reaches only interactive content nested inside a step's body.
- Keyboard map: none of its own.
- ARIA: the column is a plain block. The circled indices and the rail are decorative (`aria-hidden`, owned by `DocStep`), so assistive tech reads the step headings and bodies in document order — the same order the numbers claim.
- Contrast: inherited from `DocStep`; the column paints nothing.
- Touch target: not applicable; the component is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocStep from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-step'
  import DocSteps from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-steps'
</script>

<template>
  <DocSteps>
    <DocStep title="Access Azion Console." />
    <DocStep title="Click + Create on the homepage." />
    <DocStep title="Select your preferred template to start your project." />
    <DocStep title="Fill in the fields the template asks for." />
    <DocStep title="Customize the elements using the sidebar tools." />
  </DocSteps>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/doc-steps.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-steps.md).

# Doc Tabs

> Alternative paths through the same instruction ("macOS / Linux / Windows", "Console / CLI"). It reads the `title` of each `DocTab` child to build the strip and renders each child body in its panel, on `Tabs`, so the strip, the indicator and the keyboard model are the design system's.

- Import: `import DocTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-tabs'`
- Category: docs · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DocTabs only in documentation prose for alternative paths through one instruction (macOS / Linux); product UI uses Tabs.
- The same procedure that differs per platform or per tool.

## Do

- Two to five tabs; put the most common path first.
- Keep the panels parallel so switching compares like with like.

## Don’t

- For code-only alternatives — use `DocCodeGroup`.
- For page navigation — use links or `DocCardGroup`.

## Related

- DocTab` — the panel it reads.
- Tabs` — the surface it renders on.
- DocCodeGroup`.

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `DocTab` children, in strip order. A child without a `title` is labelled by its position. |

## States

- The first tab is selected on render; selection state comes from `Tabs`.
- `data-doc-block` on the root; the strip carries `data-doc-chrome`.

## Accessibility

- `tablist`, `tab` and `tabpanel` roles and the arrow-key model come from `Tabs`.
- Panels have no padding of their own; the first block in a panel carries the prose rhythm.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only.
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged (the underlying component handles arrow direction).

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is content and arrives through props or slots, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- The strip scrolls inside its own row on narrow screens (from `Tabs`).

<!-- components/alert.md -->

# Alert

> Use Alert for a persistent message on a console page or section (info, warning, error) — the answer for 'banner' or 'notice'. A short confirmation after an action that disappears on its own is a Toast. Inline feedback banner that communicates status, alerts, or progress. Presents a severity-colored surface with a leading icon, an optional bold `title` over the copy, and message copy that may carry inline links, plus an optional secondary action button.

- Import: `import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A status, warning or error that belongs to a page, section or form and should stay visible in context.
- A notice with an inline link, or with one follow-up action (`actionLabel` or the `actions` slot).
- A notice that needs a short headline and a sentence of detail (`title` over the copy): "Maintenance scheduled" over the window and what changes.

## Do

- Pick `severity` by meaning. `danger` and `warning` render with `role="alert"`.
- Use `label` for plain copy and the default slot when the copy needs inline links.
- Set `title` when the alert says two things: what happened (the title, a few words, no end period) and what it means or what to do (the copy). A one-sentence alert needs no title. A title alone, with no copy, is allowed for a short notice that still wants the heading weight.
- Use either the built-in action (`actionLabel` with `@action`) or the `actions` slot, not both. The slot replaces the button.
- Once `closable` or `life` dismisses the message, it stays hidden until it is remounted. Listen to `close` to keep your own state in sync.
- Use `size="small"` inside dense surfaces such as cards and drawers.

## Don’t

- A transient confirmation of an action → use `toast`.
- Validation feedback under one form field → use `field-error`.
- An admonition inside documentation prose → use `doc-callout`.
- A promotional band between page sections → use `call-to-action` with `variant="announcement"`.

## Related

- `toast` — overlay stack raised imperatively, auto-dismissing and not anchored to content.
- field-error` — field-level guidance and errors below an input.
- `doc-callout` — docs admonition rendered on the `Alert` surface.
- `empty-state` — a full zero-data block, not a status banner.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` | false | Visual severity variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token. Drives the banner height, inline padding, copy scale, and the trailing control sizes. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback message copy when the default slot is empty. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Bold heading above the message copy; hidden when empty. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class override for the leading icon. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label for the built-in secondary action button; hidden when empty. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, shows a close control that dismisses the message. |
| `life` | `number` | `0` | false | Duration in milliseconds before auto-dismiss; `0` disables auto-dismiss. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `MouseEvent` | Emitted when the built-in action button is clicked. |
| `close` | `(event: Event)` | Emitted when the message is dismissed, after the fade. Carries the originating event: the close button's `MouseEvent`, the `Escape` `KeyboardEvent`, or an `Event` of type `timeout` after `life` expires. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Custom action control; replaces the built-in Button when provided. |
| `default` | — | Alert copy. Inline content — plain text plus anchors, which the message region styles with the `.text-link` token — or flow content such as paragraphs and a list. The copy region is a flow container (a `div`, not a `p`), so block markup arriving from a server render stays inside it instead of being closed out beside the copy. Falls back to `label` when empty. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: default (per severity)
- `data-titled` on the root mirrors a non-empty `title`: the title renders above the copy in `.text-heading-2xs` (`__title`), and the copy keeps its size below it. With a title and no copy (no default slot, empty `label`), only the title renders.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/alert`. Below `@sm` of its box the action (built-in or the `actions` slot, wrapped in `[data-slot=alert-actions]`) moves to its own line under the message while the close button stays on the message line.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses inline links in the message copy, then the action and close controls when present; `Enter` follows a link, `Enter`/`Space` activates the controls; `Escape` dismisses when `closable` is true.
- ARIA: root uses `role="alert"` for danger/warning severities and `role="status"` for info/success. The title is text inside the live region, read before the copy; it is not a document heading, so it does not enter the page outline.
- Inline links are underlined, not colour-only, so they stay distinguishable against every severity surface (WCAG 1.4.1); the `.text-link` token supplies the focus outline.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the dismiss fade; nothing sets the transition inline.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`pe-`, `gap`, flex order), so the icon leads and the controls trail under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: severity glyphs and the close `×` are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key           | English source  | Override prop |
| ------------- | --------------- | ------------- |
| `alert.close` | `Close message` | —             |

- Formatting: none; `title`, `label` and the slot copy come from the consumer.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the root is `@container/alert`; below `@sm` the action moves to its own line under the message.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the title and copy wrap; the close button stays on the first line.
- Touch: the action and close take Button / IconButton sizes (28 or 32 px); no hover-only affordance.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long words break (`break-words`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'
</script>

<template>
  <Alert
    severity="info"
    label="Your workload finished deploying in 42 seconds."
    action-label="Label"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/alert.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/alert.md).

<!-- components/empty-state.md -->

# Empty State

> Centered placeholder shown when a resource list or section has no content yet. Stacks an optional standardized adornment, a title, an optional description, and a consumer-composed actions area (buttons + documentation link) to guide the user toward a first action. The adornment is a standardized, size-scaled featured-icon tile driven by the `icon` prop; the consumer may instead supply custom content via the `icon` slot, or omit both for no adornment. Unlike `Alert`, which is an inline severity banner, `EmptyState` is a full-region zero-data state and renders either inside a bordered surface card or on a plain transparent background.

- Import: `import EmptyState from '@aziontech/webkit/empty-state'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A list, table or section that has no items yet, with a first action that fills it.
- A search or filter that returned nothing, with an action to clear it.

## Do

- title` is required. Say what is missing ("No domains yet"), not that something went wrong.
- Keep the `actions` slot to one primary action, plus an optional documentation link.
- Leave the actions at their own width, centred, on every screen size (the design sample's look). Do not add `w-full` to a button in the slot to make it span a phone screen.
- Use the `icon` prop for the standard featured-icon tile. Use the `icon` slot only for custom art, and omit both when the context already explains the state.
- Use `bordered` when the block sits directly on the page. Leave it off inside a card or panel that already has a border, and use `size="small"` there.

## Don’t

- The data is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- An inline warning or error about content that is present → use `alert`.
- The empty body of a data-driven `table` → use the `table` `empty` slot, which already renders this block by default.

## Related

- `skeleton` — the loading placeholder shown before the empty state is known.
- `alert` — inline severity banner, not a zero-data block.
- `table` — renders an empty-state block in its `empty` slot.
- `button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | Primary heading announcing the empty resource. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting body copy below the title. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the standardized adornment (e.g. `ai ai-inbox`). When set, renders a size-scaled featured-icon tile; when empty and the `icon` slot is unused, no adornment renders. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token (subset — only `small` and `medium`; no `large`). Scales the whole block on one harmonic ramp — the adornment size, the title and description typography, the surrounding padding, and the gaps between adornment, text, and actions all step up together. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, wraps the content in a dashed-bordered surface card; otherwise renders on a transparent background. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | — | Custom adornment centered above the title, rendered inside an `aria-hidden` container. Overrides the `icon` prop's featured-icon tile. When neither this slot nor the `icon` prop is provided, no adornment renders. |
| `actions` | — | Action area below the description; consumer composes buttons and the documentation link. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-bordered` mirrors the `bordered` prop
- Responsive: the actions keep their own width and stay centred at every box width, as the design sample draws them (a phone included); the action column is capped at `max-w-full`, so a long label wraps inside the box instead of overflowing it.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the consumer-supplied controls in the `actions` slot in DOM order; the region itself is non-interactive.
- ARIA: root uses `role="status"` so assistive tech announces the empty-data message; the `icon` slot container is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import EmptyState from '@aziontech/webkit/empty-state'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <EmptyState
    title="No resource yet"
    description="Get started by creating your first resource."
    icon="ai ai-inbox"
  >
    <template #actions>
      <div class="flex gap-(--spacing-3)">
        <Button
          variant="secondary"
          label="Secondary Item"
        />
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          label="Create Item"
        />
      </div>
      <Link
        label="Docs"
        icon="ai ai-arrow-right"
        size="medium"
        href="#"
      />
    </template>
  </EmptyState>
</template>
```
