# File Token Group

> Use FileTokenGroup for the files picked in a form field, before and during upload; a transfer that runs in the background while the person keeps working is an UploadProgress. The files a person picked for upload, shown as removable tokens before or while they upload: each token names the file with a glyph for its type, its size and, when asked, its last-modified date, carries a progress bar while it uploads and its own error or warning line when it cannot be sent. It pairs with `file-dropzone` (which receives the files) and with a Browse files button: the product keeps the list, the group renders it and reports which token was removed. Taken from Cloudscape's file token group; the Console Kit and the design sample list files by hand.

- Import: `import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Under a `FileDropzone` or a Browse files button in a form, to show what will be uploaded and let the person drop a file before submitting.
- In an upload dialog, to show each file's progress and the files that were refused (too large, wrong type) with the reason.
- Read-only, in a review step, to list the attachments that will be sent.

## Do

- Keep the refused files in the list with their error, so the person sees why and can remove them; do not drop them silently.
- Write each error as the reason and the limit (`Larger than 300 MB`), not as a code.
- Use `limit` when more than five files are common, so the form below stays in view.
- Remove the file from your list on `remove`; the group moves focus to the next token for you.

## Don’t

- A running transfer that should follow the person around the console → use `upload-progress`.
- Files already stored in a bucket or a repository → use `table` (the file browser block).
- Free-text tags or labels → use `tag-editor` or `chip`.

## Related

- `file-dropzone` — receives dropped files; the group lists them.
- `upload-progress` — the floating card for transfers that keep running after the dialog closes. Split: FileTokenGroup lists the files picked in a form, before and while they are sent, and dies with the form; UploadProgress tracks transfers that outlive the dialog, with Cancel and Retry. Both draw a file row with a progress bar; when a transfer must survive navigation, hand it to UploadProgress instead of keeping the token.
- `chip` — a removable label without file details.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `FileTokenGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | The files, in order; each with its optional upload state, error and warning. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Vertical stacks full-width tokens; horizontal wraps compact tokens in rows. Same name as `field`'s axis. |
| `limit` | `number` | `0` | false | Shows this many tokens and a Show more toggle for the rest. 0 shows them all. |
| `showFileSize` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the size beside the name, formatted for the locale. |
| `showFileLastModified` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the last-modified date, formatted for the locale. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hides the remove buttons; the list is for reading only. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Files`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { index: number; item: FileTokenGroupItem })` | The remove button of the token at `index` was pressed. The parent removes it from `items`. Same name as Chip and AttributeEditor. |

## States

- Root `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal`; `data-readonly` when read-only.
- Token `data-status`: `idle` | `loading` | `warning` | `error` (error wins over warning, both over loading).
- Show more toggle: `aria-expanded` `true` | `false`.
- A file with a `webkitRelativePath` (picked with a folder picker or dropped as a folder on `FileDropzone directories`) is named by that path (`site/css/main.css`) in the token, its title, the remove button and the progress bar; otherwise by `name`.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `ul` (`role="list"`) named by `ariaLabel` or the catalog; each token is a `li`.
- Each remove button is an `IconButton` named `Remove <file name>`; its `aria-describedby` points at the token's error or warning line, so the reason is read with it.
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches each remove button and the Show more toggle in order; Enter or Space removes. After a removal focus moves to the remove button now at the same index, else the previous one, else the list itself (`tabindex="-1"`).
- An error or warning is shown as text with an icon, never by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1); the uploading bar is a `progressbar` named `Uploading <file name>`.
- Contrast: name and meta ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface` in both themes; the danger border ≥ 3:1.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `ps-`, `text-start`); the remove button sits at the inline end.
- Icons: file glyphs and the cross are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: Tab order follows the reading order.
- User data: file names render in `<bdi>` so a Latin name keeps its order inside rtl text.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source                                                | Override prop |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `fileTokenGroup.label`     | Files                                                         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `fileTokenGroup.remove`    | Remove {name}                                                 | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.uploading` | Uploading {name}                                              | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.modified`  | Modified {date}                                               | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.showMore`  | `Show {count} more file` / `Show {count} more files` (plural) | —             |
| `fileTokenGroup.showLess`  | Show fewer files                                              | —             |

- Formatting: sizes with `formatFileSize`, dates with `formatDate` (`dateStyle: 'medium'`), both from `useLocale`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; vertical tokens fill their container, horizontal tokens are at most `--container-3xs` wide and wrap.
- Narrow: names truncate with an ellipsis and keep the full name in `title`.
- Touch: the remove button is a small `IconButton` (32 px), 44 px hit area on `pointer: coarse` through the button.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const LIMIT = 300 * 1024 * 1024

  const inputEl = ref(null)
  const items = ref([
    { file: { name: 'logo.svg', size: 4210, type: 'image/svg+xml' } },
    { file: { name: 'index.html', size: 18432, type: 'text/html' } },
    { file: { name: 'site-backup.tar', size: 412_000_000 }, error: 'Larger than 300 MB' },
    { file: { name: 'notes.txt', size: 0, type: 'text/plain' }, warning: 'This file is empty' }
  ])

  const toItem = (file) => ({
    file,
    error: file.size > LIMIT ? 'Larger than 300 MB' : undefined,
    warning: file.size === 0 ? 'This file is empty' : undefined
  })

  const add = (files) => {
    items.value = [...items.value, ...Array.from(files).map(toItem)]
  }

  const onPick = (event) => {
    add(event.target.files ?? [])
    event.target.value = ''
  }

  const remove = (index) => {
    items.value = items.value.filter((_, position) => position !== index)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-md) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <FileDropzone
      description="Up to 300 MB per file."
      @drop="(event, files) => add(files)"
    >
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        variant="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="inputEl?.click()"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <input
      ref="inputEl"
      type="file"
      multiple
      class="hidden"
      aria-hidden="true"
      tabindex="-1"
      @change="onPick"
    />
    <FileTokenGroup
      :items="items"
      @remove="(_event, { index }) => remove(index)"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/file-token-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/file-token-group.md).

<!-- components/hint.md -->

# Hint

> Small info affordance — a muted `ai ai-circle-info` glyph on a focusable button — that reveals one short explanation on hover or focus, through `Tooltip`. It is the standard way to attach a "why does this matter?" note to a field name without spending a line of vertical space on it, and it is what `Field.Label`'s `hint` prop renders.

- Import: `import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Hint for the info glyph beside a field label or column header that explains it in one sentence. Guidance that must stay visible goes in Field.Description (inside Field) or FieldDescription.
- A field, switch or setting whose name is clear but whose consequence is not (what "Sensitive" does to a stored value).
- A short, self-contained sentence — one that reads fine in a tooltip and is not needed to complete the field.
- Beside a label, a section heading, or a table column header, where a permanent line of helper text would add noise.

## Do

- One sentence, ending in a period. If it needs two, it belongs in `field-description` or a `popover`.
- Never hide required information behind a hint — hover is not discoverable on touch, so treat it as an enhancement.
- The `content` doubles as the button's accessible name, so write it as prose a screen reader can read verbatim.
- Place it immediately after the thing it explains, not at the end of a row.

## Don’t

- Guidance the user needs while typing, or any validation message → use `field-error` (it stays on screen and is wired with `aria-describedby`).
- More than a sentence, links, or formatted content → use `popover`, which is dismissible and can hold real content.
- A plain description of an action already labelled by a control → use `tooltip` directly on that control.

## Related

- `tooltip` — the overlay `Hint` composes; reach for it when the trigger is an existing control rather than a standalone info glyph.
- field-description` — persistent guidance under a field; the right choice when the text must always be visible.
- Field.Label` — renders `Hint` from its own `hint` prop, so a field name and its note stay one component.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | true | Guidance text revealed on hover or focus; also the trigger's accessible name. |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'auto'` | `'top'` | false | Anchor side of the tooltip relative to the glyph. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`
- `data-state` values (on the root, owned by `Tooltip`): `open` | `closed`
- `data-placement` (on the root, owned by `Tooltip`): `top` | `right` | `bottom` | `left`

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a native `<button type="button">`, so it is in the tab order and the tooltip opens on `focus` as well as hover (`Tooltip` opens on `focusin`).
- The glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); the button's accessible name is the `content` prop, so the hint is reachable by screen readers that never see the tooltip.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus to the glyph and opens the tooltip; `Escape` closes it (owned by `Tooltip`); the button has no activation behaviour.
- The button's default action is prevented on click, so a `Hint` rendered inside a `<label>` never toggles the labelled control.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 between `var(--text-muted)` and `var(--bg-canvas)`; the focus ring uses `var(--ring-color)` at 2px with an offset.
- Touch target: the glyph is drawn at 20×20 px inline with 12 px label text; a `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to 24×24 px (WCAG 2.5.8), and to 44×44 px on a coarse pointer. It is an enhancement, never the only path to the information.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'
</script>

<template>
  <Hint content="Values are encrypted at rest and never displayed again after saving." />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/hint.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/hint.md).

<!-- components/input.md -->

# Input

> Single-line text input for forms and inline editing. Renders a bordered field with optional leading/trailing icon slots. Visual states (hover, focus, filled) are driven by native CSS pseudo-classes, not props. The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and error messages live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `562:6774` (Webkit / Input).

- Import: `import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture a single line of free-form text (names, titles, search terms).
- Use Input with a search icon to filter a list in place; to open the ⌘K palette use SearchTrigger.

## Do

- Wrap it in `Field` when you need a label, helper text, or validation message.
- Set an appropriate `type`/`inputmode` for the content (email, url, …).
- Set `monospace` on a field whose value is code-like: a CLI command, an ID, a token, a hash, a path. Pair it with `:spellcheck="false"`.
- A read-only command or ID the user copies: `readonly` + `monospace` inside an `InputGroup` with a `CopyButton`, and a description saying why it cannot change.
- Do not set `monospace` on prose values (names, titles, e-mails, domains typed by the user).
- Do not restyle a read-only field (dashed border, transparent fill): it is the same filled field, made non-editable; the reason belongs in the field's description.

## Don’t

- The value spans multiple lines → use `textarea`.
- The value is strictly numeric → use `number-input`.
- The user must choose from a fixed set → use `select` / `multi-select`.

## Related

- `textarea` — multi-line free text.
- `number-input` — numeric input with stepper semantics.
- `field` — wraps this input with label, description and error; the input reads its id, `aria-describedby` and state from it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `type` | `'text' \| 'email' \| 'number'` | `'text'` | false | Native input type. Restricted to single-line variants the field treats identically. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `autocomplete` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `autocomplete` token on the `<input>` (e.g. `email`, `username`, `off`). Omitted when unset. |
| `spellcheck` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `spellcheck` on the `<input>`. Set `false` for slugs, IDs and domains. Omitted when unset: the default is an explicit `undefined`, because Vue would otherwise cast an absent boolean to `false` and render `spellcheck="false"` on every field. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height only — padding and typography are constant. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only: value is visible, focusable and copyable but not editable. Keeps the filled field (surface and solid border) with no hover border and a default cursor (`data-readonly`); distinct from the disabled field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-label-code-sm`) for CLI commands, IDs, tokens and hashes (`data-monospace`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). Logical: it sits on the right under `dir="rtl"`. |
| `trailing` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                     |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''`    | `update:modelValue` | The field value via `defineModel`; updates on every native `input` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`
- Password managers: the `<input>` carries `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore`, `data-bwignore` and `data-form-type="other"` unless it is a credential or identity field — `autocomplete` set to any token but `off`, or `type="email"`. A read-only field always carries them. This keeps 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden and Dashlane from offering a sign-in on ordinary fields (names, IDs, searches) while login fields stay fillable. A consumer attr (e.g. `data-1p-ignore="false"`) wins.
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop: a read-only field keeps the editable field's fill (`var(--bg-surface)`) and solid `var(--border-default)` border, as the design sample draws it; it only drops the hover border and takes a default cursor. The value keeps `var(--text-default)` (readable and copyable, unlike `disabled`) and the field stays focusable. Why the value cannot change is said by the field's description, not by a different chrome.
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value and the placeholder render in `.text-label-code-sm` instead of `.text-label-sm`.
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; drives the warning-border treatment
- `data-leading` / `data-trailing` mirror slot presence (driven by `$slots.leading` / `$slots.trailing`), read at render time: an icon slot passed behind a `v-if` adds or removes its icon box when the condition changes, never leaving an empty box behind
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2`, with the offset color resolving `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots. A host that places the field on a surface other than the canvas (a raised popover, a drawer) declares `--input-ring-offset` on any ancestor; custom properties inherit, so one declaration retunes the ring gap of every field inside it (this is how `date-picker`'s fields panel matches its raised popover).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; standard text-editing keys apply.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; icon slots are `aria-hidden="true"` (decorative).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are intended for dense layouts where the wrapping label area extends the hit zone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the icon slots are the consumer's and do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Input
    v-model="value"
    placeholder="Type something"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/input.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/input.md).

<!-- components/input-group.md -->

# Input Group

> Composition container that joins an input primitive with any number of adjacent controls (buttons, selects, static addons) into a single visual field (an input group, as other UI kits call it). The root only orchestrates: it draws the outer border, the `focus-within` ring, and applies inline Tailwind child-selectors so the first child rounds only on the left, the last only on the right, and internal borders collapse between siblings. Everything else is a **child**: the middle input is a raw `<input>` in the root's `default` slot; sibling controls (`<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, or an `<InputGroup.Addon>` for static text like `https://` / `.com` / `$`) are dropped in directly alongside it. This is a breaking change from v3: the `#left` and `#right` named slots are gone — their static-text role moves to `<InputGroup.Addon>`, and their interactive role is served by placing the real component (`Button`, `Select`) as a direct child. Consumers therefore never wrap `Button`/`Select` in an inner `<div>` — the root's child selectors do that job.

- Import: `import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import InputGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A text input that needs static prefix or suffix content inside the same border (`https://`, `.com`, a currency symbol).
- An input joined to a control: a search field with a trailing `button`, an amount with a leading currency `select`.

## Do

- Put static text and icons in `InputGroup.Addon`; place real controls (`button`, `select`) as direct children with no wrapper `div`.
- Set the same `size` on the group and on its child controls so heights line up.
- disabled` and `invalid` on the group reach every field control inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select` and the other controls that read the Field context); a `Button` or `IconButton` in the group needs its own `disabled`. `required` styles the group only; set it on the input or on the enclosing `Field`. Inside a `Field`, the Field's state reaches the root and the controls the same way.
- Use `InputGroup.Input` for the middle input: it is borderless, picks up the enclosing `Field`'s wiring, and spares the long raw-`<input>` class string.
- The root is `role="group"`; label the inner input itself, or give the group an `aria-label`.

## Don’t

- A phone number with a dial code → use `phone-input`.
- A single input with only a decorative icon → use `input` and its `iconLeft` / `iconRight` slots.

## Related

- `field` — wrap the group in a `Field` for a label and description/error; `InputGroup.Input` takes the field's id, `aria-describedby` and state, and the root takes `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` from it.
- `phone-input` — input group with a dial-code select and a per-country mask.
- `input` — the single-field primitive with icon slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the root's height and inner addon padding. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. Matches the sibling input primitives (`Input`, `Select`) — set the same `size` on child controls to keep them visually aligned. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the error border and marks the field controls inside invalid (`aria-invalid` on the input, never on the `role="group"` root, where ARIA does not allow it). |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the required (warning) border. `aria-required` is not allowed on `role="group"`, so the required state belongs on the input (`InputGroup.Input` reads it from the Field). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the disabled visual, sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the root and disables the field controls inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select`, …) through the Field context. A `Button` or `IconButton` inside needs its own `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | On the **root**: the full row of children in visual order — any mix of `<InputGroup.Addon>`, `<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, raw `<input>`. Order in the template is the order rendered left-to-right. On **`<InputGroup.Addon>`**: the addon content — text (`https://`, `.com`, `$`), an Azion icon `<i>`, or any small inline node; kept short by convention (long content breaks the fixed row height). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon`
- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input`

## Sub-components

Folder layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/input/input-group/
├── input-group.vue                      # root
├── input-group-addon/
│   └── input-group-addon.vue            # <InputGroup.Addon>
├── input-group-input/
│   └── input-group-input.vue            # <InputGroup.Input>
└── index.ts                             # compound wire-up (Object.assign)
```

Public members of the compound:

| Member               | Attached name           | Standalone export                     | Purpose                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Root                 | — (the compound itself) | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root`  | The container. Orchestrates borders, seams, focus ring, and states.                                                                |
| `<InputGroup.Addon>` | `Addon`                 | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon` | Static-content island (icon, text like `https://`, `.com`, `$`) rendered with the darker `--bg-canvas` fill and muted text.        |
| `<InputGroup.Input>` | `Input`                 | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input` | Borderless middle `<input>`, with the same inline padding as `Input` (`--spacing-sm`). Props: `modelValue` (`''`), `type` (`'text' | 'email' | 'number' | 'password'`, default `'text'`: the restricted set of `Input`, plus `password`to mask a secret value that a reveal control in an addon toggles back to`text`), `placeholder` (`''`), `autocomplete`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `required`, `invalid`(all`false`); emits `update:modelValue`. Reads `id`, `aria-describedby`, `invalid`, `disabled`and`required`from an enclosing`Field` (an explicit prop/attribute wins). |

The root reads `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from an enclosing `Field` too, OR-ed with its own props, so a `Field`'s state styles the whole group. The root then provides the Field context to its children with `invalid` and `disabled` OR-ed with the group's own (the parent Field's id, description, title and `required` pass through), so the group's state reaches the controls inside.

## States

- Visual states on root: `default`, `hover`, `focus-within`, `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop and drives the root height (`small`=`h-7`, `medium`=`h-8`, `large`=`h-10`)
- Only one focus indicator is visible when a descendant is focused: the group draws the single `focus-within` ring on its root, and the inner input primitives' own focus rings are suppressed via `[&_*]:focus-visible:!ring-0 [&_*]:focus-within:!ring-0` so `Button`, `Select.Trigger`, `Input` wrappers, and raw `<input>` share the group's ring instead of stacking their own on top
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop; `aria-invalid` lands on the controls inside, not on the root
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop (no `aria-required` on the group root)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; sets `aria-disabled="true"`
- Border semantics mirror `input` (independent, not compound):
  - `data-invalid` → `var(--danger-border)`
  - `data-required` → `var(--warning-border)`
- Hover (only when not focus-within, not invalid, not required, not disabled): `border-(--border-strong)`
- Focus-within: 2-ring at `var(--ring-color)` with `var(--bg-canvas)` offset (suppressed when `data-disabled`)
- Disabled: `bg-(--bg-disabled)`, `text-(--text-disabled)`, `cursor-not-allowed`, hover ignored, focus-within ring suppressed
- Child seams (applied by the root via Tailwind child selectors):
  - `[&>*:first-child]:rounded-l-(--shape-control)` and `[&>*:not(:first-child)]:rounded-l-none`
  - `[&>*:last-child]:rounded-r-(--shape-control)` and `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:rounded-r-none`
  - `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r-(color:--border-default) [&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r` — a single vertical seam between adjacent children, drawn on the left child so child components keep their own left border intact
  - Child components' own outer borders remain — the root's outer border sits on top, so double lines are avoided by the child selector removing the _inner-facing_ border only

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the root shows a `focus-within` ring (`ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-2 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`) whenever any descendant (any child control or the middle input) has focus. The middle input renders `focus:ring-0 outline-none` so the group's ring is the only visible focus indicator. Suppressed when `data-disabled` is present. Child components (`Button`, `Select`) retain their own focus behavior internally but the group's ring is visually authoritative.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the children in DOM order. No custom keybindings on the group.
- ARIA: root uses `role="group"` with `aria-disabled`; `aria-invalid` is set on the controls inside (ARIA 1.2 does not allow it on `group`); `required` is styling only on the root. Each child keeps its own `aria-*` — the group does not duplicate.
- `<InputGroup.Addon>` is decorative-by-default; when its content is not conveyed elsewhere the consumer should annotate it (`aria-hidden="true"` for pure decoration, or a visible-only label the middle input references via `aria-describedby`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for addon text against `var(--bg-canvas)`; ≥3:1 for the border in every state.
- Motion: color transitions on state changes are `duration-150 ease-out` and pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥32×32 px for interactive children (matches root height `h-8`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'
</script>

<template>
  <InputGroupRoot>
    <input
      placeholder="domain"
      class="flex-1 min-w-0 h-full bg-(--bg-surface) border-0 outline-none focus:ring-0 px-(--spacing-md) text-label-sm text-(--text-default) placeholder:text-(--text-muted)"
    />
  </InputGroupRoot>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/input-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/input-group.md).

<!-- components/multi-select.md -->

# Multi Select

> Select control specialised for choosing many options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a MultiSelect sits next to other form fields without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Every option row carries a checkbox indicator (the `Checkbox` webkit component), optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<MultiSelectContent>`. Since spec v4 the trigger can also show the selection as removable chips (`variant="chips"`, capped by `chipLimit` with a `+N more` chip), take typed text to filter the options in place (`searchable`), offer an `Add "…"` row for a typed value that matches no option (`allowCustom`, emits `create`), and render its own loading, error and empty list states (`loading`, `error`, `emptyTitle`) — the same vocabulary as `combobox`. MultiSelect is the one multi-pick field (`Select` picks exactly one): `modelValue` is always an array and the indicator is always a checkbox. Aligned with Figma frame `3899:29362` (options panel). The trigger reuses the `Input`/`Select` trigger visuals.

- Import: `import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import MultiSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use MultiSelect whenever the person picks several values from a list in a form field; the chosen ones show as a count or chips in the trigger. For two to five options that fit on screen use a Checkbox per option; to build a large subset with both sides visible use TransferList.
- Choosing several values from a long list (regions, tags, permissions) in a compact field.
- A filter whose selected values stay editable from the same dropdown.
- Grouped options with icons or trailing tags, optionally with search.
- Tagging a record with labels people pick or type (`variant="chips"` + `searchable` + `allowCustom`).
- Options fetched from a server as the person types (`searchable`, `:filter="false"`, `@search`, `loading`, `error`).

## Do

- modelValue` is always an array; start it as `[]`, never `null`.
- Pass `displayValue` to summarise long selections (e.g. "3 regions") instead of a list that overflows the trigger.
- Keep each option's `value` stable and unique; selection is matched by value.
- Put a search input in the `search` slot and a create action in the `footer` slot of `MultiSelect.Content` — or set `searchable` (and `allowCustom`) to type in the trigger itself; do not combine the two.
- With `variant="chips"`, set `chipLimit` when the field sits in a dense row; leave it `0` in a form so every chip wraps and stays removable.
- create` only reports the typed value: add the new option to your list and its value to the model in the handler.
- For a server-side search, set `:filter="false"`, fetch on `search`, and drive `loading` and `error` from the request.

## Don’t

- Only one value may be chosen → use `select`.
- A labelled form field with helper/error text → put it inside a `field`.
- A handful of options that fit on screen → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
- The user builds a subset and needs the chosen and remaining items side by side → use `transfer-list`.
- Free-form tags with no list of options to pick from → use `tag-editor`.

## Related

- `select` — single-choice counterpart.
- `field` — wraps this control with its label, description and error; it hands the trigger its id and state.
- `transfer-list` — dual-list transfer for building larger subsets.
- `checkbox` — the indicator every option row renders.
- `combobox` — single-value field with typed text; `searchable`, `allowCustom`, `filter`, `loading` and `emptyTitle` share its meaning.
- `chip` — each selected value in `variant="chips"`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets `aria-required` on the trigger. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger. |
| `displayValue` | `(value: TValue[]) => string` | `undefined` | false | Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selected labels; receives the current `modelValue` array. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, the root renders one hidden input per selected value so a native `form` and `FormData` submit every selection under that name; `required` then adds a hidden required proxy that blocks an empty submit, and `disabled` leaves the values out. |
| `variant` | `'summary' \| 'chips'` | `'summary'` | false | How the trigger shows the selection: `summary` joins the labels (or `displayValue`), `chips` renders one removable chip per value. |
| `chipLimit` | `number` | `0` | false | With `variant="chips"`, the most chips shown before a `+N more` chip; `0` shows every chip and wraps. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Types in the trigger: the text filters the options, `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last value. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | `true` | false | With `searchable`, hides the options whose label does not contain the typed text. Turn off when the server filters on `search`. |
| `allowCustom` | `boolean` | `false` | false | With `searchable`, offers typed text that matches no option as an `Add "…"` row that emits `create`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the loading row in place of the options while they are fetched. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Message shown in place of the options when they failed to load; empty shows the options. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the list when no option is visible. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `modelValue` | `TValue[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` | The typed text, on each keystroke (`searchable`), and `''` when the panel closes and the text is cleared. Value event: no DOM event. |
| `create` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string)` | The `Add "…"` row was activated (`allowCustom`), by click or by `Enter` in the field or on the row; `value` is the trimmed typed text. The typed text is cleared; the consumer adds the option and the value. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition slot; receives `<MultiSelectTrigger>` and `<MultiSelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-item`

## Sub-components

- `multi-select-trigger/multi-select-trigger.vue` — With the default `variant="summary"` and no `searchable`, a bordered trigger button; otherwise a bordered field (`min-h` of the size, wrapping) that holds the chips (`…
- `multi-select-content/multi-select-content.vue` — Popover panel teleported to `body` and anchored with `usePlacement`; exposes `default` (the options), `#search` and `#footer` slots, typed with `defineSlots`, and scro…
- `multi-select-group/multi-select-group.vue` — Section wrapper for a labelled group of options; hidden while the typed filter hides every one of its options; renders a `text-label-sm` heading in `--text-muted` when `la…
- `multi-select-item/multi-select-item.vue` — Selectable option row; hidden (`v-show`) while `searchable` + `filter` and its label text does not contain the typed text (case and accent insensitive, in the active locale)…

## v-model

| Model          | Type       | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ---------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model`      | `TValue[]` | `[]`        | `update:modelValue` | The selection via `defineModel`. Always an array; each item is the `value` of a selected `<MultiSelectItem>`. Fires when an option is toggled with the next selection array. Uncontrolled when unbound. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean`  | `undefined` | `update:open`       | Open state of the dropdown via `defineModel`. Fires when the dropdown opens or closes. Unbound, the dropdown keeps its own state, seeded by `defaultOpen`.                                              |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `opened`
- `data-state` on the root and trigger: `open` | `closed`
- `data-size` on the trigger mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-filled` mirror the matching props (or the selection state for `data-filled`)
- `data-selected` on `<MultiSelectItem>` when the option's value is part of the current selection
- `data-variant` on the root and trigger mirrors `variant`; `data-searchable` on the trigger mirrors `searchable`
- `loading`: `aria-busy` on the listbox and the loading row; `error`: the message row; `empty`: the empty row — each in place of the options, in the panel
- `data-variant="create"` on the `Add "…"` row
- Typed filter: while the typed text is not empty, every chunk is mounted so the filter sees every option.
- Long lists: above 300 options the list mounts in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep their height, 32 px per option), so opening a 1,000-option list stays within its runtime budget. The first arrow, `Home` or `End` key in the list mounts every option before moving focus, so keyboard navigation always reaches every option.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and on every option row.
- Keyboard map (trigger): `Tab` focuses; `Space`/`Enter`/`ArrowDown` opens the panel; `Escape` closes it.
- Keyboard map (closed trigger): `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` open the list (focus lands as described below); `Home` opens it on the first enabled option and `End` on the last; typing a printable character opens it on the first enabled option whose label starts with that character (with a search field, focus goes to the search field instead). Clicking the trigger while the list is open closes it. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › Select keyboard and naming (APG select-only combobox).
- Keyboard map (`searchable` field): typing filters and opens the panel; `ArrowDown` opens and focuses the first visible option, `ArrowUp` the last; `Enter` activates the `Add "…"` row when it is offered, else opens the panel; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last selected value; `Escape` closes the panel, then clears the text; `Tab` closes and moves on. From the list, `Escape`, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` return focus to the field instead of a trigger button.
- Chips: each chip's remove button is in the tab order and named `Remove <label>` (from `Chip`); removing one never opens the panel. The `+N more` chip is plain text.
- Keyboard map (open panel): opening focuses the search field when there is one, else the first selected option, else the first enabled option; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between enabled options and wrap; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last enabled; `Enter`/`Space` toggles the focused option and keeps the panel open; typing a printable character moves focus to the next enabled option whose label starts with the typed text (characters typed within 500 ms add up; ignored while the search field has focus); `Escape` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes and moves focus to the control after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: trigger uses `role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` bound to open state, `aria-controls` pointing to the list. The teleported content is a plain panel holding the optional search field, the list and the optional footer; the list (not the panel) carries `role="listbox"`, so the search field sits outside it, and is named by the root's `aria-label`, else by the root's `aria-labelledby`, else by the enclosing `Field` label, else by the trigger (which always has an `id`). The list uses `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable="true"`. Each option uses `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring its selection. Decorative icons (`ai ai-chevron-down`, `ai-heart`, etc.) are `aria-hidden="true"`. The checkbox indicator is decorative for screen readers (the `role="option"` + `aria-selected` carries the semantic); the inner `Checkbox` sits in an `inert`, `aria-hidden="true"` wrapper, so the option has no focusable descendant.
- Nested overlays: the open list joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`), so inside a `Popover`, `Dialog` or `Drawer` an option click or `Escape` in the list closes only the list; the host overlay stays open.
- `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the trigger mirror the matching props.
- With `variant="chips"` or `searchable`, the `combobox` role, `id`, name and `aria-*` move from the field to its control (the `input` gets `aria-autocomplete="list"`); the field itself is a plain container.
- List states sit in `role="presentation"` rows; a visually hidden `role="status"` region announces `Loading options`, the error message, the empty text, or `{count} options` after typing.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every transition/animation-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are documented as dense-layout-only (consistent with `Input`).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="listbox"` content binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-`/`pe-`, `ms-auto`, `text-start`); chips flow from the start edge and wrap.
- Icons: the chevron is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` are not direction-dependent; `Backspace` removes the last value in reading order.
- User data: chip labels and typed text use `dir="auto"` through `Chip` and the input.
- Teleported content: see Accessibility — the panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider`.

## Internationalization

| Key                   | English source                                | Override prop |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `multiSelect.noMatch` | `No matches`                                  | `emptyTitle`  |
| `multiSelect.loading` | `Loading options`                             | —             |
| `multiSelect.add`     | `Add "{value}"`                               | —             |
| `multiSelect.more`    | `+{count} more`                               | —             |
| `multiSelect.count`   | `{count} option` / `{count} options` (plural) | —             |

- The chip remove names come from `chip.removeNamed`.
- Typed-text matching folds case and accents with the active locale (`toLocaleLowerCase`, NFD).
- `+{count} more` and `{count} options` go through the plural rules and number format of the active locale.

## Responsive

- The trigger fills its container; with `variant="chips"` and `chipLimit` `0` the chips wrap onto several lines and the field grows (`min-h` of the size, never a fixed height).
- Touch: chip remove buttons follow `Chip`'s target; options are 32 px rows.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; a long chip label truncates inside the chip.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MultiSelectContent from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content'
  import MultiSelectItem from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-item'
  import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'
  import MultiSelectTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(['opt-1'])
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div style="width: 280px">
    <MultiSelectRoot
      aria-label="Options"
      v-model="value"
      placeholder="Select options"
    >
      <MultiSelectTrigger />
      <MultiSelectContent>
        <MultiSelectItem
          v-for="o in options"
          :key="o.value"
          :value="o.value"
          >{{ o.label }}</MultiSelectItem
        >
      </MultiSelectContent>
    </MultiSelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Number Input

> Numeric input field with optional increment/decrement spinner buttons. Use when the value is strictly numeric (counts, quantities, ports, thresholds, currency without formatting). Distinct from `input` because it enforces numeric type, supports `min`/`max`/`step`, and renders chevron-up/chevron-down controls on the trailing edge.

- Import: `import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture a strictly numeric value (counts, quantities, ports, prices).

## Do

- Set `min` / `max` / `step` to constrain input rather than validating after the fact.
- Use `inputmode="numeric"` semantics for mobile keyboards.
- Set `nullable` on an optional field (a port, a limit) so a cleared field stays unset (`null`) instead of falling back to `min ?? 0`.

## Don’t

- The value is free text → use `input`.
- The user picks from a fixed set of numbers → use `select`.

## Related

- `input` — free-text sibling with the same field API.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Text shown when the input is empty. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as read-only; spinner buttons are inert. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border/ring tokens. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required for assistive tech. |
| `min` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Minimum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `max` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Maximum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | false | Increment used by the spinner buttons and arrow keys. |
| `showButtons` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Renders the chevron-up/chevron-down spinner controls. |
| `nullable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets a cleared field emit null instead of falling back to min or 0. |
| `modelValue` | `NumberInputValue<TNullable>` | `0 as NumberInputValue<TNullable>` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `number` | Emitted when the user commits the value (blur or Enter). With `nullable` the payload is `null` when the field is committed empty. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | — | Content rendered before the input (e.g. `$`). |
| `trailing` | — | Content rendered after the input, before the spinner buttons (e.g. `%`). |

## v-model

| Model     | Type                                        | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `number` (`number \| null` with `nullable`) | `0`     | `update:modelValue` | The value via `defineModel`, clamped to `min`/`max`; updates on typing and on the spinner. A cleared field falls back to `min ?? 0`; with `nullable` it emits `null` and shows the placeholder, and the spinner on a `null` value starts at `min ?? 0` (clamped). The component is generic over `nullable`, so the model and `change` are typed `number` unless `nullable` is set. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `filled`, `empty` (a `nullable` field whose value is `null` shows the placeholder)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` increment/decrement by `step`; `Home`/`End` jump to `min`/`max` when defined; `Enter` commits and emits `change`.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` (digits resolve to left-to-right inside right-to-left UI); a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `role="spinbutton"` on the input (native `<input type="number">` provides this); `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` mirror the props; `aria-invalid` mirrors `invalid`; `aria-required` mirrors `required`; spinner buttons have `aria-label` ("Increment" / "Decrement") and `tabindex="-1"` so keyboard users use arrow keys.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated state changes.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the large size; spinner buttons remain ≥24×24 px on `small`/`medium` per Figma — justified because arrow keys provide the primary interaction.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the stepper buttons point up and down and do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(1)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-[20rem]">
    <NumberInput
      v-model="value"
      :min="0"
      :max="100"
      :step="1"
      placeholder="Quantity"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/otp-input.md -->

# Otp Input

> The field for a one-time code: the six digits an authenticator app shows, or a code sent by email or SMS. It looks like a row of boxes, one character each, but it is **one real text input** laid over the boxes, so the browser's one-time-code autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), password managers, paste and screen readers all see a single field. Typing fills the next box (auto-advance), Backspace empties the last one, and a pasted code (`123 456`, `123-456`, with a line break) keeps only its valid characters and fills every box. When the last box fills it emits `complete`, so the screen can submit without a button press. It replaces six hand-wired text inputs with focus moves between them; the `account/mfa-settings` block uses it to set up and confirm an authenticator.

- Import: `import OtpInput from '@aziontech/webkit/otp-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Multi-factor authentication: set-up confirmation and sign-in challenge.
- Verifying an email address or a phone number with a short code.
- Any short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else.

## Do

- Label it with what the code is and where it comes from: `Authentication code`, and a description `The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
- Submit on `complete` only when the code is the last thing to fill; keep a Verify button for keyboard users and for a failed attempt.
- After a rejected code, mark it `invalid`, clear it, and keep focus in it.
- Use `group="3"` for codes people read aloud or copy from a phone; it draws a separator between groups and does not change the value.

## Don’t

- A password or a secret of free length → use `PasswordInput`.
- A long token or API key → use `Input` with a copy affordance.
- A number with a range → use `NumberInput`.

## Related

- `field` — wrap it in a `Field` for the label, the description and the error; the label names the input.
- `password-input` — the other credential input of the auth screens.
- `input` — the plain text field it shares tokens with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | `number` | `6` | false | How many characters the code has; one box each. |
| `mode` | `'numeric' \| 'alphanumeric'` | `'numeric'` | false | numeric` keeps digits and opens the number keypad; `alphanumeric` keeps letters and digits, upper case. |
| `group` | `number` | `0` | false | Draw a separator after every `group` boxes (`3` gives `123 – 456`). `0` draws none. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field while a code is being checked. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Danger borders on every box and `aria-invalid`; set after a rejected code. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Native `required` and `aria-required`. |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Focus the field on mount, for a screen whose only task is the code. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | `string` |  |

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                     |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''`    | `update:modelValue` | The code typed so far, via `defineModel`, already filtered by `mode` and cut to `length`. |

## States

- `data-state` on each box: `empty` | `filled`; `data-active` on the box the next character goes to while the field has focus (the last box when the code is full).
- `data-invalid`, `data-disabled` on the root.
- Separators render between groups when `group` > 0.

## Accessibility

- One `input` carries the value, the name (from the `Field` label, an `aria-label`, or the catalog's `One-time code` when nothing else names it), `aria-describedby` from the `Field`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `maxlength`, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `inputmode` (`numeric` or `text`) and `enterkeyhint="done"`. The boxes and separators are `aria-hidden`; a screen reader reads the input's value as typed.
- Keyboard: type to fill, Backspace to clear the last character, Tab leaves the field in one stop; the caret stays at the end, so Arrow and Home keys do not move it into the middle of the code.
- Focus: the active box takes the focus ring; the whole field takes one focus stop.
- Contrast: characters `--text-default` on `--bg-surface`, borders `--border-default` (3:1 non-text) in both themes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the box row is `dir="ltr"`: a code reads left to right in every locale, like a phone number, so the first character stays on the left under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: the value is ASCII letters and digits.

## Internationalization

| Key              | English source  | Override prop        |
| ---------------- | --------------- | -------------------- |
| `otpInput.label` | `One-time code` | `aria-label` (attrs) |

- Characters are not localized: digits stay ASCII so the code matches what the app shows.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: boxes are 40 px with an 8 px gap and shrink to 24 px when the row is narrower than that, so eight boxes plus a separator fit in 320 px (checked in `apps/visual`, `geometry otp input grouped`).
- Touch: the whole row is the input's hit area.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px for `length` up to 8 with a separator.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import OtpInput from '@aziontech/webkit/otp-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const code = ref('')
  const entered = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Field>
      <Field.Label>Authentication code</Field.Label>
      <OtpInput
        v-model="code"
        name="code"
        @complete="(value) => (entered = value)"
      />
      <Field.Description>The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.</Field.Description>
    </Field>
    <p
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      role="status"
    >
      {{ entered ? `Code ${entered} entered.` : '' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/password-input.md -->

# Password Input

> Single-line password input for forms. Renders a bordered field with a built-in visibility toggle button on the trailing edge that flips the native `type` between `password` and `text`. Shares the visual language of `Input` (same heights, borders, focus ring, disabled treatment). The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and strength meters live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `3714:10788` (Webkit / PasswordInput). The token mapping was originally inferred from the `input` sibling because the Figma MCP was unreachable during spec authoring; it has since been **reconciled against the frame** as rendered inside the password field frame (`2027:3212`), which corrected the trailing padding to `var(--spacing-xs)` and the visibility toggle to the 28 px (`small`) `IconButton`. One frame value is deliberately not adopted: the border width stays at the shared 1 px rather than the frame's `var(--border-width-default)` (0.8 px), because this component's contract is to share `Input`'s borders and `Input` is still on 1 px — moving one without the other would break that stated invariant. Adopting it is a coordinated follow-up across every bordered input.

- Import: `import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A bare password field whose label and errors are laid out separately (an inline re-authentication prompt, a custom form row).
- Any secret the user may need to check while typing (passwords, tokens); the built-in toggle reveals it as plain text.

## Do

- Set `autocomplete="new-password"` on sign-up and password-change forms; keep the default `current-password` on login.
- Leave `toggleable` on; turn it off only when you need the `trailing` slot, which is ignored while the toggle is shown.
- The field is a fixed 40px tall with no `size` prop; align it with `size="large"` siblings in the same row.
- Give it an accessible name: a `label` whose `for` matches an `id` passed to the input, or `aria-label`.
- Set `monospace` on a secret that is code-like: an API token, a client secret, a signing key. Pair it with `autocomplete="off"` and `:spellcheck="false"`, so a revealed token reads character by character (`0`/`O`, `l`/`1`).
- Do not set `monospace` on a person's own password: they typed it and never read it back character by character.

## Don’t

- A password field with a label, helper or error text, or a requirements row → wrap it in a `field` (with `password-requirements` for the rules row).
- The value is not secret → use `input`.

## Related

- `field` — wraps this input with its label and description; it hands the input its id, `aria-describedby` and state.
- `password-requirements` — the live checklist of password rules rendered under this input.
- `input` — plain-text field with the same borders, focus ring, and disabled treatment.
- `input` — plain single-line text input.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. The toggle button inherits the disabled state. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; value is visible but not editable. Toggle button stays operable. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |
| `toggleable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, renders the visibility toggle button on the trailing edge of the field. When false, the field behaves as a plain password input with no toggle and the `trailing` slot becomes available. |
| `autocomplete` | `'current-password' \| 'new-password' \| 'off'` | `'current-password'` | false | Native `autocomplete` hint for password managers. Use `new-password` for sign-up and password-change flows. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-label-code-sm`) for API tokens, client secrets and keys (`data-monospace`). Same prop as on `Input`. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | — | Leading adornment at the inline start of the field. Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). Same name as on `input` and `number-input`. |
| `trailing` | — | Trailing adornment at the inline end. **Only honored when `toggleable=false`** — the visibility toggle sits there when enabled. Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                     |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''`    | `update:modelValue` | The field value via `defineModel`; updates on every native `input` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`
- Single fixed height: 40px (large only)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; drives the warning-border treatment
- `data-leading` mirrors `$slots.leading` presence
- `data-trailing` mirrors `$slots.trailing` presence (only relevant when `toggleable=false`)
- `data-toggleable` mirrors the `toggleable` prop
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value (masked or revealed) and the placeholder render in `.text-label-code-sm` instead of `.text-label-sm`.
- `data-revealed` on the root mirrors the internal visibility state (`true` when the password is revealed as plain text)
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots and the visibility toggle.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input, then the visibility toggle button (when `toggleable=true`); `Enter` / `Space` on the toggle flips visibility; standard text-editing keys apply to the input.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: the visibility toggle is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed` reflecting the current visible state and an `aria-label` that switches between "Show password" and "Hide password"; `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; decorative icon slots and the eye glyph are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target: the input fills the field's single fixed 40 px height. The visibility toggle is the 28×28 px `small` `IconButton` the Figma frame specifies — above WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) at 24×24 px, and centred in the 40 px row so the practical vertical reach is the full field height. It is below the 44×44 px of SC 2.5.5 (AAA), which this AA-scoped spec does not claim.
- The toggle button never submits the surrounding form (`type="button"`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the visibility toggle does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const password = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <PasswordInput
    v-model="password"
    placeholder="Enter your password"
    autocomplete="current-password"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/password-input.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/password-input.md).

<!-- components/password-requirements.md -->

# Password Requirements

> Live checklist of password rules shown under a `PasswordInput`: a caption followed by one chip per rule, each chip turning to the success tone with a check as the typed value satisfies it. Put it in the same `Field` as the `PasswordInput`, under it; the entry also exports `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` and the `PasswordRequirementsRule` type so a form validates with the same rules it shows. `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` is typed `PasswordPatternRequirement[]` (exported too): every built-in rule has a `key` and a `RegExp` `test`, so `rule.test.test(value)` type-checks without narrowing; a custom rule list stays `PasswordRequirementsRule[]`, whose `test` may be a predicate.

- Import: `import PasswordRequirements from '@aziontech/webkit/password-requirements'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A new-password field (sign-up, reset, change password) where the user must meet explicit rules.

## Do

- Bind `value` to the same ref as the `PasswordInput` `v-model`.
- Validate on submit with `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` (or your own array) so the error and the chips never disagree.
- Pass `requirements` to replace the rule set and `title` to localize the caption.

## Don’t

- A sign-in password field → render `password-input` alone; the rules do not apply to an existing password.
- A free-form strength meter → not provided; compose your own.

## Related

- `password-input` — the control whose value this checklist evaluates.
- `field` — place both inside one `Field` so the label and description stay together.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requirements` | `PasswordRequirementsRule[]` | `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` | false | Rules rendered as chips, one per entry. Defaults to the built-in rule set; an empty array renders only the caption. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Caption that opens the row and names the group for assistive tech. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Must contain:`). |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | false | Password every rule is evaluated against; pass the PasswordInput value. |

## States

- Each chip carries `data-validated` when its rule passes.
- The row animates its height as chips wrap.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the checklist is read-only.
- Keyboard map: _none_.
- ARIA: root `role="group"` named by the caption through `aria-labelledby`; the check icons are `aria-hidden`, so each chip ends with visually hidden state text from the locale catalog (`passwordRequirements.met` / `passwordRequirements.unmet`: `met` / `not met`) and the state is never conveyed by colour and icon alone.
- Direction: the check icon slides in from the inline start (`-translate-x-1`, mirrored under `rtl:`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for chip text in both tones.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'
  import PasswordRequirements from '@aziontech/webkit/password-requirements'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const password = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Field
    required
    class="max-w-(--container-xs)"
  >
    <Field.Label>Password</Field.Label>
    <PasswordInput
      v-model="password"
      autocomplete="new-password"
    />
    <PasswordRequirements :value="password" />
  </Field>
</template>
```
