<!-- components/sticky-stack.md -->

# Sticky Stack

> A band that pins to the viewport and is read by scrolling through it: a stack of claims on one side, one piece of media on the other, and the scroll position — not a pointer — deciding which claim is open. Each claim expands in turn while the ones already read collapse and stack above it, so the column keeps one height and the reader always sees where they are in the run. The media beside it is replaced, not dimmed: the outgoing scene leaves and the incoming one mounts, so a scene that animates plays its entrance every time it is reached.

- Import: `import StickyStack from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-stack'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use StickyStack (primitive) for claims that open one by one as the reader scrolls past pinned media.
- For a sequence of claims a reader should take in one at a time, each with a medium worth looking at — five ways a platform is used, each with the file you would actually write.
- When the media is the payload and the copy is the caption: a code sample, a console shot, an official scene.
- As the one band on a page that rewards scrolling slowly, placed where a reader has already committed to the page.

## Do

- Keep the run to three to six claims. The band holds the page for `dwell` of a screen per claim, and a reader who cannot see the end of it reads it as a page that will not let go.
- Write each claim to stand alone. A reader can land mid-band from a deep link or a focus jump, so no claim may depend on the one above it.
- Keep a title to one line. The collapsed rows set the column's height, and a title that wraps changes it for every claim at once.
- Keep a description to two or three lines. Only the open claim shows one, and a long one pushes the stack past the pinned frame.
- Give every claim a medium. The frame holds one at a time and mounts it fresh, so a claim with nothing to show reads as a band that broke rather than one that is quiet.
- Use media of the same shape. The frame does not resize between claims, and a scene that changes the frame's height un-pins the band mid-read.
- Set `--sticky-stack-top` to the height of any sticky header above the band, or the first claim opens underneath it. Set it on a wrapper around the band rather than on the band's own tag: custom properties inherit, and the band is not a style seam.
- Leave `showProgress` on. It is the only thing telling a reader how much of the pin is left.
- Raise `dwell` for claims that carry code a reader must actually read; lower it for scenes that are grasped at a glance.

## Don’t

- For peer claims a reader should be able to jump between at will → use `media-tabs`, which selects on hover, click and a timer without taking the scroll.
- For one claim beside one picture → use `media-split`.
- For questions and answers, or any run longer than about six items → use `faq`. A pinned band holds the page for its whole run, and a long run holds it too long.
- On a page that is already a single short screen: there is no scroll to spend.
- For the product-page walkthrough placed from page JSON → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tabs` — the pointer-driven sibling. Same two-column anatomy; the selection moves on hover, click and a timer, and the band does not pin.
- `media-split` — one claim, one medium, no selection and no pin.
- `code-block` — the medium this band most often holds, one sample per claim.
- `illustration` — the official scene a claim's `media` slot otherwise holds.
- `section-title` — the heading above the band; this component carries no title of its own.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `StickyStackItem[]` | `[]` | false | The claims, in reading order; each item is a title, the sentence that opens with it, and the image shown while it is open. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Height the open claim is held to, and so the height of the whole stack beside the media. |
| `dwell` | `number` | `0.7` | false | Screen-heights of scrolling each claim holds while the band is pinned; the band's total scroll is one screen plus this much per claim. |
| `showProgress` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Fills a hairline along the open claim's bottom edge as its share of the scroll is spent. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active-index-change` | `number` | The open claim changed; the payload is the index now open. Fires on the scroll that moved it and on a reader selecting a claim. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | { item: StickyStackItem, index: number, active: boolean } | The claim's medium; replaces the image built from the item's own source. Mounted fresh on every change, so an entrance animation inside it replays. |
| `actions` | { item: StickyStackItem, index: number, active: boolean } | The claim's own controls, pinned to the bottom edge of the open claim. From `lg` up they show only while the claim is open and are out of the tab order while it is collapsed; below `lg` every claim is open and carries its own. Nothing renders when the slot is empty. |
| `backdrop` | — | Fills the media frame behind every claim's medium, from `lg` up. Mounted once and never swapped, so a texture or an animated surface placed here holds still while the media change over it. Nothing renders when the slot is empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible` on each claim's title control
- `data-active` marks the open claim; it holds the plain text tone and shows its description
- `data-completed` marks every claim already read; they collapse to their title and rest at a muted tone, further dimmed so the read part of the run is legible at a glance, stacked above the open one
- `data-size` carries the size token, which is what sets the open claim's height and so the stack's height
- `data-progress` is present on the root while `showProgress` is on
- The media frame shows exactly one medium: the outgoing one leaves as the incoming one mounts
- The backdrop is not part of the medium: it stays mounted across every change, under the medium that is leaving and the one arriving
- A claim's description is held to `var(--container-sm)` so the measure stays short however wide the column is
- Below `lg` the band does not pin: every claim is open, each with its own medium under it, and nothing moves
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on every claim's title control
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each claim's title control in reading order; focusing or activating one scrolls the band to that claim's share of the scroll, so a keyboard reader moves the band exactly as a pointer reader does. There is no key that scrolls the page other than the reader's own — the band never takes the scroll it is given.
- ARIA: the claim list is an `<ol>` (the run is ordered); the open claim's control carries `aria-current="true"`; the progress hairline is `aria-hidden="true"`; the scroll anchors are `aria-hidden="true"`
- Every claim's description stays in the accessibility tree while collapsed (clipped, never `display: none`), so the whole run is readable without scrolling through it
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the muted tone a read claim rests at
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` / `motion-reduce:animate-none` on every animated state; the pin itself is not motion and stays
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: each claim's control spans its whole row

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
  import StickyStack from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-stack'

  const scenes = ['ai-applications', 'live-debugging', 'deploy-secure-mcp-server']

  const items = [
    {
      title: 'Automated deployment via Git or CLI',
      description:
        'Push to a branch or run one command; the platform builds the project and puts the result in every location, with the build before it a rollback away.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Infrastructure as code with Terraform',
      description:
        'Declare workloads, rules and domains in the provider and apply them the same way as the rest of your estate, with the same review and the same plan.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Metrics and events via GraphQL API',
      description:
        'Query the same numbers the console charts, from one endpoint, so a dashboard you already run can carry the platform alongside everything else.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <StickyStack :items="items">
    <template #media="{ index }">
      <Illustration :name="scenes[index]" />
    </template>
  </StickyStack>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/sticky-stack.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/sticky-stack.md).

# Texture

> The one decorative surface every band in the system is painted on: a full-bleed, non-interactive layer that tiles a texture behind whatever sits above it. It is a material, not a container — it takes no content and claims no space, so a band composes it into its own backdrop slot and keeps ownership of its layout.

- Import: `import Texture from '@aziontech/webkit/texture'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- In a band's `background` slot (`hero`), where the opening band needs the site's own lattice under its copy.
- Behind a panel, dropzone or slide that would read as empty at a flat fill.
- Anywhere a surface should look like a technical drawing ground without shipping an image.

## Do

- Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative`) that also clips it; it fills that box and nothing else.
- Keep the texture behind copy, never over it. `dots` is the quiet default; `lines` is quieter still and reads as ruled paper; `dither` and `pixelate` are loud enough to need their ink dropped or their dense end steered away from the words.
- Do not stack two layers at different pitches — that reads as a moiré, not as a texture.
- Quiet a texture with `--texture-ink` rather than with `opacity`, so the ground keeps showing through at full strength.
- Leave it out when the band already sits inside a `registration-frame`; rules plus texture is usually one layer too many.

## Don’t

- To draw the rules between real content cells → use `registration-frame`, whose rules are structural.
- For the ruled divider between sections → use `section-gap`, which composes this layer's `lines` variant and owns that treatment.
- For a meaningful image or diagram → use `illustration`.
- As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it, inside the positioned ancestor.

## Related

- `hero` — the band whose `background` slot this is composed into.
- `registration-frame` — structural rules and corner marks, not decoration.
- `section-gap` — the hatched rhythm band between sections.
- `hero` — the marketing band that paints this texture behind its own copy.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'dots'` | false | Which texture to paint; `none` renders the layer with no texture at all. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Pitch of the tiling — how far apart the cells sit. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'none'` | false | Fades the layer out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-variant`, `data-size` and `data-fade` mirror their props and drive which texture paints, at what pitch, and how it fades out
- `variant="none"` paints nothing, so a band can switch its texture off without unmounting the layer
- `fade="none"` leaves the layer unmasked; every other value masks it so the ink reaches zero before the layer's own edge; `top` and `bottom` are a single fade — full ink at the leading edge, zero at `--texture-fade-end`; `left` and `right` fade out toward the named edge in the same way, full ink at the opposite edge, which is how a band keeps its texture behind the media and clears it under the copy. Setting `--texture-fade-lead: transparent` adds a second ramp in from zero at the leading edge, so the layer also clears whatever overlaps that edge; `hero` sets it on its backdrop because its opening band sits under the site header, and no other band needs it
- Custom properties tune a texture in place, set from the consumer's class: `--texture-ink` (every variant), `--texture-fade-start` / `--texture-fade-end` (where the fade holds full ink and where it reaches zero), `--texture-fade-lead` (the ink at the leading edge of `top` / `bottom`; `black` by default, `transparent` for the double fade), `--texture-from` / `--texture-to` / `--texture-direction` (the `dither` ramp's density span and axis), `--texture-pool-x` (where both `pixelate` light pools sit on the x axis), `--texture-pool-a` / `--texture-pool-b` (each pool's own `x y` position, so the two can sit on opposite edges; either falls back to `--texture-pool-x`), `--texture-wave-gain` (multiplies the ink of both `pixelate` waves, 1 by default, capped at full ink, so a band can make the motion read over the pools), `--texture-wave-pace` (a whole number of wave periods each loop travels, 1 by default; 2 doubles the speed without changing the animation's duration token)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the layer is decorative and holds no interactive control.
- Keyboard map: none; the layer is `pointer-events-none` and is never in the tab order.
- ARIA: the root carries `aria-hidden="true"`, so no texture is announced and the layer adds no role.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the ink is mixed down from `var(--text-default)` to a surface step, deliberately below text contrast — content above the layer keeps its own colours and its own contrast against the page canvas.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on both pixelate waves; every other variant is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, no interactive target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Texture from '@aziontech/webkit/texture'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative h-80 w-full overflow-hidden bg-(--bg-canvas)">
    <Texture
      variant="dots"
      size="medium"
      fade="none"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/texture.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/texture.md).

<!-- components/breadcrumb.md -->

# Breadcrumb

> Shows the page hierarchy so users can navigate back to parent views. Composes `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`, and `BreadcrumbSeparator` (chevron). Accepts an `items` array for the common case or slot composition for custom layouts. Reference: PrimeNG Breadcrumb (adapted to Webkit tokens).

- Import: `import BreadcrumbRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Breadcrumb (with `items`, or Breadcrumb.Item parts) for the page trail.
- A page sits two or more levels deep and the reader needs a way back to its parents (resource detail under a list, a settings sub-page).
- The trail is known as data — pass `items` and let the component render the segments, separators and the collapse when its own box is narrower than 768px.
- The trail needs a custom layout the `items` array cannot express — compose `Breadcrumb.List`, `Breadcrumb.Item` and `Breadcrumb.Separator` in the default slot.

## Do

- Prefer `items`; only `items` mode collapses the middle segments into an overflow menu when its own box is narrower than 768px. The default slot renders only when `items` is empty, and a hand-composed trail never collapses.
- Let the last entry be the current page — it is treated as current unless its `active` is set to `false`; give every ancestor an `href`.
- Handle routing in `@navigate`, which receives `(event, href)` for ancestor segments; call `event.preventDefault()` when a client-side router takes over.
- **Vue Router:** a segment has no `to`; put the route's path in `href` (for a named route, `router.resolve(to).href`) and write `@navigate="(event, href) => { event.preventDefault(); router.push(href) }"`. The segment stays a real link, so open-in-new-tab keeps working; leave a modified click (Ctrl, ⌘, Shift, middle button) to the browser.
- In slot mode, wrap each `Breadcrumb.Item` in an `li`: `Breadcrumb.List` is an `ol` and the item renders an `a` / `span`, while `Breadcrumb.Separator` is already an `li`.

## Don’t

- It is the app's primary navigation → use `navigation-menu` or `sidebar` with `sidebar-menu`.
- It moves between sibling views of the same page → use `tabs`.
- It is the previous / next pair at the end of a docs page → use `doc-previous-next`.

## Related

- `breadcrumb-item` — the single segment this component renders; use it alone only inside a hand-composed trail.
- `navigation-menu` — top-level navigation with dropdown panels, not a location trail.
- `link` — a standalone link; a breadcrumb segment is a link with the trail's muted / current styling.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BreadcrumbItemData[]` | `() => []` | false | Ordered path segments; the last entry is treated as the current page when `active` is omitted on that entry. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the navigation landmark; empty uses the locale catalog (`Breadcrumb`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent, href: string)` | Fires when an ancestor segment is activated. `event` is the activation event; `href` is the segment's destination. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Custom composition (`BreadcrumbList` + items + separators). Used when `items` is empty. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item`

## Sub-components

- `breadcrumb.vue` — Root `<nav>` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`, or the locale catalog (`Breadcrumb`) when empty; a consumer `aria-label` lands on the prop and wins.
- `breadcrumb-list.vue` — Ordered list wrapper (`<ol>`) for segments.
- `breadcrumb-item/breadcrumb-item.vue` — `Breadcrumb.Item`, the segment control; it lives in this component's folder and keeps its flat export `@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item`.
- `breadcrumb-separator.vue` — Decorative chevron between segments (`aria-hidden`).

## States

- Visual states: inherited from `BreadcrumbItem` (default, hover, focus-visible, disabled)
- Last segment in `items` is current when its `active` is not explicitly `false`

#### Responsive contract

- The trail is always a **single row**. A segment wider than the space available shrinks and ellipsizes its label; a trail that still does not fit scrolls horizontally. It never wraps to a second line and never extends past its container.
- **`items` mode** additionally collapses when the `nav`'s own width is below 768px (a `ResizeObserver` on the landmark, so a breadcrumb in a narrow panel or drawer collapses on a wide screen too): first segment, an overflow menu holding the middle segments, then the current segment. The overflow entries are links (`href`) inside the menu, so they navigate natively, open in a new tab, and still emit `navigate`. The breakpoint is owned by the component's own `use-breadcrumb-collapse` composable.
- **Slot (hand-composed) mode** keeps every segment it was given, since the root cannot know which of the consumer's children are middle segments, so on a narrow screen it degrades through the single-row rules above rather than through a collapse.
- Server render and hydration: the collapse measures the `nav` only after mount (`use-breadcrumb-collapse` reads its width in `onMounted`, then follows a `ResizeObserver`), so the server HTML and the first client render are the full trail and match; in a narrow box the collapse applies in the same tick as mount, before paint.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on each interactive `BreadcrumbItem` segment.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between ancestor links; current page is not in tab order when rendered as `span`.
- ARIA: root `nav` with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`; list uses `<ol>` / `<li>`; separators are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for labels and chevron.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on segment color transitions.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the separator chevron and any directional item `icon` mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`), so the trail reads from the start edge.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: item labels are text; page names in another script keep their own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-root'

  const items = [
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Current Page', active: true }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Breadcrumb
    :items="items"
    class="max-w-[42.5rem]"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/breadcrumb.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/breadcrumb.md).

<!-- components/breadcrumb-item.md -->

# Breadcrumb Item

> Single segment in a breadcrumb trail. Ancestor segments use muted label text and optional leading icon; the current page uses default text. Hover and focus-visible states match the Webkit navigation pattern (ghost overlay + focus ring).

- Import: `import BreadcrumbItem from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Breadcrumb.Item only as a part of Breadcrumb; for the page trail itself use Breadcrumb.
- Composing a breadcrumb trail by hand inside `Breadcrumb.List`, one segment per ancestor plus the current page.
- A single ancestor or current-page segment that must match the breadcrumb's muted / current styling and focus ring.

## Do

- Set `active` on the last segment only; it renders a `span` with `aria-current="page"`, drops out of the tab order and ignores `href`.
- Always pass a real `href` on ancestors — an empty `href` (the default) renders `#`, and the segment renders an `a`.
- Use `show-icon` together with `icon` (an Azion icon class; empty shows `ai ai-box`); `icon` alone renders nothing.
- disabled` suppresses the `click` emit and removes the segment from the tab order; prefer omitting an unreachable ancestor over disabling it.

## Don’t

- The whole trail is known as data → use `breadcrumb` with `items`, which renders the segments for you.
- It is a standalone text link in content or a page footer → use `link`.
- It is a navigation row in an app menu → use `sidebar-menu`.

## Related

- `breadcrumb` — the trail root; renders `breadcrumb-item` for each entry of `items` and re-exports it as `Breadcrumb.Item`.
- `link` — a general-purpose link without the segment's ghost hover and current-page treatment.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible segment label. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Destination when the segment is a link (ignored when `active` is true); empty renders `#`. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the current page (last segment); renders as span with `aria-current="page"`. |
| `showIcon` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, renders a leading icon before the label. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the leading icon when `showIcon` is true; empty shows `ai ai-box`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: { label: string; href: string })` | Fires when the segment's link is activated (the `active` segment renders a non-interactive `span`). `item` carries the segment's `label` and `href`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-active` mirrors the `active` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses link segments; `Enter` activates.
- ARIA: current segment uses `aria-current="page"`; disabled segments use `aria-disabled="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on interactive segments (padding + min height).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BreadcrumbItem from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item'
</script>

<template>
  <BreadcrumbItem
    label="Page Name"
    href="#"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/breadcrumb-item.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/breadcrumb-item.md).

<!-- components/context-menu.md -->

# Context Menu

> Menu of actions that opens at the pointer when the user right-clicks an area, presses `Shift+F10` or the context-menu key inside it, or long-presses it on touch. It is the right-click twin of `DropdownMenu`: the root `ContextMenu` owns open state, the pointer anchor, positioning and focus return through the same internal menu core, `ContextMenu.Trigger` marks the area that listens, and the item parts are DropdownMenu's own (`Group`, `Item` with its checkbox and radio variants, `Sub`, `SubTrigger`, `SubContent`), attached to the compound so the two menus look and behave the same.

- Import: `import ContextMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/context-menu-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import ContextMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/context-menu'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use ContextMenu for the same actions as a DropdownMenu, opened by right-click or long-press on an item; opened from a button use DropdownMenu.
- Secondary actions on an object the user is pointing at: a table row, a file in a browser, a tree node, a canvas.
- Power-user shortcuts that also exist elsewhere in the interface.

## Do

- Wrap the object, not the page: one `ContextMenu.Trigger` around the table body, the file grid or the tree, and read which row was targeted from your own state (for example the row the `contextmenu` came from, captured with a native `@contextmenu` on the row).
- Mirror the visible row-actions menu; a context menu adds speed, never exclusive actions.
- Keep it short (under about ten items), group with `ContextMenu.Group`, and put destructive actions in their own last group.
- Give the panel a name with `aria-label` when the target is not obvious from focus (for example `aria-label="Actions for production"`).
- disabled` gives the area back to the browser's native menu.

## Don’t

- The only way to reach an action. Right-click is invisible; every action in a context menu must also be reachable from a visible control (a row-actions `DropdownMenu`, a toolbar button).
- A menu opened from a button → use `dropdown-menu`.
- A searchable palette of commands → use `command`.
- Free-form content such as forms → use `popover`.

## Related

- `dropdown-menu` — same panel, items and keyboard model, opened from a trigger button; `ContextMenu` reuses its item parts.
- `popover` — free-form floating content on the same `usePlacement` positioning.
- `table` — row actions usually pair a visible `DropdownMenu` with a `ContextMenu` around the rows.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Leaves the area to the browser's native context menu and never opens the panel. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the menu panel; when empty the panel has no name of its own. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: DropdownMenuItemValue)` | Fires when an enabled option is activated, at any sub-menu depth. The panel closes and focus returns to the element that was focused in the area, except for checkbox and radio options. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place `<ContextMenu.Trigger>` (the area) followed by one or more `<ContextMenu.Group>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/context-menu-trigger`

## Sub-components

- `context-menu-trigger/context-menu-trigger.vue` — the area that opens the menu.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the area's content.
- Item parts, shared with `DropdownMenu` and attached to the compound under the same names: `ContextMenu.Group` (`dropdown-menu-group`), `ContextMenu.Item` (`dropdown-menu-item`, including `type="checkbox"` / `type="rad…

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`. While unbound the menu is uncontrolled and starts closed. Opened from the model without a pointer position, the panel anchors at the trigger area's inline-start top corner. |

## States

- Visual states of the items: as `dropdown-menu` (`default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`, checked).
- `data-state` values (root, trigger, panel): `open` | `closed`.
- `data-disabled` on root and trigger mirrors `disabled`.
- `data-placement` on the panel mirrors the resolved corner (`bottom-start` | `bottom-end` | `top-start` | `top-end`).
- `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `readonly`, `invalid`: not states of this component; it renders the items the consumer passes.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the items carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` (shared parts).
- Keyboard map:
  - Inside the trigger area: `Shift+F10` or the `ContextMenu` key opens the panel at the focused element and focuses the first enabled item.
  - Inside the panel: `Down` / `Up` move between enabled items (wrap-around); `Home` / `End` jump to the first / last; `Enter` / `Space` activate; `ArrowRight` (`ArrowLeft` under rtl) opens a sub-menu; `Esc` closes and returns focus to the element that was focused in the area; `Tab` closes. Tests: `context-menu.test.ts` › keyboard.
- ARIA: the panel is `role="menu"` named by `aria-label` when set; items are `menuitem` / `menuitemcheckbox` / `menuitemradio` (shared parts). The trigger area keeps no role: it is a region of content, and the context menu is a shortcut layer over controls that are reachable on their own.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled items (`--text-disabled`).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`.
- Teleported panel: binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`).
- Touch target: items are 32 px rows, above the 24 px floor of WCAG 2.5.8.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`text-start`, `ps-`/`pe-`); the panel binds `dir` from `WebkitProvider`.
- Icons: the sub-trigger chevron mirrors (shared part); no other icon.
- Keyboard: a keyboard-opened panel anchors at the inline-start bottom corner of the focused element (its right edge under rtl) and prefers opening toward the inline end; `ArrowLeft` opens a sub-menu under rtl. Pointer opens anchor at the pointer in both directions.
- User data: none (labels are consumer text).

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: item labels and the panel's `aria-label` come from the consumer.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the panel is sized between `--container-3xs` and `--container-2xs`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): `usePlacement` picks the corner with room and keeps the panel inside the viewport; labels truncate.
- Touch: a 500 ms long-press opens the menu at the touch point, so the right-click has a touch path; rows are 32 px.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ContextMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/context-menu'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const resources = ['production', 'staging', 'docs-site']
  const target = ref('')
  const last = ref('')

  const onSelect = (event, value) => {
    last.value = `${value} · ${target.value}`
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-sm) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <ContextMenu
      :aria-label="target ? `Actions for ${target}` : 'Resource actions'"
      @select="onSelect"
    >
      <ContextMenu.Trigger>
        <ul
          class="flex flex-col rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default) bg-(--bg-surface)"
        >
          <li
            v-for="name in resources"
            :key="name"
            tabindex="0"
            class="flex h-10 items-center border-b border-(--border-default) px-(--spacing-md) text-body-sm text-(--text-default) outline-none last:border-b-0 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)"
            @contextmenu="target = name"
            @focus="target = name"
          >
            {{ name }}
          </li>
        </ul>
      </ContextMenu.Trigger>

      <ContextMenu.Group>
        <ContextMenu.Item
          value="open"
          label="Open"
        />
        <ContextMenu.Item
          value="rename"
          label="Rename"
          command="F2"
        />
        <ContextMenu.Item
          value="duplicate"
          label="Duplicate"
        />
      </ContextMenu.Group>
      <ContextMenu.Group>
        <ContextMenu.Item
          value="delete"
          label="Delete"
        />
      </ContextMenu.Group>
    </ContextMenu>

    <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
      Right-click a row, press Shift+F10 on a focused row, or long-press it on touch.
      <span v-if="last">Last action: {{ last }}</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/context-menu.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/context-menu.md).

# Dropdown Menu

> Overlay menu that opens from a consumer-supplied trigger and renders a list of selectable options grouped into named sections. The root `DropdownMenu` owns open/closed state, positioning, focus return, and keyboard navigation; `DropdownMenu.Trigger` wires `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` onto whatever element the consumer passes through its slot; `DropdownMenu.Group` groups options under an optional label; `DropdownMenu.Item` (the shadcn / Radix name) is the selectable row with leading/trailing/command affordances, and with `type="checkbox"` or `type="radio"` it becomes a checkable item (`menuitemcheckbox` / `menuitemradio`). `DropdownMenu.Sub`, `DropdownMenu.SubTrigger` and `DropdownMenu.SubContent` nest a sub-menu that opens on hover or with `ArrowRight` and nests to any depth. Replaces and removes the legacy monolithic input `dropdown` and the previous `dropdown-menu` composition — there is one `DropdownMenu` in the project, in `navigation/`.

- Import: `import DropdownMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import DropdownMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use DropdownMenu for a list of actions opened from a button (row actions, kebab, More); for the same actions on right-click or long-press use ContextMenu, and for a searchable palette use Command.
- A menu of actions opened from a button: row actions, an account menu, an overflow ("more") menu.
- Options grouped under section labels, optionally with keyboard-shortcut hints.

## Do

- Give every `DropdownMenu.Item` a unique `value` and handle the root `select` event as `(event, value)`. The panel closes and focus returns to the trigger on its own.
- selected` is a display flag. The dropdown never sets it, so derive it from your own state.
- Use the `command` prop or the `trailing` slot on an option, not both. A `command` shortcut is live while its option is mounted (inside a group, only while the panel is open). Every menu on the page shares one `window` listener, so a shortcut fires one option only: the one in the open menu, else the one whose trigger has focus, else the first registered.
- Write `DropdownMenu.Item` (also exported as `DropdownMenuItem`); 6.0 removed the `DropdownMenu.Option` alias and the `left` / `right` slots. Items may sit directly in the root: an item outside a group renders inside the panel like a grouped one.
- Add a `label` to each `DropdownMenu.Group` when there is more than one group. Put search in the root `header` slot and footer actions in `footer`; those regions stay outside the scrolling list.
- Nest at most two levels of sub-menus; deeper menus are hard to steer with a pointer. Put the `DropdownMenu.Sub` inside a `DropdownMenu.Group`, and the sub-menu's options inside a `DropdownMenu.Group` in `DropdownMenu.SubContent`, the same way as the top level.
- Use `type="checkbox"` for independent on/off settings and `type="radio"` for one choice among the options of one `DropdownMenu.Group`. Drive `selected` from your own state in the `select` handler; checkable options keep the panel open so several can be toggled in a row.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- Choosing a value that a form submits → use `select` (inside a `field` for a label).
- A primary action joined to a menu of alternatives → use `split-button`.
- A searchable palette of commands → use `command`.
- Free-form or interactive content such as forms or filters → use `popover`.
- Vertical application navigation → use `sidebar-menu`.

## Related

- `split-button` — composes `DropdownMenu` for its chevron menu.
- `select` — form control with a field trigger and a bound value.
- `popover` — same trigger and anchoring model, with free-form content instead of option rows.
- `command` — modal ⌘K palette with search and filtering.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `'auto' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-end' \| 'top-start' \| 'top-end'` | `'bottom-start'` | false | Where the panel opens relative to the trigger. `'auto'` picks the best-fitting corner at open time based on viewport space. |
| `offset` | `number` | `4` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: DropdownMenuItemValue)` | Fires when an enabled option is activated (click, `Enter`/`Space`, or a `command` shortcut). `event` is the activation event; `value` is the activated option's identifier. The panel closes automatically and focus returns to the trigger when activated from inside the open panel, except for `type="checkbox"` / `type="radio"` options, which keep it open. Options inside a sub-menu emit on the same root event. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place `<DropdownMenu.Trigger>` followed by one or more `<DropdownMenu.Group>`. |
| `header` | — | Sticky region rendered above the scrollable group list (e.g. search input). |
| `footer` | — | Sticky region rendered below the scrollable group list (e.g. footer action). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-sub`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-sub-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-sub-trigger`

## Sub-components

- `dropdown-menu-trigger/dropdown-menu-trigger.vue` — as-child trigger.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the consumer's trigger element. The trigger forwards aria + click; the consumer must not bind those props itself.
- `dropdown-menu-group/dropdown-menu-group.vue` — labeled section.
  - Props: `label: string` default `''` — section label rendered above the options. Omit for an unlabeled group.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<DropdownMenu.Item>`; `header` — inline region rendered between the group label and the options (e.g. a per-section search or description); `footer` — inline region rendered after the options (e.g. a "see all" link).
- `dropdown-menu-item/dropdown-menu-item.vue` — selectable row, attached as `DropdownMenu.Item`.
  - Props:
    - `value: string | number` (required) — identifier emitted on the root `select` event when this option is activated.
    - `label: string` default `''` — plain-text label; falls back to the default slot when omitted.
    - `command: string` default `''` — keyboard-shortcut hint rendered on the trailing side (e.g. `'⌘P'`, `'⇧⌘P'`, `'Ctrl+,'`). A module-level registry holds one `window` `keydown` listener for every menu on the page (attached while at least one shortcut is registered); it matches the shortcut against the registered options of enabled menus and emits `select` for one match only (preventing the browser default): an option of the open menu wins, then an option of the menu whose trigger holds focus, then the first registered, so a row menu repeated on every table row fires for the row the person is on. Mutually exclusive with the `trailing` slot.
    - `disabled: boolean` default `false` — disables interaction and applies disabled tokens.
    - `selected: boolean` default `false` — marks the option as checked: `role="menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked="true"`, the selected background and a trailing `ai ai-check`.
    - `href: string` default `''` — destination URL; the row renders as an anchor (still `role="menuitem"`) that emits `select` and then follows the link, so it can be opened in a new tab. `Enter` follows it natively; `Space` clicks it.
    - `type: 'default' | 'checkbox' | 'radio'` default `'default'` — item role. `default` renders `role="menuitem"` (`menuitemradio` with `aria-checked="true"` and a trailing check when `selected`) and closes the panel on activation; `checkbox` renders `role="menuitemcheckbox"` and `radio` renders `role="menuitemradio"`, both with a leading check / dot indicator column instead of the trailing check, `aria-checked` mirroring `selected`, and the panel kept open on activation (`select` still fires). Exported as `DropdownMenuItemType`.
  - Events: _none_ (root emits `select`).
  - Slots: `default` (override of the `label` prop, for rich label content), `leading` (icon / avatar before the label), `trailing` (icon / badge after the label; mutually exclusive with `command`).
- `dropdown-menu-sub/dropdown-menu-sub.vue` — sub-menu scope.
  - Props: `defaultOpen: boolean` default `false` — opens the sub-menu when the parent panel opens (for documentation and screenshots); the user can still close it.
  - Events: _none_ (activation inside bubbles to the root `select`).
  - Slots: `default` — one `<DropdownMenu.SubTrigger>` followed by one `<DropdownMenu.SubContent>`.
- `dropdown-menu-sub-trigger/dropdown-menu-sub-trigger.vue` — the row that opens the sub-menu.
  - Props: `label: string` default `''` — plain-text label; falls back to the default slot. `disabled: boolean` default `false` — the row cannot open its sub-menu and applies disabled tokens.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` (rich label), `leading` (icon before the label).
- `dropdown-menu-sub-content/dropdown-menu-sub-content.vue` — the nested panel.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<DropdownMenu.Group>` (groups render into this panel exactly as they do at the top level), which may hold further `<DropdownMenu.Sub>`.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (trigger, option activation, `Esc`, outside click). While unbound the menu is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`, `selected`
- `data-state` values (root + trigger): `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on root, trigger, and option
- `data-selected` on option mirrors the `selected` prop
- `data-type` on option mirrors the `type` prop (`default` | `checkbox` | `radio`)
- `data-state` on sub, sub-trigger and sub-panel: `open` | `closed`; `data-disabled` on sub-trigger mirrors its `disabled` prop
- `data-placement` on the sub-panel mirrors its resolved side (`right-start` | `right-end` | `left-start` | `left-end`)
- `data-placement` on the root mirrors the `placement` prop (`'auto'` stays as `'auto'`)
- `data-placement` on the panel mirrors the resolved placement (`'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end'`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and option.
- Keyboard map:
  - On the trigger: `Enter` / `Space` opens the panel and focuses the first enabled option; `Down` opens and focuses the first option; `Up` opens and focuses the last option.
  - On a sub-trigger: `ArrowRight` (`ArrowLeft` under rtl), `Enter` or `Space` opens the sub-menu and focuses its first enabled item.
  - Inside a sub-menu: `Down` / `Up` / `Home` / `End` move within it; `ArrowLeft` (`ArrowRight` under rtl) or `Esc` closes it and returns focus to its sub-trigger; `Enter` / `Space` activate; `Tab` closes the whole menu. Tests: `dropdown-menu.test.ts` › sub-menus.
  - Inside the panel: `Down` / `Up` move between enabled options (wrap-around); `Home` / `End` jump to first/last enabled option; a printable character moves to the next enabled option whose label starts with it (typeahead: characters typed within 500 ms accumulate, a repeated character cycles); `Enter` / `Space` activate the focused option; `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes the panel and lets focus proceed to the next focusable element after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes it and returns focus to the trigger. Typing in a search field inside the header slot keeps `Home` / `End` for the caret. Tests: `dropdown-menu.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
  - Nested overlays: the open panel joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`), so inside a `Popover`, `Dialog` or `Drawer` activating an option or pressing `Esc` closes only the menu; a pointer-down inside a higher layer (a `Select` list opened from the header slot) does not close the menu.
- ARIA: the slotted control (or the wrapper, when the slot has none) exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, with a single tab stop; the panel's `aria-labelledby` follows the control's `id`; the `role="menu"` element wraps only the groups and options, and the optional header and footer slots (search fields, footers with buttons) sit beside it inside the floating panel, because a `menu` may own only menu items, groups and separators (`aria-required-children`); each group uses `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` pointing at its label id (when `label` is set); each option uses `role="menuitem"`, `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; a selected option is `role="menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked="true"` and a visible check mark; `type="checkbox"` / `type="radio"` options are `menuitemcheckbox` / `menuitemradio` with `aria-checked` mirroring `selected`; a sub-trigger is a `menuitem` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and its sub-panel is a `role="menu"` labelled by it. The check and chevron glyphs are `aria-hidden`. Options are `tabindex="-1"` (roving focus through the arrows), so `Tab` leaves the menu. While closed, a menu attaches no `document` listener; the outside-`mousedown` listener lives only while the panel is open.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled state (validated via `--text-disabled` token).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on `transition-colors` for hover/selected states.
- Teleported panel: the `role="menu"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it lays out and is announced in the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger; option rows are 32 px tall and are activated by full-row click + keyboard, satisfying the 24×24 px target floor for in-menu items per WCAG 2.5.8.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`text-start`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `gap`); the panel and every sub-panel bind `dir` / `lang` from `WebkitProvider`, so they lay out in the provider's direction under `body`.
- Icons: the sub-trigger chevron mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); the check and radio dot do not.
- Keyboard: under rtl `ArrowLeft` opens a sub-menu and `ArrowRight` closes it; the sub-panel opens at `left-start` and flips to `right-start` when it does not fit. `Up` / `Down` are unchanged.
- User data: none (labels are consumer text).

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every label comes from the consumer (`label` props and slots).

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; panels are sized between `--container-3xs` and `--container-2xs`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): `usePlacement` keeps every panel inside the viewport; a sub-panel with no room on either side overlaps the parent panel instead of leaving the screen; labels truncate.
- Touch: rows are 32 px; a sub-menu opens on tap (click) as well as hover, so nothing is hover-only.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DropdownMenuGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-group'
  import DropdownMenuItem from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-item'

  import DropdownMenuTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-trigger'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'

<template>
  <DropdownMenuRoot>
    <DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <IconButton
        variant="outline"
        icon="ai ai-plus"
        aria-label="Open menu"
      />
    </DropdownMenuTrigger>
    <DropdownMenuGroup>
      <DropdownMenuItem
        value="profile"
        label="Profile"
      />
      <DropdownMenuItem
        value="settings"
        label="Settings"
      />
      <DropdownMenuItem
        value="billing"
        label="Billing"
      />
      <DropdownMenuItem
        value="invite"
        label="Invite members"
      />
      <DropdownMenuItem
        value="logs"
        label="Audit log"
      />
      <DropdownMenuItem
        value="signout"
        label="Sign out"
      />
    </DropdownMenuGroup>
  </DropdownMenuRoot>
</template>
```

# Link

> Helps users move between views or sections. Migrated from the existing implementation at `packages/webkit/src/components/navigation/link/`. Design source: [Webkit — Link](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=3548-578) (`Size` × `State` variants; hover handled in CSS).

- Import: `import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Link when the text takes the person to another page, resource or URL.
- A standalone navigation link: a domain, a repository, a docs page, "View all".
- An in-console navigation action ("Add custom domain"): no trailing icon unless `icon` is set.

## Do

- Always set `href` and a label that names the destination; an empty `href` renders `#` so the anchor stays focusable, and an empty label falls back to the locale catalog (`Learn more`).
- Pass the label as the default slot or the `label` prop; the slot wins when both are set.
- target="_blank"` adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and, when `icon` is empty, the `ai ai-external-link` glyph so an off-site link reads as one; same-tab links show no icon unless `icon` is set.
- An icon is shown when `icon` is set.
- Match `size` to the controls around it; heights follow `button` (40 / 32 / 28 px).
- disabled` drops it from the tab order and suppresses `click`; hide a link that can never be followed instead.

## Don’t

- A link inside a sentence → use a plain anchor with the text-link class.
- An action that changes something instead of navigating → use `button`.
- A text action that runs something instead of navigating → use `button` with `variant="link"`.

## Related

- `button` — set `href` when a link must look like a button.
- `breadcrumb` — a trail of links for hierarchical location.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label, the default slot's fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Learn more`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height and typography (large 40px, medium 32px, small 28px), matching Button. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the trailing icon; set shows it. Empty shows `ai ai-external-link` only when `target` is `_blank`. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Destination URL for the anchor. Empty renders `#`. |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when navigating. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | — |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` |  | The link text. Fallback: `label`, then the locale catalog. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `hover` and `focus-visible` underline the label (`underline-offset-4`); there is no surface behind the link
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- Consumer attributes (`id`, `aria-*`, `download`, `rel`, `data-*`, listeners) land on the anchor through `v-bind="$attrs"`; a consumer `rel` overrides the computed one

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter` activates.
- ARIA: `aria-disabled` and `tabindex="-1"` when disabled.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: a URL printed as the link text is the consumer's; wrap it in `dir="ltr"` when it sits inside right-to-left prose.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <Link
    label="Learn more"
    size="large"
    href="https://example.com/docs"
    target="_blank"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/link.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/link.md).

# Navigation Menu

> The top bar of a site: a row of links and triggers whose items open large panels of grouped links (product and solution menus). The items share one hover-intent timing, one keyboard model and one animated popup that resizes and slides between panels, inside a `navigation` landmark.

- Import: `import NavigationMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import NavigationMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use NavigationMenu only to build a marketing top bar with hover panels; the site already gets one from SiteHeader, and app navigation uses SidebarMenu.
- A horizontal top bar whose items open large panels of grouped links (product and solution mega-menus).
- A mix of panel triggers and plain links in one bar that shares hover-intent timing, keyboard navigation and a single animated popup.
- Panel entries need a title plus a muted description line, a leading icon, or a featured "see all" link.

## Do

- Give every panel item a stable `value` on `NavigationMenu.Item`; `v-model` and `default-value` refer to it, and an omitted value is auto-generated and cannot be controlled.
- A top-level item with no panel is a `NavigationMenu.Trigger` with an `href`; inside panels use `NavigationMenu.Item` with `layout="entry"`, an `href`, an optional `description` and `close-on-click`.
- Render one `NavigationMenu.Viewport` per root, after the list (the shadcn shape). It holds the whole overlay: it teleports, positions the popup on the active trigger, sizes it and hosts every panel. Each `Content` is moved into it, so a menu without a `Viewport` renders no panel.
- The `Viewport` teleports to `container` when set and to `body` otherwise, passing the selector through so the server renders the same tree the client hydrates.
- Pin a wide panel to the page column with the viewport's `collision-padding`, not with override classes on the popup.
- Set `aria-label` on the root (default `'Main'`) when the page has more than one navigation landmark.
- Test ids: root fallback `navigation-menu` (its own name); every part uses its own name (`navigation-menu-list`, `navigation-menu-item`, `navigation-menu-trigger` with its chevron `navigation-menu__icon`, `navigation-menu-content`, `navigation-menu-viewport` and the viewport's inner `__portal`, `__positioner`, `__popup`, `__arrow`, `__backdrop`), and a consumer `data-testid` wins on every part; one set on the `Viewport` lands on its popup.
- Attributes on the root (`id`, `aria-labelledby`, `data-*`, listeners) land on the `nav` landmark.
- The compound has the shadcn parts only: `List`, `Item`, `Trigger`, `Content`, `Link`, `Viewport`. 6.0 folded the Base UI overlay chain (`Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup`, `Arrow`, `Backdrop`) into `Viewport` props, and the `Icon` part into the trigger, which renders its own chevron.
- NavigationMenu.Trigger` always renders a `button` (or an anchor with `href`); 6.0 removed its `native-button` prop.

## Don’t

- It is the persistent vertical navigation of an app → use `sidebar` with `sidebar-menu`.
- It is a list of actions or options opened from a button → use `dropdown-menu`.
- It shows where the current page sits in a hierarchy → use `breadcrumb`.
- It is the marketing site's whole navigation bar → use `site-header`, which already composes this menu.

## Related

- `site-header` — the marketing navigation band built on `app-header`, `brand` and `navigation-menu`.
- `app-header` — the bar layout this menu usually sits in.
- `dropdown-menu` — a single-trigger option menu, not a site-wide navigation bar.
- `sidebar-menu` — vertical, hierarchical navigation rows for a sidebar.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `NavigationMenuValue` | `null` | false | Uncontrolled initial open item value. |
| `delay` | `number` | `50` | false | Hover-open delay in milliseconds. |
| `closeDelay` | `number` | `300` | false | Hover-close delay in milliseconds. |
| `orientation` | `NavigationMenuOrientation` | `'horizontal'` | false | Menu orientation. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the root navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Main`). |
| `modelValue` | `NavigationMenuValue \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open-transition-end` | `open: boolean` | Fires when the popup finishes its open or close transition. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-link`
- `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-viewport`

## Sub-components

Every part is attached to the compound (`NavigationMenu.List`, …) and importable on its own as `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-<part>`; `@aziontech/webkit/navigation-menu-root` is the root file (`navigation-menu.vue`) alone.

- `navigation-menu-list.vue` — Public sub-component `navigation-menu-list`; `show-highlight` (default `true`) shows the sliding highlight on the root horizontal list.
- `navigation-menu-item.vue` — Public sub-component `navigation-menu-item`.
- `navigation-menu-trigger.vue` — Public sub-component `navigation-menu-trigger`.
- `navigation-menu-content.vue` — Public sub-component `navigation-menu-content`.
- `navigation-menu-link.vue` — Public sub-component `navigation-menu-link`, reached as `NavigationMenu.Link`: a top-level link of the bar (`href`, `active`, `close-on-click`) that renders the same anchor as a trigger wi…
- `navigation-menu-viewport.vue` — Public sub-component `navigation-menu-viewport`, the one overlay that hosts every panel.
- `parts/` — private, not exported: `navigation-menu-portal.vue`, `navigation-menu-positioner.vue`, `navigation-menu-popover.vue`, `navigation-menu-arrow.vue`, `navigation-menu-backdrop.vue` and `navigation-menu-viewpor…

## v-model

| Model     | Type                               | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `NavigationMenuValue \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Open item via `defineModel`; `null` closes every panel. While unbound (`undefined`) the menu is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultValue`. The event carries a second argument, `eventDetails: unknown`, describing what caused the change. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` — on the root, the list, each trigger chevron, the content, the popup and the backdrop (no `data-open` / `data-closed`)
- `data-side` on the viewport's positioner and arrow: `top` | `end` | `bottom` | `start`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between triggers and links of the bar. On a trigger, `Enter`/`Space` toggle its panel; `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move to the next/previous trigger and wrap (swapped under RTL); `ArrowDown` opens the panel and focuses its first entry; `Escape` closes an open panel. Inside a panel, `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between entries and wrap, `Tab` on the trigger of an open panel moves into it, `Shift+Tab` on the first entry returns to the trigger, `Tab` on the last entry closes the panel and moves on to the next trigger, and `Escape` closes the panel and returns focus to its trigger. Tests: `navigation-menu.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: the root is a `nav` landmark. A panel trigger is a disclosure button: `aria-expanded` reflects its panel and, while open, `aria-controls` names the panel (`role="region"`); it carries no `aria-haspopup`, since the panel is navigation, not a menu. A link trigger carries `aria-current="page"` when `active`. Tests: `navigation-menu.test.ts` › axe on the closed bar, the open panel and the vertical menu.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the trigger caret points down and does not mirror.
- Arrow: the popup arrow is a rotated square that hides two of its borders through logical utilities (`border-e-0`, `border-s-0`); under `rtl` it also flips on its inline axis (`rtl:-scale-x-100`), so the visible corner still points at the trigger.
- Keyboard: on a horizontal menu `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move to the next/previous trigger, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection` passed to the root composable); vertical menus keep `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp`.
- Motion: the content slides in from the side the pointer came from; the forward/back direction is computed in reading order, so under `rtl` moving to a later trigger slides from the start edge.
- User data: none.
- Teleported content: the `NavigationMenu.Viewport` portal binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

<!-- components/page-tabs.md -->

# Page Tabs

> The second-level navigation strip of a resource detail page: a full-bleed bar ruled at the bottom, its `Tabs` at the page boundary inset, with room for the actions the whole resource owns on the right (a staged-changes `Tag`, Deploy). It is `Tabs` plus the strip and the actions region, so every detail page stops re-creating the same bar.

- Import: `import PageTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/page-tabs'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PageTabs for the second-level navigation strip of a resource detail page; to switch peer views inside a page or panel use Tabs.
- The top of every resource detail page, under the global header.
- An account page split into tabs, such as Billing.

## Do

- Bind `v-model` to the route (or a ref) and render the section below from it. PageTabs renders only the tab list, so it takes no `Tabs.Content`: the page renders the active section itself from the `v-model` value.
- Keep the labels to one word where possible.
- Put only actions that apply to the whole resource in `actions`; page-level actions go in the `page-header`.
- Set `column` to the column the page body uses (`form` over a settings form, `data` over a list) so the tabs start where the content starts.

## Don’t

- Tabs inside a card, a drawer or a panel → use `tabs`.
- Steps of a flow → use `stepper` or `wizard`.
- Navigation between pages of the app → use `sidebar` or `navigation-menu`.

## Related

- `tabs` — the tablist it renders; pass one `Tabs.Trigger` per section in the default slot.
- `page-header` — the page heading under the strip.
- `tag` and `button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `column` | `'full' \| 'data' \| 'form' \| 'focused'` | `'full'` | false | The page column the tab row lines up with: the full width, or the data, form or focused column below it. |
| `modelValue` | `TabsValue \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | One Tabs.Trigger per section of the resource. |
| `actions` | — | The actions the whole resource owns, on the right of the strip: a staged-changes Tag, Deploy. |

## v-model

- **`v-model`** (`modelValue`) — `string | number | null`, default `null`. The active tab; it updates when a tab is picked.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the tab states are owned by `tabs`
- `data-column` mirrors the `column` prop on the root. The strip and its rule stay full bleed; with `data`, `form` or `focused` the tab row inside is capped at the same measure as the page column it sits over (`layout-column`, `layout-column-form`, `layout-column-focused`) and centred, so the first tab lines up with the content below. `full` leaves the row at the page boundary inset.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `Tabs.Trigger` and the actions.
- Keyboard map: the tablist follows `tabs` (arrows move between tabs, `Home`/`End` jump); `Tab` leaves the tablist for the actions.
- ARIA: `role="tablist"` and `role="tab"` come from `tabs`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1, owned by `tabs`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`-ms-`, `margin-inline` from the column utilities); the tabs start at the inline start and the actions sit at the inline end.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: owned by `tabs` (the arrow keys follow the reading direction).
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: the tab labels and the actions come from the consumer's slots.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the column utilities cap the tab row at the page column's measure and fall back to the full width below it.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the tablist scrolls inline inside its own region (owned by `tabs`); the actions keep their size at the inline end.
- Touch: tab targets are owned by `tabs`; no hover-only affordance.
- Reflow: no page-level horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; only the tablist scrolls.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PageTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/page-tabs'
  import Tabs from '@aziontech/webkit/tabs'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const activeTab = ref('overview')
  const tabs = [
    { value: 'overview', label: 'Overview' },
    { value: 'build', label: 'Build' },
    { value: 'deployments', label: 'Deployments' },
    { value: 'variables', label: 'Variables' },
    { value: 'rules', label: 'Rules' },
    { value: 'logs', label: 'Logs' },
    { value: 'metrics', label: 'Metrics' },
    { value: 'settings', label: 'Settings' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <PageTabs v-model="activeTab">
    <Tabs.Trigger
      v-for="tab in tabs"
      :key="tab.value"
      :value="tab.value"
      :label="tab.label"
    />
  </PageTabs>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/page-tabs.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/page-tabs.md).
