<!-- components/wizard.md -->

# Wizard

> A multi-step create flow in one surface. It puts the step rail on the start side, the current step's header and fields in the content column, and a fixed footer with Cancel, Previous and Next. On the last step, Next becomes the submit action. It owns the order, which steps can be reached and where focus goes. The consumer owns the fields, the validation and the request. It differs from its siblings by owning the **whole flow**. `stepper` is only the rail and leaves layout, actions and gating to the caller. `tabs` switches between peer views that have no order and no completion.

- Import: `import WizardRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Wizard from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Wizard for any ordered multi-step create: Stepper + step content + Cancel/Previous/Next footer; compose Stepper alone only when the footer and gating must be custom.
- Creating a resource takes several ordered decisions, and showing them all at once would overwhelm the
- The reader has to finish a step before moving on. Validation runs on Next and can stop the move.
- The flow needs a review step before the final submit, and earlier steps must stay reachable to fix

## Do

- Keep step state in the consumer (refs or a form store). Only the active step renders its content, so a
- Validate in the `next` handler and call `event.preventDefault()` synchronously to block the move. For
- Show why Next was blocked inside the step (an inline `alert` or the field's `invalid` +
- The rail reaches every step the reader has already reached, forward too. A forward jump does not
- Give every step a title that names the decision (`Settings`, `Review`) and keep it short. The same
- Make the last step a review of the answers when the resource is costly to change after creation, and
- Bind `loading` to the submit request. It disables Cancel, Previous and the rail, so the handler needs no
- Mark a step `optional` only when Next works with every field in it empty.
- Always pass `ariaLabel` naming the task (`Create edge application`). Without it, the root is an
- The wizard sets no page width. Place it inside the page's create container

## Don’t

- A short form that fits one screen. A wizard adds clicks without adding clarity → use a plain form
- A confirmation or a single decision → use `dialog`.
- Peer views with no order and no completion → use `tabs`.
- A custom multi-step layout where the caller needs its own actions or a different arrangement → compose
- Numbered instructions inside documentation → use `doc-steps` + `doc-step`.

## Related

- `stepper` — the rail this component composes. Reach for it alone when the footer and gating must be
- `tabs` — unordered peer views with no completion state.
- `dialog` — a single, short decision on an overlay.
- `drawer` — a single-step create or edit form beside the page.
- `alert` — the inline error to show inside a step when Next is blocked.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `submitLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the primary action on the last step, where Next becomes the submit action. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Create`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Submit in progress: the primary action shows its loading state, and Cancel, Previous and every rail step are disabled. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the wizard region. Name the task, for example Create edge application. |
| `modelValue` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `next` | `(event: MouseEvent, step: number)` | Fired when Next is activated on any step but the last, **before** the wizard advances. `step` is the zero-based index of the step being left, which is the one to validate. Cancelable: if a handler calls `event.preventDefault()` synchronously, the wizard stays on `step`. Otherwise it writes `step + 1` to the `v-model` index. Not fired by Previous or by rail jumps, which only reach steps the reader has already reached. |
| `submit` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Fired when the primary action is activated on the last step. The wizard changes no state. The consumer starts the request and binds `loading`. Not fired while `loading`. |
| `cancel` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Fired when Cancel is activated. The wizard changes no state, and the consumer decides where to go. Not fired while `loading`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `Wizard.Step` children, in the order they are numbered and navigated. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/wizard-step`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**. An `index.ts` beside `wizard.vue` attaches the sub-component to the
root, so `<Wizard.Step>` resolves from one import. The standalone imports remain the tree-shaking path.
The wizard has no open/closed state, so it has no `Trigger` / `Content`. The anatomy name is `Step`,
because that is what the part is.

Shared state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts` +
`composables/use-wizard-context.ts`), so the consumer wires nothing. The root provides a context with
the ordered step registry, the active index, the total, `loading`, and the functions `register`,
`attach` and `unregister`. `useWizardContext()` throws a clear error when a `Wizard.Step` is rendered
outside a `<Wizard>`. Steps are ordered by document position (the same `compareDocumentPosition`
approach `stepper` uses), not by mount order, so a step inserted later still numbers correctly.

The root composes, and does not re-implement:

- `Stepper` + `Stepper.Step` (`@aziontech/webkit/stepper`) for the rail.
  `Stepper.Step` per registered `Wizard.Step` and passes:
  - `value` = `String(index)`.
  - `title` = the step's `title`.
  - `state` = `'error'` for a step marked `invalid`; otherwise `'complete'` for every step before the
    furthest step reached, except the active one, and `'upcoming'` for the rest. The rail derives
    `current` itself.
  - `disabled` = `true` for every step after the furthest step reached, and for every step while
    `loading`. The furthest step reached is the highest index the `v-model` has held since mount.
  - `data-invalid` on the `Stepper.Step` root when the step is `invalid`. `Stepper.Step` draws the
    `error` state with the danger tokens and reads its error word (`stepper.error`, `Needs attention`)
    to screen readers.

  An `optional` step shows the word `Optional` in the `Stepper.Step` default slot. The rail's `v-model`
  is the active index as a string, and a rail activation writes `Number(value)` back to the `v-model` index.

- `Button` (`@aziontech/webkit/button`) for the three footer actions, all at the house default size
  (`large`, 40px):
  - Cancel is `variant="ghost"`, at the start of the footer.
  - Previous is `variant="secondary"`, at the end. It is not rendered (`v-if`, not hidden) on step 1.
  - Next is `variant="primary"`, at the end. On the last step its label becomes `submitLabel`, it emits
    `submit` instead of `next`, and it carries `loading`.

- `wizard-step/wizard-step.vue` — one step: its header and its content.
  root on mount and reads back its zero-based index, the total, and whether it is the active step. It
  always renders its own root (a `<div role="group">` labelled by its heading), so document-order
  registration works. When inactive, that root is `hidden` and its content is not mounted (`v-if`).
  When active, it renders:
  - The header: the counter `Step {n} of {N}` as an overline paragraph with an id from `useId()`.
  - The title as an `<h2 tabindex="-1">` with `aria-describedby` pointing at the counter, followed by
    `Optional` when `optional` is set.
  - The `description` paragraph, only when non-empty.
  - Below the header, the default slot inside a `<Transition>` that fades it in.
  - When it becomes active after the initial render, it moves focus to its heading.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — what this step decides, in the reader's words; shown in the
    rail and as the step heading), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the heading
    saying what the step is for; omitted when empty), `optional?: boolean` (default `false` — marks the
    step as skippable: shows `Optional` beside the title in the rail and in the header),
    `invalid?: boolean` (default `false` — the step holds an error: the rail shows it in the error
    state and the step root carries `data-invalid`).
  - Slot: `default` — the step's content (fields, review summary).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `wizard-step` (consumer `data-testid` wins).

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/navigation/wizard/
├── wizard.vue                   (root; owns the model, provides the registry, renders rail + footer)
├── wizard.test.ts
├── index.ts                     (compound: attaches Step to the root)
├── injection-key.ts             (shared WizardContext)
├── composables/
│   └── use-wizard-context.ts    (injects; throws outside a Wizard)
└── wizard-step/
    └── wizard-step.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only):

```jsonc
"./wizard": "./src/components/navigation/wizard/index.ts",
"./wizard-root": "./src/components/navigation/wizard/wizard.vue",
"./wizard-step": "./src/components/navigation/wizard/wizard-step/wizard-step.vue"
```

## v-model

| Model     | Type                  | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | --------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Zero-based index of the step on screen, through `defineModel<number \| undefined>()`, the primary value as on `Stepper` and every sibling. Written by Next (after an un-prevented `next`), by Previous (index − 1) and by a rail jump to any step already reached. Rendering clamps an out-of-range value to `0 … N − 1` without emitting. The rail `Stepper` identifies steps by string `value`; the wizard by numeric index, because its steps are positional. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`. Interactive states (`hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`,
  `disabled`) belong to the composed `Button` and `Stepper.Step`, not to the wizard's own elements.
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`.
- `data-active-step` on the root mirrors the clamped `v-model` index.
- `data-active` on `Wizard.Step` is present only on the step on screen.
- `data-optional` on `Wizard.Step` mirrors `optional`.
- `data-invalid` on `Wizard.Step` and on its rail step mirrors `invalid`.
- Rail step statuses come from `Stepper.Step`. A step marked `invalid` is `error`. Otherwise every step
  before the furthest step reached is `complete`, the active one is `current` (derived by the rail),
  the furthest step reached is `upcoming` and enabled, and every step after it is `upcoming` +
  `disabled`.
- No `data-state`: the wizard has no open/closed state.

State matrix:

| State        | Trigger                               | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| first step   | `modelValue === 0`                    | Previous is not rendered. The footer shows Cancel at the start and Next at the end.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| middle step  | `0 < modelValue < N − 1`              | Cancel, Previous and Next.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| last step    | `modelValue === N − 1`                | The primary action reads `submitLabel` and emits `submit`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| single step  | `N === 1`                             | Previous is not rendered, and the primary action is the submit action from the start.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| loading      | `loading`                             | The primary `Button` gets `loading` (spinner + `aria-busy`, click suppressed). Cancel and Previous are `disabled`, and every `Stepper.Step` is `disabled`.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| next blocked | `next` handler calls `preventDefault` | The wizard stays on the step. The consumer renders the reason inside the step's slot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| invalid step | `Wizard.Step` `invalid`               | The step root carries `data-invalid`. Its rail step carries `data-invalid` and renders the `Stepper.Step` `error` state: the danger dot with the warning glyph and the screen-reader word `Needs attention`.                                                                                                                                   |
| step reached | the `v-model` index once held a step  | That step and every step before it stay reachable from the rail after the reader goes back.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| narrow box   | wizard box under `@2xl`               | The rail is not displayed (`@max-2xl/wizard:hidden`). The root shows its own `Step n of N` progress line (`wizard.stepOf`, `aria-live="polite"`, `data-testid="<testid>__progress"`) at the top of the content column in place of the step header's overline, which hides at that width; the step title follows it and the footer stays below. |

Layout from `@2xl` of the wizard's own box (`@container/wizard`, so a wizard in a drawer or split view follows that box): a row with the rail column (`@2xl/wizard:w-(--container-3xs) @2xl/wizard:shrink-0`) on the start
side and the content column (`min-w-0 flex-1`) beside it. The content column stacks the active step,
then the footer. The footer is a row with Cancel at the start and Previous + Next grouped at the end,
separated from the content by a top border.

- Server render and hydration: steps register from their own setup, after the root has rendered, so until mount the root does not use the step count. The step shown, `data-active-step` and Previous follow the requested `v-model` index (clamped at 0), and the primary action reads Next; on mount the index is clamped to the registered steps and the last step reads the submit label. The server HTML and the first client render therefore match.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every focusable control is a composed `Button` or `Stepper.Step` and carries their
  ring: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2
focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`. The step heading is a programmatic focus target
  (`tabindex="-1"`), not a control, so it is out of the Tab order and draws no ring.
- Keyboard map:
  - `Tab` order: the enabled rail steps (every step up to the furthest one reached), then the step
    content, then the footer (Cancel, Previous, Next/submit).
  - `Enter` / `Space` on an enabled rail step jumps to it, back or forward.
  - `Enter` / `Space` on a footer button activates it.
  - Disabled rail steps and actions are skipped by `Tab`.
  - On every step change after the initial render, focus moves to the new step's heading, so the screen
    reader announces the title and the counter. The initial render does not steal focus.
  - No `Escape` binding: the wizard is not an overlay.
- ARIA:
  - The root is a `<section>` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel` (omitted when empty).
  - The rail is the `Stepper` `<nav aria-label="Steps">`, with `aria-current="step"` on the active step.
  - Each `Wizard.Step` is a `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading. The heading
    has `aria-describedby` pointing at the `Step n of N` counter (ids from `useId()`).
  - Inactive steps are `hidden`, so they are out of the accessibility tree.
  - While `loading`, the primary `Button` sets `aria-busy`, and the other actions are natively
    `disabled`.
  - The narrow-box progress line is a polite live region (`aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`):
    when the rail is hidden, a step change is also announced as `Step n of N` after the heading. At
    `@2xl` and wider the line is `display: none`, so the live region is silent and the rail carries
    the progress. The initial render announces nothing (the region only reads changes).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled actions while `loading`
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the step-content transition; the composed parts carry their own
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the footer buttons are `large` (40px), and the rail steps are full-width rows
  at least 40px tall (owned by `Stepper.Step`)

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: step titles are the consumer's text; the "Step n of N" line comes from the locale catalog.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'
  import Switch from '@aziontech/webkit/switch'
  import Wizard from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const step = ref(0)
  const name = ref('storefront-api')
  const region = ref('south-america')
  const environment = ref('production')
  const logging = ref(true)
  const path = ref('/api/*')
  const behavior = ref('deliver')

  const regions = [
    { value: 'north-america', label: 'North America' },
    { value: 'south-america', label: 'South America' },
    { value: 'europe', label: 'Europe' }
  ]
  const environments = [
    { value: 'production', label: 'Production' },
    { value: 'staging', label: 'Staging' },
    { value: 'development', label: 'Development' }
  ]
  const behaviors = [
    { value: 'deliver', label: 'Deliver' },
    { value: 'redirect', label: 'Redirect' },
    { value: 'deny', label: 'Deny' }
  ]
  const labelOf = (options, value) =>
    options.find((option) => option.value === value)?.label ?? 'Not set'
</script>

<template>
  <Wizard
    v-model="step"
    aria-label="Create resource"
    submit-label="Create"
  >
    <Wizard.Step
      title="Configure"
      description="Name the resource and choose where it runs."
    >
      <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
        <Field required>
          <Field.Label> Name </Field.Label>
          <Input v-model="name" />
        </Field>
        <Field>
          <Field.Label> Region </Field.Label>
          <Select v-model="region">
            <Select.Trigger />
            <Select.Content>
              <Select.Item
                v-for="option in regions"
                :key="String(option.value)"
                :value="option.value"
                :disabled="option.disabled"
              >
                {{ option.label }}
              </Select.Item>
            </Select.Content>
          </Select>
        </Field>
      </div>
    </Wizard.Step>
    <Wizard.Step
      title="Settings"
      description="Fine-tune the defaults."
    >
      <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
        <Field>
          <Field.Label> Environment </Field.Label>
          <Select v-model="environment">
            <Select.Trigger />
            <Select.Content>
              <Select.Item
                v-for="option in environments"
                :key="String(option.value)"
                :value="option.value"
                :disabled="option.disabled"
              >
                {{ option.label }}
              </Select.Item>
            </Select.Content>
          </Select>
        </Field>
        <Field orientation="horizontal">
          <Switch v-model="logging" />
          <Field.Content>
            <Field.Label> Enable logging </Field.Label>
            <Field.Description>
              Keep a record of every request this resource handles.
            </Field.Description>
          </Field.Content>
        </Field>
      </div>
    </Wizard.Step>
    <Wizard.Step
      title="Rules"
      description="Decide what happens to matching requests."
    >
      <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
        <Field>
          <Field.Label> Path pattern </Field.Label>
          <Input v-model="path" />
          <Field.Description>
            Requests whose path matches this pattern follow the behavior below.
          </Field.Description>
        </Field>
        <Field>
          <Field.Label> Behavior </Field.Label>
          <Select v-model="behavior">
            <Select.Trigger />
            <Select.Content>
              <Select.Item
                v-for="option in behaviors"
                :key="String(option.value)"
                :value="option.value"
                :disabled="option.disabled"
              >
                {{ option.label }}
              </Select.Item>
            </Select.Content>
          </Select>
        </Field>
      </div>
    </Wizard.Step>
    <Wizard.Step
      title="Review"
      description="Check every answer before creating."
    >
      <dl class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-(--spacing-xs) text-body-sm">
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Name</dt>
        <dd class="text-(--text-default)">{{ name }}</dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Region</dt>
        <dd class="text-(--text-default)">{{ labelOf(regions, region) }}</dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Environment</dt>
        <dd class="text-(--text-default)">{{ labelOf(environments, environment) }}</dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Logging</dt>
        <dd class="text-(--text-default)">{{ logging ? 'On' : 'Off' }}</dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Path pattern</dt>
        <dd class="text-(--text-default)">{{ path }}</dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Behavior</dt>
        <dd class="text-(--text-default)">{{ labelOf(behaviors, behavior) }}</dd>
      </dl>
    </Wizard.Step>
  </Wizard>
</template>
```

# Command

> Command Menu is a ⌘K command palette: a modal overlay with a search input and a filtered, keyboard-navigable list of actions. It wraps the `Dialog` primitive for its panel, backdrop, focus trap, scroll-lock, and Escape handling, and adds the palette chrome on top — a search `Input`, a scrollable `List` of `Item`s organized into optional `Group`s, an `Empty` state, and `Separator`s. The root owns open/closed state (controlled or uncontrolled), a global open shortcut (⌘K / Ctrl+K), the ranked filter, nested pages, and roving active-item navigation. The filter is fuzzy and ranked: an item matches on its label (prefix, then word start, then anywhere, then an in-order abbreviation such as `dpl` for "Deploy"), its `value`, or its extra `keywords`; better matches rise to the top of their group, groups rise by their best item, and the matched characters of a plain-text label are emphasized. An item can open a `Page` — a nested list such as "Switch project" — with a back control in the search bar. It differs from `dropdown` (a small trigger-anchored menu) and `select` (a form value picker): Command Menu is a full-screen search-first launcher for actions, not a positioned menu or an input control.

- Import: `import CommandRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/command-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Command from '@aziontech/webkit/command'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Command for the searchable ⌘K palette of actions and destinations; a short list of actions opened from a button is a DropdownMenu.
- Provide a global ⌘K launcher for navigating to pages or running actions across an app.
- Let users filter a large, grouped list of commands by typing, then activate with the keyboard.

## Do

- Write items as Title Case verb phrases describing an action ("Deploy Project"), not navigation labels.
- Keep the palette controlled via `v-model:open` so the app can open it from a button and from the global ⌘K shortcut.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.
- Group related actions with `<Command.Group label="…">` and separate distinct sections with `<Command.Separator>`.
- Give an item `keywords` for the words people type that are not in its label (`['org', 'team']` on "Switch organization"). Keywords match, they are never shown.
- Use a `Page` for a choice that needs its own list ("Switch project", "Change theme"), not for a deep tree: pages are one stack, and every page is one Backspace away from the previous one.

## Don’t

- A small menu anchored to a trigger button → use `dropdown-menu`.
- Picking a value for a form field → use `select` / `multi-select`.
- A confirmation or content modal without search/list semantics → use `dialog` directly.

## Related

- `dialog` — the overlay primitive Command Menu wraps for panel, backdrop, focus trap, and Escape.
- `kbd` — renders each item's keyboard-shortcut hint and the ⌘K affordance.
- `dropdown-menu` — trigger-anchored menu; reach for it when the list is short and positioned by a trigger.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, backdrop click and Escape close the palette. |
| `shortcut` | `string` | `'meta+k'` | false | Global `'+'`-delimited keyboard shortcut that toggles the palette open (e.g. `'meta+k'`); matched against Ctrl on non-macOS platforms. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |
| `page` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:page`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string \| number)` | Fires when an enabled item is activated (click or `Enter`). `event` is the activation event; `value` is the item's identifier. The palette closes automatically and focus returns to the element that was focused before opening. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The palette content: a `<Command.Input>` followed by a `<Command.List>`. Rendered inside the teleported dialog panel. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/command-input`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-empty`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-separator`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-page`

## Sub-components

The root ships a compound API via `index.ts` (`Object.assign` attaches every sub-component; vue-tsc emits `index.d.ts`). Root binding is PascalCase `Command`. Folder layout, one folder per part:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/overlay/command/
├── command.vue          (root — wraps Dialog, provides context)
├── index.ts                  (compound Object.assign)
├── injection-key.ts          (CommandContext + useCommandMenuContext())
├── command-match.ts          (pure ranked fuzzy matcher, no Vue)
├── command.test.ts
├── command-input/command-input.vue
├── command-list/command-list.vue
├── command-group/command-group.vue
├── command-item/command-item.vue
├── command-empty/command-empty.vue
├── command-separator/command-separator.vue
└── command-page/command-page.vue
```

- `command-input/command-input.vue` — the search field.
  - Props: `placeholder: string` default `''` — input placeholder text; empty uses the locale catalog (`Search everything` in English). `ariaLabel: string` default `''` — accessible name for the search field; when empty it falls back to `placeholder`, so the field keeps its name after the placeholder disappears on the first keystroke.
  - Events: _none_ (the query lives in the injected context).
  - Slots: _none_.
- `command-list/command-list.vue` — the scrollable results region.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<Command.Group>` / `<Command.Item>` / `<Command.Separator>`, plus an optional `<Command.Empty>`.
- `command-group/command-group.vue` — labeled section.
  - Props: `label: string` default `''` — section label; omit for an unlabeled group.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<Command.Item>`.
- `command-item/command-item.vue` — a selectable command row.
  - Props:
    - `value: string | number` (required) — identifier emitted on the root `select` event when the item is activated; also part of the searchable text.
    - `disabled: boolean` default `false` — disables interaction and applies disabled tokens; the item is skipped by roving navigation and never activates.
    - `keywords: string[]` default `[]` — extra search terms matched as substrings of the query (never shown), e.g. `['preferences', 'account']`.
    - `page: string` default `''` — the `name` of a `<Command.Page>` this item opens instead of selecting.
    - `shortcut: string` default `''` — a `'+'`-delimited shortcut hint (e.g. `'meta+d'`, `'meta+shift+p'`, `'esc'`) rendered on the right via `Kbd`. Modifier tokens (`meta`/`ctrl`/`shift`/`alt`) map to `Kbd` modifier props; the final token is the key. A named final token (`esc`/`escape`, `enter`/`return`, `space`, `tab`, `backspace`, `delete`/`del`) is printed from the locale catalog through `Kbd` `key-name` (`Esc`, `Enter`, `Espaço`…); any other key is upper-cased. Display only — it does not register a global keybinding.
  - Events: _none_ (root emits `select`).
  - Slots: `default` — the item label (rich content allowed); `leading` — leading icon/avatar; `trailing` — trailing content (mutually exclusive with `shortcut`).
  - **The icon box belongs to the item that has an icon.** An item renders the leading box only when it actually supplies a `leading`; an icon-less item puts no empty element in the DOM and pays no indent, so a list that mixes iconed and icon-less rows lets each label start at the row inset it earns rather than every label inheriting the widest row's indent. The box is a fixed `size-4` — the same glyph size a `SidebarMenu` row uses — so an oversized icon cannot widen the row and pull its own label out of line with the iconed rows around it.
- `command-empty/command-empty.vue` — the no-results state, shown only when the filter produces zero visible items.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the empty-state message (falls back to "No results found." when empty).
- `command-separator/command-separator.vue` — a thin divider between sections.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.
- `command-page/command-page.vue` — a nested list the palette swaps in when an item with a matching `page` is activated (or when `v-model:page` is set to its `name`).
  - Props: `name: string` (required) — the identifier items open with `page="…"`. `title: string` default `''` — the page title shown in the back control; empty falls back to `name`.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the page's `<Command.Group>` / `<Command.Item>` / `<Command.Separator>`.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (trigger, the `shortcut`, item activation, `Esc`, backdrop click). While unbound the palette is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`.            |
| `v-model:page` | `string`  | `''`        | `update:page` | The current page via `defineModel('page')`; `''` is the first page. Item activation with `page`, the back control, `Backspace` in an empty field and `Esc` on a nested page update it. Set it before opening to open straight on a page; otherwise each opening starts on the first page. Changing pages clears the query. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active` (roving highlight), `disabled`, `empty`
- `data-state` values (root): `open` | `closed` (inherited from the wrapped `Dialog`)
- `data-active` on an item mirrors the roving active item (keyboard/hover highlight)
- `data-disabled` on an item mirrors its `disabled` prop
- `data-ranked` on the list and on each group while the query is not empty; `data-leading` on the group ranked first
- `data-page` on the input bar names the open nested page (absent on the first page)
- `empty`: when the filter yields no visible items, the `Empty` part renders in place of the list rows

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the input; items use the roving `data-active` highlight (the input keeps DOM focus).
- Keyboard map:
  - Global: the `shortcut` combo (⌘K / Ctrl+K) toggles the palette open from anywhere.
  - Inside the palette: `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` move the active item in the order the list shows (ranked order while searching; skipping disabled, wrap-around); `Home` / `End` jump to first/last enabled item; `Enter` activates the active item (opening its page when it names one); `Backspace` in an empty field returns to the previous page; `Esc` returns to the previous page on a nested page and closes (via `Dialog`) on the first; `Tab` is trapped within the panel (via `Dialog`) and reaches the back control.
- ARIA: the panel is `role="dialog"` (from `Dialog`) with an accessible name via a visually-hidden title; the input is `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the list, and carries its own accessible name via `aria-label` (`ariaLabel`, falling back to `placeholder`) so the name survives the first keystroke; the list is `role="listbox"` (no role while nothing matches); each group is `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` referencing its heading id; each item is `role="option"` with a stable `id` (`useId`), `aria-selected` mirroring the active state and `aria-disabled` mirroring `disabled`. With DOM focus on the input, the input's `aria-activedescendant` points at the active item's `id` (absent while no item is active), so a screen reader announces each row as `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` / `Home` / `End` move; and the active row is scrolled into view (`scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })`) whenever it changes, so it never drops below the fold of the scrolling list (WCAG 4.1.2, 2.4.11). Tests: `command.test.ts` › active option is announced and kept in view.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled state (validated via `--text-disabled`).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the inherited `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on item `transition-colors`.
- Ranked order is visual (CSS `order`) while the DOM keeps the consumer's order; the roving active item, `aria-selected` and `Enter` follow the visual order, so keyboard users get the ranked sequence. Highlighted characters are a `<mark>` inside the option, so the option's accessible name stays its full label.
- Focus management: opening moves focus to the input; changing pages keeps focus in the input; closing returns focus to the element focused before the palette opened. Focus trap and scroll-lock are inherited from `Dialog`.
- Touch target: item rows are full-width click targets ≥32 px tall, satisfying the in-overlay 24×24 px floor (WCAG 2.5.8).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`text-start`, `gap-*`, `px-*`), so the bar, the back control and each row mirror under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the back `chevron-left` and the item page `chevron-right` mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); the search glyph and `Kbd` keycaps do not.
- Keyboard: navigation is vertical only (`ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`), so no arrow logic flips.

## Internationalization

| Key                   | English source      | Override prop         |
| --------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------- |
| `command.title`       | `Command menu`      | —                     |
| `command.placeholder` | `Search everything` | `placeholder` (Input) |
| `command.noMatch`     | `No results found.` | default slot (Empty)  |
| `command.back`        | `Back from {page}`  | —                     |

- Item labels, keywords, group and page headings are consumer copy.
- Matching is case-insensitive with `toLowerCase()`; it does not fold accents, so a consumer adds unaccented spellings as `keywords` when people type them.

## Responsive

- The panel width and max height come from `Dialog`; the list scrolls inside `max-h-[24rem]`.
- The back control truncates a long page heading (`truncate`, `max-w-[40%]`) so the field keeps room to type.
- Touch: rows are full-width ≥32px; the back control is 32px tall. No hover-only affordance: the highlight follows the active row and taps activate.

# Confirm Dialog

> A small confirmation dialog: a title, one sentence of description, and a Cancel plus a confirm button whose `variant` says how destructive the outcome is (`danger` for a removal or a discard, `primary` for a commit). The unsaved-changes guard uses the same shell; the `actions` slot replaces the two buttons when the guard can also save. Built from `Dialog`, `Panel` parts and `Button`.

- Import: `import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ConfirmDialog whenever the person must confirm an action they started (delete, discard, publish), including typed-name confirmation; an agent asking to run a tool uses ToolApproval, and a modal with your own body uses Dialog.
- Before a removal (Remove domain, Delete resource) or a re-run (Clear again).
- When someone leaves a form with unsaved changes.
- A deletion that needs typed confirmation: put the field in the default slot and set `disabled` until it matches.

## Do

- The confirm label repeats the verb of the title (Remove Domain, Discard changes), never OK or Yes.
- variant="danger"` only when the outcome removes or discards something; a commit is `primary`.
- Close the dialog from `@confirm` once the action has run; keep it open with `loading` while it runs.
- Below `md` the buttons stack full width with the confirm button on top, the same order as `save-bar`.

## Don’t

- A form of several fields → use `dialog` with your own body.
- A non-blocking notice → use `toast` or `alert`.
- A settings save that needs no decision → use `save-bar`.

## Related

- `dialog` — the overlay it composes; use it directly for anything that is not a yes-or-no decision.
- `button` — the trigger and the actions.
- `save-bar` — the unsaved-changes bar this dialog guards.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The question or the outcome, as the dialog title. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence that says what happens on confirm. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the confirm button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Confirm`). |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the cancel button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Cancel`). |
| `variant` | `'danger' \| 'primary'` | `'danger'` | false | Kind of the confirm button. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Width of the dialog. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a spinner on the confirm button while the action runs; Cancel, `Esc` and the overlay stop closing the dialog until it clears. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the confirm button, for a confirmation that needs input first. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | The confirm button was activated; not emitted while `disabled` or `loading`. |
| `cancel` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | The cancel button was activated; the dialog closes. Not emitted while `loading`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | — | The control that opens the dialog. |
| `default` | — | Body content under the description: a field, an alert. |
| `actions` | { close: () => void } | Replaces the Cancel and confirm buttons; receives a close function. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `undefined` (uncontrolled, starts at `defaultOpen`), the same open contract as `Dialog`. Whether the dialog is open; the trigger, `Esc`, the overlay and Cancel update it. `update:open` with `false` is the one signal that fires on every close; `cancel` fires only for the Cancel button. While `loading`, only the consumer closes it (set `open` to `false` from `@confirm` once the action settles).

## States

- Visual states: `closed`, `open`
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed` (from `dialog`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the buttons and `dialog`.
- Keyboard map: on open, focus lands on Cancel, the least destructive action (WAI-ARIA alert dialog pattern; Cancel carries `data-autofocus`, which the shared focus trap honours); with the `actions` slot it lands on the first focusable control, or on the slot control marked `data-autofocus`. `Esc` closes; `Tab` is trapped in the dialog and focus returns to the trigger on close (from `dialog`). There is no close button: an alert dialog is answered with Cancel, the confirm button or `Esc`. Tests: `confirm-dialog.test.ts` › opens with focus on Cancel.
- ARIA: the panel is `role="alertdialog"` (it interrupts with a decision), named by its title and described by its description (`DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`; `aria-describedby` only when a description renders).
- Nested: opened from a `Drawer` or a `Dialog`, it is the top overlay layer, so `Esc` closes the confirm only, and while `loading` it closes nothing.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1, owned by the composed parts.

## Examples

### Confirm

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <ConfirmDialog
    v-model:open="open"
    title="Remove domain"
    description="shop.example.com stops answering for this resource once you save. Traffic already pointed at it gets no response."
    confirm-label="Remove Domain"
    @confirm="open = false"
  >
    <template #trigger>
      <Button
        label="Remove domain"
        variant="outline"
        size="medium"
      />
    </template>
  </ConfirmDialog>
</template>
```

# Dialog

> Modal surface above the page, built on the shared Panel shell. `Dialog.Content` is the whole modal: it teleports to `body`, renders the dimmed overlay behind the panel, traps focus and scroll-locks the page, so the page behind cannot be clicked, scrolled or tabbed to while the dialog is open. The consumer composes a trigger and the panel regions (header, body, footer); the header gets the close (X) button on its own unless `closable` is false; the body is the only region that scrolls. Below `md` it renders as a full-width bottom sheet.

- Import: `import DialogRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Dialog from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A focused, blocking modal task or confirmation that should sit centered over the page and trap focus.
- The interaction must be completed or dismissed before returning to the page.

## Do

- Do not add an overlay, a portal or a close button by hand: `Dialog.Content` renders the overlay and the portal, and the header renders the close button while `closable` is true (the default). Set `:closable="false"` only when the dialog must be answered through its footer actions.
- While an action is in flight, set `:dismissible="false"` and `:closable="false"` together so neither Escape, the overlay nor the close button can close it.
- One clear primary action; keep the body scannable.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- The content is a side panel, long form, or navigation that should slide from an edge → use `drawer`.
- It is small contextual content anchored to a trigger (a menu, info bubble, picker) → use a popover / `dropdown-menu`.

## Related

- `drawer` — edge-anchored panel for secondary tasks / long content.
- `dropdown-menu` — trigger-anchored menu for actions/options.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the close (X) button at the end of the dialog header. False removes it; Escape and overlay click still follow `dismissible`. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Light-dismiss: when true, overlay click and Escape close the dialog. It does not govern the close button; see `closable`. |
| `size` | `DialogSize` | `'medium'` | false | Panel max-width preset passed to the inner Panel. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-body`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-footer`

## Sub-components

- `index.ts` — the compound: the root with every part attached by `Object.assign` (`Dialog.Trigger`, `.Content`, `.Title`, `.Description`, `.Close`), plus the shared Panel regions as `Dialog.Header`, `Dialog.Body` and `…
- `dialog-close.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-close`: the close (X) `IconButton`.
- `dialog-content.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-content`: the modal itself.
- `dialog-description.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-description`.
- `dialog-title.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-title`.
- `dialog-trigger.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-trigger`.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (trigger, `Dialog.Close`, `Esc`, overlay click). While unbound the dialog is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` (where applicable)
- `data-size` on the motion wrapper mirrors `size`, reactively (a later `size` change resizes an open dialog).
- Attributes: the `Dialog` root forwards every consumer attribute (`id`, `class`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) to its root element; `DialogContent` forwards its attributes to the `role="dialog"` element.

#### Mobile sheet, height and scroll

- Below `md` the dialog is a bottom sheet, capped at 80% of the **visible** viewport (`dvh`, not `vh`: on mobile browsers `vh` is the largest viewport with the toolbars retracted, so a `vh` sheet can extend under the URL bar with its footer off-screen).
- Exactly one element caps the sheet (the panel) and exactly one element scrolls (`panel-body`), so the title and footer actions stay reachable while the body scrolls. The motion wrapper only positions and animates; it declares no cap and no scroll of its own.
- The page behind the overlay is scroll-locked while the dialog is open, and the lock is released on close.
- Phones: below `md` the panel is a bottom sheet (full width, 80 dvh); below `sm` it becomes a full-height, full-width sheet (`h-dvh`, no radius, no border). The `PanelFooter` stays pinned under the scrolling content, its direct children stretch to equal widths and it keeps `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` clear.
- Server render and hydration: the phone layout and its motion timing are CSS breakpoints (`max-md:` / `md:` utilities), so the server HTML and the hydrated DOM are identical at every width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the dialog and moves focus to its first focusable control. Focus is trapped: `Tab` on the last control wraps to the first and `Shift+Tab` on the first wraps to the last. `Escape` closes it (unless the consumer blocks dismissal) and focus returns to the trigger; when the dialog was opened without a `Dialog.Trigger` (controlled `v-model:open`), focus returns to whatever element held it when the dialog opened. Tests: `dialog.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: the panel is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` on the `DialogTitle` id, and `aria-describedby` on the `DialogDescription` id **only while a `DialogDescription` is mounted** (it registers itself, as in `Popover`), so the dialog never references a missing id. A consumer `role` passed to `DialogContent` (for example `role="alertdialog"` from `ConfirmDialog`) replaces `dialog`.
- Nested overlays: every open `DialogContent` joins the shared overlay layer stack (`composables/use-overlay-layer`). Only the top layer handles `Escape` and `Tab` trapping, so `Escape` in a dialog opened from a `Drawer` closes the dialog only, and a `Popover` teleported out of a dialog keeps its own `Tab` containment. Tests: `dialog.test.ts` › nested overlays.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every animated element; nothing sets the transition inline. Tests: `dialog-motion.test.ts`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Overlay: every open dialog renders its overlay; there is no way to open a dialog without one, so the page behind is never clickable while it is open. Tests: `dialog.test.ts` › overlay.
- Teleported content: the portal wraps its content (overlay and panel) in a `display: contents` element that binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Dialog from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    dismissible
    size="medium"
  >
    <Dialog.Trigger>
      <Button
        label="Open dialog"
        variant="primary"
      />
    </Dialog.Trigger>
    <Dialog.Content>
      <Dialog.Header class="w-full">
        <Dialog.Title>Dialog Title</Dialog.Title>
      </Dialog.Header>
      <Dialog.Body>
        <Dialog.Description>
          Modal content. Uses the shared Panel header, body, and footer regions.
        </Dialog.Description>
      </Dialog.Body>
      <Dialog.Footer>
        <div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm) md:flex-row md:justify-end">
          <Button
            label="Cancel"
            variant="outline"
            @click="open = false"
          />
          <Button
            label="Save"
            variant="primary"
          />
        </div>
      </Dialog.Footer>
    </Dialog.Content>
  </Dialog>
</template>
```

<!-- components/drawer.md -->

# Drawer

> A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen and keeps the page behind it in view. It holds secondary work that is too large or too long-lived for a dialog: filters, a long form, the details of a row, a navigation list. `Drawer.Content` is the whole modal: it teleports to `body`, renders the dimmed overlay, traps focus and scroll-locks the page, so the page behind cannot be clicked or tabbed to while it is open. The header gets the close (X) button on its own unless `closable` is false. It closes on Escape and on an overlay click when `dismissible`, and returns focus to its trigger. `:modal="false"` is the one opt-out: no overlay, no focus trap, no scroll lock, for a side panel that works next to the page it talks about (as Radix `modal={false}`).

- Import: `import DrawerRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/drawer-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Drawer from '@aziontech/webkit/drawer'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A panel that slides in from a screen edge to add or edit one item of the screen behind it (a rule, an origin, a record inside a resource), while keeping that screen in view.
- The reader already stands on the screen that owns the item: the drawer is the last step of the path (rail, list, resource page, tab), never the first.
- A form needs a resource that does not exist yet (the certificate of a workload being created): the field offers to create it, and the drawer holds that resource's create form over the form, then selects it. Use it every time; never send the reader away to create it.
- The content is too large or persistent for a centered modal.

## Do

- Pick the edge (side) intentionally and keep it consistent across the app.
- Set `size="large"` on the first drawer of a flow. A nested drawer stacked on it is `size="medium"`, at most one, never a third. The AI assistant drawer is the one `medium` first drawer.
- Do not add an overlay, a portal or a close button by hand: `Drawer.Content` renders the overlay and the portal, and the header renders the close button while `closable` is true (the default).
- Keep the drawer modal (the default). Use `:modal="false"` only when the reader must keep reading or using the page beside the drawer, such as an assistant that answers questions about the page.
- While an action is in flight, set `:dismissible="false"` and `:closable="false"` together so nothing can close it.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- It is a short, focused confirmation/task best centered and fully blocking → use `dialog`.
- It is a small overlay anchored to a trigger → use a popover / `dropdown`.
- It opens, configures or edits a product or a resource (Configure, Settings, Edit) → navigate to the resource's page, on its settings tab.
- It needs tabs, a breadcrumb or its own navigation, or a third drawer would stack → it is a page.

## Related

- `dialog` — centered, blocking modal for focused tasks/confirmations.
- `sidebar` — persistent (non-overlay) side navigation.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the close (X) button at the end of the drawer header. False removes it; Escape and overlay click still follow `dismissible`. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Light-dismiss: when true, overlay click and Escape close the drawer. It does not govern the close button; see `closable`. |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Renders the overlay, traps focus and locks page scroll. False leaves the page beside the drawer usable: no overlay, no focus trap, no scroll lock, `aria-modal` false; Escape, the close button and focus restore still work. |
| `side` | `DrawerSide` | `'end'` | false | Edge the drawer panel slides from, in reading direction (`start` or `end`). |
| `size` | `DrawerSize` | `'medium'` | false | Panel max-width preset (`small` `--container-sm`, `medium` `--container-xl`, `large` `--container-4xl`). Height is always 100% viewport. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-body`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-footer`

## Sub-components

- `index.ts` — the compound: the root with every part attached by `Object.assign` (`Drawer.Trigger`, `.Content`, `.Title`, `.Description`, `.Close`), plus the shared Panel regions as `Drawer.Header`, `Drawer.Body` and `…
- `drawer-close.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-close`: the close (X) `IconButton`.
- `drawer-content.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-content`: the drawer itself.
- `drawer-description.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-description`.
- `drawer-title.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-title`.
- `drawer-trigger.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-trigger`.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Controlled open state through `defineModel('open')`, the single declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void`, as on `dialog` and `popover`. Fires once per transition. While unbound the drawer is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` (where applicable)
- Phones: below `md` the drawer is a bottom sheet (full width, 80 dvh); below `sm` it becomes a full-height, full-width sheet (`top-0`, `h-dvh`, no radius, no border). The `PanelFooter` stays pinned under the scrolling content with full-width actions.
- Server render and hydration: the phone layout is CSS breakpoints only (`max-md:` / `md:`), so the server HTML and the hydrated DOM are identical at every width.
- `data-side` and `data-size` on the `role="dialog"` element mirror `side` and `size`, reactively; `side`, `size` and `dismissible` are read live from the root, so `:dismissible="!saving"` locks an open drawer while it saves. The width comes from container tokens (`data-[size=small]:md:max-w-(--container-sm)`, `medium` `--container-xl`, `large` `--container-4xl`), not a JS map or an inline `max-width`.
- Attributes: the `Drawer` root forwards every consumer attribute to its root element; `DrawerContent` forwards its attributes to the `role="dialog"` element.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the drawer and moves focus to its first focusable control. Focus is trapped: `Tab` on the last control wraps to the first and `Shift+Tab` on the first wraps to the last. `Escape` closes it and focus returns to the trigger, or, when opened without a `Drawer.Trigger`, to the element that held focus when it opened. Tests: `drawer.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: the panel is `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` (`false` with `:modal="false"`, where focus moves in on open but `Tab` is not trapped), `aria-labelledby` on the `DrawerTitle` id, and `aria-describedby` on the `DrawerDescription` id only while a `DrawerDescription` is mounted.
- Nested overlays: every open `DrawerContent` joins the shared overlay layer stack, so only the top layer handles `Escape` and `Tab` trapping: `Escape` in a `ConfirmDialog` opened from the drawer closes the confirm and leaves the drawer open. Tests: `drawer.test.ts` › nested overlays.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every animated element.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Overlay: a modal drawer (the default) always renders its overlay, so the page behind is never clickable while it is open. Tests: `drawer.test.ts` › overlay.
- Teleported content: the portal wraps its content (overlay and panel) in a `display: contents` element that binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

# Hover Card

> Rich preview that appears beside a link or name when the pointer rests on it or keyboard focus reaches it, and goes away when both leave. The root `HoverCard` owns the open state, the open and close delays and positioning (the shared `usePlacement`, the same engine as `Popover`); `HoverCard.Trigger` wraps the element being previewed; `HoverCard.Content` is the floating card. It sits between `Tooltip` (one line of plain text) and `Popover` (opened by a click, holds interactive content): the card shows a few lines of supplementary context, such as a person, a resource or a commit, without asking for a click.

- Import: `import HoverCardRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/hover-card-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import HoverCard from '@aziontech/webkit/hover-card'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use HoverCard for a read-only rich preview (a definition, a user card, a link preview) shown on hover or focus; interactive content is a Popover and a one-line hint is a Tooltip.
- Previewing what a link points to before following it: a user handle in an audit log, a resource name in a table, a commit hash.
- Showing a summary (status, owner, last update) that the destination page also shows.

## Do

- Wrap a link or a button: the trigger must be focusable on its own so keyboard users get the card too.
- Keep the card to a heading line, two or three facts and at most one secondary link; it is a preview, not a page.
- Keep the default delays (500 ms to open, 300 ms to close) so the card does not flash while the pointer crosses a list; shorten `openDelay` only for a single, deliberate target.
- The pointer can move from the trigger onto the card without closing it, so a link inside the card is reachable; `Esc` closes it.

## Don’t

- A one-line label or hint for an icon → use `tooltip`.
- Content the user must act on (buttons, forms) or must be able to reach by touch → use `popover`.
- The only place a piece of information appears. Hover and focus are not available everywhere; the card must repeat what the destination already shows.

## Related

- `tooltip` — plain-text hint, same hover-and-focus model, no rich content.
- `popover` — click-opened panel with focus management for interactive content; same positioning.
- `avatar`, `tag` — typical content of a card.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `HoverCardPlacement` (a side with optional `-start` / `-end`, or `'auto'`)` | `'bottom'` | false | Side of the trigger the card opens on, flipped when it does not fit; `'auto'` picks the side with room. |
| `offset` | `number` | `8` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the card. |
| `openDelay` | `number` | `500` | false | Milliseconds the pointer or focus must stay on the trigger before the card opens. |
| `closeDelay` | `number` | `300` | false | Milliseconds after the pointer or focus leaves the trigger and the card before the card closes. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Never opens the card. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state while `v-model:open` is unbound. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place one `<HoverCard.Trigger>` and one `<HoverCard.Content>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/hover-card-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/hover-card-content`

## Sub-components

- `hover-card-trigger/hover-card-trigger.vue` — wraps the previewed element in an `inline-flex` span that carries `data-testid` (`hover-card-trigger`) and `data-state`, and is the positioning anchor.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the previewed element.
- `hover-card-content/hover-card-content.vue` — the floating card.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the card content.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`. While unbound the card is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- `data-state` (root, trigger, content): `open` | `closed`.
- `data-disabled` on the root mirrors `disabled`; the card never opens.
- `data-placement` on the content mirrors the resolved placement.
- `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `readonly`, `invalid`: not states of this component; a preview that loads data shows a `Skeleton` inside `HoverCard.Content`, owned by the consumer.

## Accessibility

- Content on hover or focus (WCAG 1.4.13): dismissible (`Esc` closes it without moving focus from the trigger, and returns focus to the trigger from inside the card), hoverable (the pointer can move onto the card; `closeDelay` and the card's own pointer handlers keep it open), persistent (it stays until pointer and focus leave or `Esc`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` onto the trigger's link opens the card after `openDelay`; while it is open, `Tab` moves into the card when the card holds a link (or any focusable element), walks its links, and the `Tab` after the last one continues to the element after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` from the first returns to the trigger. A card with nothing focusable is skipped and `Tab` away closes it after `closeDelay`. `Esc` closes it; from inside the card focus returns to the trigger. Tests: `hover-card.test.ts` › keyboard.
- ARIA: while open, the trigger's focusable element carries `aria-describedby` pointing at the card; the card has no role and no `aria-modal`. The trigger wrapper adds no role or tab stop.
- Visible focus: the focus ring belongs to the consumer's link or button.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for card text on `--bg-surface-raised`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`.
- Teleported card: binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the card binds `dir` from `WebkitProvider`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: consumer content; wrap names and domains in `<bdi>` inside the card.
- Placement: `-start` / `-end` align to the trigger's physical left / right edge, as in `Popover`.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: the card shows only consumer content.

- Formatting: none (dates or counts inside the card are formatted by the consumer with `Intl`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the card is between `--container-3xs` and `--container-xs` wide.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): `usePlacement` flips to the side with room and shifts the card inside the viewport; a long card scrolls inside a height cap.
- Touch: hover is not available on touch, so a tap follows the trigger's link and the card does not open; the destination page carries the same information (see When NOT to use). Keyboard focus opens the card.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'
  import HoverCard from '@aziontech/webkit/hover-card'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">
    Deployed by
    <HoverCard>
      <HoverCard.Trigger>
        <Link
          href="https://example.com/people/jane-doe"
          label="Jane Doe"
          size="small"
        />
      </HoverCard.Trigger>
      <HoverCard.Content>
        <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
          <Avatar label="Jane Doe" />
          <div class="flex flex-col">
            <span class="text-label-md text-(--text-default)">Jane Doe</span>
            <span class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">jane.doe@example.com</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">
          Owner of production and staging. Joined Acme in March 2024.
        </p>
      </HoverCard.Content>
    </HoverCard>
    two hours ago.
  </p>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/hover-card.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/hover-card.md).
