# Panel

> The shell inside an overlay: a sized surface with a header for the title and the close control, a body that scrolls and a footer for the actions. `DialogContent` and `DrawerContent` lay their regions out with it, and a page can render it on its own as a static preview of an overlay.

- Import: `import PanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Panel from '@aziontech/webkit/panel'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Laying out the regions inside `DialogContent` or `DrawerContent`: `PanelHeader` for the title (the overlay adds its close control), `PanelBody` for the body that scrolls, `PanelFooter` for the actions.
- A static preview of an overlay surface outside a live overlay, for example a frozen dialog on a docs or marketing page.

## Do

- Inside a dialog or drawer, use only `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody` and `PanelFooter`. The overlay already renders the `Panel` root, so a second `Panel` inside it nests two shells.
- Put long content in `PanelBody`. It is the only region that scrolls; the header and footer stay in place.
- size` caps the max width (`small`, `medium`, `large` map to the `--container-sm` / `--container-xl` / `--container-2xl` tokens). `sizeAtMd` applies that cap from `md` up only and is meant for the dialog's mobile bottom sheet.
- Panel` has no open state, no dismissal and no focus management. Don't use it alone as a modal.

## Don’t

- The surface has to open over the page and trap focus → use `dialog`.
- The surface slides in from a screen edge → use `drawer`.
- Rich content anchored to a trigger that leaves the page interactive → use `popover`.
- A card in the page layout, with header, content and footer slots → use `card`.

## Related

- `dialog` — renders a `Panel` inside `DialogContent`; compose the `Panel*` regions directly in it.
- `drawer` — renders a `Panel` inside `DrawerContent`; there `PanelBody` scrolls through a `ScrollArea`.
- `card` — in-page card with header, content and footer slots. `Panel` is the elevated overlay shell, with a large shadow and max-width presets.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `PanelSize` | `'medium'` | false | Max width of the panel shell. |
| `sizeAtMd` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the `size` max-width applies from `md` up only (dialog mobile bottom sheet). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/panel-body`
- `@aziontech/webkit/panel-footer`
- `@aziontech/webkit/panel-header`

## Sub-components

- `index.ts` — the compound: `Panel` with `Panel.Header`, `Panel.Body` and `Panel.Footer` attached by `Object.assign`, exported at `@aziontech/webkit/panel`; the root alone is `@aziontech/webkit/panel-root`.
- `panel-body.vue` — Public sub-component `panel-body`.
- `panel-footer.vue` — Public sub-component `panel-footer`.
- `panel-header.vue` — Public sub-component `panel-header`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` (where applicable)
- `data-width` on the root carries the resolved width: `small` | `medium` | `large`, the same with `-md` when `sizeAtMd` is set, or `fluid` when the internal `data-fluid` attribute is passed (Drawer). Tailwind `data-[width=…]:` variants map it to the container tokens; there is no JS class map.
- Responsive: `PanelBody` is the `@container/panel`, so the content of a dialog or a drawer lays out for the panel width. Below `sm` the `PanelFooter` wraps, stretches its direct children to equal widths (`max-sm:*:flex-1`) and pads the bottom by `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Scroll region: when `PanelBody` (outside a drawer's `ScrollArea`) overflows and holds nothing focusable, it takes `tabindex="0"` with an inset focus ring, so a keyboard user can scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1, axe `scrollable-region-focusable`); it is measured on resize and on content changes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import PanelBody from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-body'
  import PanelFooter from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-footer'
  import PanelHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-header'
  import Panel from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-root'
</script>

<template>
  <Panel size="medium">
    <PanelHeader>
      <h2 class="text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Cache settings</h2>
    </PanelHeader>
    <PanelBody>
      <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Objects are cached at the edge for the TTL set on each rule.
      </p>
    </PanelBody>
    <PanelFooter>
      <Button
        label="Cancel"
        variant="outline"
      />
      <Button
        label="Save"
        variant="primary"
      />
    </PanelFooter>
  </Panel>
</template>
```

<!-- components/popover.md -->

# Popover

> Anchored, **non-modal** overlay that opens from a consumer-supplied trigger and renders rich, interactive content — a header (title + optional description + close), a free-form body, and a footer for actions — in a floating panel anchored to the trigger. Use for inline forms, filter builders, and contextual detail or confirmation that needs interactive children. Unlike `tooltip` (plain text, non-interactive) and `dialog` (modal, centered, focus-trapped), the popover leaves the page interactive, anchors to its trigger, and closes on `Esc` or outside-click. It differs from `dropdown-menu`, which renders a menu of selectable options rather than free-form content.

- Import: `import PopoverRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Popover from '@aziontech/webkit/popover'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Popover for rich or interactive content (a form, actions) opened by a click and closed on purpose; a one-line hint is a Tooltip and a read-only hover preview is a HoverCard.
- Interactive content anchored to a trigger while the page stays usable: an inline form, a filter builder, a quick edit of one field.
- Contextual detail or a light confirmation that needs buttons or links inside it.

## Do

- Place `Popover.Trigger` first and `Popover.Content` after it. The trigger wires `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and the click toggle onto your element, so don't bind them yourself.
- Let `Popover.Trigger` show the pointer: its wrapper sets `cursor-pointer` (`cursor-not-allowed` when disabled), so a `Tag`, `Avatar` or icon slotted in reads as clickable. Don't put `cursor-pointer` on the slotted WebKit component — `webkit/no-style-override` blocks it.
- Include a `Popover.Title`. The panel takes its accessible name from it through `aria-labelledby`.
- Set `size` for forms and filter builders so the panel doesn't resize as content changes. Without it, the panel sizes fluidly between the `--container-3xs` and `--container-xs` tokens.
- Use `placement="auto"` for triggers that can sit near a viewport edge.
- Use a side placement (`right-start`, `left-start`, …) for a trigger in a narrow column or a sidebar, where the panel should open beside the trigger instead of covering the content below it. Type a placement held in a variable with the exported `PopoverPlacement` (`PopoverPlacementSide` when it cannot be `'auto'`), never a cast.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open` (or `:open` + `@update:open`, whose handler receives a `boolean`).
- Set `dismissible` to `false` only when an outside click would discard input. Then give the user a way out: `Popover.Close` or a footer action.

## Don’t

- A short, non-interactive hint on hover or focus → use `tooltip`.
- A list of actions or options to pick from → use `dropdown-menu`.
- Choosing a form value from a list → use `select`.
- A blocking task that must be completed or cancelled first → use `dialog`.
- A long form or a secondary workflow → use `drawer`.

## Related

- `tooltip` — plain text only and non-interactive; opens on hover and focus, not on click.
- `dropdown-menu` — same trigger and anchoring model, but renders option rows and emits `select`.
- `dialog` — modal and centered, traps focus and locks scroll; the popover does neither.
- `drawer` — edge-anchored modal panel for longer content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `PopoverPlacement` | `'bottom-start'` | false | Where the panel opens relative to the trigger: a side (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`), optionally aligned to its `start` or `end`, or `'auto'`, which picks the best-fitting of the four vertical corners at open time based on available viewport space. A placement that does not fit flips to the opposite side, keeping its alignment. |
| `offset` | `number` | `4` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens. |
| `size` | `PopoverSize` (`'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'`)` | `undefined` | false | Panel width preset mapped to container tokens: `'small'` (`var(--container-xs)`), `'medium'` (`var(--container-sm)`), `'large'` (`var(--container-md)`). When omitted, the panel sizes fluidly between `var(--container-3xs)` and `var(--container-xs)`. Same name as the size preset of `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `ConfirmDialog`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Light-dismiss: when `true`, the panel closes on outside-click and `Esc`. Set `false` to keep it open until the trigger or `PopoverClose` closes it. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place `<Popover.Trigger>` followed by `<Popover.Content>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-footer`

## Sub-components

The root `Popover` owns open/closed state, anchoring/placement (exposing the computed `panelStyle`), outside-click + `Esc` dismissal, focus entry on open, Tab hand-off and focus return. Shared state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`isOpen`, `triggerId`, `contentId`, `titleId`, `descriptionId`, `setOpen`, resolved `placement`, `size`, `panelStyle`, and the `panelEl` that `Popover.Content` assigns), so every sub-component is context-aware and the consumer wires nothing. **`Popover.Content` renders the single teleported, animated floating panel with its content inline** (the Select / Tooltip pattern — one `<Teleport>` + `<Transition>`, so the scale animation carries the whole panel on enter/leave); the panel element carries `role="dialog"`, the surface/border/radius/shadow tokens, the open/close `animate-popup-scale-*`, `--popup-origin` (via `panelStyle`), and `data-state` / `data-placement`, and assigns itself to the root's `panelEl` so the root's placement/focus logic operates on it. Member names mirror this component's anatomy; `Trigger` / `Content` are valid here because the popover has a real `data-state="open|closed"`.

- `popover-trigger/popover-trigger.vue` — as-child trigger.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the consumer's trigger element. The trigger forwards aria + click; the consumer must not bind those itself.
- `popover-content/popover-content.vue` — renders the floating panel via a single `<Teleport to="body">` + `<Transition>`, with its default slot (`Popover.Header`, the free-form body, `Popover.Footer`) arranged inline a…
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the popover anatomy (`Popover.Header`, body content, `Popover.Footer`).
- `popover-header/popover-header.vue` — full-width header region with a bottom divider and `py var(--spacing-sm)` / `px var(--spacing-md)` padding, laid out as a row with the title/description block on the left and the…
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — `Popover.Title`, optional `Popover.Description`, and `Popover.Close`.
- `popover-title/popover-title.vue` — title text (`.text-body-sm`, `var(--text-default)`).
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — plain-text title.
- `popover-description/popover-description.vue` — supporting description text (`.text-body-xs`, `var(--text-muted)`).
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — plain-text description.
- `popover-close/popover-close.vue` — close control.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: _none_.
- `popover-footer/popover-footer.vue` — full-width footer region with a top divider and `py var(--spacing-sm)` / `px var(--spacing-md)` padding.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — action buttons (e.g. Cancel / Apply).

## v-model

| Model          | Type                   | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ---------------------- | ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void`. Fires on every open/closed transition: trigger toggle, `Popover.Close`, `Esc`, and outside-click. While unbound (`undefined`) the popover is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values (root, trigger, floating panel): `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on root and trigger
- Cursor: the trigger wrapper shows `pointer`, and `not-allowed` with `data-disabled`
- `data-size` on the floating panel mirrors `size`
- `data-placement` on the root mirrors the `placement` prop (`'auto'` stays as `'auto'`)
- `data-placement` on the floating panel mirrors the resolved placement (any `PopoverPlacementSide`; `'auto'` resolves to one of `'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end'`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger and the close button.
- Keyboard map:
  - On the trigger: `Enter` / `Space` toggles the panel. When it opens (by click or key), focus **moves to the first focusable element in the panel**; when the panel has none, focus stays where it was. A panel that is open on first render (`defaultOpen`, a bound `open`) does not take focus.
  - `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger, from anywhere (trigger or panel).
  - `Tab` from the trigger moves to the first panel control. `Shift+Tab` on the first panel control returns to the trigger and keeps the panel open. `Tab` past the last panel control closes the panel and moves focus to the next focusable element after the trigger in the page (or, inside a `Dialog` / `Drawer`, inside that overlay, wrapping to its first control), so keyboard users can always leave a non-modal popover.
  - Outside-click closes the panel; focus is not forced back to the trigger on outside-click.
  - Nested overlays: the popover joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`) while open, so only the top layer handles `Esc`, `Tab` and outside-click. A popover opened from a `Dialog` closes on `Esc` without closing the dialog. A `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `DropdownMenu`, `Combobox` or `Tooltip` opened inside the panel is a higher layer even though it teleports to `body`: a pointer-down inside its list never counts as outside the popover, and `Esc` closes that list first, the popover on the next `Esc`.
  - Tests: `popover.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec), portalled children (overlay layer stack).
  - A text `<input>` or `<textarea>` as the trigger control keeps its textbox role and gets none of `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`, which ARIA does not allow on a textbox (`aria-allowed-attr`); a field that opens suggestions should be a `Combobox`.
- ARIA: the slotted control (or the wrapper, when the slot has none) exposes `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, with a single tab stop and in the server HTML; the floating panel (rendered by the root) uses `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="false"`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `Popover.Title` id (without a title, at the trigger control's id, so the dialog always has a name) and `aria-describedby` pointing at the `Popover.Description` id (when present); `Popover.Close` is an `IconButton` with `aria-label="Close"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled trigger state (validated via `--text-muted` / `--text-disabled` tokens).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on `transition-colors` for hover/focus states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger (consumer's element — flagged in docs); the close `IconButton` follows `IconButton`'s own target sizing.
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="dialog"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.
- `PopoverHeader` keeps its `header` tag with `role="none"`, so an open popover does not expose a `banner` landmark (pinned by `src/test/screen-reader.test.ts`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import PopoverClose from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-close'
  import PopoverContent from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-content'
  import PopoverHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-header'
  import PopoverRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-root'
  import PopoverTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-title'
  import PopoverTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-trigger'
</script>

<template>
  <PopoverRoot>
    <PopoverTrigger>
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        label="Open popover"
      />
    </PopoverTrigger>

    <PopoverContent>
      <PopoverHeader>
        <PopoverTitle>Popover title</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverClose />
      </PopoverHeader>

      <div class="p-(--spacing-md) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">
        This content is rendered inside the popover panel.
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  </PopoverRoot>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tooltip.md -->

# Tooltip

> Surfaces a short hint anchored to a trigger element when the user hovers, focuses, or long-presses it. Use for icon-only buttons, abbreviations, or any control whose meaning is not obvious from its label alone. **Not** for rich content or interactive children — use `popover` instead.

- Import: `import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Tooltip for a one-line plain-text name or hint on a control, shown on hover or focus; it cannot hold links. For rich or interactive content opened by a click use Popover; for a read-only rich preview on hover use HoverCard.
- Naming an icon-only control on hover and focus.
- Revealing the full text of a truncated label, or expanding an abbreviation.
- One short, plain-text hint that the user can do without.

## Do

- Wrap a focusable element. The tooltip opens on the wrapper's `focusin`, and the wrapper itself is not focusable.
- Keep `content` to a few words. It renders as plain text, with no markup.
- The tooltip describes its trigger (`aria-describedby`) but does not name it. Icon-only triggers still need their own accessible name.
- Use `disabled` to suppress the tooltip. An empty `content` also blocks opening, but it reads as a bug.
- Keep the default `delay` (200 ms) unless a dense toolbar needs a longer one.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- The content has links, buttons or more than one line of structure → use `popover`.
- An info glyph beside a field label or column header → use `hint`.
- A read-only rich preview (a definition, a glossed term in documentation prose) → use `hover-card`.
- Guidance or errors the user needs to complete a field → use `field-error`.

## Related

- `popover` — click-opened, interactive, with a header, body and footer.
- `hint` — the focusable info glyph that renders a `Tooltip` for you.
- `hover-card` — read-only rich preview on hover or focus; DocMarkdown's `<Tooltip>` tag renders one.
- `icon-button` — the most common trigger; it still needs its own `ariaLabel`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `—` | true | Plain text shown inside the tooltip. |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'auto'` | `'top'` | false | Anchor side relative to the trigger; `auto` picks the side with room. |
| `delay` | `number` | `200` | false | Hover-open delay in milliseconds. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables tooltip activation. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The trigger element. Tooltip anchors to its bounding box. |

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (hover, focus, `Esc`). While unbound the tooltip is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-placement`: `top` | `right` | `bottom` | `left`
- `data-anchored` on the panel once its opening position has landed — the flag that lets a re-anchor animate while the entrance stays the open animation

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger wrapper.
- Hoverable (WCAG 1.4.13): the panel takes the pointer. Leaving the trigger closes the tooltip after a 100 ms grace, and entering the panel within the grace keeps it open (so text can be read under magnification); leaving the panel closes it after the same grace. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › hoverable content.
- Touch: a long-press (500 ms `pointerdown` with `pointerType` `touch`) opens the tooltip; it hides 1.5 s after the finger lifts. A mouse press never opens it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` onto the trigger opens the tooltip at once (no hover delay); `Escape` closes it and focus stays on the trigger; `Tab` away closes it; the tooltip never takes or traps focus. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- Nested overlays: while open, the tooltip joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`) as a transient layer (it never takes focus, so it does not pause a dialog's focus trap). Inside a `Dialog`, `Drawer` or `Popover`, the first `Escape` closes only the tooltip; the next one reaches the host. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › inside an open Dialog, Escape closes only the tooltip.
- ARIA: `role="tooltip"` on the panel; the slotted control references the panel via `aria-describedby` (merged into a WebKit `Button` / `IconButton` or native control at render, otherwise forwarded onto the first focusable element in the slot after mount; on the wrapper only when the slot has none). The wrapper itself has no `role` and no tab stop. `aria-hidden="true"` when `data-state="closed"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 — text against surface verified in both light and dark modes.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the panel; reduced-motion users get instant show/hide.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger (the consumer's responsibility — flag in docs).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="tooltip"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'
</script>

<template>
  <Tooltip
    content="This is a Tooltip"
    placement="top"
  >
    <Button
      label="Hover me"
      variant="outline"
      size="medium"
    />
  </Tooltip>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/tooltip.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/tooltip.md).

<!-- components/webkit-provider.md -->

# Webkit Provider

> Sets the language and text direction of every WebKit component below it. It wraps the app once, at the root, with the user's BCP 47 locale: components then read their built-in strings (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) from the locale catalog and format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and plurals with `Intl` for that locale. English is built in; Portuguese (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR`) and Spanish (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`) are separate entries the app imports and passes through `catalogs`, so an English-only app does not ship them. The catalogs are static imports, so the server and the client render the same strings and hydration never flips after the first render. Digits are Latin unless the tag picks a numbering system (`ar-u-nu-arab`): engines ship different CLDR defaults (Node and Chromium format `ar` with Latin digits, Safari with Arabic-Indic ones), so every `Intl` formatter receives the tag through `intlLocale`, and server and client render the same text. By default everything follows the person's device: an unset `locale` (and every component with no provider mounted) uses the device locale (`navigator.language`) for the `Intl` formats and picks its catalog when one is registered, falling back to English text. The server cannot know the device, so the server render and the hydrating client render `en-US`, and the device locale applies right after mount; an explicit `locale` (the user's saved choice) renders the same on both from the start. Only what people read follows the device: values that components hand back through `v-model` stay unambiguous (Calendar a `Date`, DateRangePicker ISO 8601 instants, TagEditor `key`/`value` pairs). It also carries the reference time of relative times (`now`), so a page that must render the same text on the server and the client, or an example, fixes it once instead of on every cell. The element it renders carries `lang` and `dir`.

- Import: `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`
- Category: provider · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Once at the root of every app, with the catalogs of the languages the app offers; pass `locale` when the user chose one (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`), leave it unset to follow the device.
- Around one region that must read in another language than the rest of the page (a preview of an email in the customer's language).
- To rename a built-in string for the whole app (`messages`), instead of passing the same label prop to every instance.

## Do

- Mount one `WebkitProvider` at the app root and pass the locale the user chose, or leave it unset to follow the device; do not nest one per page.
- Register every language the app offers in `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>`; a `pt-BR` or `es` locale with no registered catalog falls back to English and warns once in development.
- Use a full BCP 47 tag (`pt-BR`, not `pt`); a tag with no registered catalog falls back to the same language, then to English.
- Override built-in strings through `messages` (partial, deep-merged), not by forking components.
- Leave `dir` on `auto`: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu locales turn the subtree right-to-left (a device locale does so only when its catalog is registered, so English text never reads right-to-left).
- Leave `now` unset in an app: relative times then read the real clock and `Table.CellTime` re-renders every minute. Set it to a fixed moment where the text must not depend on when it renders: an example or a test (`const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10, 12)`, sample dates counted back from it), or a server render whose markup the browser hydrates. Never compute that moment from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup: the server and the browser read different clocks.

## Don’t

- Translating your own product copy (titles, descriptions, button labels you pass in) → keep it in your app's own i18n; the provider only covers the strings WebKit ships.
- Changing one instance's label → pass the component's label prop (`aria-label`, `confirm-label`); a prop always wins over the catalog.
- Only flipping the layout for a right-to-left language → still use the provider with that locale; `dir` follows it.

## Related

- use-locale` — the composable components use to read the active locale, translate a key and format with `Intl`; use it in your own components to match WebKit's formatting.
- `pagination` — reads its labels and the "Showing x to y of z" line from the catalog.
- `confirm-dialog` — reads Confirm and Cancel from the catalog when no label is passed.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string` | `''` | false | BCP 47 locale of everything below the provider; picks the catalog from `catalogs` (English is built in) and the `Intl` formats. Empty follows the device locale, `en-US` on the server and until mount. |
| `catalogs` | `Record<string, Messages>` | `undefined` | false | Extra catalogs keyed by locale tag, imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`); a locale with no catalog falls back to English. |
| `messages` | `PartialMessages` | `undefined` | false | Partial catalog deep-merged over the built-in one, keyed by component group (`{ pagination: { next: 'Seguinte' } }`). |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | false | Text direction of the subtree; `auto` derives it from the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). |
| `now` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference time for every relative time below the provider (`Table.CellTime`, `useLocale().formatRelativeTime`, the day groups of `ConversationHistory`, the relative ranges of `DateRangePicker` when their own `now` is unset); unset reads the real clock, ticking each minute. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | IANA time zone every `Timestamp` below the provider shows its local time in, and every `DateRangePicker` with no `v-model:time-zone` formats in (`America/New_York`, `UTC`), for an app-wide time zone picker; empty reads the browser's zone. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The app, or the part of it that shares this locale. |

## States

- No visual states; the root carries `lang` (the locale) and `dir` (`ltr` | `rtl`).
- `locale` unset: `lang` and the formats are `en-US` in the server render and during hydration, then the device locale after mount.
- `now` set: every relative time below reads it instead of the real clock; changing it re-renders them. An empty or unparseable value reads the real clock.
- `timeZone` set: every `Timestamp` below shows its local time in that zone and renders it on the server too, and every `DateRangePicker` without its own `timeZone` formats and edits its range in it; `useLocale().formatDate` and the other formatters are unchanged. Empty reads the browser's zone after mount.

## Accessibility

- `lang` on the root lets screen readers pick the right voice and pronunciation (WCAG 3.1.1 / 3.1.2).
- `dir` on the root mirrors reading order for right-to-left languages.
- Overlays that teleport to `body` (Dialog, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, DropdownMenu, Select, MultiSelect, Toaster, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, PropertyFilter, NavigationMenu.Viewport, the doc overlays) read the provider through `usePortalLocale()` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-locale`) and set the same `dir` and `lang` on their teleported root, so they do not fall back to the document's direction and language. A consumer's own `<Teleport>` does the same with `v-bind="usePortalLocale().value"` on its root.
- Every assistive label WebKit ships (close buttons, pagination, sort state, empty states) is read in the provider's language.
- No focusable element of its own; it adds no role and no landmark.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const page = ref(1)
  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
  >
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
      <PaginationRoot
        v-model:page="page"
        :total="120"
      />
      <ConfirmDialog
        v-model:open="open"
        title="Remover domínio"
        description="shop.example.com deixa de responder por este recurso."
        size="small"
        @confirm="open = false"
      >
        <template #trigger>
          <Button
            label="Remover domínio"
            variant="outline"
            size="medium"
          />
        </template>
      </ConfirmDialog>
    </div>
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

<!-- components/architecture-tabs.md -->

# Architecture Tabs

> The architecture band of a product page: a horizontal section title with one large button, over a row of up to five tabs whose active tab draws its named diagram the full width of the frame. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'architecture-tabs', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `registration-frame`, `media-tabs` and `diagram`. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.

- Import: `import ArchitectureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/architecture-tabs'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ArchitectureTabs only when every tab shows a full-width official diagram (up to five tabs).
- To plot several architectures of one product, or one request across the platform, one diagram at a time.

## Do

- Keep to five tabs with `tabsSide` `top` or `bottom`, three with `start` or `end`; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
- Give every tab a `diagram` from the diagram library and a stable `value`.

## Don’t

- For features shown by an illustration each → use `feature-tabs`.
- For a scroll-driven walkthrough → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tabs` — the timed tab row this section renders through.
- `diagram` — the named architecture diagram each tab draws.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence beside the headline. |
| `tabsSide` | `ArchitectureTabsSide` | `'top'` | false | Side of the diagram the tabs sit on: `top`, `bottom`, `start` or `end`; start and end hold up to three tabs. |
| `tabs` | `ArchitectureTabsTab[]` | `[]` | false | The architectures, in order; each is `{ value, title, description, diagram, diagramAriaLabel? }` where `diagram` is the name of the diagram drawn while the tab is active and `diagramAriaLabel` replaces the description that diagram ships. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Opens the next tab on a timer, with the composed tabs' visible pause control. |
| `autoplayInterval` | `number` | `6000` | false | Milliseconds each tab holds before the next one opens. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Large button in the section title; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## Assets

- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the active tab, its progress and the timer are owned by `media-tabs`
- Empty: when `tabs` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set
- The timer holds each tab for `autoplayInterval` milliseconds (owned by `media-tabs`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `media-tabs` (the tabs) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the button and the tab row; the tab row's keys are owned by `media-tabs`.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; each diagram carries the description its spec ships, or the tab's `diagramAriaLabel` when one is set.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-tabs` and `diagram`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the timer never runs under reduced motion (owned by `media-tabs`).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the large button and the tab rows.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ArchitectureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/architecture-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      value: 'request-path',
      title: 'Request path',
      description:
        'A call crosses Firewall, the application and the function before it reaches a model.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway'
    },
    {
      value: 'failover',
      title: 'Provider failover',
      description: 'When a provider degrades, the gateway moves to the next model on the alias.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-provider-failover',
      diagramAriaLabel:
        'A request falls back from a degraded model provider to the next model on the alias'
    },
    {
      value: 'costs',
      title: 'Cost routing',
      description: 'Premium tokens go only where they pay off; everyone else gets a lighter model.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-model-routing'
    },
    {
      value: 'latency',
      title: 'Latency routing',
      description: 'Real-time tasks run on AI Inference, close to the user, in under 30 ms.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-latency-routing'
    },
    {
      value: 'cache',
      title: 'Response cache',
      description:
        'A repeated prompt is answered from cache, with no model call and no tokens spent.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-response-cache'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Docs',
    href: '/product-preview',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ArchitectureTabs
    eyebrow="Routing"
    title="Every AI request through one control point"
    description="Every client calls one endpoint. Firewall stops abuse, then a function checks the key, routes the call, and logs it."
    tabs-side="bottom"
    :autoplay-interval="8000"
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/article-body.md -->

# Article Body

> The reading page of an article. A brand banner sits over a three-column grid: the share, community and copy-page rail on the left; the breadcrumb, headline, byline and prose down the middle at a reading measure; and the "On this page" outline on the right. Both rails stick under the header and fold away below `lg`, leaving the column alone. The section opens the page itself, so it carries its own `section-container` instead of sitting in the page column. The prose arrives as markdown: `##` / `###` headings (each with an id slugged from its text, feeding the outline), fenced code blocks, `-` and numbered lists and paragraphs, with inline links, `**strong**`, `*emphasis*` and `` `code` `` inside paragraphs and list items. The outline follows the reader: the heading last scrolled past is active, and choosing an entry scrolls to it (smoothly unless reduced motion is set) and writes its hash to the address. The byline can carry the writers' names and their photos as overlapping avatars. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-body', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-container`, `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `breadcrumb`, `hero-title`, `divider`, `doc-prose`, `tooltip`, `icon-button`, `split-button`, `avatar` and `doc-on-this-page`; copying to the clipboard is local behaviour, confirmed by a toast.

- Import: `import ArticleBody from '@aziontech/webkit/article-body'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open every blog post and every success story page.

## Do

- Write the body as plain blocks — headings, paragraphs and `-` lists separated by blank lines; inline markdown is rendered as text.
- Mark the last breadcrumb entry `active` (it renders `aria-current="page"`).

## Don’t

- For a list of articles → use `article-index`.
- For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.

## Related

- `doc-prose` — the reading-measure typography the body renders in.
- `doc-on-this-page` — the outline rail fed by the body's headings.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the headline. |
| `article` | `ArticleBodyArticle` | `—` | true | The piece being read: its `title` (the page h1), `description`, `date`, `readTime`, canonical `href`, and optionally `author` (the writers' names) and `authors` (each a `name` and an `avatar` photo URL). |
| `trail` | `BreadcrumbItemData[]` | `[]` | false | The breadcrumb over the headline, each a `label` and an `href`, the last one marked `active`. |
| `body` | `string` | `''` | false | The article as markdown; its `##` and `###` headings feed the outline. |
| `banner` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the image over the masthead; the banner frame is omitted when empty. |
| `share` | `ArticleBodyShare` | `undefined` | false | Labels of the share group: its `title`, `copyLink`, `shareX` and `shareLinkedIn`, optional `copyFeed` with the `feed` URL it copies, and optional toast messages `copiedLink`, `copiedFeed` and `copiedPage`; the group is omitted when absent. |
| `community` | `ArticleBodyCommunity` | `undefined` | false | The community group: a `title` and `links`, each a `label`, an `href` and an `icon`; omitted when absent. |
| `copyPage` | `ArticleBodyCopyPage` | `undefined` | false | The copy-page split button: its `label` and a `menu` of entries, each a `value`, a `label` and an `icon`; omitted when absent. |
| `assistants` | `Record<string, string>` | `{}` | false | URL templates of the assistants the copy-page menu opens, keyed by menu `value`; `{prompt}` in a template is replaced by the encoded prompt to read the article. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on every link and button
- The outline lists the body's headings; it is omitted when the body has none
- Scroll-spy: the first heading is active on the server and on load; after mount the active heading is the last one whose top has scrolled above the header line (120 px), updated on scroll; choosing an outline entry scrolls its heading into view (`smooth`, or instant under reduced motion), makes it active and replaces the address hash
- The left rail renders only the groups that are set, and is omitted when none is
- Copying: the copy-link button and the `link` menu entry copy the current page URL (`article.href` when there is none); the copy-feed button (when `share.copyFeed` and `share.feed` are set) copies `share.feed`; the split button's main action copies the page as markdown (headline, deck, body); each success raises a success toast (`share.copiedLink` / `copiedFeed` / `copiedPage`, or the locale default), and a failed clipboard write raises an error toast. Toasts render where the page mounts a `Toaster`
- Copy-page menu: the `link` entry copies the URL; the `markdown` entry opens the page as plain-text markdown in a new tab; an entry whose `value` is a key of `assistants` opens that template in a new tab with `{prompt}` replaced by the encoded prompt `Read <article.href> so I can ask questions about it.`
- Byline: with `authors`, overlapping large avatars (photo, or initials without one) lead the byline; with `author`, the names sit above the date and read time
- Prose: fenced code blocks render as `pre`/`code`; numbered lists as `ol`; a full `http` link opens in a new tab

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every link and button shows a `focus-visible` ring.
- Feedback: copy results are announced by the `Toaster`'s live region; the outline's active entry carries `aria-current` (owned by `doc-on-this-page`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the breadcrumb, the rails and the prose links; the split button owns its menu keyboard map.
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div` so the page keeps its own landmarks; the headline is the page `h1` (from `hero-title`); the prose is an `article`; the two rails are `aside` landmarks, the left one named by the share title, the right one by the outline's own navigation; the share and community groups are named `section`s; icon-only share buttons are named by their labels and carry a tooltip; the banner is decorative (`aria-hidden`, `alt=""`); heading ids are slugged from their text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — owned by `icon-button` and `split-button`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the rails swap sides with the grid under `rtl`.
- Icons: share and copy glyphs and brand marks do not mirror.
- Keyboard: unchanged; the split button owns its menu map.
- User data: code blocks keep `dir="ltr"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                           | English source                                | Override prop      |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `articleBody.linkCopied`      | `Link copied`                                 | `share.copiedLink` |
| `articleBody.copiedFeed`      | `Feed link copied`                            | `share.copiedFeed` |
| `articleBody.copiedPage`      | `Page copied as markdown`                     | `share.copiedPage` |
| `articleBody.copyFailed`      | `Could not copy`                              | —                  |
| `articleBody.copyFailedHint`  | `Your browser blocked clipboard access.`      | —                  |
| `articleBody.assistantPrompt` | `Read {url} so I can ask questions about it.` | —                  |

- Every other string (labels, trail, the article) arrives through props.
- Formatting: none; the date and read time arrive pre-formatted.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; from `lg` the grid has three columns with sticky rails.
- Narrow (< `lg`): both rails fold away and the column stands alone; code blocks scroll sideways inside themselves.
- Touch: owned by `icon-button` and `split-button`.
- Reflow: no horizontal page scroll at 320 px; only a code block scrolls.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>

  import placeholderImage from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-image.svg'
</script>

<template>

    :banner="placeholderImage"
    body="## Challenge&#10;&#10;Magalu is the most innovative retail company in LATAM.&#10;&#10;## Solution&#10;&#10;Magalu counts on Azion’s platform to evolve its security posture.&#10;&#10;## Results and Impact&#10;&#10;Magalu simplified security operations by blocking millions of threats per year."
    :article="{
      title: 'Magalu Ensures High Availability at Scale with Azion',
```

<!-- components/article-cards.md -->

# Article Cards

> A titled row of three linked article cards on one hairline frame grid with no gutter, stacking to one column on mobile. Each card is a single link: a 16:9 media cell holding the article's cover — or, when it has none, the client's mark in one flat ink that follows the theme — then the headline, the deck and a `meta` overline pinned to the foot. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-cards', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame` and `card-grid`. `variant` places the heading only: `start` at the start (an article's closing row), `center` centred over the cards under an overline (a landing-page band); the cards keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import ArticleCards from '@aziontech/webkit/article-cards'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a blog post with its related articles, or a success story with its related stories.
- To show three stories as a landing-page band under a centred heading.

## Do

- Give a card either `image` or `mark`; the mark is drawn only when there is no cover.
- Keep the band to three cards so the frame row stays full.
- Set `target: '_blank'` on a card whose article lives on another site; it opens in a new tab and says so to assistive technology.

## Don’t

- For the full, filterable list of articles → use `article-index`.
- For one featured article selected from a wall → use `article-highlight`.

## Related

- `card-grid` — the frame grid the cards sit on.
- `article-highlight` — the blog's opening band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `ArticleCardsVariant` | `'start'` | false | Placement of the heading: `start` sets it at the start, `center` centres it over the cards. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Id set on the band so an in-page `#hash` link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the heading. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `items` | `ArticleCardsItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cards, in order; each is `{ id, href, title, description, meta, image?, mark?, target? }`; a card whose `target` is `_blank` opens in a new tab. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the card grid. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (the card lifts to the raised surface and its media scales up), `focus-visible` (inset ring)
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop and places the heading
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set
- `anchor` sets the band's `id`; a card whose `target` is `_blank` links with `rel="noopener"`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each card is one link with an inset `focus-visible` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves card to card; `Enter` follows the link.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the grid is a `group` named by `ariaLabel` when set; the headline is the section title's `h2` and each card's headline an `h3`; a cover is decorative (`alt=""`), a client mark is named by the client; a `_blank` card appends the visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)` to its name.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted` on the canvas.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the whole card is the target.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the frame grid mirrors through `CardGrid`.
- Icons: none; a client mark is a logo and never mirrors.
- Keyboard: unchanged (`Tab` order follows the DOM).
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source         | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- |
| `articleCards.opensInNewTab` | `(opens in a new tab)` | —             |

- Formatting: none. Every other string is editorial copy that arrives through props.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the grid is three columns from `md` and one column below (from `CardGrid`).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): the cards stack in one column and keep the 16:9 media cell.
- Touch: the whole card is the target.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import placeholderImage from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-image.svg'
</script>

<template>

    variant="start"
    title="Related Articles"
    aria-label="Related Articles"
    :items="[
      {
        id: 'how-to-reduce-ai-agent-latency',

        title: 'How Do You Reduce AI Agent Latency?',
        description:
          'Learn where latency builds up in AI agents and how to reduce delays across inference, tools, memory, and state with distributed architecture, caching, and observability.',

      },
      {
```

<!-- components/article-highlight.md -->

# Article Highlight

> The band that opens a blog under its hero. One article is shown large — its cover beside its overline, headline, deck, read time and a button into it — over a wall of the highlight articles that acts as its selector. The wall is a tablist and the large article its panel; selecting a title on the wall swaps the panel with a short slide in the direction of travel, and every article is drawn invisibly under the panel so the band keeps the height of its tallest article and never jumps. With four or more articles the wall runs four across. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-highlight', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid` and `button`; the selection is local state. With `autoplay` the band advances on its own every `autoplayInterval`, drawing a primary progress line at the panel's foot, and pauses while the pointer is over it or keyboard focus is inside it; it never autoplays under reduced motion or with one article. With `fill`, from `lg` the band fills the first viewport under the sticky site header.

- Import: `import ArticleHighlight from '@aziontech/webkit/article-highlight'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open a blog or a resource page with its newest or most important articles.

## Do

- Feature three to five articles; the wall sets one column per article from `lg`, so five sit in one row of five as on azion.com's blog.
- Give a `highlightImage` cropped for the panel when the cover does not read at that size.
- Bind `v-model` (the selected index) to open on an article other than the first; the band never advances on its own, so it holds whatever the reader or the page picked.

## Don’t

- For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.
- For the full list of articles → use `article-index`.

## Related

- `article-cards` — the closing row of related articles.
- `card-grid` — the frame grid the wall of titles sits on.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `items` | `ArticleHighlightItem[]` | `[]` | false | The highlight articles in wall order, the one at the bound index (the first by default) selected on load; each is `{ key, href, image, highlightImage?, meta, title, description, readTime }`. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the button into the selected article; the button is omitted when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the wall of titles. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Advances to the next article every `autoplayInterval`, with a visible pause control, pausing under hover and keyboard focus; off under reduced motion and with one article. |
| `autoplayInterval` | `number` | `6000` | false | Milliseconds each article is held before the band advances. |
| `fill` | `boolean` | `false` | false | From `lg` up, the band fills the first viewport under the sticky site header. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `number` | `0`     | `update:modelValue` | Index of the selected article; left unbound the band starts on the first one. A click or an arrow key writes the new index back; an index past the ends is clamped to the wall. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a wall title lights, the panel cover scales up), `focus-visible` (inset ring), `selected` (`data-active` on the selected wall title)
- `data-columns` on the wall: one column per article from `lg`, three at least and five at most
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing
- Without `autoplay` the band has no timer: the selected article changes only on a click, an arrow key or a bound `modelValue`
- Autoplay: with `autoplay`, more than one article and no reduced-motion preference, the band advances (wrapping to the first) every `autoplayInterval` ms after mount and writes the index back through `v-model`; `data-autoplay` is set while it runs; an outlined `IconButton` at the band's top end pauses and resumes it, and `data-paused` marks the band while the reader holds it; a progress line (`var(--primary)`, `aria-hidden`) grows along the panel's foot from the inline start; pointer hover over the band or a `:focus-visible` element inside it pauses it, and leaving resumes it; any selection restarts the count
- Direction: `data-direction` on the panel is `forward` or `back` (from the arrow key, the autoplay step, or the index change) and drives an out-in slide of the panel's article, mirrored under `rtl`
- Fill: `data-fill` is set; from `lg` the band's height is the viewport minus `var(--layout-header-height)` and the section gaps, the panel takes the free height and its cover drops its fixed aspect; under 50 rem of viewport height the copy tightens and the deck hides
- Reflow: the hidden layout sizer is `min-w-0`, so the panel never grows past a 320 px box.

## Accessibility

- Autoplay (WCAG 2.2.2): off by default; when on, a visible pause control ("Pause rotation" / "Resume rotation") stops and resumes it for touch and screen-reader users, and it also pauses while the pointer is over the band or keyboard focus is inside it, never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and the panel is not a live region, so an advance is never announced.
- Visible focus: the panel headline link and every wall title show an inset `focus-visible` ring.
- Keyboard map: on the wall, `ArrowRight` / `ArrowDown` select the next title, `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowUp` the previous one (wrapping), `Home` the first and `End` the last; selection follows focus and only the selected title is in the tab order (roving `tabindex`).
- ARIA: the wall is a `tablist` named by `ariaLabel`, each title a `tab` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `tabpanel` labelled by the selected tab; the panel headline is an `h2` whose link covers the article; the invisible sizer is `aria-hidden` and `inert`; covers are decorative (`alt=""`). Ids come from `useId`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted` on the canvas.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every wall title is a full-cell button.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the external-link arrow does not mirror.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move between the highlighted articles, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: article titles in another script keep their own direction.

## Internationalization

| Key                     | English source    | Override prop |
| ----------------------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| `common.pauseRotation`  | `Pause rotation`  | —             |
| `common.resumeRotation` | `Resume rotation` | —             |

- Every other visible string arrives through props.
- Formatting: none; dates and read times arrive pre-formatted.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; from `lg` the panel splits cover and copy and the wall runs one column per article (three to five).
- Narrow (< `lg`): the cover stacks over the copy and the wall stacks to one column; `fill` has no effect.
- Touch: every wall title is a full-cell button; autoplay pauses only under hover or keyboard focus, and a tap selects.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the hidden sizer is `min-w-0`.

<!-- components/article-index.md -->

# Article Index

> Every article or resource of a blog or a resource hub as one ruled list, with the controls to narrow it on one row. `filters` picks the filter bar: `category-search` draws a category picker and a search field (the blog), `facets` draws one dropdown per facet — content type, category, industry — that wraps when it runs out of room (a resource hub). Each entry is a row — its cover on the left, and on the right its overline, headline, a deck and, when it has them, its writers with the byline; the row is one link named by its headline, and from `lg` up a read cue rises into its end on hover or keyboard focus. The filters combine; a facet dropdown with more than seven options gains an option search; a load-more button reveals the next page, and when nothing matches an empty state offers to clear every filter. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-index', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `toggle-group`, `select`, `input`, `avatar`, `empty-state` and `button`; the selected category, the search term, the facet selections, each dropdown's option search and the page count are local state. A row without a cover draws its client's mark in one flat ink that follows the theme.

- Import: `import ArticleIndex from '@aziontech/webkit/article-index'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ArticleIndex for the full filterable list of articles or resources; choose the filter bar with `filters`: `category-search` for the blog (category picker and search field), `facets` for a resource hub (one dropdown per facet).

## Do

- With `filters="category-search"`, list the articles newest first and file every article under at least one of `categories`; keep the category list short enough to scroll on one row.
- With `filters="facets"`, give every item a `facets` entry per facet `id` it can be filtered by (an item without one never matches a selection on that facet), and keep each facet's `options` to values some item carries.
- Set `emptyTitle` (and `emptyActionLabel`) so a reader who filters everything away gets a way back; without it the list just disappears.
- Set `leading` to the number of entries a highlight band above already shows, so they are not listed twice until the reader filters.
- Leave `rowVariant` unset to get the layout that fits the filter bar: `byline` for `category-search`, `center` for `facets`.

## Don’t

- For a card grid of customer stories with search and facets → use `story-index`.
- For a filterable list of non-article rows (jobs) → use `listing-index`.
- For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.

## Related

- `article-highlight` — the band that opens the blog above this list.
- `story-index` — the card-grid library with search and facets.
- `listing-index` — the filterable list of job rows.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline beside the controls, rendered as the band's `h2`; it also names the band. |
| `filters` | `ArticleIndexFilters` | `'category-search'` | false | Filter bar: `category-search` draws the category picker and the search field, `facets` draws one dropdown per facet. |
| `items` | `ArticleIndexItem[]` | `[]` | false | The entries, in order; each is `{ id, href, image?, mark?, meta, title, description?, authors?, byline?, categories?, facets?, target? }`. |
| `categories` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Segments of the category picker after the show-all segment (`category-search`); the picker is omitted when empty. |
| `allLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the first category segment, which shows every category (`category-search`). |
| `categoryAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the category picker (`category-search`). |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the search field (`category-search`); the field is omitted when this and `searchAriaLabel` are both empty. |
| `searchAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the search field (`category-search`). |
| `facets` | `ArticleIndexFacet[]` | `[]` | false | The facet dropdowns, in order (`facets`); each is `{ id, label, allLabel, options }`. |
| `rowLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Read cue revealed at the end of a row under hover or focus. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the load-more button under the list; without it every match is listed and no button renders. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `12` | false | Rows listed per page when `moreLabel` is set; the load-more button reveals the next page. |
| `leading` | `number` | `0` | false | Leading entries left out until a filter applies, because a band above already shows them. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the state when nothing matches; the state renders only with it. |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the empty-state headline. |
| `emptyActionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the empty-state button that clears every filter; no button renders without it. |
| `rowVariant` | `ArticleIndexRowVariant` | `undefined` | false | Row layout: `byline` pins the writers to the foot of the copy, `center` centres the copy; unset, `byline` for `category-search` and `center` for `facets`. |
| `categoryParam` | `string` | `''` | false | Name of a URL query parameter that preselects a category on load and scrolls the band into view (`category-search`); off when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a row lights and its read cue rises in), `focus-visible` (inset ring on the row, the read cue rises in)
- `data-filters` on the list mirrors `filters`; `category-search` clamps the deck to two lines in `text-body-sm`, `facets` sets it in full in `text-body-lg`
- Filtered (`category-search`): the selected category keeps the entries whose `categories` hold it, the show-all segment keeps every one; the search matches the title and the description; both combine
- Filtered (`facets`): each facet keeps the entries whose `facets[id]` holds the selected value; its `allLabel` option keeps every one; the facets combine
- Option search (`facets`): a dropdown whose `options` number more than seven renders a search field above its options; shorter lists render none
- Paged: with `moreLabel` set, the first `pageSize` matches render and the load-more button, shown while more remain, adds the next `pageSize`; changing a filter returns to the first page
- Leading: until a filter applies, the first `leading` entries are skipped
- Empty: when no entry matches, the list and the load-more button are not rendered; with `emptyTitle` set, an `EmptyState` (search icon) renders `emptyTitle` and `emptyDescription`, and an `emptyActionLabel` button clears every filter
- `data-variant` on the list mirrors the row layout: `byline` spreads the copy so the byline sits at the foot, `center` centres it
- A row with no `image` draws its `mark` (the client's logo, flattened to one ink that inverts in the dark theme); an author with an `avatar` URL shows the photo, otherwise the initials
- A row whose `target` is `_blank` opens in a new tab (with `rel="noopener"`)
- `categoryParam` (`category-search`): on mount (client only) a query value that matches one of `categories` selects it and scrolls the band into view

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the headline link draws an inset ring over the whole row; the picker, field, dropdowns and button own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the filter controls, each row and the load-more button; the category picker owns its arrow-key map and each dropdown owns its keyboard map.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by `title` (`aria-label`) when one is set, with the title as its `h2`; the toolbar is a `search` landmark; the category picker is a radio group named by `categoryAriaLabel`, the field named by `searchAriaLabel`, each dropdown trigger named by its facet `label`; the list is named by `ariaLabel`; each row is an `article` whose headline (`h3`) link covers it; the cover is decorative (`alt=""`), a client mark is named by the client, and the read cue `aria-hidden`; a `_blank` row appends the visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)` to its link; the empty state is a `status`; an option search with no match announces itself as a `status`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every row is a full-row link.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-e`, `ps-`/`pe-`); the cover cell sits at the inline start.
- Icons: the read cue's `ai-arrow-up-right` and the search glyph do not mirror; client marks never mirror.
- Keyboard: the category picker and the dropdowns own their keyboard maps under `rtl`.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source         | Override prop |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- |
| `articleIndex.search`      | `Search`               | —             |
| `articleIndex.searchFacet` | `Search {facet}`       | —             |
| `articleIndex.noMatch`     | `No results found.`    | —             |
| `common.newTab`            | `(opens in a new tab)` | —             |

- Every other string (labels, placeholders, facet labels, the empty state's copy) arrives through props.
- Formatting: none; dates arrive pre-formatted in `meta`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; from `lg` the toolbar sits on one row and each row splits cover and copy 2:5.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): the toolbar stacks; the category picker scrolls sideways at full label width, the facet dropdowns stack at full width; each row stacks its cover above the copy; the read cue is hidden.
- Touch: every row is a full-row link; the read cue is a hover/focus extra, never the only affordance.
- Reflow: no horizontal page scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; only the category picker scrolls inside its own box, and from `sm` the facet dropdowns wrap.

<!-- components/capability-grid.md -->

# Capability Grid

> A framed grid of claims or links under an optional section title: each cell is a `FeatureItem` (optional glyph, heading, sentence) with optional bullet points, three or four to a row, and an item with an `href` turns its whole cell into a link to that page. It is the one marketing grid of claims or links: it replaces `'use-case-links'`, `'resource-grid'` and `'content-columns'`. From the design sample's site `CapabilityGrid`. Use CapabilityGrid for any grid of claims or links on a marketing page; icons and per-item links are optional.

- Import: `import CapabilityGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/capability-grid'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A product page listing what the product does, three or six at a time.
- Use cases or resources that each link to their own page: give each item an `href` (and no `icon` for a resource list).
- A bare grid (no title) under a band that already has its heading.

## Do

- Three or six items at three columns, four or eight at four, so rows stay full.
- Keep points to three short lines.
- Give either every item an `href` or none, so the grid reads as one kind of cell; do not combine `points` with an `href` (the whole cell is the link).
- Set `titleVariant: 'start'` for a band whose header sits at the start edge (the Partners page's "Why you should be a partner"); the grid keeps its title, so each capability stays an `h3`. Never wrap a bare grid in `SectionModule` to move the title: the capability headings rise to `h2` and the outline breaks.

## Don’t

- For capabilities with art — use `FeatureTiles` or `BentoGrid`.
- For use cases whose band title sits in the first grid cell with one action — use `CustomerUseCases`.
- For cells that each carry their own action or copy button — use `FeatureWidgets`.

## Related

- FeatureItem`, `CardGrid`, `RegistrationFrame`, `SectionTitle` — the parts.
- FeatureTiles` — tiles with illustrations.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the grid, rendered as the band `h2`; without it the grid is bare and each capability heading is an `h2`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences under the title. |
| `items` | `CapabilityGridItem[]` | `[]` | false | The capabilities, in order; each is `{ title, description, icon?, points?, href? }`; an item with `href` links its whole cell to that page. The band renders nothing when empty. |
| `columns` | `CapabilityGridColumns` | `3` | false | Capabilities per row from the large breakpoint up. |
| `primaryAction` | `CapabilityGridAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the section title, `secondary`; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `CapabilityGridAction` | `undefined` | false | Second button under the section title, `outline`; same shape. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `titleVariant` | `SectionTitleVariant` | `'center'` | false | Layout of the section title: `center` stacks and centers it, `start` stacks it at the start edge, `split` sets the headline and its description in two columns. |

## States

- Renders nothing without items.
- Heading level drops to `h3` under a title and rises to `h2` without one.
- An item with `href` renders its heading as a link that covers the cell.
- `titleVariant` is passed to the section title as its `variant`; it has no effect on a bare grid.

## Accessibility

- A `section` named by its title; headings nest under it.
- Points are a real list.
- Glyphs are decorative (from `FeatureItem`).
- A linked cell is one link named by its heading (from `FeatureItem`), with a visible focus ring.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-*`, `border-e`, `ms-*`).
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- One column on phones, two on medium, `columns` from large (from `CardGrid`).
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CapabilityGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/capability-grid'

  const items = [
    {
      icon: 'ai ai-bolt',
      title: 'Functions',
      description: 'Run JavaScript and WebAssembly close to every user.'
    },
    {
      icon: 'ai ai-database',
      title: 'Object Storage',
      description: 'Keep files where they are read, with no egress to plan for.'
    },
    {
      icon: 'ai ai-shield',
      title: 'Firewall',
      description: 'Stop bots and attacks before they reach your origin.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <CapabilityGrid
    eyebrow="Platform"
    title="Everything an application needs, in one place"
    description="Compute, storage and security that deploy together."
    :items="items"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Explore the platform', href: '/platform', trailing: true }"
  />
</template>
```
