<!-- components/card-carousel.md -->

# Card Carousel

> The titled card-carousel band of a product or solution page: a section title on the start of the row with the previous/next controls at its end, over a horizontally scrolling track of standalone cards. Each card is an optional overline (the category), a heading, a sentence and, when it links somewhere, a mono link label closed by an arrow ("See example", "See solution"). The band answers "see how to use", "industries", "orchestration with control" on azion.com product pages, where the cases outnumber the row. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'card-carousel', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below. It composes `carousel` (`variant="cards"`, its `header` slot, `size="medium"` items and its step controls), `section-title` and `eyebrow`, and owns only the card's inner layout.

- Import: `import CardCarousel from '@aziontech/webkit/card-carousel'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CardCarousel for four or more marketing cards the reader steps through.
- Four or more cases, industries or examples of equal weight that do not all need to be seen: the reader steps through them.
- When each case is a short card (overline, heading, one or two sentences) that may link to its own page or example.

## Do

- Give the band a `title`; its arrows sit on the title row, and the title names the row for assistive technology.
- Keep each card to a heading and one or two sentences, so the row height stays even.
- Use `eyebrow` on every card or on none; a row where some cards carry an overline reads as ragged.
- Give every card a `linkLabel` when every card has an `href`, and none when none does. The label is a visual cue; the card heading is the link.
- Pass as many cards as the content has; the track scrolls, so the count never has to fill the row.

## Don’t

- When every case must be visible, or there are three or six of equal weight → use `capability-grid` (linked grid) or `customer-use-cases` (grid with one action).
- For a quote or testimonial row → use `client-quotes`.
- For numbered principles pinned while the page scrolls → use `process-scroll` with `pinned`.
- For articles with images → use `article-cards`.

## Related

- `carousel` — the primitive this band composes; reach for it directly only for a non-card row.
- `capability-grid` — the same content as a static, fully visible grid.
- `process-scroll` — numbered dark cards, pinned on scroll with `pinned`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the band title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` at the start of the row the step controls end; the band renders no title when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `CardCarouselItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cards, in order; each is `{ eyebrow?, title, description, href?, linkLabel? }`, and a card with `href` links to it. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the card row; defaults to the title. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; each linked card has `hover` (the arrow nudges toward the end edge, the label brightens) and `focus-visible` (an inset ring on the whole card).
- Empty: with no `items` the band renders nothing — no title, no controls.
- Untitled: with no `title` the controls sit alone at the start of the row (the carousel's own layout) and the row is named by `ariaLabel` only.
- Unlinked card: without `href` the card is a plain card with no hover state and no link label.
- The step controls carry `disabled` at each end of the track, from the carousel; a row that fits shows both disabled.
- `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`: the band cannot be in these states; it renders static content from props.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: the WAI-ARIA APG carousel (`aria-roledescription="carousel"`, named region) from `carousel`; the band root is a plain container so the row is the one named region, named by `ariaLabel` or the title.
- Outline: the title is the section title's `h2`; each card heading is an `h3`.
- Links: on a linked card the `h3` holds the anchor, so the link's name is the card title; a stretched `::after` makes the whole card its hit area. The link label and its arrow are `aria-hidden` decoration.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the previous control, the next control, the track (arrow keys scroll it natively) and each card link in order; `Enter` / `Space` on a control steps one card; `Enter` on a card link follows it. A card that scrolls into focus is brought into view by the browser.
- Visible focus: card links draw `focus-visible:after:ring-2 focus-visible:after:ring-inset focus-visible:after:ring-(--ring-color)` around the whole card; the controls and track carry the carousel's ring.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: copy is `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface)`; the link label is `var(--text-muted)` at rest; the arrow is `var(--text-primary)` (≥3:1 as a graphic).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition; the track never auto-advances (WCAG 2.2.2 does not apply).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the controls are 40×40; a card link spans its whole card.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the title row keeps the title at the start edge and the controls at the end edge.
- Icons: the link arrow (`ai ai-arrow-right`) mirrors under `rtl:-scale-x-100` and its hover nudge runs toward the end edge (`rtl:group-hover/card:-translate-x-0.5`); the carousel's chevrons mirror in `carousel`.
- Keyboard: the next control steps toward the end edge in both directions (`carousel`).
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props in the page's language. The control names and the `carousel` role description come from `carousel`'s own locale group (en, pt-BR, es).
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the cards have a fixed width (`size="medium"`, `var(--container-sm)`) and the track scrolls.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): each card is 85% of the viewport wide, so one card fills a phone and the next peeks; the title wraps inside its cell while the controls stay on its row.
- Touch: the track swipes natively; the hover nudge is decoration only, and every card stays a full-card link on touch.
- Reflow: the page never scrolls sideways at 320 px; only the track does, which is the component's purpose (WCAG 1.4.10 exception for a carousel).

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/cli-terminal.md -->

# Cli Terminal

> The Azion CLI band of a product page: a horizontal section title with one outlined button, over a terminal on the pixelate texture that runs off the frame's bottom rule. The terminal is either a recorded Azion CLI session typed live by a `console-mockup` (`script`), in a fixed-height stage that rises in when it scrolls into view, or a static session whose lines enter one after another (`session`). It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'cli-terminal', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `registration-frame`, `texture`, `console-mockup` and `code-block`.

- Import: `import CliTerminal from '@aziontech/webkit/cli-terminal'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CliTerminal only on marketing pages for a full-width terminal session.
- To close a product argument on how little it takes to ship from the terminal, like Functions and Workloads.

## Do

- Keep the session to a few commands and their output; comment the output lines so the copied text still runs.
- Name the copy button with `copyAriaLabel` so a screen reader says what it copies.
- Prefer `script` on a product page: `start` types the first-project session, `deploy` the deploy session. Use `session` for a command set the recordings do not cover.
- Set `anchor` when a hero button scrolls to this band.

## Don’t

- For a config file or handler beside the claim → use `media-split-section` with `codeTabs`.
- For several capabilities, each with its own file → use `feature-scroll` with code items.

## Related

- `code-block` — the terminal session the band shows.
- `media-split-section` — the sibling band with the sample (`codeTabs`) beside the copy.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence beside the headline. |
| `script` | `CliTerminalScript` | `undefined` | false | Recorded Azion CLI session the terminal types live: `start` or `deploy`; wins over `session`. |
| `session` | `string` | `''` | false | The terminal session shown under the header when no `script` is set, commands and their output verbatim, highlighted as bash; the band renders nothing when neither is set. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the session's copy button; empty keeps the code block's own. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Outlined button in the section title; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the copy button and the button own their hover and focus states
- Empty: when neither `script` nor `session` is set the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- `script` draws the `console-mockup` `cli-terminal-start` or `cli-terminal-deploy` in a stage 18rem tall (24rem from `md` up); `data-entered` is set on the stage the first time a fifth of it is on screen, and the stage rises, grows and fades in. The widget types its session while on screen and shows its finished state under reduced motion (owned by `console-mockup`). Without `script` the `session` renders as a `code-block`
- The header renders only when `title` is set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `code-block` (copy button) and `button`; the `script` terminal has no focusable parts.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the button and the copy button; `Enter` follows the button.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; the copy button is named by `copyAriaLabel`; the `script` terminal is an `aria-hidden` picture of the console (owned by `console-mockup`), so the headline carries the meaning.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `code-block` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` — the `script` stage's entrance is skipped under reduced motion and the stage is drawn at rest; the session's line entrance is owned by `code-block` and draws at once under reduced motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the large button.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CliTerminal from '@aziontech/webkit/cli-terminal'

  const session =
    'azion link --preset javascript --name auth-handler --auto\n# Project successfully configured\n\nazion deploy --auto\n# Upload completed successfully!\n# Your Application was deployed successfully\n# Domain: https://k7q2fmx4ze.map.azionedge.net\n\ncurl https://k7q2fmx4ze.map.azionedge.net/\n# Hello World'

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Install the CLI',
    href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/azion-cli/overview/',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <CliTerminal
    eyebrow="Azion CLI"
    title="Deploy your first function in two commands"
    description="Link a project, deploy it, and curl the domain the CLI hands back. Builds run on your machine with --local, or on Azion."
    :session="session"
    copy-aria-label="Copy the deploy session"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

# Client Mosaic

> The client mosaic: a framed bento grid of customer cells where a story cell carries a photograph, the client's mark, one line of its result and a "read the case study" link, and a mark cell carries only the client's linked logo on a chosen fill. With `stories` and `logos` the layout is derived from the data: the first story spans two columns and two rows, every other story one column and two rows, every mark one cell. With `cells` the page places story and mark cells in one ordered list, each with its own column and row span, so stories and marks interleave as on the home page. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-mosaic', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `bento-grid`, `logo` and `link`.

- Import: `import ClientMosaic from '@aziontech/webkit/client-mosaic'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the home page, to show the best customer stories and a wall of marks in one band.

## Do

- Two stories and six marks fill the four-column grid exactly.
- Use `cells` when the order matters (a story between marks, a tall story at the end of a row): give each cell its `span` and `rows` (`'1'` or `'2'`) and make the spans add up to full rows of four.
- Pick `fill` and `logoTreatment` together: a `knockout` mark reads on `white` or `primary`, a `monochrome` one on `canvas` or `surface`. Left unset, a mark on `white` or `primary` takes `knockout` and every other mark `monochrome`.
- Set `stacked` on a cell whose mark is a stacked lockup (squarer than a wordmark) so it draws one step taller.
- A story without a `photo` sits on its fill; keep photos for the stories that have one.

## Don’t

- For three equal story columns → use `client-story-columns`.
- For a plain wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-section`.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the grid the cells are laid in.
- `client-story-columns` — the three-column sibling with brand-coloured faces.
- `logo` — draws every client mark in the ink its fill needs.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the grid. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the link under every story. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `stories` | `ClientMosaicStory[]` | `[]` | false | The story cells, in order; each is `{ logo, logoAlt, photo?, text, href, fill?, logoTreatment? }`. The first spans two columns and two rows, the rest one column and two rows. |
| `logos` | `ClientMosaicLogo[]` | `[]` | false | The mark cells, in order; each is `{ logo, logoAlt, href, fill?, logoTreatment? }` where `fill` is `'canvas'`, `'surface'`, `'white'` or `'primary'` and `logoTreatment` is `'color'`, `'monochrome'` or `'knockout'` (the shared `LogoTreatment`). |
| `cells` | `ClientMosaicCell[]` | `[]` | false | The cells in placement order, story and mark cells interleaved; each is `{ logo, logoAlt, href, text?, photo?, span?, rows?, fill?, logoTreatment?, stacked? }` where a cell with `text` is a story cell, `span` and `rows` are `'1'` (default) or `'2'`, and `fill` defaults to `canvas`. When set it replaces `stories` and `logos`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on each cell
- `data-cell` (`story` or `logo`), `data-span` and `data-rows` on every grid cell; `data-fill` on every cell face drives its fill; every mark is a `Logo` with `data-treatment` and `data-variant` for its ink and `data-stacked` for a stacked lockup; `data-lead` sets the larger text of the first story (from `stories`) or of a story spanning two columns (from `cells`)
- Empty: when `cells`, `stories` and `logos` are all empty the band renders nothing
- Not applicable: `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every mark cell is a link with `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`; the story link is a `link` with its own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between mark links and story links; `Enter` follows.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by `ariaLabel`; the photo of a story is decorative (`alt=""`, `aria-hidden`); every mark is a `Logo` (`role="img"`) named by `logoAlt`; the story text is a paragraph and its link is named by `linkLabel`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): story text `var(--text-default)` over the canvas gradient; marks are inked to their fill through `logoTreatment`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the fill transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each mark cell is a full grid cell.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the grid follows the reading direction (`bento-grid`); the story cell uses logical alignment (`items-start`, `self-start`).
- Icons: the story link's chevron is mirrored by `link`; logos are never mirrored.
- Keyboard: `Tab` order follows the placement order.
- User data: none beyond the client names, which are images named by `logoAlt`.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: the story lines, the client names and `linkLabel` are content the page passes.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `bento-grid` sets four columns, two below `md`.
- Narrow: a two-column span fills the phone row; cells keep a minimum height of `clamp(180px, 18vw, 240px)`.
- Touch: every mark cell is a full-cell link; story links are `link` targets.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

<!-- components/client-quotes.md -->

# Client Quotes

> The client-stories band: a framed `quote-tabs` carousel of customer quotes, each signed by its author and marked by the client's logo, with one call to action under it. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-quotes', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `quote-tabs` and `button`.

- Import: `import ClientQuotes from '@aziontech/webkit/client-quotes'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → the section (`client-quotes`). Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the primitive (`quote-tabs`).
- Use ClientQuotes for a band of customer quotes the reader browses by client.
- To let several customers speak in turn, one at a time, near the end of a page's argument.

## Do

- Three to six items; the tabs need room for each client's mark.
- Give each item either a registry `mark` or a `logo` URL with `clientName`, not both.
- On azion.com the client wall is in each brand's colours, not one ink: give each client its logo file from the package, `import gpa from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/gpa-extended-color.svg'`, then `logo: gpa`. On the dark site use `-extended-color.svg` where the colour logo reads on black (GPA, Zoop, HeroSpark, Magalu) and `-extended-reversed.svg` where the colour logo has dark lettering (Axur, Contabilizei, Dafiti, Global Fashion Group as `gfg`); on a light page use `-extended-color.svg`. A registry `mark` (one ink, follows the theme) is for a client that ships no logo file. `catalog.json` lists every file under `imports` with `"kind": "asset"`.
- Every item needs its quotation (`text`): a card is a tab that features it, and an item without one is skipped. Do not invent a quotation to fill the wall; list the clients you have quotes for, or use `logo-wall-section` for one quotation beside a logo wall.
- The band advances on a timer like azion.com's. Set `:autoplay="false"` when the page must hold one quote (a still capture, a page with other moving content), and bind `v-model` (the selected index) to open on a quote other than the first; never wrap or re-time the band yourself.

## Don’t

- For one quote beside a logo wall → use `logo-wall-section`.
- For a scrolling strip of analyst recognitions → use `recognition-marquee`.

## Related

- `quote-tabs` — the tabbed quote carousel this band frames.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the quote carousel. |
| `items` | `ClientQuotesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The quotes, in order; each is `{ text, name?, jobTitle?, mark?, logo?, clientName?, photo? }` where `mark` is a registry mark name and `logo` a mark URL named by `clientName`. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Button under the quotes; `{ label, href, trailing? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Advances to the next quote on a timer, as `quote-tabs` does, with its visible pause control; pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion. |
| `autoplayInterval` | `number` | `5000` | false | Milliseconds each quote is held before the band advances. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Marquee` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `number` | `0`     | `update:modelValue` | Index of the selected quote, passed through to `quote-tabs`; left unbound the band starts on the first quote. A click, an arrow key or the timer writes the new index back. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when no item carries `text` the band renders nothing; an item without `text` is skipped, and the `v-model` index counts the quotes that remain
- The active quote, its progress and the tab keyboard model belong to `quote-tabs`; `autoplay`, `autoplayInterval` and `v-model` are passed straight through to it

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed components.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each link or button; `Enter` follows it.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every affordance is a large `button` or spans its cell.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the carousel is `quote-tabs`' own labelled region (`ariaLabel`), so no second landmark is added.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the tab transition belongs to `quote-tabs`; this band adds no motion.

<!-- components/client-story-columns.md -->

# Client Story Columns

> Three featured success stories side by side: each column is a client's mark on a face painted in the client's own brand colour, over a one-line story that links to the case. With `reveal="hover"` each column is one card instead: the client's reversed logo on its brand face, which opens while hovered or focused to reveal the story line and a "Read story" cue, the whole card linking to the case; below the large breakpoint those cards stack and stay open. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-story-columns', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame` and `logo-wall`. The retired `'customer-spotlight'` `_id` resolves here with `reveal: 'hover'`.

- Import: `import ClientStoryColumns from '@aziontech/webkit/client-story-columns'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ClientStoryColumns for three or four client cards in brand colours linking to case studies; `reveal="hover"` shows the story on hover.

## Do

- Three cells for `reveal="always"` (the grid is three columns from the large breakpoint); three or four for `reveal="hover"`, which shares the row between them.
- With `reveal="hover"` use the client's reversed (white) logo and one sentence per story; `logoWidth` sizes the mark as a share of the card (default `35%`).
- Leave `brand` out for a client the client registry knows (`clientBrand(name)` from `@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`): the face reads its colours, and its ink, by `name`. Add a missing client to the registry rather than writing its hex colours into the page.
- Pass `brand` only for a one-off client the registry does not carry: `base` and `glow` may be any CSS colour, and `ink` is `'dark'` when the face is light enough that the link text must be dark. A cell with neither paints a black face.

## Don’t

- For a bento of client stories with photos and logos → use `client-mosaic`.
- For a quotation → use `client-quotes` or `logo-wall-section` `variant="quote"`.

## Related

- `client-mosaic` — the bento sibling.
- `logo-wall` — the single-mark wall each column's face is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of stories. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label the mark face reveals on hover and the link's accessible name. |
| `cells` | `ClientStoryColumnsCell[]` | `[]` | false | The stories, in order; each is `{ name, logo, href, story, brand?, logoTreatment?, logoWidth? }` where `brand` is `{ base, glow, ink? }` (CSS colours painting the face, `ink` `'dark'` or `'light'`) and defaults to the client registry's colours for `name`, `logoTreatment` is `'color'`, `'monochrome'` or `'knockout'` (the shared `LogoTreatment`), and `logoWidth` (read by `reveal="hover"`) sizes the mark as a share of the card. |
| `reveal` | `ClientStoryColumnsReveal` | `'always'` | false | When the story shows: `always` under each face, or `hover`, where each card opens to reveal it while hovered or focused and stays open below the large breakpoint. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` on each column (the face reveals the link line, the story fill rises)
- The face colours are bound as the `--wall-face` and `--wall-ink` custom properties from `brand`, or from the client registry by `name` when `brand` is left out; `data-treatment` on every mark drives its ink
- `reveal="hover"`: each list item carries `data-state=open|closed`; one card is open at a time on large screens, every card is open below the large breakpoint
- Empty: when `cells` is empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the mark link is `logo-wall`'s, with its ring; the story panel is a duplicate link hidden from the tab order and from assistive technology.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the three mark links; `Enter` follows.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>`; the grid is a list named by `ariaLabel` whose items are the columns; each mark carries the client `name` as `alt`; the story panel is `aria-hidden` with `tabindex="-1"` so the case is reachable once.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the link line ink follows `brand.ink`; the story text is `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)`.
- `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` on the hover fill.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each mark face spans its column.
- `reveal="hover"`: the list carries the one accessible name (`ariaLabel`, else the built-in "Customer stories"); each card is one link named "<link label>, <client>: <story>", so its logo is decorative (`alt=""`); focus opens the card the same way hover does and the ring is drawn inside the card; `ai-arrow-up-right` mirrors under right-to-left.

## Internationalization

| Key                        | English source     | Override prop                          |
| -------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `clientStoryColumns.list`  | `Customer stories` | `ariaLabel` (read by `reveal="hover"`) |
| `clientStoryColumns.story` | `Read story`       | `linkLabel` (read by `reveal="hover"`) |

<!-- components/closing-call-to-action.md -->

# Closing Call To Action

> The last ask at the end of a landing page, followed by a hatched closing frame with no rules of its own, because the site footer under it opens with one. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'closing-call-to-action', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `call-to-action`, `button`, `registration-frame` and `texture`. `variant` picks the layout only: `split` sets the headline and the primary action in a raised lead cell beside an aside cell carrying the description and the secondary action, over a tall closing frame; `panel` sets the copy and its actions on one surface, over a short closing frame; `primary` is the loud close, one centred ask on the canvas under a pixelated texture whose waves keep travelling, over a tall closing frame. All three take the same copy, the same two actions and an optional copyable shell `command` set before the actions. `frame` draws the closing frame alone, with no ask: the close of a page whose last band already carries its own action. `hatch` turns the closing frame off when another closing band stacks directly below and draws the shared one (`site-page` sets it for stacked closings). In `primary`, `audiences` turns the ask into a switch between ways in (a person or an agent): each audience swaps in its own copyable line and actions, and a typed line (`typedLead` + `typedWords`) loops under them; the switch block loads on demand, only when `audiences` is set.

- Import: `import ClosingCallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ClosingCallToAction for the last band before the site footer that asks for one action, with links or a command.
- Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → this section. Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the `call-to-action` primitive.
- In `primary` with `audiences`, to close a page whose reader may be a person or an agent, each with its own way in.
- To close a solution or product page on its one or two asks (`split`), or a page such as Careers on one action (`panel`), or a page that ends on its one loud ask (`primary`).

## Do

- Place it last on the page, right above `site-footer`, after a hatched `section-gap`. It draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column: no trailing `SectionGap` and no closing `RegistrationFrame` + `Texture` (the `shell/site` close is for a page that ends on any other band). `webkit/no-gap-after-closing-section` flags the doubled close.
- Set `anchor: 'contact'` so the page's contact links scroll to the close.
- Use `variant: 'frame'` (no copy) to close a page that ends on a band with its own actions (a listing, a legal page); `site-page` draws no gap before it.
- Turn `hatch` off only on a closing band that another closing band follows directly; the last one keeps the frame.
- Give `command` a short shell line (`npm create azion@latest`); it is copied as written and reads as a command, with the `$` prompt.
- Give `audiences` two or more entries so the switch renders; set `audiencesAriaLabel` and `lineAriaLabel` so the switch and the copyable field are named. With `audiences` set, `description` is the closing sentence under the typed line, and `command` and the two actions are not drawn.
- Mark a command line with `copy.shell` so it draws the `$` prompt; leave a prompt meant for an agent bare.
- In `split`, keep `title` and `titleMuted` to one short line each; `panel` and `primary` do not draw `titleMuted`, and `primary` does not draw `eyebrow`.

## Don’t

- For a newsletter sign-up close → use `newsletter-section`.
- For a close that lists deployable templates → use `template-gallery` with `closing`.
- For an ask in the middle of a page → compose `call-to-action` directly.

## Related

- `call-to-action` — the framed band this section renders.
- `newsletter-section` — the closing band whose ask is a subscribe form.
- `template-gallery` — with `closing`, the closing band that lists deployable templates.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `ClosingCallToActionVariant` | `'split'` | false | Layout of the band: `split` is a raised lead cell beside an aside cell over a tall closing frame, `panel` one surface over a short closing frame, `primary` a centred ask under a pixelated texture over a tall closing frame, `frame` the tall closing frame alone. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline; not drawn in `primary`. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the call to action as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `titleMuted` | `string` | `''` | false | Second line of the headline in muted ink; drawn in `split` only. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence: in the aside cell in `split`, under the headline in `panel`. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | The white button of the band, under the headline in `split`; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | The outlined button of the band, in the aside cell in `split` and beside the primary one in `panel` and `primary`; `{ label, href, trailing? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `command` | `string` | `''` | false | Shell command on a copyable line before the actions, copied as written; drawn in `split`, `panel` and `primary`. |
| `hatch` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the hatched closing frame under the band; turn it off when another closing band stacks directly below and draws the shared frame. |
| `audiences` | `ClosingCallToActionAudience[]` | `[]` | false | The ways in of the `primary` close, in switch order; each is `{ value, label, copy?, actions? }` (`copy` is `{ label, text, shell? }`, `shell` drawing the `$` prompt; an action is `{ label, href, variant?, trailing? }`) and the first one opens. Replaces the command and the two actions; the switch renders only with two or more. |
| `typedLead` | `string` | `''` | false | Fixed opening of the typed line under the audiences, before the typed word. |
| `typedWords` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Words typed, held, erased and typed again in order after `typedLead`; the typed line renders only with `audiences` and words. |
| `audiencesAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the audience switch. |
| `lineAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the read-only field that shows an audience's copyable line. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop and drives the call-to-action layout and the closing frame height
- `primary`: the call to action takes its `primary` register with a pixelated `texture` in its `background` slot; its waves stop under reduced motion (owned by `texture`)
- `frame`: only the tall closing frame renders, whatever the copy; `hatch` does not apply
- `hatch` off: the band renders without its closing frame
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root (except in `frame`)
- Each action and the command line render only when given
- `audiences` (in `primary`): picking an audience swaps the copyable line and the actions; the swapped row sits in a polite live region and fades in. After mount the typed words are typed (90 ms a character), held (1.8 s), erased (45 ms a character) and the next one typed (after 270 ms), in a loop; the timer is cleared on scope dispose. Under reduced motion every word shows at once, joined by commas, and the cursor is hidden

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed buttons.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the command line and its copy button, then the primary and the secondary action; `Enter` follows an action. With `audiences`, `Tab` reaches the switch (arrow keys move it, owned by `toggle-group`), the copy button and each action.
- With `audiences`: the switch is a `radiogroup` named by `audiencesAriaLabel`; the swapped row is `aria-live="polite"`; the read-only field is named by `lineAriaLabel` and the copy button by the audience's `copy.label`. The typed line reads its whole sentence from a visually hidden copy while the animated letters are `aria-hidden`.
- ARIA: the `call-to-action` renders the band's `<section>` named by its title; the root is a plain `div` so the band has one landmark. The closing frame is decorative.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `call-to-action` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — see the Motion table; under reduced motion nothing types or blinks, and the texture and the buttons carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the actions are large buttons.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-px` on the typed-line cursor); the split cells mirror as `call-to-action` lays them out.
- Icons: the trailing chevron on an action mirrors with `button`; the texture is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: the audience switch's arrow keys follow the direction (owned by `toggle-group`); nothing else handles arrows.
- User data: the command line renders `dir="ltr"` (owned by `copy-command`).

## Internationalization

No built-in strings of its own: every visible text is a prop from the page JSON, including the switch, field and copy-button names of `audiences` (`audiencesAriaLabel`, `lineAriaLabel`, `copy.label`). The command line's field and copy button names come from `copy-command` (`copyCommand.command`, `copyCommand.copyCommand`).

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `call-to-action` stacks the split cells below `lg`.
- Narrow (below `lg`): the lead and aside cells stack; the command line takes the full width above the actions.
- Touch: the actions are large buttons and the copy button is large; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; a long command scrolls inside its field.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ClosingCallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action'

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Start for free',
    href: 'https://console.azion.com/signup?tck=build_cta'
  }

  const secondaryAction = {
    label: 'Talk to a specialist',
    href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/contact/',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ClosingCallToAction
    variant="split"
    anchor="contact"
    eyebrow="Build"
    title="Build once."
    title-muted="Run everywhere."
    description="Get a faster path to launch, lower latency, and less infrastructure overhead."
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
    :secondary-action="secondaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/competitor-comparison.md -->

# Competitor Comparison

> The capability-by-capability comparison of Azion with one competitor on a migration landing page: a left section title over a framed table whose header row (the capability column, the Azion brand and the competitor logo) stays pinned while the page scrolls. Each category opens with a heading row; each cell is a support glyph — full, partial or none — named by a tooltip and by screen-reader text, and a capability with a definition carries an info button that opens it in a popover. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'competitor-comparison', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `brand`, `popover`, `icon-button` and `tooltip`.

- Import: `import CompetitorComparison from '@aziontech/webkit/competitor-comparison'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CompetitorComparison to compare Azion with one competitor, on an "Azion vs X" page, across a few categories of capabilities.

## Do

- Give every row a `definition`; the info popover is where a reader learns what the capability means.
- Pass the competitor's entry from `@aziontech/webkit/assets/competitor-registry` (`competitor('Akamai')`): its `logo` and `logoLight` render on first paint, server render included.
- With only a `name`, the band looks the name up in the competitor registry once the page is interactive (the registry loads on demand, outside the band's bundle) and shows the name as text until then, or for a platform the registry does not hold.
- For a platform outside the registry, ship both `competitor.logo` (dark theme) and `competitor.logoLight` (light theme), or one file with its `artwork`.
- Set `anchor` when a page links to the table (`#compare`).
- Keep `caption` equal to the title; it is the table's accessible name.

## Don’t

- To compare Azion's own plans or support tiers → use `plan-comparison`.
- For price cards with a billing-period toggle → use `pricing-plans`.

## Related

- `plan-comparison` — the plan-by-plan matrix of Pricing.
- `tooltip` — names each support glyph on hover and focus.
- `logo` — draws the competitor's mark right on both themes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2` and naming the band; no header renders when empty. |
| `caption` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader caption naming the table. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the capability column. |
| `fullLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of a full-support cell. |
| `partialLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of a partial-support cell. |
| `noneLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of an unsupported cell. |
| `competitor` | `CompetitorComparisonCompetitor` | `—` | true | The platform compared with Azion; `{ name, logo?, logoLight?, artwork? }` where `logo` is the dark-theme file and `logoLight` the light-theme one. With only a `name`, the logo is taken from the competitor registry once the page is interactive, and the name is the column head until then or when the registry has no entry. |
| `groups` | `CompetitorComparisonGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The categories, in order; each is `{ title, rows }` and a row is `{ capability, definition?, azion?, competitor? }` with each level `full`, `partial` or `none` (missing reads as `none`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- A support cell is one of `full`, `partial` or `none`, mirrored on the glyph's `data-support`
- The competitor head is a `Logo` (`data-testid="competitor-comparison__competitor-logo"`) whose `data-route` is `pair` (light/dark files), `single` (one file) or `wordmark` (the name as text: no logo and no registry entry, or before the registry loads)
- Not applicable: `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed` (the popovers own their open state)
- Empty: when `groups` is empty the band renders nothing but its root — no header, no table

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `icon-button` and `tooltip` triggers.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each definition's info button; `Enter` / `Space` opens its popover and `Esc` closes it (owned by `popover`).
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the table carries a `caption`, `scope="col"` heads, a `scope="colgroup"` head per category and a `scope="row"` head per capability, so each value is announced with its row and column. The glyphs are `aria-hidden` and every cell carries its level as `sr-only` text; the competitor logo is a `Logo` named by the platform, inside a head cell that carries the same name.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text and glyph colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the popover and tooltip carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the info button is a small `icon-button`, a secondary affordance next to the capability name.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-s`, `ps-`/`pe-`); the Azion and competitor columns follow the reading direction.
- Icons: the support glyphs and the info glyph are not mirrored; logos are never mirrored.
- Keyboard: `Tab` order follows the DOM.
- User data: the competitor name drawn as a wordmark is wrapped in `dir="auto"` by `Logo`.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source       | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------- |
| `competitorComparison.about` | `About {capability}` | —             |

- The column and level labels (`columnLabel`, `fullLabel`, `partialLabel`, `noneLabel`), the caption and every capability are content the page passes.
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the head row's logos step up from 12 px to 16 px (`sm`) and 24 px (`md`).
- Narrow: the capability column keeps its text, the two platform columns narrow to their glyphs.
- Touch: the info button is a small `icon-button`, a secondary affordance next to the capability name.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the head row stays pinned under the site header.

<!-- components/compliance-logos.md -->

# Compliance Logos

> The compliance band: a framed media split whose copy states the certifications and whose media is a frame grid of badges, each a picture over a check-marked pill, closed by a "see more" cell. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'compliance-logos', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `media-split` and `card-grid`.

- Import: `import ComplianceLogos from '@aziontech/webkit/compliance-logos'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On security, enterprise or pricing pages, to list the certifications and link to the compliance page.

## Do

- Four or five certifications plus the link cell fill two rows of three.
- Give every badge an `alt` naming the certification; the pill repeats it for sighted readers.

## Don’t

- For client logos → use `logo-wall-section` or `client-mosaic`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the copy-beside-media band this section renders through.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the badge list. |
| `certifications` | `ComplianceLogosCertification[]` | `[]` | false | The badges, in order; each is `{ label, badge, alt }` where `badge` is the picture URL and `label` the pill text. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | The closing "see more" cell; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on the see-more cell
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing; when `certifications` is empty the media holds only the see-more cell, if any

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the see-more cell carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the see-more link; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the named landmark is `media-split`'s own section (labelled by `title`), so no second landmark is added; the badge grid is a list (`role="list"` named by `ariaLabel`) of list items; each badge image carries its `alt`; the check bubble and chevron are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): pill `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface-raised)`; see-more `var(--text-muted)` rising to `var(--text-default)` on hover.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on both transitions above.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the see-more cell is a full grid cell.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the "more" chevron mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`) and its hover nudge moves toward the end edge.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every visible and announced text is a prop from the page JSON.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `media-split` stacks the copy over the grid below its breakpoint.
- Narrow (below `md`): the badge grid drops from three columns to two.
- Touch: the see-more cell is a full grid cell; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ccpaSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/ccpa-symbol-color.svg'
  import gdprSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/gdpr-symbol-color.svg'
  import lgpdSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/lgpd-symbol-color.svg'
  import pciDssSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/pci-dss-symbol-color.svg'
  import socSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/soc-symbol-color.svg'
  import ComplianceLogos from '@aziontech/webkit/compliance-logos'
</script>

<template>
  <ComplianceLogos
    eyebrow="Compliance"
    title="Meet your compliance requirements"
    description="Azion's certifications help customers and global partners meet a wide range of compliance requirements."
    aria-label="Compliance certifications"
    :certifications="[
      {
        label: 'SOC 2 & 3',
        badge: socSymbolColor,
        alt: 'AICPA SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 badge'
      },
      {
        label: 'PCI DSS',
        badge: pciDssSymbolColor,
        alt: 'PCI DSS badge'
      },
      {
        label: 'LGPD',
        badge: lgpdSymbolColor,
        alt: 'LGPD badge'
      },
      {
        label: 'GDPR',
        badge: gdprSymbolColor,
        alt: 'GDPR badge'
      },
      {
        label: 'CCPA',
        badge: ccpaSymbolColor,
        alt: 'CCPA badge'
      }
```

<!-- components/console-showcase.md -->

# Console Showcase

> A full-width framed panel that presents a product scene (a console mock or a diagram) under a section title, on a texture, with optional tabs that each play one beat of the scene. The scene is a slot: the page passes a `ConsoleMockup` or a diagram and reads the selected tab from the slot scope. In `console` variant the scene keeps a 1.9:1 aspect and can be cropped and faded at the bottom. From the design sample's site `ConsoleShowcase`.

- Import: `import ConsoleShowcase from '@aziontech/webkit/console-showcase'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ConsoleShowcase for a marketing band that plays a product scene under a section title.
- Showing the product itself on a landing page.
- A tour of three or four views of one screen.

## Do

- Two to four tabs, each a different view, labelled with one word.
- Crop the scene only to remove empty space at its bottom (0.1–0.3).

## Don’t

- For a screenshot with copy beside it — use `MediaSplitSection`.
- For code — use `MediaSplitSection` with `codeTabs`, or `CliTerminal`.

## Related

- ConsoleMockup` — the console scenes it frames.
- ToggleGroup` — the tab control.
- Texture`, `RegistrationFrame`, `SectionTitle`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'console' \| 'diagram'` | `'console'` | false | What the panel frames: `console` crops and fades a console mock at a fixed aspect, `diagram` lets a scene keep its own height. |
| `titleVariant` | `SectionTitleVariant` | `'center'` | false | Layout of the headline block. |
| `titlePadding` | `SectionTitlePadding` | `'medium'` | false | Vertical padding of the headline block. |
| `size` | `SectionTitleSize` | `'medium'` | false | Step of the headline on the heading scale. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences under the headline. |
| `texture` | `TextureVariant` | `'pixelate'` | false | Texture the panel is grounded with. |
| `textureFade` | `TextureFade` | `'top'` | false | Axis the texture fades out along. |
| `tabs` | `ConsoleShowcaseTab[]` | `[]` | false | Tabs over the frame, each `{ value, title }`; each plays its own beat of the scene. |
| `tabsAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the tab control; empty uses the built-in "Console views". |
| `crop` | `number` | `0` | false | Share of the scene height clipped off its bottom, from 0 to 0.5, from the medium breakpoint up. |
| `primaryAction` | `ConsoleShowcaseAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline, `secondary`; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ConsoleShowcaseAction` | `undefined` | false | Second button under the headline, `outline`; same shape. Shown only with a label and a link. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scene` | { tab: string | undefined }` \| The scene the band presents; `tab` is the selected tab value (undefined without tabs). |

## States

- `data-variant` mirrors `variant`.
- The first tab is selected on render.
- `--console-mockup-fade-start` / `--console-mockup-fade-end` are set for a `ConsoleMockup` scene when cropped.

## Accessibility

- A `section` named by its title.
- Tabs are a `ToggleGroup` (radio group) named by `tabsAriaLabel` or "Console views"; arrow keys move between them.
- The scene supplies its own accessible content (a mock is usually `aria-hidden` with a description in the copy).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-*`, `border-e`, `ms-*`).
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

| Key                     | English source  | Override prop   |
| ----------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `consoleShowcase.views` | `Console views` | `tabsAriaLabel` |

- Every other string is marketing copy passed through props.

## Responsive

- Below medium the console scene is square and uncropped; from medium it is 1.9:1 with the crop applied.
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConsoleMockup from '@aziontech/webkit/console-mockup'
  import ConsoleShowcase from '@aziontech/webkit/console-showcase'

  const tabs = [
    { value: 'workloads-list', title: 'Workloads' },
    { value: 'workload-deployments', title: 'Deployments' },
    { value: 'workload-deploy-logs', title: 'Logs' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ConsoleShowcase
    eyebrow="Console"
    title="One console for every workload"
    description="Deploy, observe and secure from the same place."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :crop="0.2"
  >
    <template #scene="{ tab }">
      <ConsoleMockup :name="tab ?? 'workloads-list'" />
    </template>
  </ConsoleShowcase>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/console-showcase.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/console-showcase.md).

<!-- components/contact-hub.md -->

# Contact Hub

> The band under the Contact title band: the team lanes side by side (Sales and Support), each with its scope in one sentence and the action that reaches that team, over a row of self-serve channels. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'contact-hub', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `feature-item`, `button` and `status-indicator`. Lanes and channels share one frame, the channels in the rows under the lanes. A lane can carry a second button and a link to the system status page, so a reader can check for an incident before opening a ticket.

- Import: `import ContactHub from '@aziontech/webkit/contact-hub'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the Contact page, to route a reader to the team or channel that answers them.

## Do

- Give it as many lanes and channels as the page has: both rows balance themselves (`card-grid` `layout: 'balanced'`), so two channels split the row in halves, three in thirds, four into 2 × 2 and five into 3 + 2, with no empty cell.
- Don't pad `channels` to three or drop one to make the row fit.
- Keep each lane's description to one sentence that states what that team handles.
- Set `target: '_blank'` on a channel or status link that leaves the site.
- Lead each lane with its `action`; add a `secondaryAction` only for a second route to the same team (an outlined button after the first).
- Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.

## Don’t

- For a closing ask at the end of a page → use `closing-call-to-action`.
- For a grid of product use cases → use `customer-use-cases`.

## Related

- `feature-item` — each self-serve channel is a linked topic.
- `customer-use-cases` — the sibling band of icon-led topics.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `lanes` | `ContactHubLane[]` | `[]` | false | The team lanes side by side, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description, action?, secondaryAction?, statusLink? }` where `action` is the lane's leading button, `secondaryAction` an outlined button after it, and `statusLink` the system status link beside them. |
| `channels` | `ContactHubChannel[]` | `[]` | false | The self-serve channels in the rows under the lanes, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description, href, target? }`, rendered as a linked topic. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: with neither `lanes` nor `channels` the band renders nothing but its root
- Empty frame: with neither lanes nor channels the frame is left out; lanes alone or channels alone still draw one frame
- A lane's action, secondary action and status link render only when given, in that order
- Status link: the pill carries a `status-indicator` (success dot and the link's label)
- One frame: lanes fill rows of up to two and the channels the rows under them, up to three per row, each group balanced so every row is full
- Anchor: the root carries `id` = `anchor` when set, with a scroll margin so a `#hash` jump clears a sticky header

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the status link carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; buttons and topics own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each lane action, its secondary action, the status link and each channel; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the band is an unnamed `<section>`; each lane heading and each channel is an `h2`, so the outline reads one entry per route. Glyphs are `aria-hidden`; the status pill's dot belongs to `status-indicator`, which hides it and keeps the label as the link's name. A link with `target: '_blank'` carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): lane heading `var(--text-muted)`, description `var(--text-default)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the status link's colour transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the status link is at least `h-10` (`min-h-10`), buttons are large, channels are whole-cell links.
- Reflow: the status link has `min-h-10` and `max-w-full`, and the lane floor wraps its buttons and the status link onto new lines, so nothing overflows a narrow column or a 200% zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>

</script>

<template>
  <ContactHub
    :lanes="[
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-briefcase',
        title: 'Sales',
        description:
          'Discuss your requirements, get custom pricing, or see the platform running on your own workload.',
        action: { label: 'Talk to sales', href: '/contact/sales' }
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-headphones',
        title: 'Support',
        description:
          'Log in with your Azion account to open a ticket. Our engineers pick it up 24/7 on paid support plans.',

        },

        icon: 'ai ai-shield',
```

<!-- components/copy-command.md -->

# Copy Command

> A one-line command or agent prompt with a copy button, set in a large `InputGroup` under hero or section copy ("npm create azion", "Ask your agent to …"). With `shell` a `$` prompt leads the line. From the design sample's site `CopyCommand`.

- Import: `import CopyCommand from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-command'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CopyCommand for a one-line command or agent prompt with a copy button on a marketing page.
- The one command that starts a product, beside or instead of a call to action.
- A prompt to paste into an AI agent (`shell` off).

## Do

- One line that works when pasted as is.
- Place it in a hero or section-title actions slot.

## Don’t

- For several lines or output — use `CodeBlock` or `CliTerminal`.
- For an editable field — use `Input`.

## Related

- CopyButton`, `InputGroup` — the parts.
- CliTerminal` — a full terminal session.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | Text on the line, copied as written. |
| `shell` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the shell prompt before the text; turn off for a prompt meant for an agent. |

## States

- Read-only input; the copy button shows its copied state (from `CopyButton`).

## Accessibility

- The read-only input is named "Command" or "Prompt"; the copy button is named "Copy command" or "Copy prompt".
- The `$` is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard: `Tab` reaches the field (text can be selected) and the copy button.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities.
- The command is `dir="ltr"` so a shell line keeps its order inside right-to-left pages.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source | Override prop |
| ------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `copyCommand.command`     | `Command`      | —             |
| `copyCommand.prompt`      | `Prompt`       | —             |
| `copyCommand.copyCommand` | `Copy command` | —             |
| `copyCommand.copyPrompt`  | `Copy prompt`  | —             |

- The command itself is content.

## Responsive

- Fills its column up to `--container-xs`; fixed at that width from large.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyCommand from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-command'
</script>

<template>
  <CopyCommand value="npm create azion@latest" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/copy-command.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/copy-command.md).

<!-- components/customer-use-cases.md -->

# Customer Use Cases

> The "what teams use it for" band of a product page: a three-column frame whose first cell carries the band's overline, headline, lead and one call to action, followed by one cell per use case. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'customer-use-cases', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `card-grid`, `registration-frame`, `eyebrow`, `feature-item` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import CustomerUseCases from '@aziontech/webkit/customer-use-cases'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use CustomerUseCases when the band's title sits in the first grid cell with one action.
- On a product or solution page, right after the opening band, to name the concrete jobs the product is bought for.
- Whenever a page needs three to six short, icon-led use cases with one link out to the documentation.

## Do

- Keep `items` to four or so; the first cell spans two rows at `lg`, so four cases fill the grid exactly.
- Write `title` as the heading the page's outline needs; it is the band's `h2`.
- Give `primaryAction` an `href` to the documentation and set `trailing` so the chevron reads as "go".
- Leave `eyebrow` as the product name; it is the overline the reader scans first.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For use cases that each link to their own page, or any grid of claims with no single action → use `capability-grid`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `feature-item` directly.

## Related

- `feature-item` — the icon, title and description cell each use case is rendered with.
- `card-grid` — the frame grid this band lays its cells in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the headline in the title cell, closed by the blinking cursor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` in the title cell. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One-line lead under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Button pinned to the foot of the title cell; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `items` | `CustomerUseCasesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The use cases rendered as frame cells, in order; each item is `{ icon, title, description }`. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the title cell, not the frame — because a use-case band with no use cases is absent from the page, not an `empty-state`
- The title cell spans two rows from `lg`, so four items fill a three-column grid exactly

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`, whose anchor carries the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the action link; `Enter` follows it. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` labelled by its `h2` (`aria-labelledby`); each use case is a `feature-item` with an `h3`, so the outline reads band → use cases. The overline is decorative text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): headline `var(--text-default)`, lead `var(--text-muted)`; icon colours are `feature-item`'s.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the overline cursor and the button's hover belong to `eyebrow` and `button`, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the action is a large `button`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the composed `card-grid`, `registration-frame` and `feature-item` use logical utilities, so the intro cell sits at the inline start.
- Icons: the trailing chevron of the action is the `button`'s own and follows its mirroring.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: the eyebrow, title, description, items and action label are marketing copy passed through props.

## Responsive

- Below large the intro cell and the use cases stack in one column; from large the intro cell spans two rows beside the use cases.
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CustomerUseCases from '@aziontech/webkit/customer-use-cases'
</script>

<template>
  <CustomerUseCases
    eyebrow="SQL Database"
    title="What teams use SQL Database for"
    description="Teams use it to:"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Docs', href: '/site/docs', trailing: true }"
    :items="[
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-comments',
        title: 'RAG Applications',
        description: 'Build topic-specific chatbots with the topic data stored in SQL Database.'
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-search',
        title: 'Search Applications',
        description: 'Power search with vector similarity queries on stored embeddings.'
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-sync',
        title: 'AI Context Injection',
        description: 'Give AI applications relevant context from vector embeddings.'
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-globe',
        title: 'AI Workflows',
        description: 'Pair stored embeddings with AI Inference to run RAG applications on Azion.'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/faq-section.md -->

# Faq Section

> The frequently asked questions band near the end of a landing page: the heading in the left column and the questions on the right, each answer closed until the reader opens it, one at a time. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'faq-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module` and `faq`. An answer is a markdown string, so it can run to several paragraphs (split by a blank line) and `- ` bullet lists, and a sentence can carry a link, bold or italic text, all without a slot or `v-html`.

- Import: `import FaqSection from '@aziontech/webkit/faq-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use FaqSection for the questions band of a marketing page placed from page JSON (Markdown answers).
- Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → the section (`faq-section`). Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the primitive (`faq`).
- To answer the handful of questions a reader still has before the closing call to action.

## Do

- Use one FAQ section per page and give it `anchor: 'faq'` so a page can link straight to it.
- Keep an answer short; links use `[label](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/href)`, bold `**text**` and italic `*text*`.
- Separate paragraphs with a blank line; start each bullet with `- ` and keep the list in its own block.
- Absolute `https://` links open in a new tab; site-relative links stay in the tab.

## Don’t

- For answers that need content beyond paragraphs, bullet lists and inline links (tables, images, code) → compose `faq` with its `answer` slot.
- For a single highlighted question with an action → use `call-to-action`.

## Related

- `faq` — the framed accordion band this section renders.
- `closing-call-to-action` — the band that usually follows it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the FAQ as its `h2` in the left column. |
| `items` | `FaqSectionItem[]` | `[]` | false | The questions in display order; each is `{ question, answer }` where `answer` is markdown carrying paragraphs, bullet lists, links, bold and italic text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `open` (one answer at a time, owned by the composed accordion)
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing but its root
- An answer renders `[label](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/href)` as a link, `**text**` as bold and `*text*` as italic; any other text is shown as written
- An answer with a blank line or `- ` lines renders as stacked paragraphs and an ARIA list (`role="list"` / `listitem`, inside the accordion's paragraph); a single-paragraph answer renders as inline text, as before

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed accordion triggers and the answer links.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the questions and the links of an open answer; `Enter` / `Space` toggles a question.
- ARIA: the `faq` renders the band's `<section>` labelled by its `h2`; the root is a plain `div` so the band has one landmark. A link that opens a new tab carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `faq`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the accordion carries its own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — owned by the accordion triggers.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FaqSection from '@aziontech/webkit/faq-section'
</script>

<template>
  <FaqSection
    anchor="faq"
    title="Frequently asked questions"
    :items="[
      {
        question: 'What types of storefronts can I build and deploy on Azion?',
        answer:
          'You can build and deploy storefronts, marketplaces, campaign pages, and supporting retail apps. Any web app or website runs on Azion. The platform also covers much of the backend, for static and dynamic workloads on a distributed architecture.'
      },
      {
        question: 'Which frameworks are compatible?',
        answer:
          'Azion is compatible with modern frameworks such as Next.js, React, Vue, Astro, Angular, Nuxt, Svelte, and others, so you can reuse your current stack without a full rewrite. See the full [frameworks compatibility list](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/en/documentation/products/devtools/azion-edge-runtime/frameworks-compatibility/).'
      },
      {
        question: 'How do preview deployments work?',
        answer:
          'You can validate storefront changes in preview environments before release, share results across teams, and promote approved versions to production with a controlled workflow.'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```
