<!-- components/feature-scroll.md -->

# Feature Scroll

> The walkthrough band of a product page: a large section title over one screen per feature. From the large breakpoint up the features scroll through a sticky stack — the copy advances while the feature's live scene or illustration stays pinned in a framed, textured stage with one small action under each step (a step may pin a one-file code sample instead, for a code-led walkthrough); below it the same features are a three-column grid of media tiles. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-scroll', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `media-tile`, `illustration`, `code-block`, `sticky-stack`, `texture`, `button` and the webkit scene assets (a `ConsoleMockup` console fragment, most often).

- Import: `import FeatureScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-scroll'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use FeatureScroll for the product-page walkthrough, one pinned screen (scene or code) per feature.
- To walk through four to six capabilities of one product, each with a picture of its own.
- To walk through capabilities each shown by the file you would write: give each item a `code` sample.

## Do

- Four to six items; the stack needs enough steps to earn the scroll.
- Give every item a `scene`, a `code` sample or an `illustration`; it is the pinned picture on large screens and the tile media on small ones. On a product page prefer a `scene` naming a `ConsoleMockup` (`{ component: 'ConsoleMockup', props: { name } }`): it shows the console itself.
- Keep `action` to a short label such as "Docs" — it sits under the step copy at the small size.

## Don’t

- For three reasons with no scroll story → use `feature-tiles`.
- For one claim beside one code sample → use `media-split-section` with `codeTabs`.
- In a hand-built SFC that needs its own media slot → use `sticky-stack` directly.

## Related

- `sticky-stack` — the scroll engine the large layout runs on.
- `media-tile` — the cell the small layout renders each feature with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the large section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `FeatureScrollItem[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order; each is `{ title, description, scene?, code?, illustration?, action? }` where `scene` is `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset (drawn live in the stack, still in the grid), `code` is a one-file sample `{ fileName, code, language?, fileIcon?, copyAriaLabel? }` drawn when no scene is set, `illustration` is a registry name drawn when neither is set, and `action` is `{ label, href, trailing?, target?, variant? }` rendered as a small button under the step, secondary unless `variant` says otherwise. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Below the large breakpoint the features render as a three-column grid of media tiles; from it up they render as a sticky stack whose active step is `sticky-stack`'s own
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frames
- Media: an item's `scene` wins over its `code`, which wins over its `illustration`; a `code` sample is a one-file `code-block` with line numbers, typed in once in the stack and loaded on demand; in the stack the scene receives `active` for the open step only, so a console fragment plays its beat while its step is open and rests on its settled frame otherwise; in the grid every scene is drawn still (`active: false`) in a 20rem window. A scene name that is not registered draws nothing.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each step's action and a code sample's copy button; `Enter` follows it; the stack's own progression is scroll-driven and never traps focus.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the step headings are `sticky-stack`'s and `media-tile`'s; the texture layer and the pinned illustration are decorative; a scene carries its own semantics (a `ConsoleMockup` is a decorative console picture).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the step transition belongs to `sticky-stack`, which carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the per-step action is a small `button` on the large layout only, where pointer precision is available.

<!-- components/feature-tabs.md -->

# Feature Tabs

> The feature walkthrough band of a product page: a horizontal section title, with its button beside the headline, over up to three tabs on one side and the active tab's media on the other. A tab's media is its own code file (a `code-block` with line numbers whose lines rise in while the tab is open, on a pixelate texture in a taller stage), the band's live scene (handed the open tab's `value`), or the tab's illustration. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tabs', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `media-tabs`, `code-block`, `illustration`, `button`, `link` and the webkit scene assets. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.

- Import: `import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use FeatureTabs for up to three tabs beside a media on a product page.
- To walk through the two or three features behind one claim, one picture at a time, like Functions' Observability.

## Do

- Keep to three tabs; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
- Give every tab an `illustrationLabel` saying what its picture shows.
- Use tab `code` when the feature is an API a developer reads; keep each file short enough to read in the stage. Set `copyAriaLabel` to say what the copy button copies.
- Use the band `scene` when one console widget plays a different beat per tab (`{ component: 'ConsoleMockup', props: { name: 'functions-start' } }` with tab `value`s naming its tabs); give every tab a `value` then.

## Don’t

- For architectures drawn as diagrams across the full width → use `architecture-tabs`.
- For a scroll-driven walkthrough of more features → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tabs` — the timed tabs this section renders through.
- `illustration` — the picture a tab shows when it has no code and the band has no scene.
- `code-block` — the code file a tab opens as its media.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `tabs` | `FeatureTabsTab[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order, at most three; each is `{ title, description, value?, code?, illustration?, illustrationLabel? }` where `value` is the stable key handed to the band scene as its `tab`, `code` is the `{ label, value, code, language?, fileName?, fileIcon? }` file the tab opens as its media, `illustration` is a registry name drawn when the tab has no code and the band no scene, and `illustrationLabel` its accessible name. |
| `scene` | `FeatureTabsScene` | `undefined` | false | Live scene drawn as the media of every tab without code, `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset; it receives the tab's `value` as `tab` and whether the tab is open as `active`. Wins over the illustrations. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Opens the next tab on a timer, with the composed tabs' visible pause control. |
| `autoplayInterval` | `number` | `5200` | false | Milliseconds each tab holds before the next one opens. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the copy button on each tab's code file; empty keeps the code block's own. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Button in the section title, beside the headline (under the frame when the band has no title); `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the active tab, its progress and the timer are owned by `media-tabs`
- Empty: when `tabs` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; the action renders only when `primaryAction` is set — as a secondary `button` in the header, or as a `link` under the frame when there is no header
- Media per tab: its `code` wins, then the band `scene`, then its `illustration`; when any tab carries `code` the stage grows from 24rem to 30rem and draws the pixelate texture, and an open tab's code lines rise in (owned by `code-block`, never under reduced motion). A scene name that is not registered draws nothing.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `media-tabs` (the tabs), `code-block` (the copy button), `button` and `link`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the action, the tabs and the open file's copy button; the tabs' keys are owned by `media-tabs`.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; each illustration is named by its tab's `illustrationLabel`, or decorative when empty; a code file is real text a screen reader reads, with a named copy button.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-tabs`, `code-block`, `button` and `link`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the timer never runs under reduced motion (owned by `media-tabs`).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the tab rows and the large header button; the under-frame link is supplementary to them.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      title: 'Trace',
      description:
        'The run as a waterfall: each step placed against the invocation it belongs to, nested where it nested.',
      illustration: 'live-debugging',
      illustrationLabel: 'A trace waterfall of one invocation'
    },
    {
      title: 'Logs',
      description:
        'Structured output on the same clock as the trace, filtered by level, searchable in place.',
      illustration: 'traffic-and-cost-bar-chart',
      illustrationLabel: 'Structured logs filtered by level'
    },
    {
      title: 'Request path',
      description:
        'The workload, application, function and connector it travelled, each captioned with the time spent there.',
      illustration: 'distributed-apis',
      illustrationLabel: 'The path a request took through the platform'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Open an invocation',
    href: '/product-preview',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureTabs
    eyebrow="Observability"
    title="Inspect every run end-to-end"
    description="Every invocation of a function is traced on the platform itself — spans, logs and the path the request took. Nothing to configure, no storage to attach. Pick a document to open it."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/feature-tiles.md -->

# Feature Tiles

> The reasons band of a marketing page: an optional centered section title over a frame grid of media tiles, each an image or an illustration above a short heading and a sentence. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tiles', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `media-tile` and `illustration`. `variant` picks the layout only: `artwork` is four columns with marks on every corner, `illustrated` is three columns with marks on the bottom rule; the tiles keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import FeatureTiles from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tiles'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use FeatureTiles for a static set of picture tiles.
- To state three or four reasons to buy, each with a picture, under a product or pricing argument.

## Do

- Match the tile count to the variant: four tiles for `artwork`, three for `illustrated`.
- Give a tile either `image` (a URL) or `illustration` (a registry name), not both; `scale` only matters with `illustration`.
- Leave `title` empty to drop the header when the band sits under a hero that already states it; set `anchor` when a link above scrolls to the band.

## Don’t

- For linked use cases or a grid of claims without pictures → use `capability-grid`.
- For a scroll-driven walkthrough with one screen per feature → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tile` — the picture-over-copy cell each tile is rendered with.
- `feature-widgets` — the sibling band whose cells carry an action each.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `FeatureTilesVariant` | `'artwork'` | false | Layout of the grid: `artwork` is four columns with marks on every corner, `illustrated` three columns with marks on the bottom rule. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the centered section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `tiles` | `FeatureTilesTile[]` | `[]` | false | The tiles rendered as frame cells, in order; each is `{ title, description, image?, alt?, illustration?, scale? }` where `image` is a picture URL, `alt` its alternative text (empty keeps the picture decorative), `illustration` a registry name drawn fluid, and `scale` its media scale. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop and drives the column count and the frame marks
- Empty: when `tiles` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set
- A tile picture carries its `alt`; without one it is decorative (`alt=""`, `aria-hidden`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2` and each tile's heading is `media-tile`'s; illustrations are decorative and named by the tile's heading; a tile picture is named by its `alt`, or hidden from assistive technology when `alt` is empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title` and `media-tile`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

<!-- components/feature-widgets.md -->

# Feature Widgets

> The "three ways to start" band of a product page: a centered section title with up to two calls to action, over a bento grid where every cell is a live console scene (or an illustration) above a bold-led sentence and its affordances — a link button, a copy button that puts a prompt on the clipboard and confirms it with "Copied" for two seconds, or both. A cell's scene plays its beat while the pointer is over the cell. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-widgets', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `registration-frame`, `bento-grid`, `illustration`, `highlight-button` and the webkit scene assets.

- Import: `import FeatureWidgets from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-widgets'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use FeatureWidgets when each cell has its own action or copy button.
- To offer the same outcome through two or three entry points (agent, console, terminal), each with its own next step.

## Do

- Give each item an `action` (a link), a `copy` (text to put on the clipboard), or both when the reader may want the docs and the prompt.
- On a product page give each item a `scene` naming a `ConsoleMockup` fragment (`{ component: 'ConsoleMockup', props: { name } }`); keep `illustration` for cells with no console to show.
- Keep `copy.text` self-contained; it is what the reader pastes into their agent.
- Set `anchor` when a hero button scrolls to this band.

## Don’t

- For reasons without an action per cell → use `feature-tiles` (with pictures) or `capability-grid` (without).
- For a long argument per feature → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the grid the cells are laid in.
- `highlight-button` — the copy affordance a cell renders when it carries `copy`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2`, and the accessible name of the band. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `titleVariant` | `SectionTitleVariant` | `'center'` | false | Alignment of the section title over the grid: `center`, `start` or `split`. |
| `columns` | `FeatureWidgetsColumns` | `2` | false | Column count of the grid from the medium breakpoint up: `2`, `3` or `4`. |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label a cell's copy button shows for two seconds after a copy; empty uses the catalog's `Copied`. |
| `items` | `FeatureWidgetsItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cells, in order; each is `{ title, description, scene?, illustration?, action?, copy? }` where `scene` is `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset drawn in a 20rem window and handed `hover` while the pointer is over the cell, `illustration` is drawn when no scene is set, `action` is `{ label, href }` rendered as an outlined link button and `copy` is `{ label, text }` rendered as a copy button that puts `text` on the clipboard; a cell may carry both. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; the two actions ride with it
- A cell's copy button writes `copy.text` to the clipboard on activation, then reads `copiedLabel` (or the catalog's `Copied`) with a check icon for two seconds before it returns to its label; the timer is cleared when the band unmounts. A failed write leaves the label as it was
- A cell with both `action` and `copy` renders the link button first, then the copy button
- Media per cell: `scene` wins over `illustration`; the scene receives `hover: true` while the pointer is over its cell (also on `pointermove`, so a pointer left still while the page scrolls under it counts). A scene name that is not registered draws nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button` and `highlight-button`, which carry the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the header actions and each cell's buttons; `Enter` / `Space` activates. The scene's hover beat is decorative, so keyboard users lose nothing without it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the grid is an unnamed `bento-grid` inside that landmark, so the name is not duplicated; the cell lead is a `strong` inside the sentence, not a heading, so the outline stays the band's `h2`; the action row is a polite live region, so the copy button's "Copied" is announced.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): lead `var(--text-default)`, copy `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the buttons' motion carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the cell buttons are medium `button` / `highlight-button`.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/hero-form-section.md -->

# Hero Form Section

> The opening band of a lead-capture page, where the form is the reason for the page: the hero copy and a list of highlights on one side, the form on the other, above the fold, with the client strip on the floor. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-form-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `feature-item`, `field`, `input`, `select`, `phone-input`, `textarea`, `button` and `alert`. The fields are data: each entry of `fields` picks its control by `type`, so the Contact page and the Under attack page are the same block with different `fields`. The block never sends: it validates the fields locally (required fields and the email format, with the messages from `messages`) and on a valid submit emits `submit` with the event and the values keyed by field `name`; the site posts them and reports the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.

- Import: `import HeroFormSection from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-form-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use HeroFormSection when the page exists to capture a lead and the form sits above the fold.
- To open a page whose purpose is a lead form, such as Contact sales or Under attack.

## Do

- Give every field a unique `name`; it is the key of the submitted value.
- Mark half-width fields in pairs so each row stays full.
- Set `visuallyHiddenLabel` on a field the page labels by its placeholder alone (azion.com's phone field): the label stays the control's accessible name for assistive tech but is not drawn, so give that field a `placeholder` that says what to type.
- Keep the headline to a short phrase; the band sets it on a narrower measure than the description (`--container-md`), so "Grow as an Azion Partner" breaks over two lines as on the site. There is no width prop to tune.
- Set `loading` while the values are sent, then `submitted` or `failed` with the outcome.

## Don’t

- For a newsletter sign-up with one email field → use `newsletter-section`.
- For an opening band with calls to action and no form → use `hero-section`, which takes every other marketing page opening.

## Related

- `newsletter-section` — the other form section; same `submit` and state contract.
- `alert` — renders the success and failure messages.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `messages` | `HeroFormSectionMessages` | `—` | true | Copy of the form outcomes: `{ missing, invalidEmail, success, error }`. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `titleHighlight` | `string` | `''` | false | Opening words of the headline, painted in the brand accent. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `descriptionLink` | `HeroFormSectionLink` | `undefined` | false | A link continuing the description inline, such as a phone line; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `descriptionAfter` | `string` | `''` | false | Copy after the inline link, closing the description's sentence. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `items` | `HeroFormSectionItem[]` | `[]` | false | The highlights under the description, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. The list renders only when there are items. |
| `formAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field group, read as its legend. |
| `fields` | `HeroFormSectionField[]` | `[]` | false | The form fields in order; each is `{ name, type, label, placeholder?, required?, half?, options?, country?, visuallyHiddenLabel? }`; `visuallyHiddenLabel` keeps the label as the accessible name but does not draw it. |
| `submitLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the submit button. |
| `marqueeLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the client marquee. |
| `marqueeMarks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the client marks, in order; the marquee renders only when there are marks. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site is sending the values: the button shows its loading state and a submit is ignored. |
| `submitted` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site sent the values: the form gives way to `messages.success`. |
| `failed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site could not send the values: `messages.error` shows under the form. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, values: Record<string, string>)` | Fired on a valid submit, not while `loading`; `values` holds every field by `name`, trimmed, with a phone number prefixed by its dial code. The block never sends it. |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Marquee` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `invalid`, `loading`, `submitted`, `failed`
- `invalid`: on submit, an empty required field shows `messages.missing` and a malformed email `messages.invalidEmail` under the field; focus moves to the first field in error; editing the field clears it; nothing is emitted
- `loading` (prop): the button shows its loading state, every field is disabled (the scope locks off the one flag) and a submit emits nothing; `data-loading` on the root
- `submitted` (prop): the form is replaced by a success `Alert` with `messages.success`, which takes focus when focus was in the form; `data-submitted` on the root
- `failed` (prop): a danger `Alert` with `messages.error` shows under the button; the form stays editable; `data-failed` on the root
- A field with `visuallyHiddenLabel` renders its `Field.Label` visually hidden (`sr-only`), so the control keeps its accessible name and the page shows only the placeholder
- The headline caps at `--container-md` while the description and highlights keep the `lg` column
- `descriptionLink` renders inline after `description`, underlined, followed by `descriptionAfter`, so the copy reads as one sentence
- Without `items`, the copy block is sticky from `lg` (it stays in view while the taller form scrolls past); with `items` it scrolls with the highlights
- `loading` also sets `disabled` on the `fieldset`, so the browser locks every control in it
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; when `items` is empty the list is omitted; when `marqueeMarks` is empty the strip is omitted

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the field controls and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the inline description link and the actions under the copy, then walks the fields in order and the button; `Enter` in a text field or on the button submits.
- ARIA: the band is the `hero` `<section>` named by the title (`aria-label`); the root is a plain `div`. The fields sit in a `fieldset` whose visually hidden `legend` is `formAriaLabel`; each control is labelled through its own `Field.Label` with an id from `useId`; each label is a `Field.Label` rendered by the band, carrying the persistent Required tag of a `required` field from first render. An `email` field is an `<input type="email">` with `autocomplete="email"` and `spellcheck="false"`. Validation runs on submit only: a required field left empty takes the field's amber `required` state (warning border, `type=required` helper, `aria-required`), a malformed email the red `invalid` state (`aria-invalid`), never both at once; the message is the field's helper text, and editing the field clears it. The success message is a `status` region and the failure message an `alert`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the inline description link's colour transition; the composed components carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the text fields and the button are large.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the copy and the form swap sides under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the action chevrons mirror with `button`; highlight icons are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key handling beyond the select's own.
- User data: email and phone values render as typed.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every label, placeholder, message and action is a prop from the page JSON (`fields`, `messages`, `submitLabel`, `formAriaLabel`).

- Formatting: none of its own; the phone field formats the number for its country (owned by `phone-input`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the copy and the form sit side by side from `lg` and stack below it.
- Narrow (below `lg`): the copy, the highlights and the form stack; below `sm` every field takes the full row (`half` fields stop pairing).
- Touch: the fields and the buttons are large; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

<!-- components/hero-section.md -->

# Hero Section

> The opening band of a marketing page: the page `h1` with its overline, accent phrase, sentence and up to two actions, full width above the page column, with an optional client strip on the floor. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `button` and `illustration`, plus `flow-diagram` and `tag` for the topology and `section-container`, `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `card-grid`, `feature-item` and `section-gap` for the argument grid. `variant` picks the layout only: `center` fills a screen over a dot field with the copy centered, `title-band` is a padded band with the copy centered, `pixel-floor` sets the copy at the start over an animated pixel floor, `copy-beside-art` sets an illustration (or an `image`) beside the copy, sized from that illustration's own drawn bounds so it bleeds past the column edge and trims its empty top and bottom, and `copy-on-top-art` fills a screen with the copy centered over a scene in its `top` or `bottom` slot, unpadded so the scene reaches the band's edges, and draws a `FlowDiagram` topology from `levels` in the bottom window when neither slot is given, so page JSON can carry the scene as data; every layout takes the same copy, actions and client strip, and any layout can set a framed grid of arguments (`items`, three to a row, each a `FeatureItem`) under the band. The client strip's overline falls back to the locale catalog (`Proven on mission-critical workloads`).

- Import: `import HeroSection from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use HeroSection for every marketing page opening; pick the layout with `variant`.
- To open a home, solution, product, listing or contact page with its headline and main actions; add `items` for a grid of arguments under it, or `levels` with `variant="copy-on-top-art"` for a topology under the copy.
- Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → the section (`hero-section`). Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the primitive (`hero`).

## Do

- Use `title-band` with `size="large"` for a product page and `size="medium"` for a page whose bands start right under the headline.
- Give `illustration` and `illustrationAriaLabel` only to the `copy-beside-art` layout; the other layouts ignore them.
- Leave `titleLength` at `short` for a headline of up to about seven words: like azion.com, the `center`, `title-band` and `center-band` layouts set it on a narrower measure than the sentence under it, so "Certifications and Compliance" breaks over two lines. Use `long` only for a headline that would run to three lines.
- Leave `headerOffset` at its default under `SiteHeader`: it takes the bar's `--layout-header-height` out of a band that fills a screen, so the band fills exactly the first screen with it. Set it empty only on a page with no header above the band; never a literal length.

## Don’t

- When the page exists to capture a lead and the form sits above the fold → use `hero-form-section`.
- In a hand-built SFC that needs slots HeroSection does not offer → use the `hero` primitive.
- For a band inside the page column → use `section-module` or a sibling section.

## Related

- `hero` — the band primitive every layout is rendered with.
- hero-title` — the headline block rendered inside it.
- `hero-form-section` — the opening band with a lead form beside the copy.
- `flow-diagram` — the diagram primitive the `levels` topology is drawn with.
- `feature-item` — the icon, heading and sentence each argument of `items` is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `HeroSectionVariant` | `'title-band'` | false | Layout of the band: `center` fills a screen over a dot field, `title-band` is a padded band, `center-band` is a large site-wide band with the copy centered, `compact-band` is a short site-wide band with the copy at the start, `pixel-floor` sets the copy over an animated pixel floor, `copy-beside-art` sets an illustration or an image beside the copy, `copy-on-top-art` fills a screen with the copy centered over a scene in the `top` or `bottom` slot. |
| `size` | `HeroSectionSize` | `'medium'` | false | Vertical rhythm of the band; `large` is the opening a product page leads with. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `titleHighlight` | `string` | `''` | false | Opening words of the headline, painted in the brand accent; reads as one sentence with `title`. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `marqueeLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the client marquee; empty uses the locale catalog (`Proven on mission-critical workloads`). |
| `marqueeMarks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the client marks on the band floor, in order; the marquee renders only when it has marks. |
| `illustration` | `string` | `''` | false | Registry name of the illustration set beside the copy in the `copy-beside-art` layout. |
| `illustrationAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible description of the illustration. |
| `image` | `HeroSectionImage` | `undefined` | false | Image set beside the copy in the `copy-beside-art` layout when no `illustration` is given; `{ src, alt, width, height }`. A portrait image (taller than wide) is drawn at half width, centered, below `md`. |
| `eyebrowPrefix` | `HeroTitleEyebrowPrefix` | `'//'` | false | Mark set before the eyebrow (`//`, `<>`, `</>`, or empty for none); drawn only with an eyebrow. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `headerOffset` | `string` | `'var(--layout-header-height)'` | false | Height of the site header above the band, taken out of a band that fills a screen; defaults to the `SiteHeader` bar's token, any CSS length, empty for a page with no header above it. |
| `titleLength` | `HeroSectionTitleLength` | `'short'` | false | Length of the headline: `short` sets it on the site's narrow headline measure in the centered layouts, so a four-to-seven-word headline breaks over two balanced lines while the sentence under it keeps the full column; `long` lets the headline take the whole column. |
| `plain` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Drops the dot texture of the `center` layout. |
| `levels` | `HeroSectionLevel[]` | `[]` | false | Columns of the topology the `copy-on-top-art` layout draws under the copy when neither scene slot is given, left to right; each is `{ nodes }`, the cards top to bottom, each `{ eyebrow, icon, title, label, severity, lit? }`. A card without `title` is skipped. |
| `items` | `HeroSectionItem[]` | `[]` | false | Arguments in a framed grid under the band, three to a row; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. The grid renders only when there are items. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `top` | — | A scene in the window above the copy (`ConsoleMockup`, a diagram). The design sample's hero scenes render here. |
| `bottom` | — | A scene in the window under the copy; it enters after the copy (`animate-content-enter`, off under reduced motion) and fades at the inline edges on narrow containers. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Marquee` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop and drives the hero's height, width, backdrop and the copy alignment
- `data-title-measure="narrow"` on the root when the headline is set on the narrow measure (`titleLength: 'short'` in the `center`, `title-band` and `center-band` layouts); the headline then caps at `--container-lg` while the description keeps the column
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root
- The client strip renders only when `marqueeMarks` has marks; each action renders only with a label and a link; the art renders only in the `copy-beside-art` layout with `illustration` or `image` set (`illustration` wins when both are given)
- `copy-beside-art` art bounds: a registered illustration whose drawn area is known (the `azion-to-*` comparisons and the solution illustrations) takes a width, a bleed past the column's end edge and a top and bottom trim computed from where it is drawn on its canvas, set as `--hero-section-art-width`, `--hero-section-art-bleed`, `--hero-section-art-trim-top` and `--hero-section-art-trim-bottom` on the art box from `md` up; any other illustration keeps the default bounds (161.45 % wide, 35.73 % bleed, no trim); an `image` fills the media column. Below `md` the art takes the column width
- `data-orientation="portrait"` on an `image` taller than it is wide
- Topology: in `copy-on-top-art` with no `top` or `bottom` slot, `levels` draws a `FlowDiagram` in the bottom window, one column per level and one card per node with a title; a level left with no card is dropped, and with none left the window is not drawn. A lit node carries `data-lit` and a brand glow. Other layouts ignore `levels`, and a slotted scene wins over it
- Argument grid: `items` renders a framed three-column `CardGrid` of `FeatureItem`s (headings at level 2) inside a site-wide `SectionContainer` under the hero, closed by a hatched `SectionGap`; only with a title and at least one item

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions; the client strip is not focusable.
- ARIA: the hero `<section>` is named by the full headline (`aria-label`); the headline is the page `h1`; the illustration is named by `illustrationAriaLabel`, decorative when empty; an `image` carries its `alt`. The topology cards are static text (eyebrow, title, status tag), not focusable; each argument heading is an `h2` under the page `h1`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `hero-title` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the pixel floor and the client strip stop under reduced motion in `texture` and `marquee`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the large buttons meet it.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; in `copy-beside-art` the art bleeds past the end edge (`-me-`) and moves to the start side under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the action chevrons mirror with `button`; illustrations, images and client marks are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key handling.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source                       | Override prop  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------- |
| `heroSection.carouselLabel` | Proven on mission-critical workloads | `marqueeLabel` |

- Formatting: none; every other text is a prop from the page JSON.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the `bottom` scene window reads its container (`@max-2xl` fades its inline edges); the layouts switch at viewport breakpoints.
- Narrow (below `md`): in `copy-beside-art` the copy centres and stacks over the art, which takes the column width with no bleed or trim; a portrait image takes half the width, centered.
- Touch: the large buttons meet 40 px; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; the art bleed applies from `md` only and is clipped by the hero.

## Examples

    :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: 'https://console.azion.com/signup/' }"

# Investor Marks

> The investors band: a centered section title over a two-column bento grid where each cell is an investor's mark, linked to its site, that lifts on hover to reveal a "visit website" line. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'investor-marks', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame` and `bento-grid`.

- Import: `import InvestorMarks from '@aziontech/webkit/investor-marks'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the company page, to name the investors with their marks.

## Do

- Give each item a `logoLight` when its mark needs a different file on the light theme; otherwise one `logo` serves both.
- Keep `linkLabel` short; it is revealed under the mark on hover and read before the investor name.

## Don’t

- For client marks → use `client-mosaic` or `logo-wall-section`.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the grid the marks are laid in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the centered section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Line revealed under a mark on hover, and the start of each link's accessible name. |
| `items` | `InvestorMarksItem[]` | `[]` | false | The investors, in order; each is `{ name, logo, logoLight?, href }` where `logo` is the mark on the dark theme and `logoLight` the one on the light theme. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on each cell (fill rises, mark lifts, the link line appears)
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each cell link carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset` and shows the same reveal as hover.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between investor links; `Enter` follows one (opens in a new tab).
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); each link's accessible name is "`linkLabel`, `name` (opens in a new tab)"; the revealed line is `aria-hidden` since the name already carries it; the two theme marks share the investor's name as `alt`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): link line `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-hover)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on every transition above.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each link is a full 12rem-tall cell.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the two-column grid mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the arrow-up-right glyph and the investor marks are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key handling; `Tab` order follows the grid.
- User data: investor names render as given.

## Internationalization

| Key                    | English source       | Override prop |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- | ------------- |
| `investorMarks.newTab` | (opens in a new tab) | —             |

- Formatting: none; the revealed link line is the `linkLabel` prop.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `bento-grid` lays the cells in two columns.
- Narrow (below `md`): the cells keep two columns and the marks scale down to their `max-w-48` box.
- Touch: each link is a full 12rem-tall cell; the hover reveal also shows on focus, and the link works without it.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

<!-- components/job-posting.md -->

# Job Posting

> The body of a careers posting page, under the posting's title band: the description in rows, one per section of the posting (a heading, then its paragraphs and bullet lists), beside a sticky rail that restates the posting (its area, its title and its facets such as department, location and contract) with the link to the application; then the application form, and a dialog that confirms a sent application with a way back to the open positions. From the design sample's careers job page. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'job-posting', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `section-title`, `eyebrow`, `button`, `field`, `label`, `input`, `phone-input`, `file-dropzone`, `file-token-group`, `alert`, `dialog` and `panel`. It collects data, so it follows the forms exception of the page-section contract: it validates on submit only and emits `submit`; the site sends the application and hands the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.

- Import: `import JobPosting from '@aziontech/webkit/job-posting'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the page of one open position, under a `hero-section` (`variant: 'title-band'`) that carries the posting's title and its apply link.

## Do

- Write each section as a short heading and its `blocks`: a `text` block per paragraph, a `list` block per bullet list, in the posting's order.
- Keep `facets` to the four the listing states (department, location, work arrangement, contract), each with a glyph.
- Set `form.anchor` (for example `apply`) and point the title band's action at `#apply`; the rail's apply button links there too.
- Put the format and size limits of a `file` field in its `helper`, and the accepted types in `accept`.
- Mark only what the team needs as `required`; say "Optional." in the `helper` of the rest.
- Send the application from the `submit` handler, read the file from `new FormData(event.target)`, and set `loading`, then `submitted` or `failed`.

## Don’t

- For the list of open positions → use `listing-index`.
- For a lead or contact form at the top of a landing page → use `hero-form-section`.
- For a newsletter sign-up at the end of a page → use `newsletter-section`.

## Related

- `hero-section` — the title band above the posting; its action links to `#` plus `form.anchor`.
- `hero-form-section` — the sibling page section that also emits `submit` and takes `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `JobPostingForm` | `—` | true | The application form: `{ title, description?, submitLabel, anchor?, ariaLabel?, fields }`, where `anchor` is the id of the apply section the rail button links to and a field is `{ name, type, label, required?, helper?, placeholder?, accept?, autocomplete?, country? }`. |
| `messages` | `JobPostingMessages` | `—` | true | Copy of the form and its outcomes: `{ missing, invalidEmail, invalidUrl, error, successTitle, successDescription, done, browse }`. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `area` | `string` | `''` | false | Area the posting is filed under, the overline of the rail. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the posting, restated at the top of the rail; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `facets` | `JobPostingFacet[]` | `[]` | false | Facts about the posting listed in the rail, in order; each is `{ label, icon? }`. |
| `applyLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the rail button that links to the application form; the button is left out when empty. |
| `sections` | `JobPostingSection[]` | `[]` | false | The description, one row per section in order; each is `{ title, blocks }` where a block is `{ variant: 'text', text }` or `{ type: 'list', items }`. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Link in the confirmation dialog back to the open positions; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site is sending the application: the submit button shows its loading state, every control is disabled and a submit is ignored. |
| `submitted` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site sent the application: the confirmation dialog opens. |
| `failed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site could not send the application: `messages.error` shows under the submit button. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, values: Record<string, string>)` |  |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `invalid`, `loading`, `submitted`, `failed`
- `invalid`: on submit, an empty required field shows `messages.missing`, a malformed email `messages.invalidEmail` and a URL that does not start with `http://` or `https://` `messages.invalidUrl` under the field; focus moves to the first field in error; editing the field (or picking a file) clears its message; nothing is emitted
- `loading` (prop): the submit button shows its loading state, the `fieldset` and every control are disabled and a submit emits nothing; `data-loading` on the root
- `submitted` (prop): when it turns on, the confirmation dialog opens with `messages.successTitle`, `messages.successDescription`, the `secondaryAction` link and a `messages.done` button; closing the dialog (Done, the close button, `Escape` or the overlay) clears the form; `data-submitted` on the root
- `failed` (prop): a danger `Alert` with `messages.error` shows under the submit button; the form stays editable; `data-failed` on the root
- File field: an inline `file-dropzone` with a browse button takes one file; once picked, the file shows in a `file-token-group` whose remove button clears it and brings the dropzone back
- Description: each section row after the first draws a rule above it (`data-ruled`); a `list` block is a bulleted list
- Rail: shown from the large breakpoint up, sticky under the site header while the description scrolls; the apply button renders only when `applyLabel` is set
- Disabled, readonly: not states of the band; `loading` is the only lock
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; with no `sections` the description column is empty and the rail still renders; with no `facets` the facet list is left out

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`, `input`, `phone-input`, `file-token-group` and `dialog` controls.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` walks the rail's apply link, then the fields in order (the file field's browse button, or its remove button once a file is picked), then the submit button; `Enter` in a text field or on the submit button submits; `Enter` or `Space` on the browse button opens the file picker. In the confirmation dialog `Tab` cycles the secondary action, Done and the close button (focus is trapped), and `Escape` closes it and returns focus (`dialog`'s Dialog (Modal) pattern).
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div` (the posting's title is the title band's heading); each description section heads with an `h2` through `section-title`; the rail restates the title as a paragraph, not a heading, so the outline lists the posting once. The fields sit in a `fieldset` whose visually hidden `legend` is `form.ariaLabel`, or `form.title`; each control is labelled through its own `Field.Label` with an id from `useId`, carrying the persistent Required tag of a `required` field from first render. An `email` field is an `<input type="email">` with `autocomplete="email"` and `spellcheck="false"`, a `url` field a text input with `inputmode="url"`. The file field's dropzone is a named `group`; its browse button is named `messages.browse` followed by the field label. Validation runs on submit only: a required field left empty takes the amber `required` state, a malformed value the red `invalid` state (`aria-invalid`), never both at once; the message is the field's helper text. The failure message is an `alert`; the confirmation is a modal `dialog` named by its title and described by its description.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components; copy uses the text tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the composed button, dropzone and dialog carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the text fields, the buttons and the dialog actions are large or medium controls at least 40 px tall.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-s` on the rail, `ps-` on the bullet lists, `text-start`); the rail sits at the inline end.
- Icons: the apply button's `ai ai-chevron-right` is mirrored by `button`; facet glyphs are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key interaction of its own.
- User data: the posting copy is passed as props and inherits the page direction; field values are typed by the reader.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every visible string and accessible name comes from the props (`title`, `area`, `facets`, `applyLabel`, `sections`, `form`, `messages`, `secondaryAction`). The composed `dialog` close button and `file-dropzone` title keep their own locale catalogs.

| Key | English source | Override prop |
| --- | -------------- | ------------- |
| —   | —              | —             |

- Formatting: none; the file size in the file token is formatted by `file-token-group` with `Intl.NumberFormat`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the band follows the page breakpoints.
- Narrow (below `lg`): the rail is hidden and the description takes the full width; the title band's apply link and the form remain. Below `sm` the form's fields stack in one column; from `sm` they sit two to a row, the file field across both.
- Touch: targets ≥ 40 px; no hover-only affordance.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; the description holds a reading measure and wraps.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import JobPosting from '@aziontech/webkit/job-posting'
  import { nextTick, ref } from 'vue'

  const facets = [
    {
      label: 'Engineering',
      icon: 'ai ai-sitemap'
    },
    {
      label: 'San Francisco, California',
      icon: 'ai ai-map-pin'
    },
    {
      label: 'Hybrid',
      icon: 'ai ai-building'
    },
    {
      label: 'Full-time',
      icon: 'ai ai-clock'
    }
  ]

  const sections = [
    {
      title: 'About Acme',
      blocks: [
        {
          type: 'text',
          text: 'Acme builds the platform teams use to ship and run their applications worldwide. We are a small team with a big footprint, and we care about tools that get out of the way.'
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'About the role',
      blocks: [
        {
          type: 'text',
          text: 'As a Senior Platform Engineer you will turn quality into a built-in capability of our engineering platform: automation, internal tools and standards that remove manual steps from the delivery cycle.'
        },
        {
          type: 'text',
          text: 'You will work with the development, platform and infrastructure teams on self-service tools, standard pipelines and automated release checks.'
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'What you will do',
      blocks: [
        {
          type: 'list',
          items: [
            'Build and evolve standard CI/CD pipelines for tests, checks and releases.',
            'Write internal frameworks and tools for test automation.',
            'Automate functional, integration and end-to-end tests.',
            'Guide engineers in testing and automation practices.'
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'What you bring',
      blocks: [
        {
          type: 'list',
          items: [
            'Experience with test automation and quality engineering.',
            'Solid experience with CI/CD and pipeline automation.',
            'Tooling written in TypeScript, Python or Go.',
            'Working knowledge of Linux and containers.'
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const form = {
    anchor: 'apply',
    title: 'Do you want to build with us?',
    description: 'Fill in the form to apply for this position.',
    submitLabel: 'Submit application',
    fields: [
      {
        name: 'name',
        type: 'text',
        label: 'Name',
        required: true,
        autocomplete: 'name'
      },
      {
        name: 'email',
        type: 'email',
        label: 'Email address',
        required: true,
        helper: 'We answer every application at this address.'
      },
      {
        name: 'phone',
        type: 'phone',
        label: 'Contact number',
        required: true
      },
      {
        name: 'linkedin',
        type: 'url',
        label: 'LinkedIn profile URL',
        helper: 'Optional.'
      },
      {
        name: 'resume',
        type: 'file',
        label: 'Resume',
        required: true,
        accept: 'application/pdf,.docx,.doc',
        helper: '.pdf, .docx or .doc, up to 5 MB'
      }
    ]
  }

  const messages = {
    missing: 'This field is required.',
    invalidEmail: 'Enter an email address like name@example.com.',
    invalidUrl: 'Enter the full URL, starting with https://.',
    error: 'We could not send your application. Try again in a few minutes.',
    successTitle: 'Application sent',
    successDescription:
      'Thank you for applying. We read every application and will reply by email.',
    done: 'Done',
    browse: 'Browse files'
  }

  const submitted = ref(false)

  const send = async () => {
    submitted.value = false
    await nextTick()
    submitted.value = true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <JobPosting
    area="Engineering"
    title="Senior Platform Engineer"
    apply-label="Apply for this position"
    :facets="facets"
    :sections="sections"
    :form="form"
    :messages="messages"
    :secondary-action="{ label: 'See open positions', href: '/careers' }"
    :submitted="submitted"
    @submit="send"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/listing-index.md -->

# Listing Index

> The full, browsable listing of a page such as the Careers jobs list: a headline over a toolbar (a search field, one select per facet and one for the order) and every row under its group, as a table from the small breakpoint up and as a list of items below it, with an empty state when nothing matches. A row may carry its client's mark, drawn before the name on the table and above it on phones; a pointer click anywhere on a table row follows the row link; the other columns are metadata in the small overline, each cut to one line with its full text as a tooltip; group headings stick under the site header while their rows scroll. Below the large breakpoint the toolbar folds to the search field and a filter button that reveals the selects, with each applied facet listed under it as a removable chip. A select with more than seven options gains an option search. Search, facets and order are local state over the rows the page carries; a facet is seeded from `?<id>=` in the URL when the value is one the page offers. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'listing-index', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `input`, `select`, `table`, `item`, `chip`, `empty-state` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import ListingIndex from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-index'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ListingIndex for a filterable list of non-article rows (jobs): a listing a reader narrows by text and by a few facets, such as open positions grouped by department.
- When every row links to its own page and the listing fits in the page JSON.

## Do

- Name the first column after what the row is (`Role`); it is the row's link, and the second column describes the row on phones.
- Give every row the facet values it carries under the facet's `id`, so the selects narrow it.
- Keep `groups` in the order the reader scans; rows of a group not listed there are not shown.
- Make the first entry of `sorts` the order the page is authored in, with an empty `by`.

## Don’t

- For a short, unfiltered preview of the same rows → use `listing-table`.
- For a data table with sorting, selection and pagination inside the product → use `table`.
- For a grid of linked topic cards → use `subject-grid`.
- For the full filterable list of articles or resources → use `article-index`.
- For a card grid of customer stories with search and facets → use `story-index`.

## Related

- `table` — the composed rows and cells the listing renders from the small breakpoint up.
- `item` — the list rows the listing renders below the small breakpoint.
- `empty-state` — the state shown when the search and facets match nothing.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page `id` of the band, the target of a `#hash` link. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the listing, rendered by the section title as its `h2` and naming the band. |
| `columns` | `ListingIndexColumn[]` | `[]` | false | The columns, left to right; each is `{ key, label, grow?, align? }`. The first names the row and links it, the second describes it on phones. |
| `data` | `ListingIndexRow[]` | `[]` | false | Every row, in source order; each is `{ href, group, values, facets, mark? }` where `values` and `facets` are keyed by column and facet and `mark` is the client's `{ name, logo }`. |
| `groups` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | The groups the rows are listed under, in order; a group with no matching row is not shown. |
| `facets` | `ListingIndexFacet[]` | `[]` | false | The facet selects; each is `{ id, label, allLabel, options }` where `id` matches a row facet and seeds it from `?id=` in the URL, and every option is `{ value, label }`. |
| `sorts` | `ListingIndexSort[]` | `[]` | false | The orders, the first the default; each is `{ value, label, by? }` where `by` is the column it sorts on and an empty `by` keeps the source order. |
| `sortAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the order select. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the search field from the large breakpoint up; the field is omitted when this and `searchAriaLabel` are both empty. |
| `searchShortPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Shorter placeholder of the search field below the large breakpoint; empty uses `searchPlaceholder`. |
| `searchAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the search field. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the state shown when nothing matches; the state renders only with it. |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the empty-state headline. |
| `emptyActionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the empty-state button that clears the search and every facet; no button renders without it. |
| `filterLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the filter button below the large breakpoint; empty uses the locale catalog (`Filters`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `filtered`, `empty`
- Filtered: the search matches a row when any of its values contains the query, ignoring case; every facet set to a value keeps only the rows carrying it; the order select sorts on its column or keeps the source order
- Empty: when the search and facets match no row, `empty-state` replaces the table and the list, and its `emptyActionLabel` button clears the search and every facet; without `emptyTitle`, nothing is shown in their place
- Seeded: on mount a facet takes the value of `?<id>=` in the URL when it is one of its options
- Absent: when `data` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the toolbar
- The table renders from the small breakpoint up, the list below it; below the large breakpoint the search field shows `searchShortPlaceholder`
- Folded toolbar (below the large breakpoint): a filter button (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) beside the search field shows or hides the facet and order selects, stacked (the panel carries `data-state="open|closed"`); its label carries the number of applied facets; every facet set to a value renders a removable `chip` (`<facet label>: <option label>`) whose remove clears that facet. From the large breakpoint the selects sit on the toolbar row and the button and chips are hidden (CSS only, so server and client markup match)
- Option search: a facet or order select with more than seven options renders a search field above its options and a `status` line when nothing matches
- Marked: a row with `mark` draws the client's logo (flattened to one ink that inverts in the dark theme) before the name in the table and above the title in the list
- Whole-row navigation: a click on a table row outside its link is forwarded to the link, keeping `ctrl`/`meta`/`shift`/`alt`; a click that ends a text selection is not forwarded
- Metadata cells (every column after the first) render `text-overline-sm`, truncated to one line, with their full value as `title`; the list's description renders `text-overline-sm`
- Sticky groups: each group heading row sticks under `var(--layout-header-height)` while its rows scroll
- Server render and hydration: the large-breakpoint check runs only after mount, so the server HTML and the first client render both use `shortPlaceholder` and match; the full placeholder applies on mount.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `input`, `select` and `button`; each row link draws `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the filter button (below the large breakpoint), the search field, the selects, the applied-filter chips and the row links in reading order; a select opens on `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown`, moves with the arrows and closes on `Escape` (all `select`'s own); `Enter` follows a row link.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the toolbar is a `role="search"` region; the search field is named by `searchAriaLabel`, each facet select by its `label` and the order select by `sortAriaLabel`; the filter button reports `aria-expanded` and controls the selects; each applied chip's remove button is named by the chip; a client mark is named by the client; each group is an `h3`; the table is `table`'s `role="table"`, and the phone list is `item`'s `role="list"` of `role="listitem"` rows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): row links and group headings `var(--text-default)`, headers and meta `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the field, select and button transitions belong to the composed components, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the search field, selects and empty-state button are large; each phone row link stretches over its whole item and each table row is a whole-row target.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-`/`pe-`); a mark sits at the inline start of its flex row; columns mirror with the table.
- Icons: the filter and search glyphs do not mirror; client marks never mirror.
- Keyboard: the selects own their keyboard map under `rtl`.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                           | English source      | Override prop |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| `listingIndex.filters`        | `Filters`           | `filterLabel` |
| `listingIndex.filtersApplied` | `{label} ({count})` | —             |
| `listingIndex.search`         | `Search`            | —             |
| `listingIndex.searchFacet`    | `Search {facet}`    | —             |
| `listingIndex.noMatch`        | `No results found.` | —             |

- Every other string (title, column labels, facet labels, placeholders, the empty state) arrives through props.
- Formatting: none; values arrive pre-formatted.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow (< `lg`): the toolbar folds to the filter button and the search field; the selects stack inside the disclosure; applied facets wrap as chips.
- Narrow (< `sm`): the table is hidden and the rows render as an item list under sticky group headings.
- Touch: each phone row is a whole-item link; each table row is a whole-row target; the button, field and selects are large.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; metadata truncates instead of widening the table, its full text in the tooltip.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ListingIndex from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-index'
</script>

<template>
  <ListingIndex
    title="Open positions"
    :columns="[
      { key: 'role', label: 'Role', grow: 2 },
      { key: 'team', label: 'Team and location', grow: 2 },
      { key: 'type', label: 'Work type', align: 'end' }
    ]"
    :data="[
      {
        href: '/careers/software-engineer-go',
        group: 'Engineering',
        values: {
          role: 'Software Engineer (Go)',
          team: 'Engineering · San Francisco',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        },
        facets: { area: ['Engineering'], location: ['San Francisco'] }
      },
      {
        href: '/careers/grc-analyst',
        group: 'Security',
        values: {
          role: 'GRC Analyst (Governance, Risk & Compliance)',
          team: 'Compliance and Corporate IT · San Francisco / New York',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        },
        facets: { area: ['Security'], location: ['San Francisco', 'New York'] }
      }
    ]"
    :groups="['Engineering', 'Security']"
    :facets="[
      {
        id: 'area',
        label: 'Department',
        allLabel: 'All departments',
        options: [
          { value: 'Engineering', label: 'Engineering' },
          { value: 'Security', label: 'Security' }
        ]
      },
      {
        id: 'location',
        label: 'Location',
        allLabel: 'All locations',
        options: [
          { value: 'New York', label: 'New York, United States' },
          { value: 'San Francisco', label: 'San Francisco, United States' }
        ]
      }
    ]"
    :sorts="[
      { value: 'newest', label: 'Newest posted', by: '' },
      { value: 'title', label: 'Title (A–Z)', by: 'role' }
    ]"
    sort-aria-label="Sort positions"
    search-placeholder="Search by title, team, or location"
    search-short-placeholder="Search positions"
    search-aria-label="Search positions"
    empty-title="Nothing here yet"
    empty-description="No open positions match your search."
    empty-action-label="View all open positions"
  />
</template>
```
