<!-- components/listing-table.md -->

# Listing Table

> A titled preview of a longer listing: a few linked rows in columns, and one outlined button into the full list. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'listing-table', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `table` and, below `sm`, `item`. Each row is one link named by its first column; a pointer click anywhere on the row follows that link (with the same modifier keys), and the link stays the keyboard and screen-reader path. The other columns are metadata in the small overline, each cut to one line with its full text as a tooltip. Below `sm` the same rows become a list of items, the first column as the title and the second as the description in the small overline, with the button going full width.

- Import: `import ListingTable from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-table'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To preview the latest entries of a listing (open roles, releases, events) with a way into the full list.

## Do

- Keep three columns at most; the first names the row and the second describes it on phones.
- Give the wide columns `grow: 2` and align a short trailing column to `end`.
- Keep the preview to a handful of rows and point `primaryAction` at the full listing.

## Don’t

- For a filterable or paginated listing → use `listing-index`.
- For a comparison of plans or features → use the pricing matrix.

## Related

- `table` — the composition table the wide layout renders.
- `listing-index` — the full listing this band links into.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the left-aligned section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `columns` | `ListingTableColumn[]` | `[]` | false | The columns left to right; each is `{ key, label, grow?, align? }` where `key` picks the row value, `grow` is the flex weight (1, 2 or 3) and `align` is `start` or `end`. The first column names the row and the second describes it on phones. |
| `data` | `ListingTableRow[]` | `[]` | false | The linked rows, in order; each is `{ href, values }` where `values` maps a column key to its text. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Outlined button into the full listing, in the table footer; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row fill `var(--bg-hover)` in both the table and the list)
- Whole-row navigation: a click on a row outside its link is forwarded to the link, keeping `ctrl`/`meta`/`shift`/`alt`; a click that ends a text selection is not forwarded
- Metadata cells (every column after the first) render `text-overline-sm`, truncated to one line, with their full value as `title`
- Empty: when `data` or `columns` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; the footer button only when `primaryAction` is set
- Below `sm` the table is hidden and the rows render as an item list

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the row links and the composed `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each row's link and then the button; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the table keeps its native column headers; the phone list is the same rows as list items.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): row titles `var(--text-default)`, values `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the button carries its own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each phone row is a whole-item link; the button is large.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-`/`pe-`); columns mirror with the table.
- Icons: the button's trailing chevron mirrors (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Column labels, row values and the action arrive through props.
- Formatting: none; values arrive pre-formatted.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow (< `sm`): the table is hidden and the rows render as an item list, the description in the small overline, the button full width.
- Touch: each phone row is a whole-item link; each table row is a whole-row target.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; metadata truncates instead of widening the table, its full text in the tooltip.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import ListingTable from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-table'
</script>

<template>
  <ListingTable
    title="Latest roles"
    :columns="[
      { key: 'role', label: 'Role', grow: 2 },
      { key: 'team', label: 'Team and location', grow: 2 },
      { key: 'type', label: 'Work type', align: 'end' }
    ]"
    :data="[
      {
        href: '/careers/senior-platform-engineer',
        values: {
          role: 'Senior Platform Engineer',
          team: 'Delivery Engineering · San Francisco',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        }
      },
      {
        href: '/careers/senior-quality-automation-engineer',
        values: {
          role: 'Senior Quality Automation Engineer',
          team: 'Delivery Engineering · San Francisco',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        }
      },
      {
        href: '/careers/software-engineer-go',
        values: {
          role: 'Software Engineer (Go)',
          team: 'Engineering · San Francisco',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        }
      },
      {
        href: '/careers/software-engineer-rust',
        values: {
          role: 'Software Engineer (Rust and/or C/C++)',
          team: 'Platform Engineering · San Francisco / New York',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'

      },
      {
        href: '/careers/senior-infrastructure-analyst',
        values: {
          role: 'Senior Infrastructure Analyst',
          team: 'SRE · San Francisco / New York',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        }
      },
      {
        href: '/careers/software-engineer-frontend',
        values: {
          role: 'Software Engineer (Frontend)',
          team: 'UX Engineering · San Francisco',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        }
      }
    ]"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'See all 23 roles', href: '/careers/jobs', trailing: true }"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/logo-wall-section.md -->

# Logo Wall Section

> The customers band: a section title over a framed logo wall of linked client marks with one signed quote in its aside, closed by a call to action. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'logo-wall-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `logo-wall`, `quote` and `button`.

- Import: `import LogoWallSection from '@aziontech/webkit/logo-wall-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use LogoWallSection for customer logos plus one featured quote.
- To prove adoption with marks and let one customer speak, early on a home or solution page.

## Do

- Eight or nine logos fill the rectangle wall beside the aside.
- Pass client registry entries (`@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`) as they stand: each carries `name`, `logo` and either `logoLight` (a light-theme drawing) or `artwork` (which theme a single file must be inverted on), and every mark renders through `Logo`.
- Without a registry entry, set `logoTreatment` per mark: `monochrome` for a mark drawn in one ink that must follow the theme, `knockout` for a black mark on a coloured fill, `color` for a colour mark, and `artwork: 'light'` for a reversed mark that must flip on the light theme; give a `logoLight` file instead when the light theme needs a different drawing.
- Give the quote's company mark a `logoLight` (or an `artwork`) the same way, so it stays legible on both themes.
- Keep to one or two actions under the quote: the primary (`secondary` variant) and an optional outlined `secondaryAction`.

## Don’t

- For several quotes in turn → use `client-quotes`.
- For marks with photos and stories in a mosaic → use `client-mosaic`.

## Related

- `logo-wall` — the wall the marks are laid in, with the quote in its aside.
- `logo` — draws every mark (the wall's and the quote's) right on both themes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `LogoWallSectionVariant` | `'wall'` | false | Layout of the band: `wall` sets the client marks with the quote in their aside, `quote` sets the quote alone as a full-width band (the design sample's QuoteBand) and needs no logos. |
| `quoteVariant` | `LogoWallSectionQuoteVariant` | `'signed'` | false | Register of the quote in the `quote` layout: the featured `highlight` or the band-sized `signed` sentence. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the logo wall. |
| `logos` | `LogoWallSectionLogo[]` | `[]` | false | The client marks, in order; each is `{ name, logo, logoLight?, logoTreatment?, artwork?, href? }` where `logoTreatment` is the shared `LogoTreatment` (`'color'`, `'monochrome'` or `'knockout'`, the `Logo` looks) and `artwork` is the registry's `'color'`, `'light'` or `'dark'`. |
| `quote` | `LogoWallSectionQuote` | `undefined` | false | The signed quote in the wall's aside; `{ text, name, jobTitle, logo, logoAlt, logoLight?, artwork? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Button under the quote; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Outlined button beside the primary one under the quote; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `logos` is empty the band renders nothing
- Each mark is a `Logo` carrying `data-treatment` (the `logoTreatment`, default `color`), `data-variant`, `data-artwork` and `data-route` (`pair`, `single` or `wordmark`), so the theme-following inks are driven by data attributes
- Not applicable: `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `logo-wall` (each mark link) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between mark links and the action; `Enter` follows.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the wall is `logo-wall`'s own list named by `ariaLabel`; every mark is a `Logo` (`role="img"`) named by the client `name`, announced once even when a light/dark pair renders; the quote is a `blockquote` signed by its author.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components; marks follow the theme through their treatment.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each mark link spans its wall cell.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the composed `section-title`, `logo-wall`, `quote` and `button` use logical utilities; the band adds none of its own.
- Icons: the trailing chevron of an action is mirrored by `button`; logos are never mirrored.
- Keyboard: `Tab` order follows the DOM, which follows the reading direction.
- User data: a client name drawn as a wordmark is wrapped in `dir="auto"` by `Logo`.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: the title, the quote, the client names and the action labels are content the page passes.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `logo-wall` reflows the marks and moves the aside under them on narrow widths.
- Narrow: the marks cap at the wall cell's width (`max-w-full`), widening to a 96 px cap from `sm`.
- Touch: each mark link spans its wall cell (well over 44 px); actions are `large` buttons.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

      },
      {

        logo: zoopExtendedColor,

      {

<!-- components/media-split-section.md -->

# Media Split Section

> One claim beside its picture, on its own frame: the copy cell with its overline, headline and sentence on one side, and the media on a raised, pixel-textured surface on the other. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, a framed `media-split`, `button`, `code-block`, `illustration`, `console-mockup`, `diagram` and the webkit scene assets. The media is a scene, a code sample (one file or a tab strip of files), a product console widget, a request-flow diagram, an image (cover or framed) or an illustration; with one action the whole band links to it (unless `linked` is off), with two the band stays unlinked. The media sits beside the copy, or under it when `orientation` is `vertical`.

- Import: `import MediaSplitSection from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → the section (`media-split-section`). Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the primitive (`media-split`).
- Use MediaSplitSection for one marketing claim beside its picture, scene or code.
- To make one point beside one picture and move on (a values statement, a single product claim).
- To set a claim beside the code that delivers it (`codeTabs`), with the files in a tab strip.

## Do

- Give the band exactly one media: `scene`, `codeTabs`, `widget` (a `ConsoleMockup` name), `diagram` (a `Diagram` name), `image` or `illustration`; when several are set the first of that order wins.
- A code sample holds controls of its own (tabs, copy), so the band never links to its lone action while it shows code; give it a `variant: 'ghost'` action for a quiet "Learn more".
- On a product page prefer `widget` or `diagram`: they show the product itself. Do not drop to `media-split` and its `media` slot to place one.
- Set `image.framed` for a picture that is an object rather than a scene (a badge, a logo, a screenshot): it sits whole on a rounded, bordered plate inset in the cell instead of covering it.
- Use `size="large"` for a band that carries only its headline and description.
- Use `orientation="vertical"` for a wide scene that needs the full width of the frame under the copy.
- Turn `linked` off when the media holds controls of its own, so a click in it is not taken as a click on the band.
- Set `anchor` when another part of the page links to the band.
- Give an `image` its `width` and `height` so the page reserves its box before it loads.

## Don’t

- For several claims stacked one after the other → use `media-split-stack-section`.
- For a full-width terminal session with no copy column → use `cli-terminal`.
- For copy beside one piece of media in a hand-built SFC that needs the `media` slot → use `media-split`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the band primitive the section is rendered with.
- `media-split-stack-section` — the stacked sibling for a run of claims.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2` and naming its region; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph under the headline. |
| `size` | `MediaSplitSectionSize` | `'medium'` | false | Type scale of the copy; `large` sets the headline at heading-xl and centres the copy beside the media, `medium` aligns it to the top of the media. |
| `orientation` | `MediaSplitSectionOrientation` | `'horizontal'` | false | Axis the band splits on; `vertical` stacks the media under the copy for a wide scene. |
| `texture` | `TextureVariant` | `'pixelate'` | false | Texture painted under the media: `dots`, `grid`, `lines`, `dither`, `pixelate` or `none`. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Links the whole band to a lone action; turn it off when the media holds controls of its own. |
| `scene` | `MediaSplitSectionScene` | `undefined` | false | Scene drawn in the media cell, `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset and the props bound onto it; wins over every other media. |
| `codeTabs` | `MediaSplitSectionCodeTab[]` | `[]` | false | Files of the code sample drawn in the media cell when no scene is set, in order; each is `{ label, value, code, language?, fileName?, fileIcon?, icon? }` where `icon` is a mark beside the tab label. A tab without `code` is skipped. |
| `defaultFile` | `string` | `''` | false | value` of the code tab open first; empty, or a value no tab carries, opens the first tab. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the code sample's copy button; empty keeps the code block's own. |
| `widget` | `ConsoleMockupName` | `undefined` | false | Name of the product console widget drawn in the media cell when neither a scene nor code is set. |
| `diagram` | `DiagramName` | `undefined` | false | Name of the request-flow diagram drawn in the media cell when neither a scene nor a widget is set. |
| `image` | `MediaSplitSectionImage` | `undefined` | false | Picture drawn in the media cell when no scene, widget or diagram is set; `{ src, alt?, width?, height?, framed? }`, where `framed` sets it whole on a rounded plate instead of covering the cell. |
| `illustration` | `string` | `''` | false | Registry name of the illustration drawn in the media cell when no other media is set. |
| `illustrationAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the illustration; empty keeps it decorative. |
| `primaryAction` | `MediaSplitSectionAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, icon?, target?, variant? }`. When it is the only action it renders outlined with a trailing chevron, and the whole band links to it (not over code); `variant` overrides the drawn variant. |
| `secondaryAction` | `MediaSplitSectionAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, icon?, target?, variant? }`. With two actions the band stays unlinked. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `size` is forwarded to the media split and drives its type scale and copy alignment
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; with no media set the media cell is omitted
- With exactly one action the band is a link to that action's `href` (unless `linked` is `false`), and that lone action renders as an outlined button closed by the trailing chevron; with two the first is secondary, the second outlined, and the band is not a link
- `size="medium"` aligns the copy to the top of the media, `size="large"` centres it
- `orientation` and `texture` are forwarded to the media split
- Media precedence: `scene`, `codeTabs`, `widget`, `diagram`, `image`, `illustration`. Code, a widget, a diagram and a framed image are inset from the cell's edges (`media-split`'s `mediaPadded`); a scene, a plain image (which covers the cell) and an illustration run flush
- A widget plays its beat while the pointer is over the band, and shows its finished state on touch and under reduced motion (owned by `console-mockup`); it draws no collaborator cursor (`cursor` off), so the band reads as the product screen
- Scenes, code block, widget and diagram load on demand (`defineAsyncComponent`)
- Code: the sample opens on `defaultFile` (or the first tab), numbers its lines and types them in once; the band does not link to a lone action while it shows code
- An action's `variant` (`secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`) wins over the drawn default; an action's `icon` is drawn before the label when it has no trailing chevron

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button` and `media-split`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions, and through the media link when the band links; over code it moves through the code block's tabs and copy button (owned by `code-block`).
- ARIA: the media split's `<section>` is the band's named region (`aria-label` from `title`), so the root is a plain `div`; the headline is its `h2`; an image is named by `alt`, an illustration by `illustrationAriaLabel`, and both are decorative when empty; a diagram is a `figure` named by the description its library entry carries; a widget is an inert, `aria-hidden` picture of the console, so the copy carries its meaning.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `media-split` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the scenes stop under reduced motion on their own.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the medium buttons meet it.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (owned by `media-split`).
- Icons: a trailing chevron on an action mirrors (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props in the page's language. Widget and diagram text is product UI copy owned by `console-mockup` and `diagram`.
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; `media-split` stacks the media under the copy below `lg`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): one column; a widget, a diagram and a framed image scale down with the cell.
- Touch: a widget shows its finished state instead of the hover beat.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MediaSplitSection from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-section'
</script>

<template>
  <MediaSplitSection
    eyebrow="Our values"
    title="Four values shape every role at Azion"
    description="Quality, Drive, Accountability, and Innovation. They guide how we work every day: we set high standards and measure what we deliver, take on hard problems with persistence, own our commitments and mistakes, and use AI and new technology to solve problems in new ways. Together, they help us earn and keep the trust of our customers."
    size="large"
    :scene="{ component: 'BrandGlobeScene' }"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/media-split-stack-section.md -->

# Media Split Stack Section

> A run of large media-split bands that pile up under the site header as the page scrolls, each a centered claim with an outlined "learn more" button beside its picture, the whole band linking through. An optional large centered section title opens the run. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-stack-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `section-stack`, `media-split`, `illustration`, `console-mockup`, `diagram` and `button`. A band's picture is one of four things: a `ConsoleMockup` console mock (`widget`), a `Diagram` request-flow figure (`diagram`), a registry `illustration`, or an `image` URL, plain or `imageFramed` on its own plate. `variant` picks the layout only: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band; the bands keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import MediaSplitStackSection from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-stack-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use MediaSplitStackSection for a run of linked claims that pile up as the reader scrolls.
- To list the solution areas or the claims of a page, one large band each, with a link through to its own page.

## Do

- Give a band one picture: `widget` (a `ConsoleMockup` name — the product's console screen), `diagram` (a `Diagram` name — its request flow), `illustration` (a registry name, with `illustrationLabel`) or `image` (a URL, with `imageAlt` when it says something). When several are set the first in that order wins; a band with none renders without its media cell.
- Prefer `widget` or `diagram` on a product page: they show the product itself, where an illustration only evokes it. Do not drop to `media-split` and its `media` slot to place one.
- Set `imageFramed` for a picture that is an object rather than a scene — a badge, a logo, a screenshot: it sits whole on a rounded, bordered plate inset in the cell. A plain `image` is scaled to fit the cell and never overflows it.
- Give every band an `action`; it is both the button and the link the whole band follows.

## Don’t

- For a single claim beside its picture, scene or code → use `media-split-section`.
- For small reasons in a grid → use `feature-tiles`.

## Related

- `section-stack` — the sticky run the bands pile up in.
- `media-split` — the band each entry renders through.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `MediaSplitStackSectionVariant` | `'media-end'` | false | Layout of the run: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the run so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the run, rendered by the large centered section title as its `h2`; the run renders no header when empty, and with a header each band's headline drops to an `h3`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the section title. |
| `bands` | `MediaSplitStackSectionBand[]` | `[]` | false | The bands, in order; each is `{ title, description, eyebrow?, href?, scene?, widget?, diagram?, image?, imageAlt?, imageFramed?, illustration?, illustrationLabel?, action? }` where `eyebrow` is the band's overline, `href` the link the whole band follows (falling back to the action's), `scene` a `{ component, props? }` webkit scene asset, `widget` a `ConsoleMockup` name, `diagram` a `Diagram` name, `image` a picture URL, `illustration` a registry name, and `action` `{ label, href }` the outlined button. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; hovering a linked band reveals its link affordance (owned by `media-split`)
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop
- Empty: when `bands` is empty the run renders nothing — not the header, not the stack
- The header renders only when `title` is set; a band renders its button only when it has an `action`, links as a whole to its `href` (or its action's when it has none), and renders its media cell only when it has a picture; a band's `eyebrow` sits above its headline
- Band headlines are `h2` when the run has no header and `h3` under the section title, so the outline never repeats a level
- Media precedence per band: `scene`, then `widget`, then `diagram`, then `illustration`, then `image`. A widget or a diagram is inset from the cell's edges (`media-split`'s `mediaPadded`), and so is a framed image; an illustration and a plain image run flush
- A widget plays its beat while the pointer is over its band (`hover`), and shows its finished state on touch and under reduced motion (owned by `console-mockup`); it draws no collaborator cursor (`cursor` off), so the band reads as the product screen
- Widget and diagram load on demand (`defineAsyncComponent`): a run that uses neither never downloads them

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button` and `media-split`'s media link.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each band's media link and button; `Enter` follows them.
- ARIA: the run is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; each band is `media-split`'s own section named by the band's title, with its headline as an `h3` under the run's `h2` (an `h2` when the run has no title); illustrations are named by `illustrationLabel` and images by `imageAlt`, or decorative when empty; a diagram is a `figure` named by the description its library entry carries; a widget is an inert, `aria-hidden` picture of the console, so the band's copy carries its meaning.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-split` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the run adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the medium buttons and the band links.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; `alternating` swaps the media side with the reading direction (owned by `media-split`).
- Icons: the button's trailing chevron mirrors (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props in the page's language. Widget and diagram text is product UI copy owned by `console-mockup` and `diagram`.
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; `media-split` stacks the media under the copy below `lg`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): one column per band; a widget, a diagram and a framed image scale down with the cell.
- Touch: a widget shows its finished state instead of the hover beat; the whole band stays one link.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

<!-- components/network-section.md -->

# Network Section

> The infrastructure band of a marketing page: a tall framed panel with the world network map drawn behind a small start-aligned title, a claims eyebrow and a row of claim chips, closed by a floor of client outcomes (a quote with its highlights and, when given, the client's mark), benefits (a topic each) or stats (headline figures). It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'network-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `network-map`, `section-title`, `card-grid`, `quote`, `feature-item` and `stats`. `variant` picks the floor only: `outcomes` renders the quotes on one column per entry — two at least, four at most; `benefits` renders the topics on up to three columns, balanced so every row is full; `stats` renders the figures as a `stats` row. The band above is the same.

- Import: `import NetworkSection from '@aziontech/webkit/network-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To state the network's reach with figures and back it with client results, product benefits or headline figures.

## Do

- Four short `claims`; they are chips, not sentences. Give a claim as `{ label, mobile: false }` to keep it to the medium breakpoint and up when the phone band has room for fewer chips.
- Two to four `outcomes`: the floor sets one column per entry, so it closes the grid; a fifth entry wraps to a second row.
- Three `benefits` (or six), each a short `title`, a `description` and an optional `icon`; each renders as a topic with its title as an `h3`.
- Four `stats` on the `stats` floor, each a `value` and a `label`, with an optional `prefix` and `suffix`.
- Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.
- Leave `logo` out of an outcome when the site shows the figure alone; the cell then renders no mark row.
- Use `logoTreatment: 'monochrome'` for a dark mark that must invert in the dark theme; leave `color` for a colour mark.

## Don’t

- For figures alone, without the map band → use `stats-section`.
- For a logo wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-section`.

## Related

- `network-map` — the animated map behind the copy.
- `quote` / `feature-item` — the cell types of the `outcomes` and `benefits` floors.
- `stats` — the row the `stats` floor renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `NetworkSectionVariant` | `'outcomes'` | false | Which floor closes the band: `outcomes` renders the client quotes, `benefits` the benefit topics on up to three columns, `stats` the headline figures. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the small section title as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `claimsEyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow-set line above the claims. |
| `claims` | `(string \| NetworkSectionClaim)[]` | `[]` | false | Short figures rendered as chips under the claims eyebrow, in order; each is a string or `{ label, mobile? }`, where `mobile: false` hides the chip below the medium breakpoint. |
| `outcomes` | `NetworkSectionOutcome[]` | `[]` | false | Client results for the `outcomes` floor, in order, one column each up to four; each is `{ logo?, logoAlt?, logoTreatment?, text, highlights? }` where `logo` is the mark URL (the cell renders no mark without it), `logoAlt` names the client, `logoTreatment` is `'monochrome'` or `'color'` (`LogoTreatment` without `knockout`), and `highlights` are the phrases of `text` set in the accent. |
| `benefits` | `NetworkSectionBenefit[]` | `[]` | false | Topics for the `benefits` floor, in order, on up to three columns balanced so every row is full; each is `{ title, description, icon? }`, rendered as a topic whose title is an `h3`. |
| `stats` | `NetworkSectionStat[]` | `[]` | false | Figures for the `stats` floor, in order, rendered by `stats`; each is `{ value, label, prefix?, suffix? }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop and selects the floor (`outcomes`, `benefits` or `stats`)
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing; when the selected floor's array is empty the band renders without a floor
- An outcome without `logo` renders its quote with no mark row
- The `benefits` floor is `card-grid`'s `balanced` layout with `columns: 3`, so three benefits fill one row and four split 2 × 2; every benefit is a `feature-item` with an `h3`, led by its glyph when it has an `icon`
- The `stats` floor is a `stats` row under a rule; `stats` picks its own column count so no cell is left empty
- Claims: a chip is `h-6` with `text-label-sm` below the small breakpoint and `h-7` with `text-label-md` from it; a claim with `mobile: false` carries `data-mobile="hidden"` and is hidden below the medium breakpoint
- Anchor: the root carries `id` = `anchor` when set, with a scroll margin so a `#hash` jump clears a sticky header
- The map renders twice: a faded top-right world from the medium breakpoint up, a centered masked world below it, framed close on the network (`scale` 3.3); both are `network-map`'s own animation

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the headline is the section title's `h2`; the claims are a real list; the maps are decorative and hidden from assistive technology by `network-map`; each outcome's mark carries the client name as `alt`; benefit topics are `h3`s; the `stats` floor is `stats`, one `figure` per stat with its label as the caption. A claim hidden below the medium breakpoint is `display: none` there, so assistive technology skips it too.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): claims eyebrow `var(--text-muted)`, claims `var(--text-default)` on a tinted canvas; the map sits at low opacity behind the copy and never under the text column on large screens.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the map animation belongs to `network-map`, which carries its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities and the composed components' own mirroring, so the network map, title, chips and floor fill from the inline start.
- Icons: action chevrons mirror (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props.

## Responsive

- Below medium the map is drawn as a strip under the copy (the full-height map column is hidden); from medium the map sits behind the copy, its fade widened between medium and large.
- The floor follows `card-grid`: outcomes take one column per entry, benefits up to three, stats the `stats` row.
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

<!-- components/newsletter-section.md -->

# Newsletter Section

> The closing band whose ask is a newsletter sign-up: the overline and a large headline on the lead side, a subscribe form labelled by the ask on the other, over a strip lit by the pixelated primary wave, then the hatched closing frame. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'newsletter-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `registration-frame`, `eyebrow`, `field`, `input`, `button` and `texture`. The block never sends: it validates the address locally (an empty field and a malformed address each show their message under the field) and on a valid submit emits `submit` with the event and `{ email }`; the site posts the address and reports the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`, which the band renders with the messages from `form`.

- Import: `import NewsletterSection from '@aziontech/webkit/newsletter-section'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use NewsletterSection when the closing ask is an email field.
- To close the Blog or the Resource Hub on a newsletter subscription.

## Do

- Set `loading` while the address is sent, then `submitted` or `failed` with the outcome.
- Keep `description` to one sentence; it is set as the large headline.
- Write `form.invalidMessage` with an example address so the fix is obvious.
- Place it last on the page, right above `site-footer`, after a hatched `section-gap`. It draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column: no trailing `SectionGap` and no closing `RegistrationFrame` + `Texture` (the `shell/site` close is for a page that ends on any other band). `webkit/no-gap-after-closing-section` flags the doubled close.

## Don’t

- For a close on one or two link actions or a command → use `closing-call-to-action`.
- For a close that lists deployable templates → use `template-gallery` with `closing`.
- For a lead form with several fields → use `hero-form-section`.

## Related

- `closing-call-to-action` — the closing band whose ask is a link action.
- `alert` — renders the success and failure messages.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `NewsletterSectionForm` | `—` | true | Copy of the subscribe form: `{ placeholder, submitLabel, successMessage, errorMessage, requiredMessage, invalidMessage }`. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow on the lead side, closed by the blinking cursor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The ask, rendered as the label of the email field; it also names the band. Empty, the field keeps a visually hidden built-in label. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | The pitch, rendered as the band's large `h2` on the lead side. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site is sending the address: the field is disabled, the button shows its loading state and a submit is ignored. |
| `submitted` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site sent the address: the form gives way to `form.successMessage`. |
| `failed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site could not send the address: `form.errorMessage` shows under the form. |
| `hatch` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the hatched closing frame under the band; turn it off when another closing band stacks directly below and draws the shared frame. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, values: Record<string, string>)` | Fired on a valid submit, not while `loading`; `values` is `{ email }` with the trimmed address. The block never sends it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `invalid`, `loading`, `submitted`, `failed`
- `invalid`: an empty field takes the amber `required` state with `form.requiredMessage`, a malformed address the red `invalid` state with `form.invalidMessage`, under the field (never both at once); focus returns to the field; typing clears it; nothing is emitted
- `loading` (prop): the field is disabled, the button shows its loading state and a submit emits nothing
- `submitted` (prop): the form is replaced by a success `Alert` with `form.successMessage`, which takes focus when focus was in the form
- `failed` (prop): a danger `Alert` with `form.errorMessage` shows under the form, which stays editable
- `hatch` off: the band renders without its closing frame, so the closing band stacked below draws the page's one close

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `input` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the field then the button; `Enter` in the field or on the button submits.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the ask is a `<label for>` bound to the field with `useId`, and without a title a visually hidden label ("Email address") keeps the field named; the field is an `<input type="email">` with `autocomplete="email"` and `spellcheck="false"`; the validation message is the field's helper text, an empty submit sets `aria-required` and a malformed address `aria-invalid`. The success message is a `status` region and the failure message an `alert`. The texture strip is `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): headline and ask `var(--text-default)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the texture and the button carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the field and the button are large.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the lead side and the form mirror under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the button glyph follows `button`; the texture and the mark are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key handling.
- User data: the email field is `type="email"` and renders the address as typed.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source  | Override prop |
| ------------------------- | --------------- | ------------- |
| `newsletterSection.email` | `Email address` | `title`       |

The ask, the button label and every message are props from the page JSON (`title`, `form.*`); the built-in label names the field only when `title` is empty.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the lead side and the form stack below `lg`.
- Narrow (below `lg`): the headline sits over the form, the field and the button share the row and the message drops under them.
- Touch: the field and the button are large; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NewsletterSection from '@aziontech/webkit/newsletter-section'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const form = {
    placeholder: 'Your email',
    submitLabel: 'Subscribe',
    successMessage: 'Thanks for subscribing to the Azion newsletter',
    errorMessage: 'We could not subscribe you. Try again.',
    requiredMessage: 'Enter your email address.',
    invalidMessage: 'Enter an email address like name@example.com.'
  }

  const subscribedEmail = ref('')

  const onSubmit = (event, values) => {
    subscribedEmail.value = values.email
  }
</script>

<template>
  <NewsletterSection
    anchor="contact"
    eyebrow="Stay up to date"
    title="Subscribe to our newsletter"
    description="Product updates, event highlights, and industry insights, delivered to your inbox."
    :form="form"
    :submitted="subscribedEmail !== ''"
    @submit="onSubmit"
  />
</template>
```

# Photo Marquee

> The office band of the careers page: a horizontal section title over a framed strip of photographs of varied aspect ratios that scrolls continuously and pauses on hover, on focus or from its pause control; the loop is the one `marquee` runs on. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'photo-marquee', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title` and `registration-frame`.

- Import: `import PhotoMarquee from '@aziontech/webkit/photo-marquee'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PhotoMarquee for a decorative moving strip of photos.
- To show a place or a team in pictures without a grid.

## Do

- Give every photo its `width` and `height` so the strip reserves each slot before the picture loads.
- Leave `duration` at `0` to let the strip pace itself (ten seconds per photo).

## Don’t

- For quotes → use `recognition-marquee`.

## Related

- `recognition-marquee` — the sibling strip of quotes with the same loop.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph beside the headline. |
| `descriptionWidth` | `PhotoMarqueeDescriptionWidth` | `'narrow'` | false | Width the description is capped at: `narrow` or `wide`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds one loop of the strip takes; `0` paces it at ten seconds per photo. |
| `photos` | `PhotoMarqueePhoto[]` | `[]` | false | The photographs, in order; each is `{ src, alt, width, height }`. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, paused while the strip is hovered or holds focus, or while its pause control is pressed (the track carries `data-paused`)
- Empty: when `photos` is empty the band renders nothing
- The list is rendered twice for a seamless loop; the duplicate is `aria-hidden`, its photos carry an empty `alt`, and it is hidden under reduced motion, where the region scrolls by hand instead

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the scrolling region is focusable and carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region, which pauses the loop, then the pause control (`Enter` / `Space` toggles it, WCAG 2.2.2); under reduced motion the control is hidden and arrow keys scroll the region.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the strip is a `region` named by `ariaLabel`; every photo carries its `alt` once — the duplicate copy is `aria-hidden` with empty `alt`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the strip; the duplicate list is hidden so nothing moves and nothing repeats.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable beyond the focusable region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: under `dir="rtl"` the marquee track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed, so photos flow in reading order; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every visible and announced text is a prop from the page JSON.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: the strip is a fixed-height row that loops horizontally.
- Narrow (below `sm`): photos are 20rem tall instead of 28rem.
- Touch: the strip is one focusable region; hover pauses the loop on a pointer device and focus pauses it on any device.
- Reflow: the strip clips inside its frame, so the page never scrolls horizontally at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

<!-- components/plan-comparison.md -->

# Plan Comparison

> The feature-by-feature matrix under the plan cards on Pricing: one column per plan with its name and action button pinned in the header while the page scrolls, one band per product with an overline, a title and a lead, and one row per feature saying what each plan includes — an included mark, a not-included mark, or the allowance as text. The recommended plan carries an accent bar, and below the large breakpoint the table folds to one plan picked from a searchable select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'plan-comparison', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `select`, `input`, `button`, `icon-button`, `popover`, `tooltip`, `eyebrow`, `tag` and `link`.

- Import: `import PlanComparison from '@aziontech/webkit/plan-comparison'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PlanComparison for a feature matrix across plans or support tiers: on Pricing under the plan cards, product by product, and on Support with one column per support tier.

## Do

- Give every plan a stable `id`; the narrow-screen picker selects by it.
- Mark one plan `highlighted`; it gets the accent bar, the secondary button and opens the picker.
- Give every row's `values` one entry per plan, in plan order.
- Use a row's `hint` to define the term its label names; it opens in a popover titled with the label, so it can run to a sentence or two.
- Set `includedLabel` and `excludedLabel` to the page's words; left empty, the marks read the locale's Included and Not included.

## Don’t

- To compare Azion with one competitor → use `competitor-comparison`.
- For price cards with a billing-period toggle → use `pricing-plans`.

## Related

- `pricing-plans` — the plan cards this matrix sits under.
- `competitor-comparison` — Azion against one competitor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `caption` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader caption naming the table. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the feature column, shown from the large breakpoint up. |
| `pickerAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the plan picker shown below the large breakpoint. |
| `includedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of an included cell; empty uses the locale catalog (`Included`). |
| `excludedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of a not-included cell; empty uses the locale catalog (`Not included`). |
| `plans` | `PlanComparisonPlan[]` | `[]` | false | The plan columns, in order; each is `{ id, name, description?, highlighted?, action }` with `action` as `{ label, href }`; a plan without a name is dropped. |
| `sections` | `PlanComparisonSection[]` | `[]` | false | The product bands, in order; each is `{ eyebrow, title, description, rows, action? }` (`action` closes the band, `{ label, href }`) and a row is `{ label, values, group?, hint?, tag? }` with one value per plan: `true` or `✓` is included, `—` is not included, other text shows as written, empty is blank; `hint` defines the label in a popover. |
| `primaryAction` | `SectionTitleAction` | `undefined` | false | Closing link under the table, opened in a new tab; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The highlighted plan carries the accent bar and the secondary button; the others carry an outlined button
- Below the large breakpoint only the picked plan's column shows (`data-folded` on the others); the picker opens on the highlighted plan, or the first
- Picker search: the picker's list carries a search field that narrows the plans by name; with no match it shows a `role="status"` line from the locale catalog (`No results found.`); the query clears each time the list opens or closes
- Cells: an included cell is a `ai ai-circle-check` mark and a not-included cell an `ai ai-circle-minus` mark, each with a tooltip of its label on hover and the same label as `sr-only` text
- Hint: a row with `hint` ends its label with an info icon button that opens a popover titled with the label and described by the hint
- Closing rule: when neither the last band nor the table carries a closing link, the last row draws a bottom rule (`data-closing`) so the table never ends open
- Below the large breakpoint the plan button's label wraps (auto height, at least 40 px) instead of widening the table, so the folded matrix fits a 320 px screen whatever the font metrics.
- A group row (`group: true`) reads in the default text colour and draws a top rule unless it opens its band
- Empty: when no plan has a name the band renders nothing but its root

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `select`, `input`, `button`, `icon-button` and `link`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the picker (below `lg`), each plan button, each hint button and the closing link; the picker's keyboard map is `select`'s and its search field takes typing while the list is open; `Enter` or `Space` on a hint button opens its popover and `Escape` closes it, returning focus to the button (`popover`'s map).
- ARIA: the table carries a `caption`, `scope="col"` plan heads, a `scope="colgroup"` head per band and a `scope="row"` head per feature, so each value is announced with its row and plan. The included and not-included marks are `aria-hidden` and carry their label as `sr-only` text (the tooltip repeats it for pointer users); each hint button is named `About <label>` from the locale catalog and its popover is titled by the label; the picker's search field is named `Search <picker name>` and its no-match line is a `status`; the accent bar is decorative; the plan names stay readable to screen readers below `lg`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the composed controls carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the plan buttons and the picker are `large`.
- Reflow: below `lg` (one plan column beside the row labels) the header cells, the section headings and the row labels use `var(--spacing-sm)` side padding instead of `var(--spacing-lg)`, so the two columns fit a 640px box at 200% zoom; from `lg` the padding is unchanged.

## Examples

### Band links

```vue

    }
  ]

  const sections = [
    {
      eyebrow: 'Compute',
      title: 'Functions',
      description: 'Run code close to users.',
      rows: [
        { label: 'Requests per month', values: ['1M', '10M'] },

      ],

<template>

```

<!-- components/platform-directory.md -->

# Platform Directory

> A directory of Azion's products under a section title: one column per product group (Build, Store, Secure, Observe), each row an icon, a product name and one line about it, linking to that product. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'platform-directory', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame` and `link-directory` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import PlatformDirectory from '@aziontech/webkit/platform-directory'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PlatformDirectory for the Azion products directory band.
- On Home, right under the hero, to show every product the platform offers at a glance.
- On a solution, product or pricing page that repeats the full product map.

## Do

- Keep to four groups or fewer; the directory fans out to one column per group at the large breakpoint, up to four, so one, two or three groups never leave an empty cell.
- Give each item an `href`; an item without a title or a link is skipped, and a group left with no items is skipped too.
- Set `ariaLabel` so the directory's navigation landmark is told apart from the site navigation; left empty, the landmark takes the `title`.
- Use `eyebrow` for the short label above the headline (the page's name for the product map) and `description` for one sentence under it.
- Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.

## Don’t

- For a handful of icon-led use cases → use `customer-use-cases`.
- For a site-wide navigation menu → use `navigation-menu`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `link-directory` directly.

## Related

- `link-directory` — the named navigation landmark whose columns and rows this band fills.
- `section-title` — the headline over the directory.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short label above the headline; shown only with a title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the directory, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header, eyebrow or description when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence under the headline; shown only with a title. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the directory's navigation landmark; empty uses the title. |
| `groups` | `PlatformDirectoryGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The columns, in order; each is `{ title, items }` where every item is `{ icon, title, description, href }`. Items without a title or an `href` are skipped, and so are groups left empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- One column per group from the large breakpoint, up to four (`link-directory`'s `columns` is 2, 3 or 4), one column below the small one; the column layout is `link-directory`'s own
- No empty cell: a single group spans the whole row (`data-span="full"`), and with three groups the third spans both columns between the small and the large breakpoints (`data-span="pair"`), so the rule colour never shows through a missing column
- Header: with a `title`, the section title renders the eyebrow and the description that are set around the headline; without one, no header renders
- Anchor: the root carries `id` = `anchor` when set, with a scroll margin so a `#hash` jump clears a sticky header
- Empty: when no group carries a linked item the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `link-directory` item links.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the product links in reading order; `Enter` follows one. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the directory is `link-directory`'s `nav`, named by `ariaLabel` (or the title when `ariaLabel` is empty), and each column's overline heading names its list of rows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the row hover belongs to `link-directory`, which carries its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each row is a full-width link taller than 40 px.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities and the composed components' own mirroring, so the directory cells fill from the inline start.
- Icons: action chevrons mirror (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props.

## Responsive

- One cell per row on phones (`mobileColumns: 1`); from the grid's breakpoints the cells fill the computed track count, wide cells spanning two tracks from small and large.
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

<!-- components/pricing-plans.md -->

# Pricing Plans

> The plan cards at the top of Pricing: a billing-period toggle over a framed row of pricing cards, each with its plan name, its price for the picked period, what it includes and one button. The recommended plan sits on a raised surface and carries a tag. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'pricing-plans', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `registration-frame`, `toggle-group`, `card-grid`, `pricing-card` and `button`; the picked period is local state. The band runs full bleed (the page's inline inset only, closed by a bottom rule) and centres its frame at the site measure, with rules on its sides.

- Import: `import PricingPlans from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-plans'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PricingPlans for price cards with a billing-period toggle on the public pricing page, the plans side by side at the top of Pricing.

## Do

- Give every plan one price per period, matched by `period`; a price without a `period` applies to every period.
- Highlight one plan; it is raised and is the only card that shows its tag.
- Put terms that hold for every period in the plan's `description`; a price's own `details` replaces it for that period.
- Keep `features` to five or so short labels led by an icon.

## Don’t

- To compare plans or support tiers feature by feature → use `plan-comparison`.
- To compare Azion with one competitor → use `competitor-comparison`.

## Related

- `pricing-card` — the card each plan renders with.
- `plan-comparison` — the matrix that sits under these cards.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `periods` | `PricingPlansPeriod[]` | `[]` | false | The billing periods of the toggle, in order; each is `{ label, value }`. The toggle shows with two or more and opens on the first. |
| `periodsAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the billing-period toggle. |
| `plans` | `PricingPlansPlan[]` | `[]` | false | The plan cards, in order; each is `{ name, description?, highlighted?, tagLabel?, prices, featuresTitle?, features?, action? }` where a price is `{ period?, value, prefix?, suffix?, details? }`, a feature is `{ icon, label }` and `action` is `{ label, href }`; `description` stands in for a price without `details`, a plan without a name is dropped, and an action without a label or href is dropped. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The picked period selects each plan's price; a plan with no price for it falls back to its period-less price
- Price change: every card is `animated`, so a period switch fades the old price out and the new one in (the card's reduced-motion fallback swaps it in place)
- Terms: the line under the price is the price's `details`, else the plan's `description`, else empty
- Layout: a full-width band (`__band`) on `var(--bg-canvas)` with the page's inline inset `var(--layout-boundary-inline)` and a bottom rule, and inside it a `registration-frame` with side rules and bottom marks capped at `var(--layout-measure-site)` and centred
- The highlighted plan sits on `var(--bg-surface)`, shows its tag and carries the secondary button; the others sit on `var(--bg-canvas)` with an outlined button
- Empty: when no plan has a name the band renders nothing but its root

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `toggle-group` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the toggle and each card's button; the toggle's arrow-key map is `toggle-group`'s.
- ARIA: the toggle is named by `periodsAriaLabel`; each plan is a `pricing-card` article with its name as `h3`; the features are a list and their glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the toggle indicator belongs to `toggle-group` and the price fade to `pricing-card`, each with its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion of its own.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the toggle and the buttons are `large`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities and the composed components' own mirroring, so the plan cards fill from the inline start.
- Icons: action chevrons mirror (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props.

## Responsive

- The plan cards follow `card-grid`: stacked on phones, side by side as the grid widens; the billing `toggle-group` stays above them.
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

<!-- components/process-scroll.md -->

# Process Scroll

> The stages of a process as a row of numbered dark cards on a pixel texture, under a section title. On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways with snap; from the large breakpoint up the cards share the width, or, with `pinned`, keep a 26rem card width while the band pins under the site header and the page scroll slides the row sideways until its last card is in view (azion.com's careers hiring process). The retired `'sticky-carousel'` `_id` resolves here with `pinned: true` and `titleVariant: 'center'`. From the design sample's site `ProcessScroll`.

- Import: `import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ProcessScroll for numbered stage cards; set `pinned` to pin them under the header while they slide.
- How something works in three to five ordered stages (build, deploy, observe), or five to eight short numbered points pinned on scroll (`pinned`, `title-variant="center"`).

## Do

- Name each stage with a verb.
- Keep descriptions to two lines.
- Set `pinned` when the stages run wider than the page column (five tall cards, as the careers hiring process): the band stays on screen while the page scroll walks the row. Do not nest a pinned band in a container that clips overflow; sticky positioning needs the page scroll.

## Don’t

- For more than five stages or stages with art — use `FeatureScroll`.

## Related

- Texture`, `RegistrationFrame`, `SectionTitle`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the title. |
| `titleVariant` | `SectionTitleVariant` | `'split'` | false | Alignment of the section title over the card row. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph beside the headline. |
| `descriptionWidth` | `SectionTitleDescriptionWidth` | `'narrow'` | false | Column span of the paragraph: `wide` runs it across the middle column too. |
| `steps` | `ProcessScrollStep[]` | `[]` | false | The stages, in order; each is `{ title, description }` and gets its own numbered card. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrollable card row; defaults to the title. |
| `pinned` | `boolean` | `false` | false | From the large breakpoint, pins the band under the site header while the page scrolls and slides the card row sideways until its last card is in view; below it, or under reduced motion, the row scrolls sideways on its own. |
| `headerOffset` | `string` | `'var(--layout-header-height)'` | false | Height of the sticky site header a pinned band sticks under; defaults to the SiteHeader bar's token, any CSS length. |

## States

- Renders nothing without a title or steps.
- Cards are `data-theme="dark"` in both themes (the sample's design).
- `data-pinned` on the root mirrors `pinned`. From `lg` with motion allowed, the band is `sticky` under `headerOffset` and one screen tall, the root (the runway) grows by the row's overflow, and the row's `translate` follows the page scroll (mirrored in right-to-left); below `lg` or under `prefers-reduced-motion` the band does not pin and the row scrolls inside itself. The runway is measured on mount and on scroll/resize, so the server HTML is the unpinned band.

## Accessibility

- The band root is a plain container; the scroll row is the one focusable `region`, named by `ariaLabel` or the title, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys and the page has one landmark per band.
- Stages are an ordered list; the big number is `aria-hidden` because the list already orders them.
- Each stage heading is an `h3`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-*`, `border-e`, `ms-*`).
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- Below large: cards are `min(22rem, 80vw)` wide and snap; the row scrolls inside itself, never the page.
- From large: cards share the width; with `pinned`, cards keep a 26rem width and the pinned band slides them sideways.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'

  const steps = [
    { title: 'Push', description: 'Every push to the main branch builds a new version.' },
    { title: 'Build', description: 'The build runs in an isolated worker with your settings.' },
    {
      title: 'Deploy',
      description: 'The version goes live everywhere at once, with no regions to pick.'
    },
    { title: 'Observe', description: 'Metrics and logs for the new version arrive in seconds.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ProcessScroll
    eyebrow="How it works"
    title="From commit to production"
    description="Four stages, all automatic once the repository is connected."
    :steps="steps"
  />
</template>
```

# Recognition Marquee

> The analyst-recognition band: a section title over a framed strip of signed quotes — one per report, marked by the firm's logo — that scrolls continuously and pauses on hover, on focus or from its pause control; the loop is the one `marquee` runs on. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'recognition-marquee', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame` and `quote`.

- Import: `import RecognitionMarquee from '@aziontech/webkit/recognition-marquee'`
- Category: section · Surface: site · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use RecognitionMarquee only for a looping row of analyst or press quotes.
- To list analyst reports and awards on a page that needs third-party proof.

## Do

- Five to eight items; the loop needs enough width to read as continuous.
- Leave `duration` at `0` to let the strip pace itself (twelve seconds per item).

## Don’t

- For office photos → use `photo-marquee`.
- For customer quotes → use `client-quotes`.

## Related

- `quote` — the signed card each recognition renders with.
- `photo-marquee` — the sibling strip of pictures with the same loop.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Eyebrow above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds one loop of the strip takes; `0` paces it at twelve seconds per item. |
| `items` | `RecognitionMarqueeItem[]` | `[]` | false | The recognitions, in order; each is `{ text, reportName, date?, firmName, logo, logoLight? }` where `logo` is the firm's mark on the dark theme and `logoLight` the one on the light theme. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, paused while the strip is hovered or holds focus, or while its pause control is pressed (the track carries `data-paused`)
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing
- The list is rendered twice for a seamless loop; the duplicate is `aria-hidden` and hidden under reduced motion, where the region scrolls by hand instead

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the scrolling region is focusable and carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region, which pauses the loop, then the pause control (`Enter` / `Space` toggles it, WCAG 2.2.2); under reduced motion the control is hidden and arrow keys scroll the region.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the strip is a `region` named by `ariaLabel`; the second copy of the list is `aria-hidden`; each firm mark carries `firmName` as `alt`; each recognition is a `blockquote` signed by its report and date.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `quote` on `var(--bg-surface)`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the strip; the duplicate list is hidden so nothing moves and nothing repeats.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable beyond the focusable region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: under `dir="rtl"` the marquee track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every visible and announced text is a prop from the page JSON.

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: the strip is a fixed-height row that loops horizontally.
- Narrow (below `sm`): each card is 85 % of the viewport wide, capped at `--container-md`.
- Touch: the strip is one focusable region; hover pauses the loop on a pointer device and focus pauses it on any device.
- Reflow: the strip clips inside its frame, so the page never scrolls horizontally at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples
